chunks.title: 101 Billion Arabic Words
chunks.text: 101 Billion Arabic Words (by ClusterlabAi), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The 101 Billion Arabic Words Dataset is a pretraining corpus of Arabic web text, mixing Modern Standard Arabic and dialects, for training and fine-tuning language models. Arabic content was extracted from Common Crawl WET files, then cleaned and deduplicated, yielding about 101 billion words in 33 million documents.

chunks.title: 101 Billion Arabic Words
chunks.text: 101 Billion Arabic Words (by ClusterlabAi), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It is curated by the Clusterlab team.

chunks.title: A2UI
chunks.text: A2UI (by Google), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: A2UI (Agent-to-User Interface) is an open protocol that lets an AI agent describe an interface as declarative JSON, which the client draws from its own catalog of trusted components instead of running code the agent wrote.

chunks.title: A2UI
chunks.text: A2UI (by Google), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: Its repository holds the specification, renderers for Lit, Angular and React, and agent SDKs for Python and Dart, and messages travel over A2A or AG-UI. Google created it, with contributions from CopilotKit.

chunks.title: Accelerate
chunks.text: Accelerate (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Accelerate is a Hugging Face PyTorch library that runs raw PyTorch training scripts across CPUs, multiple GPUs and TPUs with mixed precision, adding only a few lines of code.

chunks.title: Accelerate
chunks.text: Accelerate (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It abstracts the boilerplate of distributed setup and device placement while leaving the training loop under the caller's control, and provides a CLI for configuration.

chunks.title: ACE-Step
chunks.text: ACE-Step (by ACE-Step), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: ACE-Step is an open music generation model family from the ACE Studio and StepFun collaboration that writes full songs, vocals included, from lyrics and a style prompt.

chunks.title: ACE-Step
chunks.text: ACE-Step (by ACE-Step), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: ACE-Step 1.5 pairs a diffusion transformer, up to 4B parameters in its XL variants, with a language model that plans the song, and supports cover generation, repainting, completion and LoRA training.

chunks.title: ACI.dev
chunks.text: ACI.dev (by Aipotheosis Labs), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Open-source tool-calling platform connecting more than six hundred tools to agents through direct function calling or a unified MCP server, with multi-tenant OAuth flows and secrets management so an agent can act on behalf of a named end user.

chunks.title: Adobe PDF Extract API
chunks.text: Adobe PDF Extract API (by Adobe), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Document-extraction API from Adobe that returns a PDF's text, tables and figures as structured JSON with the reading order and styling information the format carries, built on Adobe's own PDF engine rather than on OCR of a rendered page.

chunks.title: Aegis AI Content Safety
chunks.text: Aegis AI Content Safety (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Aegis AI Content Safety is NVIDIA's content-safety classifier, now also called Llama Nemotron Safety Guard Defensive. It is a parameter-efficient tune of Meta's LlamaGuard-7b, built on Llama 2 7B and trained on NVIDIA's Aegis dataset across 13 critical risk categories.

chunks.title: Aegis AI Content Safety
chunks.text: Aegis AI Content Safety (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Although it was trained only to classify user prompts, it can also label responses through the same template, and it ships beside a permissive variant.

chunks.title: African UltraChat
chunks.text: African UltraChat (by Masakhane), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: African UltraChat is a multi-turn chat dataset of about 55,000 conversations in 11 African languages, among them Amharic, Hausa, Igbo, Kinyarwanda, Swahili, Yoruba and isiZulu, with a small test split. Each record holds a user prompt and the exchange of user and assistant messages, tagged by language. Masakhane publishes it.

chunks.title: AfriDocMT
chunks.text: AfriDocMT (by Masakhane), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: AfriDocMT is a translation dataset of whole documents in which 334 health and 271 information technology news documents were translated by people from English into Amharic, Hausa, Swahili, Yoruba and isiZulu. It ships in both document and sentence form, with train, dev and test splits for each domain.

chunks.title: AfriDocMT
chunks.text: AfriDocMT (by Masakhane), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Its builders were funded by the Lacuna Fund, and Masakhane hosts the release.

chunks.title: AfriHate
chunks.text: AfriHate (by AfriHate), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: AfriHate is a hate speech and abusive language dataset of tweets in 15 African languages, including Algerian and Moroccan Arabic, Amharic, Hausa, Nigerian Pidgin, Swahili, Yoruba and isiZulu. Native speakers familiar with the local culture labeled each tweet as hate, abusive or normal.

chunks.title: AfriHate
chunks.text: AfriHate (by AfriHate), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The accompanying paper reports classification baselines from fine-tuned encoders such as AfriBERTa to prompted LLMs such as Llama 3.1 and Gemma 2.

chunks.title: Afrivoice
chunks.text: Afrivoice (by Digital Umuganda), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Afrivoice is a family of speech datasets, mostly recorded by speakers describing photographs aloud, with transcriptions for all or part of the audio.

chunks.title: Afrivoice
chunks.text: Afrivoice (by Digital Umuganda), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Releases cover Kinyarwanda, Swahili, five Ethiopian languages, a set including Shona, Lingala, Wolof and Somali, and a batch for Kirundi, Ndau, Ndebele, Oshiwambo and Gamo, about 15,000 hours across the current releases. Digital Umuganda collects and publishes it.

chunks.title: AfriVoices-KE
chunks.text: AfriVoices-KE (by African Next Voices Kenya), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: AfriVoices-KE is a speech dataset of about 3,000 hours in five Kenyan languages, Dholuo, Kikuyu, Kalenjin, Maasai and Somali, recorded on smartphones by 4,777 native speakers.

chunks.title: AfriVoices-KE
chunks.text: AfriVoices-KE (by African Next Voices Kenya), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: About 750 hours are scripted readings across eleven domains and the rest is spontaneous speech prompted by text and images, checked by human reviewers. The Kenyan arm of the African Next Voices project publishes one repository per language.

chunks.title: AfroBench
chunks.text: AfroBench (by McGill NLP), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: AfroBench is an evaluation suite for large language models covering 64 African languages, 15 tasks and 22 datasets.

chunks.title: AfroBench
chunks.text: AfroBench (by McGill NLP), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It carries AfriMMLU, AfriXNLI, AfriMGSM, AfriSenti, MasakhaNER, MasakhaNEWS, MasakhaPOS, AfriQA, MAFAND-MT, SALT, Uhura, InjongoIntent, NaijaRC, NollySenti, NTREX African and AfriADR, with lm-evaluation-harness configs and a public leaderboard. It is published from the McGill-NLP GitHub organization, with its data in a Masakhane collection.

chunks.title: AG-UI Protocol
chunks.text: AG-UI Protocol (by AG-UI Protocol), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: Open event-based protocol standardizing how an AI agent connects to a user-facing application. Agent backends emit one of about sixteen standard event types over any transport, and front ends consume them through community SDKs in eight languages.

chunks.title: Agent Client Protocol
chunks.text: Agent Client Protocol (by Agent Client Protocol), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: Open protocol standardizing how a code editor talks to a coding agent, so any editor can drive any agent over one JSON-RPC interface. Published by Zed with a Rust schema crate and a TypeScript library alongside the specification.

chunks.title: Agent Infra Sandbox
chunks.text: Agent Infra Sandbox (by Agent Infra), catalog entry under Deployment: Agent Infra Sandbox, shipped as AIO Sandbox, bundles a VNC browser, shell, file service, Jupyter, VSCode Server and preconfigured MCP servers into a single Docker container, so an agent reaches all of them over one shared filesystem instead of coordinating separate services.

chunks.title: Agent Infra Sandbox
chunks.text: Agent Infra Sandbox (by Agent Infra), catalog entry under Deployment: Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs drive it through an HTTP API, and it deploys with Docker Compose or a plain Kubernetes manifest. The agent-infra organization maintains it.

chunks.title: agent-manager
chunks.text: agent-manager (by Yoan Wai), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Terminal UI that runs coding-agent CLIs side by side, each in its own persistent tmux session on a private tmux server.

chunks.title: agent-manager
chunks.text: agent-manager (by Yoan Wai), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: It launches the user's own installed CLI unmodified, shows every session's live status in one foldable project tree, answers a session without attaching to it, revives or forks a session on its own conversation, and opens a full-file diff review whose line comments go back to the agent as one prompt.

chunks.title: agent-manager
chunks.text: agent-manager (by Yoan Wai), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: It supports Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Grok Build, Gemini CLI, Pi, Command Code, Hermes Agent and Muse Code, and ships as a Go binary for macOS, Linux and Windows under WSL2.

chunks.title: Agent QA
chunks.text: Agent QA (by Vostride), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Agent that tests web and mobile apps from tests written in natural language. It plans and carries out each action, re-observes the interface and tries another path when a step fails, and keeps memory from earlier runs to reuse proven actions. It ships a CLI, a dashboard, MCP and agent skills, and runs on the model the user brings.

chunks.title: Agent2Agent Protocol
chunks.text: Agent2Agent Protocol (by A2A Project (Google-initiated)), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: Agent2Agent Protocol is an open protocol for communication and interoperability between opaque agentic applications. Where MCP connects agents to tools, A2A connects agents to other agents, defining task delegation, status updates and result passing between autonomous systems.

chunks.title: Agent2Agent Protocol
chunks.text: Agent2Agent Protocol (by A2A Project (Google-initiated)), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: Contributed by Google and hosted by the Linux Foundation, it has reference SDKs in Python, Go, JavaScript, Java, .NET and Rust, and integrations in Azure AI Foundry, Copilot Studio and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

chunks.title: Agenta
chunks.text: Agenta (by Agenta AI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Multiplayer workspace for building and running agents without writing code, where a team builds an agent by chatting with it.

chunks.title: Agenta
chunks.text: Agenta (by Agenta AI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Each agent gets a shared folder, reusable skills and an isolated sandbox, with more than a thousand integrations reachable directly or over MCP, human approval and permissions, and background agents on a schedule or an event trigger. Tracing covers every model and tool call.

chunks.title: AgentDojo
chunks.text: AgentDojo (by ETH Zurich SPY Lab), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Benchmark for evaluating prompt-injection attacks and defenses on tool-using LLM agents. It ships realistic task suites across workspace, banking, travel and Slack environments together with injection test cases, and grades agents on both task completion and security.

chunks.title: AgentDojo
chunks.text: AgentDojo (by ETH Zurich SPY Lab), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: The suite installs from PyPI and publishes results for common models and defenses.

chunks.title: AgentOps
chunks.text: AgentOps (by AgentOps AI), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Python SDK for AI agent monitoring and LLM cost tracking. It tracks multi-step agent sessions, tool calls, and costs across frameworks including CrewAI, Agno, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain, and Autogen, with setup in two lines of code. A self-hostable dashboard and API backend is available alongside the hosted app.

chunks.title: AgiBot World
chunks.text: AgiBot World (by AgiBot), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: AgiBot World is AgiBot's large-scale robot manipulation dataset, collected on a fleet of mobile dual-arm robots with dexterous hands and visual-tactile sensors.

chunks.title: AgiBot World
chunks.text: AgiBot World (by AgiBot), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: The Beta release holds about one million trajectories from a hundred robots across more than a hundred replicated real-life scenarios, with the curated Alpha subset and a 2026 release beside it.

chunks.title: AI Toolkit
chunks.text: AI Toolkit (by Ostris), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: AI Toolkit is a training suite for fine-tuning diffusion models, covering image, instruction-edit, video and audio model families including FLUX.1, FLUX.2, Qwen-Image and Wan. It trains LoRA and LyCORIS adapters, ships a web UI for configuring and monitoring runs, and provides recipes for running on RunPod and Modal.

chunks.title: AI Verify
chunks.text: AI Verify (by AI Verify Foundation), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: AI Verify is an AI governance testing framework and toolkit that runs standardized tests on classification and regression models against internationally recognized principles, with plugins that include a process checklist. It runs inside an enterprise's own environment, and its test algorithms can run as separate Python modules.

chunks.title: AI Verify
chunks.text: AI Verify (by AI Verify Foundation), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: The AI Verify Foundation, a subsidiary of Singapore's IMDA, maintains it.

chunks.title: AI2 ARC
chunks.text: AI2 ARC (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Benchmark of 7,787 grade-school science questions assembled to study advanced question answering, split into an Easy set of 5,197 and a Challenge set of 2,590. Published by the Allen Institute for AI in 2018, it remains a standard multiple-choice reasoning evaluation in model release reports.

chunks.title: Aider
chunks.text: Aider (by Aider AI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Terminal AI pair-programming tool that edits code directly in a local git repository, planning changes across the repo and committing them with generated messages. It supports 20+ model providers and uses a diff-based editing approach that keeps token use down. It installs from PyPI and runs as a command-line program.

chunks.title: AIFS
chunks.text: AIFS (by ECMWF), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: AIFS is the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts' data-driven forecasting system, a graph-neural-network encoder and decoder around a sliding-window transformer processor.

chunks.title: AIFS
chunks.text: AIFS (by ECMWF), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: AIFS Single v1.0 is the first operationally supported version, runs four times daily beside ECMWF's physics-based model, and ships its checkpoint alongside the Anemoi pretraining and fine-tuning configurations that produced it.

chunks.title: AI-Hub
chunks.text: AI-Hub (by National Information Society Agency (NIA)), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: AI-Hub is South Korea's national platform for AI training data, run by the National Information Society Agency (NIA) for the Ministry of Science and ICT.

chunks.title: AI-Hub
chunks.text: AI-Hub (by National Information Society Agency (NIA)), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: It publishes datasets built by companies and research groups under the government's data programme, in fields from Korean language and vision to healthcare and transport, alongside data other institutions contribute. Korean nationals apply to download each dataset, through the website or the aihubshell command-line tool.

chunks.title: AIMET
chunks.text: AIMET (by Qualcomm), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: AIMET (AI Model Efficiency Toolkit) quantizes and compresses trained models to cut the compute and memory they need on edge devices such as phones and laptops. It works on PyTorch and ONNX models and combines post-training techniques with fine-tuning that recovers accuracy lost to quantization. Qualcomm Innovation Center develops it.

chunks.title: AIRI
chunks.text: AIRI (by Moeru AI), catalog entry under UI & API: AIRI is a self-hosted AI companion platform from Moeru AI. It pairs a character-driven chat persona with speech synthesis and recognition, vision input, persistent memory and MCP tool access, and ships in three form factors: a browser build, a desktop build and a mobile build. It connects to many model providers through the xsAI client library.

chunks.title: AIStore
chunks.text: AIStore (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: AIStore is a distributed storage cluster built for AI workloads, presenting an S3-compatible object interface over local drives while also operating directly on remote cloud buckets. It scales out linearly, runs with or without Kubernetes, and offloads ETL and batch transformation into the storage layer so training jobs read transformed data in place.

chunks.title: AIStore
chunks.text: AIStore (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: NVIDIA develops it.

chunks.title: Aksharantar
chunks.text: Aksharantar (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Aksharantar is a transliteration corpus of about 26 million word pairs between English romanization and 21 Indic languages written in 12 scripts. Most pairs were mined from monolingual and parallel corpora such as IndicCorp and Samanantar, and human annotators added transliterated words and named entities, plus a test set of 103,000 pairs.

chunks.title: Aksharantar
chunks.text: Aksharantar (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: AI4Bharat built it alongside the IndicXlit transliteration model.

chunks.title: Algolia AI Search
chunks.text: Algolia AI Search (by Algolia), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Algolia AI Search is a hosted search API that combines keyword and semantic retrieval with AI ranking and personalization, built mainly for search on websites and in apps. Through its agent integrations and MCP server, an AI agent can also use it to search product catalogs, documentation and other indexed content.

chunks.title: ALIA-40b
chunks.text: ALIA-40b (by Barcelona Supercomputing Center), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Spain's national open LLM: a 40.4B-parameter decoder-only transformer pretrained from scratch by the Barcelona Supercomputing Center on the MareNostrum 5 supercomputer, under Spain's National Language Technology Plan.

chunks.title: ALIA-40b
chunks.text: ALIA-40b (by Barcelona Supercomputing Center), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: It was trained on 9.37 trillion tokens across 35 European languages and 92 programming languages, focusing on Spanish and the co-official Catalan, Valencian, Basque and Galician, with 48 layers, a 32,768-token context and a 256k vocabulary.

chunks.title: all-MiniLM
chunks.text: all-MiniLM (by UKP Lab (TU Darmstadt)), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: all-MiniLM maps a sentence or paragraph to a 384-dimensional dense vector for semantic search, clustering and retrieval-augmented generation. It runs a six-layer distilled MiniLM encoder contrastively fine-tuned on more than a billion sentence pairs, and truncates input beyond 256 word pieces.

chunks.title: all-MiniLM
chunks.text: all-MiniLM (by UKP Lab (TU Darmstadt)), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: A paraphrase-multilingual sibling carries the same architecture across fifty-odd languages. The Sentence-Transformers project ships both.

chunks.title: AlpacaEval
chunks.text: AlpacaEval (by Tatsu Lab (Stanford)), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Automatic judge-based evaluator for instruction-following models: a model annotator compares a candidate's outputs against a reference on a fixed instruction set to produce a win rate and a leaderboard. AlpacaEval 2.0 adds a length-controlled win rate to remove the bias toward longer outputs, which raises correlation with Chatbot Arena.

chunks.title: AlphaEarth Foundations
chunks.text: AlphaEarth Foundations (by Google), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: AlphaEarth Foundations is Google DeepMind's embedding field model for Earth observation.

chunks.title: AlphaEarth Foundations
chunks.text: AlphaEarth Foundations (by Google), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: It assimilates spatial, temporal, and measurement context from Landsat, Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and other sources into a 64-dimensional embedding for every 10-meter pixel of terrestrial land and shallow coastal water, published as annual Satellite Embedding layers in Google Earth Engine covering 2017 onward.

chunks.title: AlphaFold
chunks.text: AlphaFold (by Google), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: AlphaFold is Google DeepMind's biomolecular structure prediction line. AlphaFold 3, the current tier, predicts the joint structure of complexes of proteins, nucleic acids, ligands, ions and modified residues from sequence together with genetic-search and template inputs.

chunks.title: AlphaFold
chunks.text: AlphaFold (by Google), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: The inference source is Apache-2.0 in both generations, but the model parameters are licensed separately, and separately in each generation.

chunks.title: AlphaGenome
chunks.text: AlphaGenome (by Google), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: AlphaGenome is Google DeepMind's genomic sequence model for predicting gene expression, splicing, chromatin features, contact maps, and variant effects. It accepts sequences up to one million base pairs and produces most outputs at single-base-pair resolution through an API, a precomputed Atlas, and a gated downloadable checkpoint.

chunks.title: Amazon Bedrock Custom Models / Fine-Tuning
chunks.text: Amazon Bedrock Custom Models / Fine-Tuning (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Amazon Bedrock Custom Models is AWS's managed service for customizing Bedrock foundation models, covering supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement fine-tuning and distillation from a teacher model into a student model.

chunks.title: Amazon Bedrock Custom Models / Fine-Tuning
chunks.text: Amazon Bedrock Custom Models / Fine-Tuning (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Reinforcement fine-tuning grades responses through reward functions written as AWS Lambda functions rather than labeled examples, and reports training metrics in real time.

chunks.title: Amazon Bedrock Evaluations
chunks.text: Amazon Bedrock Evaluations (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Managed evaluation service inside Amazon Bedrock for scoring foundation models and RAG systems. It runs programmatic metrics including BERTScore and F1, a judge model over custom prompt datasets, and human evaluation using either the customer's own workforce or one AWS manages.

chunks.title: Amazon Bedrock Evaluations
chunks.text: Amazon Bedrock Evaluations (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Evaluation code: RAG evaluation covers retrieval and retrieve-and-generate, and the service can also score externally supplied inference responses.

chunks.title: Amazon Nova Pro
chunks.text: Amazon Nova Pro (by Amazon), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Amazon Nova is a family of multimodal foundation models that Amazon serves through Amazon Bedrock. The scored release, Nova Pro, is an understanding model with a 300K context window that takes text, images and video.

chunks.title: Amazon Nova Pro
chunks.text: Amazon Nova Pro (by Amazon), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: The second generation, Nova 2, adds Lite, Sonic speech-to-speech and multimodal embeddings models with up to 1 million tokens of context, and lists Pro and Omni tiers in preview.

chunks.title: Amazon Q Developer
chunks.text: Amazon Q Developer (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Amazon Q Developer is an AWS coding assistant with an agent mode that implements features, fixes bugs, writes tests and transforms code across a codebase. It is delivered as a managed service through IDE plugins, a command-line client and the AWS console, with a free tier and a paid Pro tier.

chunks.title: Amazon Rekognition
chunks.text: Amazon Rekognition (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: AWS's managed image and video analysis service, with pretrained APIs for labels, text, faces, face search and liveness, celebrities, content moderation and protective equipment.

chunks.title: Amazon Rekognition
chunks.text: Amazon Rekognition (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Custom Labels trains classifiers and detectors for a customer's own objects from as few as ten images with automated machine learning, inside the same service. It runs only as a hosted AWS API.

chunks.title: AmericasNLP shared-task data
chunks.text: AmericasNLP shared-task data (by AmericasNLP), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The AmericasNLP shared-task data pairs Spanish with ten Indigenous languages of the Americas, including Aymara, Bribri, Asháninka, Guarani, Wixarika, Nahuatl, Otomí, Quechua, Shipibo-Konibo and Rarámuri, for machine translation.

chunks.title: AmericasNLP shared-task data
chunks.text: AmericasNLP shared-task data (by AmericasNLP), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Training sets gather existing parallel corpora, while development and test sets were translated by hand for the task. The AmericasNLP workshop organizers publish it with each shared task.

chunks.title: Annoy
chunks.text: Annoy (by Spotify), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Annoy (Approximate Nearest Neighbors Oh Yeah) is a C++ library with Python bindings for approximate nearest neighbour search over random projection trees, built so that indexes are static files memory-mapped into a process. Many processes share one index without loading it each, which is what it was built for at Spotify.

chunks.title: Anthropic Internal Coding Evals
chunks.text: Anthropic Internal Coding Evals (by Anthropic (Internal)), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Anthropic Internal Coding Evals are coding evaluation sets Anthropic uses internally to benchmark Claude models during development. One of them is the take-home exam Anthropic sets for performance-engineering candidates, which it also runs new models against.

chunks.title: Antigravity
chunks.text: Antigravity (by Google), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Google's agent-first development platform, shipping a desktop application, a CLI, an IDE and an SDK. It runs agentic development workflows on macOS, Windows and Linux with model optionality across Google, Anthropic and OpenAI models, and integrates with Google Cloud, Firebase and Android. Its CLI supersedes the earlier Gemini CLI.

chunks.title: Anyscale Fine-Tuning
chunks.text: Anyscale Fine-Tuning (by Anyscale), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Anyscale Fine-Tuning is a managed, Ray-based platform for post-training open-weight language models. It runs LLaMA-Factory, SkyRL, and Ray Train across Ray clusters for continued pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization (DPO, KTO, PPO, ORPO), and RLVR or agentic tuning, then serves the checkpoints with multi-LoRA support.

chunks.title: AnythingLLM
chunks.text: AnythingLLM (by Mintplex Labs), catalog entry under UI & API: All-in-one desktop and Docker application for private chat over local documents, combining retrieval-augmented generation, no-code agents with web browsing, and support for 40+ LLM providers including local Ollama.

chunks.title: AnythingLLM
chunks.text: AnythingLLM (by Mintplex Labs), catalog entry under UI & API: The desktop build bundles an embedder and vector database so it runs without configuration; the Docker build adds multi-user permissioning and embeddable widgets.

chunks.title: Apache TVM
chunks.text: Apache TVM (by Apache Software Foundation), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Apache TVM is a machine learning compilation framework that lowers models from high-level descriptions into deployable modules for CPUs, GPUs and accelerators. Compiler pipelines are written and customized in Python, and the project targets LLVM, CUDA, ROCm, Metal, OpenCL, SPIR-V and WebGPU among others.

chunks.title: Apache TVM
chunks.text: Apache TVM (by Apache Software Foundation), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: It is developed under the Apache Software Foundation's committer model.

chunks.title: Apertus
chunks.text: Apertus (by Swiss AI Initiative), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Switzerland's national open LLM family from the Swiss AI Initiative at EPFL, ETH Zurich and CSCS. The current 1.5 models at 8B and 70B take image and audio input alongside text, run a deliberation mode and handle a 262,144-token context.

chunks.title: Apertus
chunks.text: Apertus (by Swiss AI Initiative), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: The line covers 1,811 languages, including Swiss German and Romansh, and about 40 percent of its pretraining data is non-English.

chunks.title: Apheris Networks
chunks.text: Apheris Networks (by Apheris), catalog entry under Federated learning: Apheris's federated networks and the Compute Gateway that runs them.

chunks.title: Apheris Networks
chunks.text: Apheris Networks (by Apheris), catalog entry under Federated learning: Each data custodian deploys the Gateway into its own environment from Apheris's Helm chart; the Gateway polls the Apheris orchestrator, checks every computation against the custodian's asset policies and privacy controls, and runs federated statistics or federated training, with NVIDIA FLARE as the main federation framework.

chunks.title: Apheris Networks
chunks.text: Apheris Networks (by Apheris), catalog entry under Federated learning: Apheris runs industry networks for drug discovery on it, such as the AI Structural Biology network of pharmaceutical companies.

chunks.title: Apify
chunks.text: Apify (by Apify), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Apify is a web scraping and automation platform with a marketplace of tens of thousands of pre-built scrapers, called Actors, that target specific websites. It provides cloud infrastructure for running them at scale, proxy management and anti-bot handling, plus an MCP server that exposes Actors to agent clients.

chunks.title: Apify
chunks.text: Apify (by Apify), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Crawlee, Apify's open-source crawling framework, is offered alongside the managed platform.

chunks.title: APPFL
chunks.text: APPFL (by Argonne National Laboratory), catalog entry under Federated learning: Privacy-preserving federated learning framework from Argonne National Laboratory. It simulates synchronous and asynchronous algorithms on HPC systems with MPI, and runs real federations over gRPC or Globus Compute with client authentication, with global and local differential privacy.

chunks.title: Apple Core ML Runtime
chunks.text: Apple Core ML Runtime (by Apple), catalog entry under Inference code: Apple Core ML is an on-device inference runtime that executes models across Apple's CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine, shipped as a system framework with iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS. It partitions model graphs across the available hardware and runs .mlpackage and .mlmodel files, which the separately distributed coremltools package produces.

chunks.title: Apple Core ML Runtime
chunks.text: Apple Core ML Runtime (by Apple), catalog entry under Inference code: Apple's own on-device features, including Apple Intelligence, are built on it.

chunks.title: APPS
chunks.text: APPS (by Hendrycks et al. (UC Berkeley)), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: APPS is a benchmark for Python code generation: 10,000 coding problems split evenly between train and test, at introductory, interview and competition difficulty, drawn from open-access coding challenge sites and shipped with 131,777 test cases and Python solutions.

chunks.title: APPS
chunks.text: APPS (by Hendrycks et al. (UC Berkeley)), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Published at NeurIPS 2021, it ranges from simple one-line solutions to substantial algorithmic challenges.

chunks.title: ArabicMMLU
chunks.text: ArabicMMLU (by Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: ArabicMMLU tests language models on 14,575 multiple-choice questions in Modern Standard Arabic across 40 tasks, drawn from school exams in countries of North Africa, the Levant, and the Gulf.

chunks.title: ArabicMMLU
chunks.text: ArabicMMLU (by Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Ten native speakers from several countries built it, grouping questions into STEM, social science, humanities, Arabic language, and other subjects. MBZUAI leads the work with university and industry partners.

chunks.title: ArabicWeb24
chunks.text: ArabicWeb24 (by LightOn), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: ArabicWeb24 is a pretraining corpus of Arabic web text from a custom crawl, processed with the datatrove library; the card gives more than 28 billion tokens for the fully cleaned and deduplicated version.

chunks.title: ArabicWeb24
chunks.text: ArabicWeb24 (by LightOn), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: A second version skips the sentence deduplication step, and the processing code and small ablation models trained on both versions are released alongside. LightOn built it with INSAT.

chunks.title: Arctic Embed
chunks.text: Arctic Embed (by Snowflake), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Arctic Embed is a family of retrieval embedding models sized from xs to l. The 2.0 releases build on the BGE-M3 RetroMAE backbone to handle multilingual retrieval at up to 8,192 tokens without giving up English quality.

chunks.title: Arctic Embed
chunks.text: Arctic Embed (by Snowflake), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Matryoshka representation learning and quantization-aware training let a vector be truncated to 256 dimensions or compressed to 128 bytes per document. Snowflake develops and publishes the family.

chunks.title: Arduino UNO Q
chunks.text: Arduino UNO Q (by Arduino), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Hybrid single-board computer in the Arduino UNO form factor, pairing a Qualcomm Dragonwing QRB2210 quad-core applications processor with an Adreno GPU and dual ISP running Debian Linux, alongside an STM32U585 microcontroller for real-time control.

chunks.title: Arduino UNO Q
chunks.text: Arduino UNO Q (by Arduino), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: It targets AI-accelerated vision and sound applications, is programmed through the Arduino App Lab, and ships in 2GB/16GB and 4GB/32GB variants. Arduino, now a Qualcomm company, makes it.

chunks.title: AReaL
chunks.text: AReaL (by AReaL Project), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: AReaL is a reinforcement learning system for training reasoning and agentic language models. It uses a fully asynchronous training paradigm that decouples rollout generation from policy updates, and supports FSDP and Megatron training backends with vLLM and SGLang inference backends. It was developed by the AReaL Team at Tsinghua IIIS and Ant Group.

chunks.title: Arize
chunks.text: Arize (by Arize AI), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Observability and evaluation platform for AI agents and LLM applications, covering tracing, evaluations, experiments and production issue detection. It includes an embedded AI engineering agent called Alyx and a GenAI trace datastore called adb. It is built by the same team as Phoenix and is offered as SaaS or, on the Enterprise tier, self-hosted.

chunks.title: Arm Compute Library
chunks.text: Arm Compute Library (by Arm), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Arm Compute Library is a collection of low-level machine learning functions optimized for Arm Cortex-A and Neoverse CPUs and Mali GPUs, using NEON and OpenCL. Arm develops and releases it with prebuilt binaries alongside the source.

chunks.title: Armada
chunks.text: Armada (by Armada), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Multi-cluster batch queuing system for high-throughput workloads on Kubernetes, built at G-Research for quantitative research and machine-learning jobs. Armada holds a queue in front of many Kubernetes clusters, applies per-queue fair share across them, and decides which cluster each job is sent to, so a fleet of clusters behaves as one pool.

chunks.title: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
chunks.text: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (by Artificial Analysis), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Independent benchmarking service that runs a fixed suite of academic and agentic evaluations against every major model and publishes a composite Intelligence Index with confidence intervals.

chunks.title: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
chunks.text: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (by Artificial Analysis), catalog entry under Evaluation code: The composite weights four categories - agents, coding, scientific reasoning and general - unequally, and the methodology is published in full.

chunks.title: arXiv API
chunks.text: arXiv API (by arXiv), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: arXiv's public query API at export.arxiv.org/api/query, which searches the arXiv preprint server by title, author, abstract, comment, journal reference, category or report number, or looks papers up by identifier. Results come back as an Atom feed giving each paper's title, authors, abstract and categories, with links to its abstract page and PDF.

chunks.title: arXiv API
chunks.text: arXiv API (by arXiv), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: It needs no key, and arXiv's terms ask for no more than one request every three seconds.

chunks.title: ATLAS
chunks.text: ATLAS (by AI Singapore), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: ATLAS is AI Singapore's catalog of datasets for underrepresented languages, centered on Southeast Asia. It describes each dataset by language, modality, license and task, imports dataset cards from Hugging Face, and publishes contributions after a human review.

chunks.title: ATLAS
chunks.text: ATLAS (by AI Singapore), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: A chat search and a read-only MCP API let people and agents query the catalog, and coverage maps show which languages still lack data.

chunks.title: Atlaset
chunks.text: Atlaset (by AtlasIA), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Atlaset is a Moroccan Darija text corpus for pretraining and training language models, about 155 million tokens in its training split. It combines dozens of existing sources, including social media comments, news summaries, Wikipedia, YouTube subtitles, and translated instruction sets such as ShareGPT and FLAN, each listed with its row count.

chunks.title: Atlaset
chunks.text: Atlaset (by AtlasIA), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Abdelaziz Bounhar curated it, and AtlasIA publishes it.

chunks.title: Atropos
chunks.text: Atropos (by Nous Research), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Atropos is an environment microservice framework for asynchronous reinforcement learning with language models: environments run as services, and a trajectory API collects their rollouts and serves batches to a trainer.

chunks.title: Atropos
chunks.text: Atropos (by Nous Research), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: It ships environments for dataset evaluation, games, RLHF and RLAIF judging, code execution, and multimodal tasks, and integrates with the Axolotl and Tinker trainers. Nous Research archived the repository read-only on 2026-07-04, leaving 0.4.0 as the last release.

chunks.title: Attention Gym
chunks.text: Attention Gym (by RiseAI-Sys), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Attention-Gym is a Triton-based collection of sparse and quantized attention kernel implementations - Flash Attention 2, sliding-tile attention and several SageAttention variants - built for researchers to rapidly implement, test and validate new attention mechanisms.

chunks.title: AudioCraft
chunks.text: AudioCraft (by Meta), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: AudioCraft is Meta's PyTorch library for audio generation research, carrying both inference and training code. It hosts MusicGen and MAGNeT for text-to-music, AudioGen for text-to-sound, JASCO for chord- and melody-conditioned music, the EnCodec neural codec, Multi Band Diffusion decoding and the AudioSeal watermark.

chunks.title: AudioCraft
chunks.text: AudioCraft (by Meta), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: The model weights it loads are published separately under their own terms.

chunks.title: Aurora
chunks.text: Aurora (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Aurora is Microsoft's Earth-system foundation model for atmospheric and environmental forecasting. The published family includes specialized checkpoints for medium- and high-resolution weather, air pollution, ocean waves, and tropical-cyclone tracks, built from a common pretrained architecture and multiple public reanalysis and forecast datasets.

chunks.title: AutoRound
chunks.text: AutoRound (by Intel), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: AutoRound is Intel's post-training quantization toolkit for large language and vision-language models, using sign-gradient descent (SignRound) to reach 2-4 bit weights at high accuracy with minimal tuning, across broad CPU, GPU and NPU hardware compatibility.

chunks.title: AutoGen
chunks.text: AutoGen (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Microsoft's framework for agentic AI built around multi-agent conversation, where model-backed agents collaborate, critique each other and run tools and code. Its event-driven redesign and code-execution focus distinguish it from graph- or role-based frameworks.

chunks.title: AutoGen
chunks.text: AutoGen (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Microsoft now directs new work to the Microsoft Agent Framework, which merges AutoGen with Semantic Kernel.

chunks.title: AutoGluon
chunks.text: AutoGluon (by AutoGluon), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Automated machine-learning library that trains, tunes and stack-ensembles models for tabular prediction, time-series forecasting and multimodal image, text and tabular tasks from a few lines of code.

chunks.title: AutoGluon
chunks.text: AutoGluon (by AutoGluon), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Its tabular predictor fits gradient-boosted trees, neural networks and tabular foundation models such as Mitra, TabICL and TabPFN side by side, and its forecaster includes Chronos. Developed at Amazon, which also offers it as a managed service.

chunks.title: AutoGPT
chunks.text: AutoGPT (by Significant Gravitas), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Autonomous agent platform where a user defines a goal and the agent breaks it into sub-tasks, executes them and adapts from the results. It began as a command-line experiment and is now centered on a low-code visual builder with a marketplace, where agents run on demand, on a schedule or from a trigger.

chunks.title: AutoGPT
chunks.text: AutoGPT (by Significant Gravitas), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Hosted and self-hosted deployment are both offered.

chunks.title: AWS Lambda
chunks.text: AWS Lambda (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Deployment: AWS Lambda runs event-triggered functions on AWS-managed compute, with no server for the caller to provision. It supports Java, Go, PowerShell, Node.js, C#, Python and Ruby natively and any other language through a Runtime API, taking code as a .zip archive or a container image.

chunks.title: AWS Lambda
chunks.text: AWS Lambda (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Deployment: Each function runs isolated on a Firecracker microVM, and Lambda MicroVMs extends the same substrate to user- and AI-generated code with near-instant resume and state persistence.

chunks.title: AWS MCP Servers
chunks.text: AWS MCP Servers (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: AWS's own suite of MCP servers - 58 of them across infrastructure, data, machine learning, developer tooling, messaging and cost - each exposing one AWS service to an agent over stdio, using the caller's existing AWS credentials.

chunks.title: AWS Neuron
chunks.text: AWS Neuron (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Inference code: AWS Neuron is the SDK and runtime for running machine learning on AWS's custom Inferentia and Trainium accelerators (Inf1/Inf2 and Trn1/Trn2/Trn3 instances). Its compiler converts models from PyTorch and JAX into executables for the custom silicon, with serving through a vLLM plugin and a kernel-authoring interface (NKI).

chunks.title: AWS Neuron
chunks.text: AWS Neuron (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Inference code: AWS distributes it as a separate SDK, publishing samples and some tooling on GitHub.

chunks.title: Axelera Metis AIPU
chunks.text: Axelera Metis AIPU (by Axelera AI), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Edge AI inference accelerator from Axelera AI in the Netherlands, built on a quad-core digital in-memory-compute architecture. Each Metis chip delivers up to 214 TOPS at about 15 TOPS per watt and is sold as M.2 modules, PCIe cards and single-board computers. The Voyager SDK supports more than 100 models.

chunks.title: Axolotl
chunks.text: Axolotl (by Axolotl AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Axolotl is a YAML-config-driven fine-tuning framework built on Hugging Face's TRL and PEFT, plus bitsandbytes for quantization, that runs full fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, and GRPO from a single configuration file rather than a custom training script.

chunks.title: Axolotl
chunks.text: Axolotl (by Axolotl AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: It scales from a single GPU to multi-node clusters through FSDP, DeepSpeed, Torchrun, and Ray, and supports models from across the Hugging Face Hub. Axolotl AI builds and maintains it.

chunks.title: Axon
chunks.text: Axon (by Axon), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Local observability tool for LangChain and OpenTelemetry-instrumented AI agents. A single CLI-launched server ingests OTLP trace data and serves a real-time React dashboard with transcript, waterfall, tree and raw span views, writing everything to a local SQLite database. No cloud account is required and no trace data leaves the machine it runs on.

chunks.title: Aya Collection
chunks.text: Aya Collection (by Cohere), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Multilingual instruction-tuning dataset spanning more than 114 languages, built from templated and translated subsets for tasks including classification, summarization and translation. It holds hundreds of millions of examples across 64 subsets, and was created by Cohere Labs as part of the Aya open-science initiative.

chunks.title: Microsoft Foundry Models
chunks.text: Microsoft Foundry Models (by Microsoft Azure), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: The model catalog in Microsoft Foundry, listing models from Microsoft, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Meta, Mistral, Cohere, NVIDIA and a Hugging Face collection. Entries are either sold and hosted by Azure or provided by partners and community publishers, and are deployed as serverless APIs or on managed compute.

chunks.title: Microsoft Foundry Models
chunks.text: Microsoft Foundry Models (by Microsoft Azure), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: The catalog carries version and lifecycle information per model, and users can request additions.

chunks.title: Azure AI Foundry Observability
chunks.text: Azure AI Foundry Observability (by Microsoft Azure), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Microsoft's GenAI observability surface inside Microsoft Foundry, providing evaluation, monitoring and tracing for LLM applications and agents.

chunks.title: Azure AI Foundry Observability
chunks.text: Azure AI Foundry Observability (by Microsoft Azure), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: It is built on OpenTelemetry and feeds Azure Monitor Application Insights, with built-in evaluators for quality, RAG groundedness and relevance, safety, and agent-specific measures such as tool-call accuracy and task completion.

chunks.title: Azure AI Foundry Observability
chunks.text: Azure AI Foundry Observability (by Microsoft Azure), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Tracing covers LangChain, LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK and the Microsoft Agent Framework.

chunks.title: Azure AI Content Safety
chunks.text: Azure AI Content Safety (by Microsoft Azure), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Microsoft's content-safety service on Azure offers hosted APIs that moderate text and images across hate, sexual, violence and self-harm categories.

chunks.title: Azure AI Content Safety
chunks.text: Azure AI Content Safety (by Microsoft Azure), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: It also provides Prompt Shields against direct and indirect prompt injection, groundedness detection, protected-material detection for copyrighted text and code, a task-adherence check for AI agents, and custom categories trained from examples. Preview containers run a subset of these checks outside Azure.

chunks.title: Azure AI Document Intelligence
chunks.text: Azure AI Document Intelligence (by Microsoft Azure), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Managed document-processing service on Azure, formerly Form Recognizer, that converts documents into markdown or structured JSON with layout, tables, selection marks and key-value pairs, and supports custom models trained on a customer's own forms.

chunks.title: Grounding with Bing Search (Microsoft Foundry)
chunks.text: Grounding with Bing Search (Microsoft Foundry) (by Microsoft Azure), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Agent tool in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service that grounds a model's answer in live Bing results. The developer never sees the search results: the agent formulates queries, Bing returns results to the model, and the model's answer comes back with URL citations.

chunks.title: Azure Machine Learning Pipelines
chunks.text: Azure Machine Learning Pipelines (by Microsoft Azure), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Managed pipeline service in Azure Machine Learning. A pipeline breaks a machine-learning task into components that Azure runs in sequence on compute targets the workspace defines, managing the dependencies between steps and reusing cached outputs where inputs have not changed.

chunks.title: Azure OpenAI Fine-Tuning
chunks.text: Azure OpenAI Fine-Tuning (by Microsoft Azure), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Azure OpenAI Fine-Tuning is Microsoft's managed fine-tuning service inside Microsoft Foundry, covering OpenAI models and open-weight models such as Llama, Qwen, Ministral and gpt-oss.

chunks.title: Azure OpenAI Fine-Tuning
chunks.text: Azure OpenAI Fine-Tuning (by Microsoft Azure), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: It supports supervised fine-tuning, direct preference optimization, and reinforcement fine-tuning, with per-epoch checkpoints and optional automatic deployment. Jobs run under Foundry role-based access controls.

chunks.title: BAGEL
chunks.text: BAGEL (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under Multimodal models: BAGEL is ByteDance Seed's unified multimodal model, a decoder-only mixture-of-transformers with 7B active and 14B total parameters that both understands images and generates and edits them. It was pretrained on interleaved text, image, video and web data and extends to free-form visual manipulation and multiview synthesis.

chunks.title: BAGEL
chunks.text: BAGEL (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under Multimodal models: ByteDance publishes the training code.

chunks.title: BeagleY-AI
chunks.text: BeagleY-AI (by BeagleBoard.org Foundation), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Open single-board computer from the BeagleBoard.org Foundation built around the Texas Instruments AM67A vision processor.

chunks.title: BeagleY-AI
chunks.text: BeagleY-AI (by BeagleBoard.org Foundation), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: It pairs a quad-core Cortex-A53 at 1.4 GHz with a dual C7x DSP and matrix multiply accelerator rated up to 4 TOPS, an IMG BXS GPU and Cortex-R5 real-time cores, with 4GB LPDDR4 and a 40-pin Raspberry Pi-compatible header. It targets vision, robotics and smart cameras.

chunks.title: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
chunks.text: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails is a managed AWS service of configurable policies covering denied topics, content and word filters, PII redaction, prompt-attack detection, contextual-grounding checks and Automated Reasoning checks, applied to any Bedrock model.

chunks.title: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
chunks.text: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Through the ApplyGuardrail API the same policies can screen models hosted outside Bedrock, though the guardrail itself runs at AWS.

chunks.title: BeeAI Framework
chunks.text: BeeAI Framework (by IBM), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Toolkit for production multi-agent systems with feature parity across Python and TypeScript, which sets it apart from the Python-first frameworks around it. It covers caching, memory and OpenTelemetry observability, constraint-based agent governance, native MCP and A2A interoperability, and more than ten model backends.

chunks.title: Belebele
chunks.text: Belebele (by Meta), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Belebele is a multiple-choice reading comprehension benchmark in 122 language variants, with 900 questions per variant written about short FLORES-200 passages. Every question has four answers, one correct, and the set is fully parallel so scores compare directly across languages.

chunks.title: Belebele
chunks.text: Belebele (by Meta), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Annotators wrote the questions in English under quality checks before translation. Meta FAIR released it.

chunks.title: Berkeley Humanoid Lite
chunks.text: Berkeley Humanoid Lite (by UC Berkeley), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Berkeley Humanoid Lite is an open-source bipedal humanoid robot from UC Berkeley's Hybrid Robotics lab, built for under $5k in parts from 3D-printed cycloidal gearboxes and widely available parts.

chunks.title: Berkeley Humanoid Lite
chunks.text: Berkeley Humanoid Lite (by UC Berkeley), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: The project publishes the CAD and robot descriptions, the low-level C controller over CAN, and Isaac Lab environments for training locomotion policies that transfer from simulation to the hardware.

chunks.title: Beta9
chunks.text: Beta9 (by Beam Cloud), catalog entry under Deployment: Beta9 is a serverless runtime for AI workloads driven from a Python interface, covering isolated sandboxes for model-generated code, autoscaling inference endpoints and background task queues. A custom container runtime, scheduler and embedded cache launch containers in under a second, alongside scale-to-zero, mounted distributed volumes and GPU support.

chunks.title: Beta9
chunks.text: Beta9 (by Beam Cloud), catalog entry under Deployment: Beam Cloud develops it as the engine behind its managed platform, and it can be self-hosted instead.

chunks.title: BGE
chunks.text: BGE (by Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI)), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: BGE (BAAI General Embedding) covers text embedding and reranking for retrieval pipelines.

chunks.title: BGE
chunks.text: BGE (by Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI)), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The bge-m3 checkpoint works across more than 100 languages and inputs up to 8,192 tokens, emitting dense, sparse and multi-vector representations from a single pass; the English v1.5 encoders span small to large, and the bge-reranker line supplies cross-encoder relevance scores.

chunks.title: BGE
chunks.text: BGE (by Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI)), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence maintains the family and the FlagEmbedding toolkit around it.

chunks.title: BGE Reranker
chunks.text: BGE Reranker (by Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI)), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: BAAI's cross-encoder reranking line within the BGE/FlagEmbedding project, separate from the BGE bi-encoder embedders.

chunks.title: BGE Reranker
chunks.text: BGE Reranker (by Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI)), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: bge-reranker-v2-m3 is the workhorse - a multilingual 0.6B model built on bge-m3 - and the line also ships the earlier XLM-R base and large rerankers plus LLM-based v2-gemma and layerwise v2-minicpm variants that trade latency for accuracy. It is the second most downloaded reranker family on the Hub.

chunks.title: BibleTTS
chunks.text: BibleTTS (by Masakhane), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: BibleTTS is a text-to-speech corpus of studio-quality, single-speaker Bible readings at 48kHz, with up to 86 hours of aligned speech per language. OpenSLR hosts aligned audio and text for six languages, Akuapem Twi, Asante Twi, Ewe, Hausa, Lingala and Yoruba, and the paper covers four more without alignment.

chunks.title: BibleTTS
chunks.text: BibleTTS (by Masakhane), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Researchers from Masakhane and Coqui built it from Biblica's open.bible recordings.

chunks.title: Bielik
chunks.text: Bielik (by SpeakLeash Foundation), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Bielik is an open language model for Polish from the SpeakLeash Foundation, developed with the support of the ACK Cyfronet AGH computing center.

chunks.title: Bielik
chunks.text: Bielik (by SpeakLeash Foundation), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Bielik 11B v3 extends Mistral 7B v0.2 to 11 billion parameters by duplicating layers, continues pretraining on Polish, English and other European languages, and is then instruction-tuned, preference-trained and refined with reinforcement learning.

chunks.title: bigcode-dataset
chunks.text: bigcode-dataset (by BigCode Project), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Preprocessing, quality filtering, decontamination, and PII detection/anonymization for large code corpora. The filtering and PII pipeline behind The Stack and StarCoder training data.

chunks.title: BigCodeBench
chunks.text: BigCodeBench (by BigCode Project), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Evaluation harness for code-generation models over 1,140 practical programming tasks that require using multiple libraries and tools, scored with branch-coverage tests. It tests real library use rather than self-contained algorithmic puzzles, ships Complete and Instruct splits, and runs end to end locally or against a hosted evaluator.

chunks.title: BiRefNet
chunks.text: BiRefNet (by ZhengPeng7), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: High-resolution dichotomous image segmentation model that separates a foreground object from its background, widely used for background removal and matting. Its Bilateral Reference design refines a coarse mask with high-resolution image patches and gradient cues.

chunks.title: BiRefNet
chunks.text: BiRefNet (by ZhengPeng7), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Checkpoints cover general use, a lighter model, 2K inputs, matting, portraits, camouflaged and salient objects, with training code in the repository.

chunks.title: bitsandbytes
chunks.text: bitsandbytes (by bitsandbytes Foundation), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: bitsandbytes provides k-bit quantization for PyTorch, reducing the memory a model needs for inference and training. Three pieces carry that: 8-bit optimizers using block-wise quantization, the LLM.int8() mixed-precision inference path that isolates outlier features, and the 4-bit quantization QLoRA fine-tuning is built on.

chunks.title: Blaxel Sandbox
chunks.text: Blaxel Sandbox (by Blaxel), catalog entry under Deployment: Blaxel gives AI agents microVM sandboxes that suspend after a few seconds of inactivity and resume in about 25 milliseconds with filesystem and memory state intact. Around the sandbox sit batch jobs, durable volumes, outbound allow-lists and static IPs.

chunks.title: Blaxel Sandbox
chunks.text: Blaxel Sandbox (by Blaxel), catalog entry under Deployment: The in-sandbox HTTP API and a hub of image templates are published; the scheduler that allocates and resumes machines is the commercial layer, offered as managed cloud, self-hosted or VPC.

chunks.title: BLIP
chunks.text: BLIP (by Salesforce), catalog entry under Multimodal models: BLIP is Salesforce's family of vision-language models for captioning, visual question answering and image-text matching. BLIP-2 connects a frozen image encoder to a frozen language model through a lightweight querying transformer, and InstructBLIP adds instruction tuning.

chunks.title: BLIP
chunks.text: BLIP (by Salesforce), catalog entry under Multimodal models: xGen-MM, also called BLIP-3, continues the line with Phi-3-based models that read interleaved images and text; BLIP-3-Video is a separate video model that Salesforce built on it.

chunks.title: Block Sparse Attention
chunks.text: Block Sparse Attention (by MIT HAN Lab), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Block Sparse Attention is a library of sparse attention kernels from MIT HAN Lab supporting streaming attention at token and block granularity plus block-sparse attention, modified from FlashAttention to reduce the compute and memory cost of long-context LLM inference.

chunks.title: Bloom Library datasets
chunks.text: Bloom Library datasets (by SIL Global), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Bloom Library datasets turn the community-written storybooks on SIL's Bloom Library into four multilingual resources: text for language modeling, image captioning, visual storytelling, and aligned speech. They cover more than 350 languages across over 30 families, many with only a few stories each.

chunks.title: Bloom Library datasets
chunks.text: Bloom Library datasets (by SIL Global), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: SIL Global builds Bloom, the book-authoring software behind the library.

chunks.title: Boltz
chunks.text: Boltz (by Jeremy Wohlwend), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Boltz is a family of biomolecular interaction models. Boltz-1 was the first fully open-source model to approach AlphaFold 3 accuracy, and Boltz-2 jointly models complex structure and binding affinity, reporting a log10(IC50) value alongside a binder-versus-decoy probability.

chunks.title: Boltz
chunks.text: Boltz (by Jeremy Wohlwend), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: It runs from a YAML specification of the complex, optionally pulling MSAs from a ColabFold server.

chunks.title: Bharat Parallel Corpus Collection
chunks.text: Bharat Parallel Corpus Collection (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Bharat Parallel Corpus Collection (BPCC) is an English-Indic parallel text corpus of about 230 million sentence pairs covering all 22 scheduled Indian languages.

chunks.title: Bharat Parallel Corpus Collection
chunks.text: Bharat Parallel Corpus Collection (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Most pairs are mined from the web or drawn from corpora such as Samanantar and NLLB, while BPCC-Human holds about 2.2 million human-translated pairs, including new Wikipedia and everyday-use sets. AI4Bharat released it to train IndicTrans2, together with back-translated data.

chunks.title: Braintrust
chunks.text: Braintrust (by Braintrust), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Enterprise AI product development platform with logging, tracing, evaluation and a prompt playground, built around the loop from evaluation to production. It discovers patterns across production traffic, scores outputs continuously and gates releases on quality.

chunks.title: Braintrust
chunks.text: Braintrust (by Braintrust), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: It runs on Brainstore, a database purpose-built for agent observability, and is SOC 2 Type II certified.

chunks.title: Brave Search API
chunks.text: Brave Search API (by Brave Software), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Search API over Brave's own web index, sold as one plan covering three endpoints: Web Search for human-readable results, LLM Context for pre-extracted page chunks aimed at models, and the specialized news, video, image, place, autosuggest and spellcheck endpoints.

chunks.title: Browser Use
chunks.text: Browser Use (by Browser Use), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Agent framework that makes websites usable by AI agents, covering autonomous browsing, form filling, data extraction and multi-step online tasks.

chunks.title: Browser Use
chunks.text: Browser Use (by Browser Use), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Built on Playwright, it gives a model a structured way to observe page state, plan actions and execute browser interactions, and ships both a CLI for one-off tasks and a Python library for repeatable automation with custom tools and structured output.

chunks.title: Browserbase
chunks.text: Browserbase (by Browserbase), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Cloud-hosted headless browsers built for AI agents, handling authentication persistence, CAPTCHA solving and anti-bot detection that self-hosted Playwright does not manage easily.

chunks.title: Browserbase
chunks.text: Browserbase (by Browserbase), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: It exposes a Browser API, a Search API, a Fetch API, Functions for deploying and scheduling agents, and a Model Gateway, and it maintains Stagehand, a browser agent SDK, alongside.

chunks.title: bubblewrap
chunks.text: bubblewrap (by Containers), catalog entry under Deployment: bubblewrap (bwrap) is a small Linux tool that lets unprivileged users build sandboxes from kernel user namespaces. Each sandbox starts from an empty mount namespace on a tmpfs hidden from the host, with optional PID, IPC, network and UTS namespaces and seccomp filters.

chunks.title: bubblewrap
chunks.text: bubblewrap (by Containers), catalog entry under Deployment: Rather than shipping a security policy of its own, it leaves the policy to whatever calls it, which is how Flatpak and Anthropic's Sandbox Runtime use it. The project lives in the containers GitHub organization.

chunks.title: C2PA SDK (Content Authenticity Initiative)
chunks.text: C2PA SDK (Content Authenticity Initiative) (by Content Authenticity Initiative), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: The Content Authenticity Initiative's open-source SDK for C2PA Content Credentials: it writes, signs and validates the cryptographically signed manifests that record where a piece of media came from and how it was edited.

chunks.title: C2PA SDK (Content Authenticity Initiative)
chunks.text: C2PA SDK (Content Authenticity Initiative) (by Content Authenticity Initiative), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: The core is a Rust library, with Python bindings and a command-line tool built on it.

chunks.title: C4
chunks.text: C4 (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Cleaned version of Common Crawl created for the T5 paper and hosted by AI2. It ships several variants, including a cleaned English split of about 305GB and the multilingual mC4 covering 108 languages at roughly 9.7TB.

chunks.title: Cambrian
chunks.text: Cambrian (by NYU VisionX), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Cambrian is a family of open multimodal models from New York University's VisionX lab, built around a vision-centric study of how image encoders shape multimodal models.

chunks.title: Cambrian
chunks.text: Cambrian (by NYU VisionX), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Cambrian-S extends the line to video and spatial reasoning on Qwen2.5 language models, and Cambrian-P adds per-frame camera tokens so that one model answers spatial questions about a video and estimates the camera's pose.

chunks.title: Canary
chunks.text: Canary (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Speech & audio: NVIDIA's multitask speech recognition and translation models. Canary 1B v2 transcribes 25 European languages and translates between English and 24 of them; Canary-Qwen-2.5B pairs the Canary encoder with a Qwen language model for English transcription.

chunks.title: CARLA
chunks.text: CARLA (by CARLA Simulator), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: CARLA is an open-source simulator for autonomous driving research, built on Unreal Engine, for developing, training and validating driving systems. It supplies open urban maps, buildings and vehicles, configurable sensor suites and environmental conditions, and a Python API for controlling every actor.

chunks.title: CARLA
chunks.text: CARLA (by CARLA Simulator), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: It is developed at the Computer Vision Center of the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona.

chunks.title: CATalog
chunks.text: CATalog (by Projecte Aina), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: CATalog is a Catalan pretraining corpus of about 17.45 billion words drawn from 26 sources, including filtered Common Crawl snapshots, news media, forums, digital libraries and public institutions. Every document carries a heuristic quality score from the CURATE pipeline, so users can filter at their own threshold instead of a fixed cut.

chunks.title: CATalog
chunks.text: CATalog (by Projecte Aina), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Language Technologies Unit at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center builds it for Projecte AINA.

chunks.title: CatBoost
chunks.text: CatBoost (by Yandex), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Gradient-boosted decision tree library from Yandex, known for handling categorical features natively and for ordered boosting, which reduces overfitting on small data. It trains on CPU or GPU for classification, regression and ranking, takes text and embedding features, and exports models to ONNX, CoreML, PMML and several runtime languages.

chunks.title: CCNet
chunks.text: CCNet (by Meta), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: The CCNet pipeline: downloads and cleans Common Crawl into high-quality monolingual corpora via language identification, KenLM perplexity filtering, and deduplication. Built CC-100.

chunks.title: Cendol Collection
chunks.text: Cendol Collection (by IndoNLP), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Cendol Collection is the instruction-tuning data IndoNLP used to train the Cendol family of language models for Indonesian and the country's local languages. Version 1 holds task-specific prompts built from NLP datasets for sentiment analysis, translation, summarization and question answering.

chunks.title: Cendol Collection
chunks.text: Cendol Collection (by IndoNLP), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Version 2 adds general-knowledge and human-centric prompts used for the Cendol-Chat models. Both are described in the Cendol paper.

chunks.title: Cerebras Inference
chunks.text: Cerebras Inference (by Cerebras Systems), catalog entry under Inference code: Cerebras Inference runs on the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine (WSE-3), a single silicon wafer with 4 trillion transistors and 44GB of on-chip SRAM. It is delivered as a hosted, API-only cloud service that serves a catalog of models through an OpenAI-compatible API. Cerebras Systems builds and operates the underlying hardware and service.

chunks.title: Chai
chunks.text: Chai (by Chai Discovery), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Chai-1 is Chai Discovery's multi-modal model for molecular structure prediction, giving unified predictions over proteins, small molecules, DNA, RNA, glycosylations and modified residues.

chunks.title: Chai
chunks.text: Chai (by Chai Discovery), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: It runs from a FASTA file with optional MSAs and templates, and uniquely accepts user-specified experimental restraints, inter-chain contacts and covalent bonds at several resolutions, to guide the folding of a complex.

chunks.title: Chandra
chunks.text: Chandra (by Datalab), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Document OCR and layout model from Datalab that converts PDFs and images into Markdown, HTML and JSON while preserving structure - reading order, tables, forms, handwriting and mathematical notation. It is the successor model to the same team's Marker pipeline and is served both as open weights and as a hosted API.

chunks.title: Character.AI
chunks.text: Character.AI (by Character.AI), catalog entry under UI & API: Consumer chat product built around user-created AI characters. Users design characters with their own personas and hold text or voice conversations with them, and the app carries a large library of characters other users have published. It is aimed at storytelling, roleplay and conversational entertainment. Character Technologies, Inc. publishes it.

chunks.title: Chatbot Arena
chunks.text: Chatbot Arena (by LMArena), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Hosted arena that ranks language models on blind pairwise human preference, turning crowd votes into an Elo-style leaderboard. Where a harness scores a model against fixed tasks, this scores it against another model as judged by whoever is at the keyboard. Formerly LMSYS Chatbot Arena and then LMArena, it now runs as Arena at arena.ai.

chunks.title: ChatGPT
chunks.text: ChatGPT (by OpenAI), catalog entry under UI & API: OpenAI's consumer ChatGPT product, distributed as an app over a chat interface. It generates original images from a description and transforms existing ones, and offers an advanced voice mode. Custom GPTs let a user tailor ChatGPT to a specific use case with instructions, attached knowledge documents and connections to third-party services.

chunks.title: Chatterbox
chunks.text: Chatterbox (by Resemble AI), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Resemble AI's open text-to-speech family: zero-shot voice cloning with an emotion-exaggeration control, the original English model, Turbo and Nano variants, and Chatterbox Multilingual V3 across 23 languages. Every output carries Resemble's Perth watermark.

chunks.title: Chitu
chunks.text: Chitu (by Tsinghua PACMAN Lab), catalog entry under Inference code: Chitu is a production-grade inference engine from Tsinghua's PACMAN group focused on running large models across many kinds of hardware, from pure CPU through single GPU to multi-node clusters with prefill-decode separation.

chunks.title: Chitu
chunks.text: Chitu (by Tsinghua PACMAN Lab), catalog entry under Inference code: It serves DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM and Kimi models on NVIDIA GPUs and on Chinese accelerators including Ascend 910B, Muxi, Hygon and Moore Threads, with FP8 and FP4 weights converted online to run on hardware without native support. A single chitu.run executable launches multi-node and multi-instance deployments.

chunks.title: ChrEn
chunks.text: ChrEn (by Shiyue Zhang), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: ChrEn is a Cherokee-English parallel corpus of about 14,000 sentence pairs for machine translation of an endangered language, with in-domain and out-of-domain splits and about 5,000 Cherokee monolingual sentences for semi-supervised training. Pairs come from published books and articles, and a Cherokee Old Testament set was added later.

chunks.title: ChrEn
chunks.text: ChrEn (by Shiyue Zhang), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Shiyue Zhang, Benjamin Frey and Mohit Bansal at UNC released it.

chunks.title: Chroma
chunks.text: Chroma (by Chroma), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Chroma is a retrieval database for AI applications, storing embeddings with their documents and metadata behind a four-function API. It runs embedded in a Python or JavaScript process, as a self-hosted server, or on the vendor's hosted service, and the core is implemented in Rust. Hybrid and full-text search sit beside vector search.

chunks.title: CIDAR
chunks.text: CIDAR (by ARBML), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: CIDAR (Culturally Relevant Instruction Dataset for Arabic) holds 10,000 Arabic instruction and response pairs for tuning language models.

chunks.title: CIDAR
chunks.text: CIDAR (by ARBML), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: About 9,109 come from the Alpagasus set translated into Arabic with ChatGPT and about 891 are native Arabic grammar questions from Al Jazeera's Ask the Teacher site; about 12 reviewers corrected every pair for cultural fit. ARBML publishes it with two 100-item evaluation sets.

chunks.title: Civitai
chunks.text: Civitai (by Civitai), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Community hub at civitai.com where users upload and download image-generation model files: checkpoints, LoRAs, textual inversions, VAEs, ControlNets and upscalers, each published as a model with one or more versions. A public REST API lists and searches models and resolves versions by file hash without a token.

chunks.title: Civitai
chunks.text: Civitai (by Civitai), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Civit AI publishes the site's Next.js code under Apache-2.0.

chunks.title: CLARIN Virtual Language Observatory
chunks.text: CLARIN Virtual Language Observatory (by CLARIN ERIC), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: The CLARIN Virtual Language Observatory (VLO) is a faceted search portal over descriptions of language resources held by the centers of the CLARIN research infrastructure.

chunks.title: CLARIN Virtual Language Observatory
chunks.text: CLARIN Virtual Language Observatory (by CLARIN ERIC), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: It harvests the centers' metadata records over OAI-PMH, converts them to the CMDI metadata standard and indexes them in Solr, so that people can filter resources by language, type and availability before going to the center that holds them.

chunks.title: Claude Agent SDK
chunks.text: Claude Agent SDK (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Python library that puts Claude Code's agent loop inside an application.
