It starts the Claude Code command-line binary as a subprocess and exposes its built-in file, shell and search tools, permission controls, sessions, hooks and subagents through Python calls, with custom tools written as Python functions served as in-process MCP servers.

chunks.title: Claude Agent SDK
chunks.text: Claude Agent SDK (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Anthropic publishes the wrapper and bundles the Claude Code binary in each platform wheel.

chunks.title: Claude.ai
chunks.text: Claude.ai (by Anthropic), catalog entry under UI & API: Anthropic's consumer chat product on web, desktop and mobile, for working with the Claude model family. The surface adds Projects, Artifacts for live-rendered code and documents, web search, voice, integrations and multimodal upload.

chunks.title: Claude Code
chunks.text: Claude Code (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Agentic coding tool from Anthropic that runs in the terminal, reads a whole codebase and executes multi-step development tasks including code generation, refactoring, git workflows and testing. It extends through a skills and hooks system and supports MCP tools natively, and also runs in VS Code, a desktop app, the web, Slack and mobile.

chunks.title: Claude Fable
chunks.text: Claude Fable (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Claude Fable is Anthropic's Mythos-class tier, built for demanding reasoning, long-horizon agentic coding, knowledge work, vision and scientific research.

chunks.title: Claude Fable
chunks.text: Claude Fable (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Fable 5, made generally available in June 2026, is the same underlying model as Claude Mythos 5, wrapped in safeguards that route sensitive cybersecurity, biology, chemistry and distillation requests to a less capable Claude model, with a one-million-token context window and up to 128K output tokens. Fable 5.1 is the current release.

chunks.title: Claude Haiku
chunks.text: Claude Haiku (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Claude Haiku is Anthropic's small, fast tier, built for high-volume, low-latency coding and chat where cost and speed matter more than peak reasoning. It sits beneath Sonnet and Opus, and the name persists across successive generations rather than pinning to one release.

chunks.title: Claude Haiku
chunks.text: Claude Haiku (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Weights are closed, and it is available through the Anthropic API and the Claude apps.

chunks.title: Claude Opus
chunks.text: Claude Opus (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Claude Opus is Anthropic's heavy-reasoning tier, tuned for long-running agentic coding, knowledge work and long-horizon planning across large codebases. The tier runs from the Opus 4.x line through Opus 5 to Opus 5.5, the current release, which Anthropic recommends as the starting model for most workloads.

chunks.title: Claude Opus
chunks.text: Claude Opus (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: It is available through the Anthropic API and claude.ai, and earlier releases through Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Vertex AI.

chunks.title: Claude Sonnet
chunks.text: Claude Sonnet (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Claude Sonnet is Anthropic's mid-tier Claude model, positioned between Haiku (small, high-volume) and Opus (complex, judgment-heavy work), and aimed at everyday coding, agent and knowledge-work tasks.

chunks.title: Claude Sonnet
chunks.text: Claude Sonnet (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: The name is applied to whichever generation is currently shipping rather than to one fixed release, from Sonnet 4.6 through Sonnet 5 to Sonnet 5.5. Weights are closed, and the model is available through the Anthropic API, cloud platforms and the Claude apps.

chunks.title: Clay
chunks.text: Clay (by Clay Foundation), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Clay is an Earth-observation foundation model that embeds satellite imagery together with location, time, and sensor metadata. The release provides pretrained weights and a configurable training interface for representation learning and downstream geospatial tasks. The Clay Foundation develops and distributes it.

chunks.title: ClearML
chunks.text: ClearML (by ClearML), catalog entry under ML orchestration: End-to-end machine-learning platform covering experiment management, data management, pipelines and remote execution. Tasks are enqueued and a ClearML Agent running on a worker machine pulls them, reproduces the original environment in a container and runs the code.

chunks.title: ClearML
chunks.text: ClearML (by ClearML), catalog entry under ML orchestration: The Python SDK is Apache-2.0; the server the platform runs on is licensed under the Server Side Public License.

chunks.title: ClimaX
chunks.text: ClimaX (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: ClimaX is Microsoft's foundation model for weather and climate, pretrained on five CMIP6 climate-simulation datasets and adapted to global forecasting, regional forecasting, and climate projection.

chunks.title: ClimaX
chunks.text: ClimaX (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: The release documents the corpus download and preprocessing pipeline, the pretraining run, and per-task fine-tuning configurations, and publishes checkpoints at two grid resolutions.

chunks.title: Cline
chunks.text: Cline (by Cline), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Autonomous coding agent available as a VS Code extension, a CLI and an SDK. It creates and edits files, runs terminal commands, drives a browser and orchestrates multi-step development tasks with human approval at each step. The SDK exists so the agent can be embedded in other products.

chunks.title: CLIP
chunks.text: CLIP (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: CLIP is OpenAI's 2021 contrastive image-text model and the origin of the whole cross-modal embedding line. An image encoder and a text encoder are trained to put matching pairs close together in one shared space, which makes image-text retrieval and zero-shot classification the same operation.

chunks.title: CLIP
chunks.text: CLIP (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Five years on it remains the single most downloaded vision model on the Hub, mostly as the frozen text or image tower inside diffusion and VLM stacks rather than as a retriever in its own right.

chunks.title: Cloudflare Sandboxes
chunks.text: Cloudflare Sandboxes (by Cloudflare), catalog entry under Deployment: Cloudflare offers two paths for running agent-generated code on its own network.

chunks.title: Cloudflare Sandboxes
chunks.text: Cloudflare Sandboxes (by Cloudflare), catalog entry under Deployment: Dynamic Workers lets a Worker load fresh code at runtime into a separate V8 isolate, starting in milliseconds with network access blocked or intercepted per load; the Sandbox SDK backs the same idea with containers on Workers and Durable Objects, for arbitrary commands, files, background processes and exposed services.

chunks.title: Cloudflare Sandboxes
chunks.text: Cloudflare Sandboxes (by Cloudflare), catalog entry under Deployment: Both are reached only through Cloudflare's platform.

chunks.title: CodeContests
chunks.text: CodeContests (by Google), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Competitive-programming dataset built for the AlphaCode paper, holding 4,044 problems collected from Codeforces, CodeChef and other contest platforms, each with a description, correct and incorrect human solutions in several languages, and public, private and generated test cases.

chunks.title: CodeGemma
chunks.text: CodeGemma (by Google), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Google's code-specialized Gemma family: a 2B pretrained model for fast fill-in-the-middle completion, a 7B pretrained model for infilling and natural language, and a 7B instruction-tuned variant for code chat. All are further-trained on 500 billion to a trillion tokens of public code, mathematics and synthetic data.

chunks.title: CodeLlama Instruct
chunks.text: CodeLlama Instruct (by Meta), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Code Llama Instruct is a code-specialized, instruction-tuned family built on Llama 2 at 7B, 13B, 34B and 70B and fine-tuned for coding chat. Meta trained it during 2023.

chunks.title: Coder OSS
chunks.text: Coder OSS (by Coder), catalog entry under Deployment: Coder OSS provisions self-hosted cloud development environments on a team's own infrastructure, with each workspace defined in Terraform over EC2 VMs, Kubernetes pods or Docker containers, reached through a Wireguard tunnel and shut down automatically when idle.

chunks.title: Coder OSS
chunks.text: Coder OSS (by Coder), catalog entry under Deployment: Coder Agents runs a coding agent's loop in the control plane rather than the workspace, so model credentials stay out of developer environments and every action carries a user identity.

chunks.title: Codestral
chunks.text: Codestral (by Mistral AI (API)), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Mistral's code-completion and fill-in-the-middle specialist, instruction-tuned with a chat mode and reached through Mistral's API, a customer VPC or on-premises deployment. It sits in a broader coding stack alongside Codestral Embed for retrieval, Devstral as the open-weight agentic counterpart, and the Mistral Vibe CLI.

chunks.title: Codex CLI
chunks.text: Codex CLI (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Terminal coding agent from OpenAI, written in Rust. It reads a codebase, proposes a plan and executes multi-file changes with sandboxed command execution, and documents writable roots, permission profiles, agent approvals, auto-review, MCP connectors and skills. Desktop builds are offered for Linux and Windows.

chunks.title: Cohere Embed
chunks.text: Cohere Embed (by Cohere), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Cohere’s embedding model line, currently embed-v4.0: a single multimodal model that embeds text, images and mixed text/image payloads such as PDFs into one space. It carries a 128k context, Matryoshka output dimensions of 256, 512, 1024 or 1536, and is sold through Cohere’s Embed endpoint, AWS SageMaker and Bedrock, and Azure AI Foundry.

chunks.title: Cohere Rerank API
chunks.text: Cohere Rerank API (by Cohere), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Reranking API that takes a query and a list of documents and returns them reordered by relevance. It is built for RAG pipelines: an agent retrieves candidates from a vector database, then calls Rerank to pick the most relevant before passing them to a model.

chunks.title: Cohere Rerank API
chunks.text: Cohere Rerank API (by Cohere), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: It is offered standalone rather than bundled into a vector database, and applied as a single API call.

chunks.title: Cohere Transcribe
chunks.text: Cohere Transcribe (by Cohere), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Cohere's 2B-parameter Conformer encoder-decoder speech recognition model, trained from scratch for transcription in 14 languages. Released on the Hugging Face Hub, where downloading requires accepting a contact-sharing prompt; an Arabic variant followed.

chunks.title: ColBERT
chunks.text: ColBERT (by Stanford Future Data Systems), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: ColBERT is the canonical late-interaction retriever from Stanford Future Data Systems.

chunks.title: ColBERT
chunks.text: ColBERT (by Stanford Future Data Systems), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Instead of collapsing a passage into one vector, it encodes every token into its own embedding and scores a query against a passage with a MaxSim operator over the two token matrices, which recovers fine-grained term matching at the cost of a larger index.

chunks.title: ColBERT
chunks.text: ColBERT (by Stanford Future Data Systems), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The released colbertv2.0 checkpoint pairs that architecture with residual compression and denoised distillation supervision, and the repository ships the trainer, the PLAID index and the LoTTE benchmark alongside it.

chunks.title: ColPali
chunks.text: ColPali (by ILLUIN Technology), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: ColPali applies the ColBERT late-interaction recipe to page screenshots: a vision-language model embeds each image patch of a rendered document page, a query is embedded token by token, and MaxSim scores the two multi-vector sets. That removes the OCR-and-chunk pipeline from document retrieval entirely.

chunks.title: ColPali
chunks.text: ColPali (by ILLUIN Technology), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The line has grown past the original PaliGemma-based ColPali into ColQwen2, ColQwen2.5, the sub-1B ColSmol checkpoints and ColQwen-Omni, all released from the vidore Hub org with the shared colpali-engine training and inference code.

chunks.title: ComfyUI
chunks.text: ComfyUI (by Comfy Org), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: ComfyUI is a node-graph application and local engine for running generative media models: a workflow wires loaders, samplers, encoders and decoders together, and the same graph can be reused, shared or served through its local API. It runs image, image-editing, video, audio and 3D generation models side by side.

chunks.title: ComfyUI
chunks.text: ComfyUI (by Comfy Org), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Comfy Org maintains it and sells a separate hosted version.

chunks.title: Comma v0.1
chunks.text: Comma v0.1 (by EleutherAI), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: A 7B base model from the EleutherAI-led Common Pile collaboration, trained on 2 trillion tokens drawn entirely from the Common Pile v0.1, an 8TB corpus of public domain and openly licensed text. It exists to test whether competitive models can be trained without unlicensed data, and performs comparably to budget-matched models like Llama 2 7B.

chunks.title: Command R+
chunks.text: Command R+ (by Cohere), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Command A+ is Cohere's enterprise language model, a 218B-parameter sparse mixture-of-experts (25B active) with vision input, conversational tool use and native citation generation through grounding spans that link claims to source documents.

chunks.title: Command R+
chunks.text: Command R+ (by Cohere), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: It supports 48 languages and a 128K context window, and runs on a single B200 or two H100 GPUs with W4A4 quantization. It succeeds the 104B Command R+ of 2024.

chunks.title: Common Corpus
chunks.text: Common Corpus (by PleIAs), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Multilingual pretraining dataset of roughly 2.27 trillion tokens, assembled by PleIAs with partners including the AI Alliance from uncopyrighted or openly licensed content only.

chunks.title: Common Corpus
chunks.text: Common Corpus (by PleIAs), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: It is organized into six curated collections - public-domain books, government documents, academic content, code, semantic data and web text - with document-level provenance and toxicity filtering. Its card reports 33 languages with more than 1 billion tokens each.

chunks.title: Mozilla Common Voice
chunks.text: Mozilla Common Voice (by Mozilla Foundation), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Mozilla Common Voice is a crowdsourced corpus of transcribed read speech in hundreds of languages, built for training and evaluating speech recognition. Volunteers record sentences on the Common Voice platform and other volunteers validate each clip; a smaller spontaneous-speech collection sits beside the scripted one.

chunks.title: Mozilla Common Voice
chunks.text: Mozilla Common Voice (by Mozilla Foundation), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Releases are distributed per language through Mozilla Data Collective. The Mozilla Foundation runs the project.

chunks.title: Compar:IA
chunks.text: Compar:IA (by DINUM / beta.gouv.fr (French Government)), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Blind model-comparison arena created by the French government's betagouv and DINUM with the Ministry of Culture. A user types a prompt, two anonymous models reply, and the user votes; the identities and each model's estimated energy cost are revealed afterward.

chunks.title: Compar:IA
chunks.text: Compar:IA (by DINUM / beta.gouv.fr (French Government)), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Its purpose is building large non-English human-preference datasets. It deploys with Docker on a single server, and another instance, AI-arenaen, runs in Denmark.

chunks.title: Compar:IA Datasets
chunks.text: Compar:IA Datasets (by Ministere de la Culture (France)), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Compar:IA Datasets is human-preference data released from the French government's Compar:IA chatbot arena and published by the Ministere de la Culture. Its comparia-votes dataset holds conversation-level pairwise preference votes on French-language conversations.

chunks.title: COMPL-AI
chunks.text: COMPL-AI (by COMPL-AI), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: COMPL-AI is a compliance-centered evaluation framework for large language models: a technical interpretation of the EU AI Act paired with an open benchmarking suite, now 29 benchmarks, that covers the Act's technical requirements. It is built on the Inspect evaluation framework and publishes results on a public leaderboard.

chunks.title: COMPL-AI
chunks.text: COMPL-AI (by COMPL-AI), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: ETH Zurich, INSAIT and LatticeFlow AI maintain it.

chunks.title: Compliance Trestle
chunks.text: Compliance Trestle (by OSCAL Compass), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: Compliance Trestle creates, validates and governs compliance documentation in NIST's OSCAL format, the machine-readable standard for control catalogs, profiles, component definitions and assessment results.

chunks.title: Compliance Trestle
chunks.text: Compliance Trestle (by OSCAL Compass), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: It is built to run as a CI/CD pipeline over compliance artifacts kept in git, splitting large OSCAL documents into reviewable pieces. It is part of the OSCAL Compass project.

chunks.title: Composable Kernel
chunks.text: Composable Kernel (by AMD), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Composable Kernel provides a programming model and template library for performance-critical machine learning kernels, decomposing GEMM, convolution and attention operations into tile-level pieces that recombine and fuse. It targets AMD GPUs through ROCm and includes a code generator for instance selection.

chunks.title: Composable Kernel
chunks.text: Composable Kernel (by AMD), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: AMD develops it in the ROCm/rocm-libraries monorepo, with the standalone ROCm/composable_kernel repository kept as a read-only mirror.

chunks.title: Composio
chunks.text: Composio (by Composio), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Agent tooling platform providing more than a thousand pre-built tool integrations with managed authentication, context management and a sandboxed execution environment.

chunks.title: Composio
chunks.text: Composio (by Composio), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: It handles OAuth flows, API pagination and rate limiting so agent builders do not have to, adds tool search and a sandboxed workbench, and can expose a session's tools as a hosted MCP endpoint.

chunks.title: Confer
chunks.text: Confer (by Confer Labs), catalog entry under UI & API: End-to-end encrypted AI chat assistant from Confer Labs. Prompts are encrypted on the device and sent over Noise-protocol pipes into a Trusted Execution Environment on a confidential VM, processed by open-weights models, then re-encrypted before leaving; history is encrypted with passkey-derived keys.

chunks.title: Confer
chunks.text: Confer (by Confer Labs), catalog entry under UI & API: Remote attestation, reproducible builds and an append-only transparency log are what make the claim checkable.

chunks.title: Confident AI
chunks.text: Confident AI (by Confident AI), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Hosted platform layered on the DeepEval library, adding dataset management, regression tracking, human annotation, custom dashboards, online evaluations against live traffic, alerting and incident response.

chunks.title: Confident AI
chunks.text: Confident AI (by Confident AI), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: It also covers red teaming against adversarial attacks and AI governance, and gates CI so a build fails when quality drops below a defined threshold. Self-hosting into a customer VPC or on-premises is an enterprise option.

chunks.title: Content Seal (Meta Seal)
chunks.text: Content Seal (Meta Seal) (by Meta), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: Content Seal is Meta's suite of invisible watermarking research code across audio, image, video and text. It collects AudioSeal, Video Seal and Pixel Seal, Watermark Anything, Stable Signature, TextSeal and related work on generation-time and in-model watermarking, each with released models and detectors.

chunks.title: Content Seal (Meta Seal)
chunks.text: Content Seal (Meta Seal) (by Meta), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: Meta states that the image version it deploys in production is a separate proprietary implementation.

chunks.title: Context7
chunks.text: Context7 (by Upstash), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Documentation retrieval service that supplies agents and coding assistants with current, version-correct library documentation and code examples, addressed over a hosted MCP endpoint or a CLI. The MCP server, CLI and SDK are published; the API backend, parsing engine and crawling engine that produce the index are not.

chunks.title: Continue
chunks.text: Continue (by Continue), catalog entry under UI & API: AI code assistant for VS Code and JetBrains, offering inline completion, chat, edit and agent modes against any model backend including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama and llama.cpp. It differs from Copilot in being model-agnostic and from Cursor in living inside an existing IDE rather than replacing it. Cursor acquired the project in 2026.

chunks.title: Coop
chunks.text: Coop (by ROOST), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Coop is a self-hosted review and moderation console from the nonprofit ROOST, run with Docker Compose. It provides review queues, routing, automated enforcement rules, analytics, and REST/GraphQL APIs, plus a child-safety workflow with HMA hash matching, NCMEC CyberTipline reporting, and OpenAI Moderation and Google Content Safety integrations.

chunks.title: Coop
chunks.text: Coop (by ROOST), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: It orchestrates AI safety signals rather than being a guardrail model itself. Musubi offers a hosted version.

chunks.title: Core ML Tools
chunks.text: Core ML Tools (by Apple), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Core ML Tools converts trained models from PyTorch and TensorFlow, and from non-neural libraries such as scikit-learn, XGBoost and LibSVM, into Apple's Core ML format. Beyond conversion it reads, writes and optimizes Core ML models, applying quantization, palettization and pruning, and verifies conversions by running predictions on macOS.

chunks.title: CorpusNós
chunks.text: CorpusNós (by Proxecto Nós), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: CorpusNós is a Galician pretraining corpus of about 1.9 billion tokens in 7.9 million documents, covering books, research articles, press and blogs, government texts, encyclopedic data, web crawls and translation corpora. It is split into public data and material obtained through transfer agreements with rights holders.

chunks.title: CorpusNós
chunks.text: CorpusNós (by Proxecto Nós), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Proxecto Nós builds it within the Spanish ILENIA program.

chunks.title: Cosmopedia
chunks.text: Cosmopedia (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Synthetic pretraining dataset of more than 31 million textbooks, blog posts, stories and educational articles, about 25 billion tokens, generated with Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct from seed samples drawn from web data, Stanford courses, OpenStax, Khan Academy and WikiHow.

chunks.title: Cosmopedia
chunks.text: Cosmopedia (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: It was built by Hugging Face's Smol Models Research team as a reference corpus for synthetic-data pretraining recipes.

chunks.title: CosyVoice
chunks.text: CosyVoice (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Alibaba's multilingual voice generation line (CosyVoice, CosyVoice 2 and Fun-CosyVoice 3), with zero-shot voice cloning and instruction control over dialect, emotion and speed in 9 languages and more than 18 Chinese dialects. The repository ships inference, training and deployment code.

chunks.title: Crawl4AI
chunks.text: Crawl4AI (by UncleCode), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Open-source web crawler and scraper built for LLM pipelines, turning pages into clean Markdown or structured JSON for retrieval and agent use. Runs on a managed headless browser with session reuse, hooks and proxy rotation, and ships CSS, XPath, regex and LLM-driven extraction strategies, a Docker deployment and a CLI.

chunks.title: Credo AI Governance Platform
chunks.text: Credo AI Governance Platform (by Credo AI), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: Credo AI is a closed AI governance platform for registering AI agents, models and applications, assessing their risk and tracking compliance.

chunks.title: Credo AI Governance Platform
chunks.text: Credo AI Governance Platform (by Credo AI), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: Pre-built policy packs map requirements from the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001 and other frameworks to controls, and the platform generates audit-ready evidence and audit trails.

chunks.title: CrewAI
chunks.text: CrewAI (by CrewAI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Role-based multi-agent orchestration framework built around crews and flows, where agents take defined roles and hand work between them. A commercial platform is sold alongside it, adding SSO, role-based access control, workload identity, PII redaction and deployment to the vendor's cloud, a customer VPC or on-premises infrastructure.

chunks.title: Croissant
chunks.text: Croissant (by MLCommons), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: Croissant is MLCommons' metadata format for machine-learning datasets, combining a dataset's metadata, file descriptions, record structure and default ML semantics in one JSON-LD file built on schema.org.

chunks.title: Croissant
chunks.text: Croissant (by MLCommons), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: The mlcroissant Python library validates and loads Croissant files, and a Responsible AI extension records provenance, collection and bias information. Major dataset hubs publish Croissant descriptions.

chunks.title: CRUXEval
chunks.text: CRUXEval (by Meta), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: 800 Python function, input and output triples evaluating code reasoning and execution through two paired tasks: predicting the input given a function and its output, and predicting the output given a function and its input.

chunks.title: CRUXEval
chunks.text: CRUXEval (by Meta), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Bootstrapped by Meta FAIR using Code Llama 34B and filtered to short, low-compute problems, it was published at ICML 2024 and spawned a multilingual community extension.

chunks.title: CSGHub
chunks.text: CSGHub (by OpenCSG), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Self-hostable platform for managing large-model assets, positioned by OpenCSG as a private, on-premise counterpart to Hugging Face Hub. Users upload and version models, datasets, code, prompt and MCP repositories and application Spaces through a web UI, git, a CLI or the CSGHub SDK, backed by a Git server with Git LFS and object storage.

chunks.title: CSGHub
chunks.text: CSGHub (by OpenCSG), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Its API is compatible with Hugging Face clients, and it can synchronize repositories from remote hubs.

chunks.title: CUDA Tile IR
chunks.text: CUDA Tile IR (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: CUDA Tile IR is NVIDIA's MLIR-based intermediate representation and compiler infrastructure for CUDA kernel optimization, providing a tile dialect, Python bindings and a bytecode format for expressing and lowering tile-based tensor computations that target NVIDIA tensor core units.

chunks.title: cuLA
chunks.text: cuLA (by inclusionAI (Ant Group)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: cuLA (CUDA Linear Attention) provides hand-tuned CUDA kernels, written in CuTe DSL and CUTLASS C++, for linear attention variants including GLA, KDA, GDN and Lightning Attention, targeting NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs.

chunks.title: cuLA
chunks.text: cuLA (by inclusionAI (Ant Group)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: It shares its interface with the flash-linear-attention library as an early-stage standalone precursor to a planned integration.

chunks.title: CulturaX
chunks.text: CulturaX (by University of Oregon NLP (UONLP)), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Multilingual web corpus for pretraining containing 6.3 trillion tokens across 167 languages, combined and cleaned from mC4 and OSCAR by the University of Oregon NLP group.

chunks.title: CulturaX
chunks.text: CulturaX (by University of Oregon NLP (UONLP)), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Its pipeline applies language identification, URL filtering, metric-based cleaning, document refinement and MinHash fuzzy deduplication, and it is distributed as roughly 16TB of parquet.

chunks.title: cuML
chunks.text: cuML (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated machine-learning library in the RAPIDS suite, with scikit-learn-style estimators for clustering, regression, classification, dimensionality reduction, nearest neighbors and time series - more than fifty algorithms, including GPU versions of UMAP and HDBSCAN.

chunks.title: cuML
chunks.text: cuML (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Its cuml.accel mode runs existing scikit-learn, UMAP and HDBSCAN code on the GPU with no code changes, and it scales across GPUs and nodes with Dask.

chunks.title: Cursor
chunks.text: Cursor (by Anysphere), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: AI-first code editor, forked from VS Code, with an agent mode that makes multi-file changes autonomously, runs terminal commands and iterates against errors. The agent works alongside manual editing rather than replacing it, and a background agent completes tasks asynchronously.

chunks.title: CUTLASS
chunks.text: CUTLASS (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: CUTLASS is a collection of C++ template abstractions for implementing matrix-matrix multiplication and related computations at every level of the CUDA parallelization hierarchy. Tiling sizes, data types and algorithmic policy are template parameters, so kernels are specialized and tuned rather than hand-written.

chunks.title: CUTLASS
chunks.text: CUTLASS (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: PyTorch and FlashAttention vendor it as a submodule for their GEMM paths.

chunks.title: Danish Dynaword
chunks.text: Danish Dynaword (by Danish Foundation Models), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Danish Dynaword is a continually updated Danish pretraining corpus of more than 9 billion tokens, assembled only from openly licensed sources across legal text, parliament records, news, books, conversation, social media and the web, including the Bornholm and South Jutland dialects.

chunks.title: Danish Dynaword
chunks.text: Danish Dynaword (by Danish Foundation Models), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Each source has its own datasheet, and contributors add new ones through a tested submission process. Danish Foundation Models maintains it.

chunks.title: DarijaMMLU
chunks.text: DarijaMMLU (by Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: DarijaMMLU tests language models on 22,027 multiple-choice questions in Moroccan Darija across 44 subjects.

chunks.title: DarijaMMLU
chunks.text: DarijaMMLU (by Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The questions are selected subsets of MMLU and ArabicMMLU, machine-translated into Darija with Claude 3.5 Sonnet and then manually reviewed and adapted, with technical and culturally inappropriate topics left out. MBZUAI-Paris built it as part of the Atlas-Chat evaluation suite.

chunks.title: Darts
chunks.text: Darts (by Unit8), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Time-series forecasting and anomaly-detection library from Unit8 with one fit/predict interface over many model kinds - baselines, statistical models such as ARIMA, ETS, Theta and TBATS, regression models on scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost and CatBoost, deep models such as N-BEATS, N-HiTS, TFT, TiDE and TSMixer

chunks.title: Darts
chunks.text: Darts (by Unit8), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: and pretrained foundation models such as Chronos-2 and TimesFM that forecast without training. It adds backtesting, ensembling, conformal prediction and covariate support.

chunks.title: Data-Juicer
chunks.text: Data-Juicer (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Data processing system for foundation models: 200+ composable operators for cleaning, deduplicating, synthesizing, and analyzing text and multimodal LLM training data.

chunks.title: Datadog LLM Observability
chunks.text: Datadog LLM Observability (by Datadog), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Enterprise LLM monitoring integrated into the Datadog APM platform. Traces LLM calls alongside existing infrastructure, application, and security monitoring. For organizations already using Datadog who want unified observability across their entire stack including AI/LLM components.

chunks.title: Datadog LLM Observability
chunks.text: Datadog LLM Observability (by Datadog), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Covers agent monitoring, prompt tracking and management, quality monitoring, and correlation of LLM spans with APM.

chunks.title: datamap-rs
chunks.text: datamap-rs (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Rust JSONL map-filter-annotate pipeline for cleaning and filtering large text corpora. The data-cleaning stage of the Dolma 3 pipeline.

chunks.title: Datasette Agent
chunks.text: Datasette Agent (by Datasette), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Agent plugin for Datasette, the tool for exploring and publishing structured data in SQLite. A chat interface answers natural-language questions against a database: the agent writes and runs SQL, explores the data in the background and renders results.

chunks.title: Datasette Agent
chunks.text: Datasette Agent (by Datasette), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: It calls models through the datasette-llm plugin and exposes an extensible tool surface for charts and image generation.

chunks.title: datatrove
chunks.text: datatrove (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Platform-agnostic library of composable pipeline blocks for large-scale text data processing (reading, filtering, deduplication, tokenization) that runs unchanged across local, Slurm, and cloud backends. The reference pretraining-data pipeline behind the FineWeb family.

chunks.title: DatologyAI
chunks.text: DatologyAI (by DatologyAI), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Automated training-data curation platform deployed into the customer's own cloud: deduplication, model-based quality filtering, embedding-based selection and pruning, data ordering, and synthetic-data steps for pretraining corpora.

chunks.title: Daytona Sandbox
chunks.text: Daytona Sandbox (by Daytona), catalog entry under Deployment: Daytona provisions stateful sandboxes for running AI-generated code, putting sandbox creation, execution and deletion under programmatic control through SDKs for Python, TypeScript, Ruby, Go and Java. The same API exposes process execution with streamed output, file system operations, Git and a built-in language server. Daytona sells it as a hosted cloud.

chunks.title: DCLM pipeline
chunks.text: DCLM pipeline (by DataComp-LM (ML Foundations)), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: The DataComp-LM toolkit and competition harness: a standardized Common Crawl pool, open_lm training recipes, a 50+ task eval suite, and the reference curation pipeline that produces DCLM-baseline.

chunks.title: DCLM-baseline
chunks.text: DCLM-baseline (by DataComp-LM (ML Foundations)), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Curated pretraining dataset derived from Common Crawl, about 4 trillion tokens across 3 billion documents and roughly 7.2TB, produced by the DataComp-LM project.

chunks.title: DCLM-baseline
chunks.text: DCLM-baseline (by DataComp-LM (ML Foundations)), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: It was built with heuristic cleaning, Bloom-filter deduplication and fastText model-based quality filtering, and is the reference dataset for the DCLM benchmark.

chunks.title: DDGS
chunks.text: DDGS (by deedy5), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Metasearch library that runs one query against ten public web search services - Bing, Brave, DuckDuckGo, Google, Grokipedia, Mojeek, Startpage, Yandex, Yahoo and Wikipedia - and returns their results in one list. Ships a CLI, an optional FastAPI server and an optional MCP server, all run by the caller with no account and no key.

chunks.title: decon
chunks.text: decon (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Decontamination tool that flags and removes training documents overlapping evaluation benchmarks. The decontamination stage of the Dolma 3 pipeline.

chunks.title: Deep Lake
chunks.text: Deep Lake (by Activeloop), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Deep Lake is a database for AI built on a storage format designed for deep-learning access patterns, holding embeddings alongside the audio, text, video, image, DICOM and PDF records they were derived from. It serves two jobs from one store: vector and metadata retrieval for LLM applications, and dataset management and streaming for training.

chunks.title: Deep Lake
chunks.text: Deep Lake (by Activeloop), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Activeloop develops it, with a C++ core, a Postgres integration and Python bindings in the repository.

chunks.title: DeepChat
chunks.text: DeepChat (by ThinkInAI), catalog entry under UI & API: DeepChat is a cross-platform desktop assistant that connects to multiple model providers. It supports MCP tools, the Agent Client Protocol, a skills system, remote control of a running instance, and any provider with an OpenAI- or Gemini-compatible API, alongside local models served through Ollama.

chunks.title: DeepEval
chunks.text: DeepEval (by Confident AI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Pytest-style evaluation framework for LLM applications, with dozens of built-in metrics including G-Eval, faithfulness, hallucination, task completion and RAG-specific scores. Metrics run locally and drop into an existing test suite, so a merge can be gated on a metric threshold.

chunks.title: DeepGEMM
chunks.text: DeepGEMM (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: DeepGEMM is a tensor-core kernel library for FP8, FP4 and BF16 GEMMs, fused mixture-of-experts with overlapped communication, and MQA scoring, in one CUDA codebase. Kernels compile at runtime through a JIT module, so installation performs no CUDA compilation, though running it needs the CUDA Toolkit and an NVIDIA SM90 or SM100 GPU.

chunks.title: DeepGEMM
chunks.text: DeepGEMM (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: It borrows concepts from CUTLASS and CuTe without relying heavily on their templates.

chunks.title: Deepgram Nova
chunks.text: Deepgram Nova (by Deepgram), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Deepgram's hosted speech recognition models; Nova-3 adds real-time multilingual transcription with code-switching across 10 languages and real-time redaction. Offered as a cloud API and as a self-hosted deployment for enterprises, with no public weights.

chunks.title: DeepProve
chunks.text: DeepProve (by Lagrange Labs), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: DeepProve is a zero-knowledge proof system for neural-network inference that proves full transformer forward passes, with GPT-2, Gemma 3 and Llama 2 confirmed end to end, as well as MLP and CNN models. It uses sumchecks and logup GKR rather than arithmetic circuits to keep proving time sublinear in model size.

chunks.title: DeepProve
chunks.text: DeepProve (by Lagrange Labs), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: Lagrange Labs publishes it as a Rust workspace.

chunks.title: DeepSeek-V4-Pro
chunks.text: DeepSeek-V4-Pro (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: DeepSeek-V4-Pro is DeepSeek's 1.6T-parameter mixture-of-experts model, with 49B parameters active per token, a one-million-token context and a hybrid attention design that combines Compressed Sparse Attention with Heavily Compressed Attention.

chunks.title: DeepSeek-V4-Pro
chunks.text: DeepSeek-V4-Pro (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: It was pretrained on more than 32T tokens and ships as base and instruct checkpoints, alongside the smaller V4-Flash and the multimodal V4.1-Flash.

chunks.title: DeepSeek Chat
chunks.text: DeepSeek Chat (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under UI & API: Hosted consumer chat product from DeepSeek, at chat.deepseek.com and in iOS and Android apps, fronting the company's own model family with long-context handling, file reading and agent capabilities. It runs as a free hosted service, distinct from the model weights of the same name.

chunks.title: DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct
chunks.text: DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Dedicated coding mixture-of-experts model, instruction-tuned for generation, completion and chat, built on a DeepSeek-V2 checkpoint with six trillion additional code tokens. It ships in a 236B-total variant with 21B active parameters and a 16B Lite variant, supports 338 programming languages and a 128K context.

chunks.title: DeepSeek Harness
chunks.text: DeepSeek Harness (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: DeepSeek Harness (dsh) is an agent harness that reads and edits workspace files, runs commands, delegates work to sub-agents and keeps a plan. It runs as a local Web UI, a desktop app, a headless command, an Agent Client Protocol server or behind TypeScript and Python SDKs.

chunks.title: DeepSeek Harness
chunks.text: DeepSeek Harness (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Everything from the agent loop to tools, model adapters and sandboxing is a plugin on the Cordis framework. DeepSeek develops it, and it is in developer preview.

chunks.title: DeepSeek-V4-Pro / V4-Flash
chunks.text: DeepSeek-V4-Pro / V4-Flash (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: DeepSeek-V4-Pro and V4-Flash are open-weight mixture-of-experts language models with a one-million-token context window. V4-Pro has 1.6T total parameters (49B active) and V4-Flash has 284B (13B active). Both are published on Hugging Face by DeepSeek.

chunks.title: DeepSeek-OCR
chunks.text: DeepSeek-OCR (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Vision-language model from DeepSeek that treats a page image as a compressed carrier of text, converting document images into linearised markdown-like output.

chunks.title: DeepSeek-OCR
chunks.text: DeepSeek-OCR (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: It was released as a study in optical context compression - how far a page of text can be represented by vision tokens rather than text tokens - and the OCR capability is the demonstration of it.

chunks.title: DeepSeek-R1
chunks.text: DeepSeek-R1 (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: DeepSeek-R1 is a reasoning model, released in January 2025, that uses large-scale GRPO reinforcement learning to develop chain-of-thought before answering. It is a 671B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 37B active parameters and a 128K context window, post-trained on DeepSeek-V3-Base and released alongside 1.5B to 70B distilled variants.

chunks.title: DeepSeek-R1
chunks.text: DeepSeek-R1 (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: The DeepSeek-V4 family has since followed it.

chunks.title: DeepSeek-VL
chunks.text: DeepSeek-VL (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Multimodal models: DeepSeek-VL is DeepSeek's line of vision-language models, released separately from its general chat models.

chunks.title: DeepSeek-VL
chunks.text: DeepSeek-VL (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Multimodal models: DeepSeek-VL2 is a mixture-of-experts model in three sizes, from 1.0B to 4.5B activated parameters, that answers questions about images, reads documents, tables and charts, and grounds objects with bounding boxes across a few images per conversation.

chunks.title: DeepSpeed
chunks.text: DeepSpeed (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: DeepSpeed is a deep-learning optimization library for efficient distributed training and inference of very large models. It provides ZeRO memory optimization, ZeRO-Infinity, 3D parallelism, Ulysses sequence parallelism and mixture-of-experts support, and has been used to train models such as BLOOM (176B) and Megatron-Turing NLG (530B).

chunks.title: DeepSpeed
chunks.text: DeepSpeed (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It integrates with Hugging Face Transformers, Accelerate and PyTorch Lightning.

chunks.title: DeepTeam
chunks.text: DeepTeam (by Confident AI), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: DeepTeam is a red-teaming framework for LLM systems from Confident AI that simulates adversarial attacks, including jailbreaking, prompt injection and multi-turn exploitation.

chunks.title: DeepTeam
chunks.text: DeepTeam (by Confident AI), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: It ships more than fifty vulnerability checks and twenty attack methods mapped to the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs and for Agents, NIST AI RMF and MITRE ATLAS, alongside seven runtime guardrails. The framework runs locally and is built on Confident AI's DeepEval evaluation framework.

chunks.title: Depth Anything
chunks.text: Depth Anything (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Depth-estimation model line from ByteDance Seed. Depth Anything 3, the current release, predicts consistent depth and camera pose from one image or many, with or without known poses, using a plain DINO-style transformer, and ships any-view, metric-depth, monocular and nested checkpoints from Small to Giant.

chunks.title: Depth Anything
chunks.text: Depth Anything (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Depth Anything V1 and V2 remain widely used for single-image depth.

chunks.title: Desktop Commander MCP
chunks.text: Desktop Commander MCP (by Eduard Ruzga), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: MCP server giving an agent control of the local machine: terminal execution, filesystem search and editing, process control, and readers for Excel, PDF and DOCX. Commands run under the caller's own user.

chunks.title: Detectron2
chunks.text: Detectron2 (by Meta), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Meta AI's library for object detection, segmentation and other visual recognition tasks, the successor to Detectron and maskrcnn-benchmark.

chunks.title: Detectron2
chunks.text: Detectron2 (by Meta), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: It implements Faster and Mask R-CNN, RetinaNet, keypoint, panoptic and DensePose models among others, with a model zoo of COCO, LVIS and Cityscapes baselines and training tools that many research projects build on. It installs from source or from Linux wheels Meta hosts, not from PyPI.

chunks.title: Determined
chunks.text: Determined (by Determined AI), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Machine-learning platform for distributed training, hyperparameter search and experiment tracking on a cluster it manages itself. An experiment configuration names slots_per_trial, and Determined's scheduler allocates that many GPUs - spanning whole agent machines where the number requires it - so every trial starts with all its resources at once.

chunks.title: Determined
chunks.text: Determined (by Determined AI), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Searchers run many trials against one configuration.

chunks.title: Devin
chunks.text: Devin (by Cognition), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Devin is a hosted autonomous software-engineering agent that takes a task, works in a cloud development environment and delivers a pull request. It is reached through a web interface, a CLI, a desktop app and an API, and sessions can run on customer-managed machines through Devin Outposts. Cognition builds and sells it.

chunks.title: Devstral
chunks.text: Devstral (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Devstral is an open-weight family of agentic coding models from Mistral, built for software-engineering tasks such as exploring codebases and editing multiple files. Devstral Small 2 is a 24B instruct model with a 256K context window that runs on a single RTX 4090 or a Mac with 32GB RAM, and the 123B Devstral 2 is the larger model in the release.

chunks.title: DiffSynth-Studio
chunks.text: DiffSynth-Studio (by ModelScope (Alibaba)), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: DiffSynth-Studio is the ModelScope team's Python engine for running and training diffusion models.

chunks.title: DiffSynth-Studio
chunks.text: DiffSynth-Studio (by ModelScope (Alibaba)), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: It supports inference and full or LoRA training for image models (FLUX, Qwen-Image, Z-Image and others), video models (Wan, LTX-2, MiniMax H3) and audio models (ACE-Step, YuE2, MiniMax-Music3), and powers ModelScope's hosted generation service.

chunks.title: Diffusers
chunks.text: Diffusers (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Diffusers is a PyTorch library from Hugging Face providing pretrained diffusion models for generating images, video, audio, and 3D molecular structures. It offers ready-to-use inference pipelines, interchangeable noise schedulers, and pretrained models that serve as building blocks for custom diffusion systems.

chunks.title: Diffusers
chunks.text: Diffusers (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It is Hugging Face's primary library for diffusion-based generative models.

chunks.title: Dify
chunks.text: Dify (by LangGenius), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Platform for building LLM applications, combining a visual workflow builder, RAG pipelines, agent tooling and model management across providers in one workspace. It deploys to the vendor's cloud, a customer VPC or self-hosted infrastructure with a single Docker command.

chunks.title: DINO (DINOv2, DINOv3)
chunks.text: DINO (DINOv2, DINOv3) (by Meta), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Meta's self-supervised vision backbones, trained without labels to produce general image features. DINOv3, the current release, spans ViT models from 21 million to 7 billion parameters and ConvNeXt models, trained on 1.7 billion curated web images, with a satellite-imagery variant.

chunks.title: DINO (DINOv2, DINOv3)
chunks.text: DINO (DINOv2, DINOv3) (by Meta), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Meta also publishes heads that turn the features into classification, depth, detection and segmentation, and dino.txt for text-prompted zero-shot tasks. DINOv2 was the Apache-licensed predecessor.

chunks.title: DiskANN
chunks.text: DiskANN (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: DiskANN is a Microsoft Research vector indexing library built around the Vamana graph algorithm, with disk-resident and in-memory index variants for large-scale approximate nearest neighbour search. It ships as a composable library exposing build and query APIs rather than a standalone server.

chunks.title: distilabel
chunks.text: distilabel (by Argilla), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Framework for building synthetic-data and AI-feedback pipelines: LLM-driven generation, labeling, and preference-data construction with pluggable model backends.

chunks.title: dlib
chunks.text: dlib (by davisking), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: C++ toolkit of machine-learning algorithms and supporting tools, with Python bindings, maintained by Davis King. It provides support vector machines, relevance vector machines, kernel methods, structural SVMs, clustering and a deep-learning API, and is best known for its face detection, facial landmark and face recognition models.

chunks.title: dlib
chunks.text: dlib (by davisking), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: The trained models are published separately, mostly in the public domain.

chunks.title: DLRover
chunks.text: DLRover (by Ant Group), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Distributed deep-learning training system from Ant Group, built to keep large training jobs running. It manages elastic training on Kubernetes - scaling workers up and down during a run, detecting and replacing failed nodes, and resuming from checkpoints - so that a job survives the failures that would otherwise restart it.

chunks.title: Docling
chunks.text: Docling (by IBM), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: SDK and CLI that parses PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, EPUB, images, audio and video into unified structured output - Markdown, lossless JSON, HTML, WebVTT and DocTags - for generative-AI and RAG pipelines.

chunks.title: Docling
chunks.text: Docling (by IBM), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Unlike URL-to-Markdown services it does deep local document understanding: layout and reading-order analysis, table-structure recognition, formula and code extraction, OCR, and vision and speech model integration. It also reads application-specific XML schemas including USPTO patents, JATS articles and XBRL filings, and ships its own MCP server.

chunks.title: DOFA
chunks.text: DOFA (by Zhu X Lab), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: DOFA (Dynamic One-For-All) is a wavelength-conditioned Earth-observation foundation model from the Technical University of Munich's Chair of Data Science in Earth Observation.

chunks.title: DOFA
chunks.text: DOFA (by Zhu X Lab), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: A dynamic hypernetwork, inspired by neural plasticity, generates patch-embedding weights from the wavelengths of whatever bands are supplied, so a single checkpoint accepts Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2, NAIP RGB, Gaofen multispectral, and hyperspectral imagery with any number of channels.

chunks.title: Dolci
chunks.text: Dolci (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Ai2's post-training data suite for Olmo 3, with separate mixes for supervised fine-tuning, DPO preference tuning and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) across the Instruct and Think variants.

chunks.title: Dolci
chunks.text: Dolci (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: The mixes combine existing sets such as OpenThoughts 3, FLAN v2, OpenAssistant, Aya, Tulu 3 persona data and WildChat with new Ai2 prompts for precise instruction following, Python algorithms, logic puzzles and tool use.

chunks.title: Dolma
chunks.text: Dolma (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Open pretraining corpus of roughly 3 trillion tokens drawn from Common Crawl web text, academic publications, code, books and encyclopedic material. It was created by the Allen Institute for AI and used to train the OLMo family, and the release includes a toolkit for replicating and curating the data.

chunks.title: Dolma 3
chunks.text: Dolma 3 (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Ai2's pretraining data release behind OLMo 3: a pool of about 9 trillion tokens drawn from Common Crawl, olmOCR-processed scientific PDFs, Stack-Edu code and FineMath, alongside the quality-upsampled mixes used in training - Dolma 3 Mix, Dolmino mid-training and Longmino long-context.

chunks.title: Dolma 3
chunks.text: Dolma 3 (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: The pool, every mix and the curation tooling are released together.

chunks.title: Dolma toolkit
chunks.text: Dolma toolkit (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Toolkit for curating language-model pretraining data: built-in taggers (Gopher, C4, OpenWebText), custom taggers, and Rust Bloom-filter deduplication. Runs on a single machine, a cluster, or in the cloud, including S3-compatible storage.

chunks.title: Dolt
chunks.text: Dolt (by DoltHub), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Dolt is a SQL database with version control built into the storage engine: tables are committed, branched, merged, pushed and pulled the way Git handles files, and the history is queryable through system tables and functions. It speaks the MySQL wire protocol, so existing clients connect unchanged, and it ships a Git-style command line beside the server.

chunks.title: Dolt
chunks.text: Dolt (by DoltHub), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: DoltHub develops it.

chunks.title: dots.ocr
chunks.text: dots.ocr (by Studio Dots AI), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Multilingual document-parsing model that performs layout detection and content recognition in a single vision-language model rather than a pipeline of separate stages, switching task by prompt. It emits layout blocks with their reading order and the text inside them.

chunks.title: Doubao
chunks.text: Doubao (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under UI & API: ByteDance's consumer AI assistant, for questions, study help, and work tasks such as summarizing material, analyzing data, writing code and generating documents and presentations. It edits images from a spoken instruction and generates images and video, and takes voice input and photographs as well as text.

chunks.title: Doubao
chunks.text: Doubao (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under UI & API: A work-task mode runs multi-step jobs and scheduled tasks.

chunks.title: Doubao Seed
chunks.text: Doubao Seed (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: ByteDance's closed-weight Seed model line, served through the Doubao consumer app and the Volcano Engine API. Seed 2.0, released on 14 February 2026, shipped Pro, Lite and Mini general-purpose agent models plus a dedicated Code model.

chunks.title: Doubao Seed
chunks.text: Doubao Seed (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: The Seed2.1 family that followed, in Pro and Turbo, is the current release and is aimed at general agents and code engineering.

chunks.title: DROID
chunks.text: DROID (by DROID Dataset Team), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: DROID (Distributed Robot Interaction Dataset) is a large in-the-wild robot manipulation dataset recorded by 50 collectors in North America, Asia and Europe on copies of one Franka-based robot platform: about 76k trajectories and 350 hours across 564 scenes and 86 tasks.

chunks.title: DROID
chunks.text: DROID (by DROID Dataset Team), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: It is distributed through TensorFlow Datasets and Cloud Storage, with a LeRobot-format copy on the Hugging Face Hub.

chunks.title: Dryad
chunks.text: Dryad (by Dryad), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: Dryad is a non-profit repository for research data from all fields, where every submitted dataset is checked by Dryad's curators before it is published. Published datasets carry DataCite metadata and a DOI, keep their versions, and can be listed and downloaded through a REST API.

chunks.title: Dryad
chunks.text: Dryad (by Dryad), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: Publishing carries a charge unless an institution, journal or funder sponsors it, and downloads are free.

chunks.title: ds4
chunks.text: ds4 (by antirez (Salvatore Sanfilippo)), catalog entry under Inference code: ds4 (DwarfStar 4) is a native local LLM inference engine by antirez (Salvatore Sanfilippo), optimized first for DeepSeek V4 Flash and deliberately narrow rather than a general GGUF runner. It also runs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM 5.x and Qwen3.8 Flash Next.

chunks.title: ds4
chunks.text: ds4 (by antirez (Salvatore Sanfilippo)), catalog entry under Inference code: The C/CUDA/Objective-C engine draws on llama.cpp/GGML kernels and quantization formats, adding model loading, prompt rendering, tool calling, and KV state streaming to RAM and SSD. It ships an HTTP server with OpenAI-style and Anthropic-style endpoints and a coding agent.

chunks.title: DSPy
chunks.text: DSPy (by Stanford NLP), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Stanford framework for programming rather than prompting language models. Typed declarative modules - signatures with Predict, ChainOfThought and ReAct - compose into pipelines, which optimizers such as MIPROv2, BootstrapFewShot and GEPA then auto-tune against a metric, adjusting prompts or weights.

chunks.title: dstack
chunks.text: dstack (by dstack), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Control plane for GPU provisioning and orchestration across any GPU cloud, Kubernetes cluster or on-premise fleet.

chunks.title: dstack
chunks.text: dstack (by dstack), catalog entry under ML orchestration: A run declares the resources it needs - including NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU or Tenstorrent accelerators - and dstack provisions a fleet to satisfy it, places development environments, training tasks and inference services onto it, and tears it down after.

chunks.title: Duck.ai
chunks.text: Duck.ai (by DuckDuckGo), catalog entry under UI & API: DuckDuckGo's anonymous AI chat surface, on the web and inside the DuckDuckGo browser, letting users chat with third-party models without an account. It strips personal metadata including the IP address before prompting a provider, and conversations are not used for training. The proxy sits in front of model APIs DuckDuckGo does not operate.

chunks.title: duplodocus
chunks.text: duplodocus (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Rust deduplication tool for large text corpora: exact and fuzzy MinHash-LSH dedup. The dedup stage of the Dolma 3 pipeline.

chunks.title: DVC
chunks.text: DVC (by Treeverse), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: DVC (Data Version Control) versions datasets and models by keeping their contents in external storage and their version metadata in Git, so a repository records which data produced which result. It also defines pipelines as a dependency graph and tracks experiment runs and metrics against them.

chunks.title: DVC
chunks.text: DVC (by Treeverse), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: A command-line tool and a VS Code extension are the two interfaces.

chunks.title: NVIDIA Dynamo
chunks.text: NVIDIA Dynamo (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Inference code: Dynamo is NVIDIA's datacenter-scale inference serving stack, the orchestration layer that turns clusters running vLLM, SGLang or TensorRT-LLM into one coordinated system.

chunks.title: NVIDIA Dynamo
chunks.text: NVIDIA Dynamo (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Inference code: It disaggregates prefill and decode into independently scalable pools, routes requests by KV cache overlap, offloads KV blocks across GPU, CPU, SSD and remote storage, and autoscales against latency SLAs. It is built in Rust and Python and deploys on Kubernetes.

chunks.title: Dynatrace AI Observability
chunks.text: Dynatrace AI Observability (by Dynatrace), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Enterprise AI observability integrated into the Dynatrace platform. Monitors LLM-powered applications with automatic distributed tracing, token tracking, cost analysis, and anomaly detection. Leverages Dynatrace's Davis AI engine for automated root cause analysis of LLM application issues.

chunks.title: Dynatrace AI Observability
chunks.text: Dynatrace AI Observability (by Dynatrace), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Targets large enterprises with existing Dynatrace deployments.

chunks.title: E2B Sandbox
chunks.text: E2B Sandbox (by E2B), catalog entry under Deployment: E2B hands an AI agent an ephemeral Linux sandbox, each one a Firecracker microVM, created and driven through a Python or TypeScript SDK. Sandboxes accept custom templates, expose configurable CPU and RAM, and can stay alive for up to 24 hours. The SDKs and the infrastructure running the hosted cloud are both published, so the same stack can be self-hosted.

chunks.title: E5
chunks.text: E5 (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: E5 embeds queries and passages for retrieval, trained by contrastive pre-training on weakly supervised text pairs and then on labelled retrieval data.

chunks.title: E5
chunks.text: E5 (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The multilingual checkpoints initialize from XLM-RoBERTa and cover 100 languages at a 512-token limit, while e5-mistral-7b-instruct is a decoder-based, instruction-conditioned variant with a longer context. Every input carries an explicit "query:" or "passage:" prefix. A Microsoft Research team publishes the weights under the intfloat account.

chunks.title: Elasticsearch
chunks.text: Elasticsearch (by Elastic), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Elasticsearch is a distributed search and analytics engine that indexes documents for full-text retrieval and stores dense vectors for approximate nearest neighbor and hybrid search.

chunks.title: Elasticsearch
chunks.text: Elasticsearch (by Elastic), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: It underpins retrieval-augmented generation alongside its older logging, metrics and security-analytics uses, and runs as a clustered data store with sharding and replication.

chunks.title: ElevenLabs TTS
chunks.text: ElevenLabs TTS (by ElevenLabs), catalog entry under Speech & audio: ElevenLabs' hosted text-to-speech models, from Eleven v3 and v3 Conversational (70+ languages, audio tags for emotional control) to the low-latency Flash v2.5, sold through its API and creator apps.

chunks.title: EmbeddingGemma
chunks.text: EmbeddingGemma (by Google), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: EmbeddingGemma is Google's 308M-parameter multilingual text embedding model, built on Gemma 3 and aimed at running on phones, laptops and tablets rather than in a datacenter.

chunks.title: EmbeddingGemma
chunks.text: EmbeddingGemma (by Google), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: It takes up to 2K tokens of context and emits 768-dimension vectors, truncatable to 512, 256 or 128 via Matryoshka Representation Learning, and is distributed alongside a quantization-aware-trained checkpoint for low-memory deployment. The weights are downloadable but gated behind acceptance of the Gemma Terms of Use.

chunks.title: Epoch AI Benchmarks
chunks.text: Epoch AI Benchmarks (by Epoch AI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Independent benchmarking lab that runs and maintains leaderboards for hard evaluations, including SWE-bench Verified, GPQA Diamond and MATH Level 5, and operates its own FrontierMath benchmark across four difficulty tiers. Its public dashboard scores frontier models on all of them.

chunks.title: ERNIE 5.1
chunks.text: ERNIE 5.1 (by Baidu), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: ERNIE 5.1 is Baidu's fifth-generation flagship model, released in May 2026, a mixture-of-experts design with elastic depth, width and sparsity, aimed at text generation, reasoning, agentic tool use and creative writing.

chunks.title: ERNIE 5.1
chunks.text: ERNIE 5.1 (by Baidu), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Baidu positions it on cost efficiency, with roughly a third of the total parameters and half the active parameters of the previous generation.

chunks.title: ESM-2
chunks.text: ESM-2 (by Meta), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: ESM-2 is Meta's masked-language model family for protein sequences. The family spans several parameter sizes and produces representations that can be fine-tuned for protein prediction tasks; the Hugging Face release includes downloadable PyTorch, TensorFlow, and safetensors checkpoints and points to task-specific fine-tuning notebooks.

chunks.title: ESM-3
chunks.text: ESM-3 (by EvolutionaryScale), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: ESM-3 is a generative masked language model that reasons jointly over protein sequence, structure and function, each represented as a track of discrete tokens at both input and output. Prompted with partial inputs on any combination of tracks, it iteratively unmasks positions to design or complete a protein.

chunks.title: ESM-3
chunks.text: ESM-3 (by EvolutionaryScale), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: The 1.4B esm3-sm-open-v1 checkpoint is the downloadable tier; the 7B and 98B models are served through the hosted platform API.

chunks.title: EuroEval
chunks.text: EuroEval (by EuroEval), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Benchmarking framework for language models across 30+ European languages, maintained at the Alexandra Institute and formerly known as ScandEval. It evaluates encoders, decoders and instruction-tuned models alike and publishes per-language leaderboards at euroeval.com.

chunks.title: EuroLLM
chunks.text: EuroLLM (by EuroLLM), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: EuroLLM is an open-weights multilingual LLM family from a European consortium led by Unbabel and DeepSPIN at Instituto Superior Técnico, under the UTTER Horizon Europe project.

chunks.title: EuroLLM
chunks.text: EuroLLM (by EuroLLM), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: The 22B flagship, plus 9B and 1.7B siblings, is trained from scratch on ~4 trillion tokens across the EU's 24 official languages plus 11 more, on the MareNostrum5 supercomputer under a EuroHPC grant.

chunks.title: EuroLLM
chunks.text: EuroLLM (by EuroLLM), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Released under Apache-2.0 with base and instruct variants, per-phase Megatron-Core checkpoints, the EuroWeb and EuroBlocks datasets, and an eval harness; the full pretraining corpus and training recipe are not released.

chunks.title: EvalPlus
chunks.text: EvalPlus (by EvalPlus Team (UIUC)), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Extensions of HumanEval and MBPP that add roughly 80 times and 35 times more test cases through automated mutation, exposing models that pass weak tests while emitting buggy code. Published at NeurIPS 2023, with an EvalPerf companion for efficiency, and integrated with the bigcode evaluation harness.

chunks.title: EvalScope
chunks.text: EvalScope (by ModelScope (Alibaba)), catalog entry under Evaluation code: One-stop evaluation framework from the ModelScope community that runs LLM, VLM, embedding and AIGC benchmarks and inference stress tests from a single CLI. It drives OpenCompass and VLMEvalKit as pluggable backends and adds the performance benchmarking side that plain accuracy harnesses leave out.

chunks.title: Evidently
chunks.text: Evidently (by Evidently AI), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Open-source framework to evaluate, test and monitor ML and LLM-powered systems, over both tabular and text data. Reports and Test Suites compute and gate on more than 100 built-in metrics, from data drift detection to LLM-as-judge scoring, and a Monitoring UI service visualizes those metrics and test results over time.

chunks.title: Evidently
chunks.text: Evidently (by Evidently AI), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: The full monitoring dashboard is self-hostable; Evidently Cloud is a separate hosted product adding dataset and user management, alerting and no-code evals on top of the same open core.

chunks.title: Evo 2
chunks.text: Evo 2 (by Arc Institute), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Evo 2 is Arc Institute's autoregressive DNA language-model family for genome modeling and sequence design. It works at single-nucleotide resolution with contexts up to one million base pairs, spans multiple model sizes, and provides local inference, sequence generation, embeddings, and documented training and fine-tuning paths.

chunks.title: Exa Search API
chunks.text: Exa Search API (by Exa), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Exa Search API is a hosted neural search service, formerly known as Metaphor, that matches queries on meaning rather than keywords and ranks results by semantic similarity. A single search request can return links along with page text, highlights or a schema-shaped summary for each result.

chunks.title: Exa Search API
chunks.text: Exa Search API (by Exa), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Exa is offered as a semantic alternative to keyword-based search APIs.

chunks.title: ExecuTorch
chunks.text: ExecuTorch (by PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Inference code: ExecuTorch is PyTorch's stack for running models on device, from phones, laptops and browsers down to microcontrollers.

chunks.title: ExecuTorch
chunks.text: ExecuTorch (by PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Inference code: Models captured with torch.export are lowered to a .pte file for each target and run by a C++ runtime that links only the operators a deployment needs, with backends from Apple, Arm, Qualcomm, MediaTek, Samsung, Intel, NVIDIA and others.

chunks.title: EZKL
chunks.text: EZKL (by Zkonduit), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: EZKL turns a neural network exported to ONNX into a zero-knowledge circuit and proves that an inference was run on that model, without revealing the inputs or weights the prover chooses to keep private. Proofs use the Halo2 proof system and verify in a browser, on a device or on-chain in the Ethereum Virtual Machine.

chunks.title: EZKL
chunks.text: EZKL (by Zkonduit), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: Zkonduit maintains it as a Rust library with Python bindings, and publishes a JavaScript engine package on npm.

chunks.title: F5-TTS
chunks.text: F5-TTS (by SWivid), catalog entry under Speech & audio: A flow-matching diffusion-transformer text-to-speech model for zero-shot voice cloning in English and Chinese, released with its training and fine-tuning code. The project is led by SJTU X-LANCE researchers under the SWivid account.

chunks.title: Faiss
chunks.text: Faiss (by Meta), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Faiss is a library for similarity search and clustering of dense vectors, carrying the widest set of index structures in common use - flat, IVF, product quantization, HNSW and their composites - with GPU implementations of the most useful ones. It is written in C++ with Python bindings and includes evaluation and parameter-tuning code.

chunks.title: Faiss
chunks.text: Faiss (by Meta), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Meta's Fundamental AI Research group develops it, and other vector stores build on it.

chunks.title: Falcon 3
chunks.text: Falcon 3 (by Technology Innovation Institute), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: TII's open-weights model line from Abu Dhabi. The Falcon 3 family spans 1B to 10B and was trained on 14 trillion tokens of web, code and STEM data.

chunks.title: Falcon 3
chunks.text: Falcon 3 (by Technology Innovation Institute), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: It has since been extended by Falcon-H1, a hybrid Mamba-transformer architecture from 0.5B to 34B with native support for eighteen languages, and by an Arabic-specialized Falcon-H1 line at 3B, 7B and 34B.

chunks.title: Fara
chunks.text: Fara (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Fara is Microsoft's family of computer-use agent models, which look at webpages and act by scrolling, typing and clicking at predicted coordinates without accessibility trees. Fara1.5 comes in 4B, 9B and 27B sizes built on Qwen3.5 and trained on data from the FaraGen1.5 pipeline, and can pause to ask the user before irreversible actions.

chunks.title: Fara
chunks.text: Fara (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Fara-7B was the first release.

chunks.title: fastai
chunks.text: fastai (by fast.ai), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: High-level deep-learning library on PyTorch from fast.ai, built for training strong models in a few lines.

chunks.title: fastai
chunks.text: fastai (by fast.ai), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Its Learner API covers image classification and segmentation, text, tabular data and recommendation, with transfer learning from pretrained torchvision and timm backbones, a learning-rate finder, one-cycle training and callbacks, and it underpins fast.ai's free deep-learning course.

chunks.title: FastAPI-MCP
chunks.text: FastAPI-MCP (by Tadata), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: Turns an existing FastAPI application into an MCP server: every endpoint becomes an MCP tool, keeping the request and response schemas and the endpoint documentation, and reusing the app's own FastAPI dependencies for authentication.

chunks.title: FastDeploy
chunks.text: FastDeploy (by PaddlePaddle), catalog entry under Inference code: FastDeploy is an inference and deployment toolkit for large language models and vision language models built on PaddlePaddle, shipping out-of-the-box deployment paths for production serving.

chunks.title: faster-whisper
chunks.text: faster-whisper (by SYSTRAN), catalog entry under Speech & audio: A reimplementation of OpenAI's Whisper on the CTranslate2 inference engine, up to four times faster than the reference code at the same accuracy and using less memory, with 8-bit quantization on CPU and GPU, and batched inference.

chunks.title: FastMCP
chunks.text: FastMCP (by Prefect), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: High-level Python framework for building MCP servers and clients with minimal boilerplate. Provides decorator-based tool definitions, automatic schema generation, and built-in testing utilities. Organized around servers that expose tools, resources and prompts, apps that give those tools an interactive surface, and a client side. Maintained by Prefect.

chunks.title: FATE (Federated AI Technology Enabler)
