chunks.text: FATE (Federated AI Technology Enabler) (by FederatedAI (FATE)), catalog entry under Federated learning: Industrial federated learning framework hosted by the Linux Foundation.

chunks.title: FATE (Federated AI Technology Enabler)
chunks.text: FATE (Federated AI Technology Enabler) (by FederatedAI (FATE)), catalog entry under Federated learning: Parties deploy their own FATE clusters, from docker-compose or KubeFATE on Kubernetes, and exchange encrypted intermediate values through a routing layer, with secure-computation protocols built on homomorphic encryption and multi-party computation, for horizontal and vertical federated learning.

chunks.title: FATE (Federated AI Technology Enabler)
chunks.text: FATE (Federated AI Technology Enabler) (by FederatedAI (FATE)), catalog entry under Federated learning: FATE-Flow schedules the multi-party jobs.

chunks.title: Feast
chunks.text: Feast (by Feast project), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Feast is a feature store that keeps one definition of a feature and serves it from two places: an offline store for building training sets with point-in-time correctness, and an online store for low-latency retrieval at inference. Materialization moves values between them, and a registry holds the definitions.

chunks.title: Fed-BioMed
chunks.text: Fed-BioMed (by Inria), catalog entry under Federated learning: Collaborative learning framework for biomedical research from Inria and Université Côte d'Azur.

chunks.title: Fed-BioMed
chunks.text: Fed-BioMed (by Inria), catalog entry under Federated learning: Hospitals run Fed-BioMed nodes that hold and manage their datasets through a node GUI, and a researcher component sends PyTorch or scikit-learn training plans to them for federated learning or federated analytics, with Joye-Libert or low-overhead masking secure aggregation.

chunks.title: Federated Compute Platform
chunks.text: Federated Compute Platform (by Google), catalog entry under Federated learning: Google's libraries for running federated programs and computations in the cross-device setting.

chunks.title: Federated Compute Platform
chunks.text: Federated Compute Platform (by Google), catalog entry under Federated learning: The repository holds the client-side code and the service and data-format definitions that run in production in Google's federated learning infrastructure, and a client for confidential federated computations that verifies TEE-hosted server applications by remote attestation. The production server is not published.

chunks.title: FedJAX
chunks.text: FedJAX (by Google), catalog entry under Federated learning: JAX-based library for federated learning simulations, built for research ease of use, with federated datasets, models and algorithm implementations, and fast simulation on accelerators.

chunks.title: FedTree
chunks.text: FedTree (by Xtra-Computing), catalog entry under Federated learning: Federated learning system for gradient-boosted decision trees from Xtra Computing (MLSys 2023). It trains horizontal or vertical federated GBDTs as a standalone simulation or with separate distributed server and party binaries, on multi-core CPUs and GPUs, with homomorphic encryption, secure aggregation and differential privacy.

chunks.title: Feluda
chunks.text: Feluda (by Tattle), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Feluda is a configurable engine by Tattle for analyzing multilingual, multimodal content (images, text, video), built around a modular 'operators' plugin architecture. It supports vector embeddings, hash-based search, text extraction from images, and entity extraction.

chunks.title: Feluda
chunks.text: Feluda (by Tattle), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It was built for analyzing social-media content, particularly in Indian-language contexts.

chunks.title: Figshare
chunks.text: Figshare (by Digital Science), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: Figshare is a research repository where researchers deposit datasets alongside figures, papers, software and other outputs, each published with a DataCite DOI. Items keep numbered versions, and a REST API covers creating, uploading, publishing and fetching them.

chunks.title: Figshare
chunks.text: Figshare (by Digital Science), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: The public figshare.com repository is free for individual researchers, and Digital Science sells the same software to institutions and publishers as hosted repositories.

chunks.title: Filesystem MCP Server
chunks.text: Filesystem MCP Server (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: The official reference Filesystem MCP server (TypeScript) in the modelcontextprotocol/servers monorepo, providing secure file operations within configurable allowed directories - read/write/edit files, directory trees, search, media reads - with the MCP Roots protocol for dynamic access scoping.

chunks.title: Finch.jl
chunks.text: Finch.jl (by Finch.jl), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Finch.jl is a Julia-to-Julia compiler for sparse and structured multidimensional arrays. It lets users write high-level array programs that Finch transforms behind the scenes into fused, customized sparse kernels, generalizing sparse tensor compiler techniques to a wider range of array formats.

chunks.title: FineMath
chunks.text: FineMath (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: FineMath is a classifier-filtered mathematical web corpus extracted from Common Crawl by Hugging Face. It is released in two quality tiers, FineMath-3+ at 34 billion tokens and FineMath-4+ at 9.6 billion tokens, alongside a similarly filtered English portion of InfiMM-WebMath.

chunks.title: FineMath
chunks.text: FineMath (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: It is part of the SmolLM2 and SmolLM3 pretraining mixtures and one of the sources in the Dolma 3 pool behind Olmo 3.

chunks.title: FineWeb
chunks.text: FineWeb (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: FineWeb is an English pretraining dataset of more than 18.5 trillion tokens of cleaned and deduplicated text derived from Common Crawl snapshots dating back to 2013. It is distributed as Parquet in date-based subsets, and its processing pipeline was built with the datatrove library. Hugging Face's FineWeb team releases it.

chunks.title: FineWeb-2
chunks.text: FineWeb-2 (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Multilingual successor to FineWeb, covering more than a thousand languages and writing systems with over a trillion tokens of filtered and deduplicated Common Crawl text. Each language runs through its own pipeline with deduplication and quality filtering, extending the FineWeb work beyond English.

chunks.title: FineWeb-Edu
chunks.text: FineWeb-Edu (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Educational subset of FineWeb holding about 1.3 trillion tokens, produced by filtering FineWeb with an educational-quality classifier trained on Llama-3-70B annotations and keeping the text scored as highly educational. It targets knowledge- and reasoning-heavy evaluation relative to unfiltered web data.

chunks.title: Firecracker
chunks.text: Firecracker (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Deployment: Virtual machine monitor written in Rust that uses KVM to run workloads in lightweight microVMs, combining hardware-virtualization isolation with container-like startup and density.

chunks.title: Firecracker
chunks.text: Firecracker (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Deployment: It ships a deliberately minimal guest device model - network, block I/O, timer, KVM clock, serial console and a partial keyboard - to shrink the memory footprint and attack surface, and jails its own process with cgroups and seccomp BPF. AWS built it to run Lambda and Fargate.

chunks.title: Firecrawl
chunks.text: Firecrawl (by Mendable), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Firecrawl is a web scraping and crawling API built for LLM consumption, turning a URL into clean markdown or structured data while handling JavaScript rendering, pagination and anti-bot measures. It offers scrape, crawl, map, search, batch and agent-extract endpoints. Firecrawl can run as a self-hosted deployment or as a hosted service.

chunks.title: Fireworks Fine-Tuning
chunks.text: Fireworks Fine-Tuning (by Fireworks AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Fireworks Fine-Tuning runs managed supervised, DPO and ORPO preference, and reinforcement fine-tuning on open-weight models such as Llama, Mistral, Qwen and DeepSeek, producing LoRA adapters that can warm-start from a prior checkpoint.

chunks.title: Fireworks Fine-Tuning
chunks.text: Fireworks Fine-Tuning (by Fireworks AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: A Training API adds custom Python training loops on Fireworks-managed GPUs, with full-parameter training on dedicated capacity. Trained models are served only from Fireworks on-demand deployments, either merged into the base model or as multi-LoRA adapters sharing hardware.

chunks.title: Fireworks Inference
chunks.text: Fireworks Inference (by Fireworks AI), catalog entry under Inference code: Fireworks Inference runs open models on FireAttention, an in-house attention engine of custom CUDA and AMD-GPU kernels, combined with speculative decoding. It hosts many models and LoRA adapters concurrently, supports function calling, and offers both serverless per-token endpoints and dedicated GPU deployments.

chunks.title: Fireworks Inference
chunks.text: Fireworks Inference (by Fireworks AI), catalog entry under Inference code: Its vendor, Fireworks AI, was founded by former Meta PyTorch engineers, including CEO Lin Qiao.

chunks.title: FLAML
chunks.text: FLAML (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Microsoft's fast AutoML and hyperparameter-tuning library. Given training data and a task type, its AutoML class searches across learners such as LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, random forests, linear models and time-series models and their hyperparameters within a time budget, using cost-aware search methods, and can stack the results.

chunks.title: FLAML
chunks.text: FLAML (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Its tune module runs the same search over any user function.

chunks.title: FLAN Collection (v2)
chunks.text: FLAN Collection (v2) (by Google Research), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Google Research's instruction-tuning compilation drawing on P3, Super-NaturalInstructions and chain-of-thought data, which trained Flan-T5 and Flan-PaLM. It remains a building block for later instruction mixes, including the Tulu 3 SFT mixture and Olmo 3's Dolci.

chunks.title: FlashAttention
chunks.text: FlashAttention (by Dao AI Lab), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: FlashAttention is the reference implementation of IO-aware exact attention, computing attention without materializing the full attention matrix and so cutting memory traffic rather than approximating the result.

chunks.title: FlashAttention
chunks.text: FlashAttention (by Dao AI Lab), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: The repository carries FlashAttention and FlashAttention-2 alongside the papers describing them, with FlashAttention-3 Hopper kernels in a separate tree and FlashAttention-4, written in CuTeDSL, for Hopper and Blackwell.

chunks.title: Flash Sparse Attention
chunks.text: Flash Sparse Attention (by HKUST(GZ) Data Intelligence and Analytics Lab (DIAL)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Flash-Sparse-Attention is a trainable sparse attention kernel library from HKUST(GZ)'s Data Intelligence and Analytics Lab, combining Flash Attention's memory efficiency with sparse and gated attention for long-sequence Transformer training and inference

chunks.title: Flash Sparse Attention
chunks.text: Flash Sparse Attention (by HKUST(GZ) Data Intelligence and Analytics Lab (DIAL)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: including grouped-query attention, paged attention and fused-quant low-precision computation.

chunks.title: FlashInfer
chunks.text: FlashInfer (by FlashInfer project), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: FlashInfer is a kernel library and generator for LLM inference, exposing unified APIs for attention, GEMM and mixture-of-experts operations over several backend implementations including FlashAttention-2 and -3, cuDNN, CUTLASS and TensorRT-LLM. Kernels are compiled just in time for the shapes a workload actually uses.

chunks.title: FlashKDA
chunks.text: FlashKDA (by Moonshot AI), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: FlashKDA provides high-performance Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) kernels built on CUTLASS, powering Moonshot AI's Kimi model line. It is auto-dispatched as a backend from the flash-linear-attention library's chunk_kda operator.

chunks.title: FlashMLA
chunks.text: FlashMLA (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: FlashMLA is DeepSeek's library of optimized attention kernels for serving its own models on NVIDIA GPUs and Huawei Ascend NPUs.

chunks.title: FlashMLA
chunks.text: FlashMLA (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: It carries sparse (DeepSeek Sparse Attention) prefill and decoding kernels over FP8 or FP4 KV caches, dense multi-head attention kernels for the forward and backward passes, and a fused kernel for the small operations around attention. Support for Hopper GPUs and earlier DeepSeek models was dropped from the main line.

chunks.title: FlashQLA
chunks.text: FlashQLA (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: FlashQLA is a linear attention kernel library from the Qwen team, built on TileLang, applying operator fusion to the forward and backward passes of Gated DeltaNet (GDN) chunked prefill. It serves as a backend for the flash-linear-attention library's GDN operators through the standard FLA API.

chunks.title: Flax
chunks.text: Flax (by Google), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Flax is a neural network library and ecosystem for JAX designed for flexibility, providing network components such as Linear, Conv, BatchNorm and attention alongside training utilities like checkpointing and serialization. It is developed and maintained by Google DeepMind.

chunks.title: Flax
chunks.text: Flax (by Google), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Its newer Flax NNX API emphasizes Python reference semantics, so networks are built from ordinary Python objects.

chunks.title: FLEURS
chunks.text: FLEURS (by Google), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech benchmark in 102 languages, made by recording people reading the FLORES sentences aloud. Each language has roughly ten hours of training speech plus separate development and test speakers, and it supports speech recognition, spoken language identification, speech translation and retrieval.

chunks.title: FLEURS
chunks.text: FLEURS (by Google), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Google built it as the speech counterpart of FLORES.

chunks.title: Florence-2
chunks.text: Florence-2 (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Florence-2 is Microsoft's prompt-based vision foundation model, in 0.23B and 0.77B sizes, that performs captioning, object detection, phrase grounding, dense region captioning and OCR from short task tokens. It was trained on FLD-5B, a set of 5.4 billion annotations over 126 million images, and fine-tuned variants cover downstream tasks.

chunks.title: FLORES+
chunks.text: FLORES+ (by Open Language Data Initiative), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: FLORES+ is a multilingual machine translation benchmark of sentences sampled from Wikinews, Wikijunior and Wikivoyage and translated from English into more than 200 language varieties, with dev and devtest splits aligned across every language. It continues Meta's FLORES-200, and a separate blind test set stays with Meta.

chunks.title: FLORES+
chunks.text: FLORES+ (by Open Language Data Initiative), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Open Language Data Initiative maintains it and accepts community fixes and new languages.

chunks.title: Flower
chunks.text: Flower (by Flower Labs), catalog entry under Federated learning: Federated learning framework from Flower Labs. The same app runs in its simulation engine or on its deployment runtime, where a SuperLink coordinates SuperNodes that each organization runs next to its own data over TLS with node authentication.

chunks.title: Flower
chunks.text: Flower (by Flower Labs), catalog entry under Federated learning: It ships SecAgg and SecAgg+ secure aggregation and differential privacy, and works with PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, MLX and Hugging Face.

chunks.title: FLUX
chunks.text: FLUX (by Black Forest Labs), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: FLUX is Black Forest Labs' family of rectified-flow transformer models for text-to-image generation and image editing. The open-weight releases span FLUX.1 [dev] and [schnell] with their Kontext, Krea, Fill, Redux, Depth and Canny variants, the 32B FLUX.2 [dev], and the smaller FLUX.2 [klein] models that run on consumer GPUs.

chunks.title: FLUX
chunks.text: FLUX (by Black Forest Labs), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: The strongest tiers, FLUX.2 [pro], [flex] and [max], are served only through the vendor's API.

chunks.title: Fly Sprites
chunks.text: Fly Sprites (by Fly.io), catalog entry under Deployment: Gives an AI agent its own persistent Linux computer rather than an ephemeral sandbox. Each Sprite is a Firecracker microVM with its own kernel and a 100 GB POSIX volume that survives sleep and moves between host machines, plus live copy-on-write checkpoints an agent can roll back to.

chunks.title: Fly Sprites
chunks.text: Fly Sprites (by Fly.io), catalog entry under Deployment: Fly.io operates it as a managed service with CLI, REST and language SDK clients and an outbound API gateway.

chunks.title: Flyte
chunks.text: Flyte (by Union.ai), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Kubernetes-native orchestrator for machine-learning and data workflows, written as typed Python tasks. Flyte's control plane, Propeller, walks the workflow graph and emits one pod per task against the resources that task declared, caching results and passing typed artifacts between steps.

chunks.title: Flyte
chunks.text: Flyte (by Union.ai), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Plugin task types cover PyTorch, Spark, Ray and Dask training jobs alongside plain containers.

chunks.title: FreeTensor
chunks.text: FreeTensor (by Shizhi Tang (roastduck)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: FreeTensor is a compiler and embedded Python DSL for writing and optimizing loop-based tensor programs, supporting dynamic tensor shapes, OpenMP and CUDA parallelization, explicit loop and memory-layout transformations, and reverse-mode automatic differentiation, compiling down to native code.

chunks.title: GAIA (General AI Assistants)
chunks.text: GAIA (General AI Assistants) (by Meta), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: GAIA is a benchmark for general AI assistants: 466 real-world questions across three difficulty levels that require reasoning, multimodality, web browsing and tool use. Answers to 300 of them are withheld to power a submission-scored leaderboard, leaving a fully public development split.

chunks.title: Galileo
chunks.text: Galileo (by Galileo), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Galileo, now called Splunk Agent Observability, is an AI observability and reliability platform that combines offline evaluation, online production guardrails and tracing.

chunks.title: Galileo
chunks.text: Galileo (by Galileo), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Its Luna-2 small judge models detect hallucinations, tool errors and policy violations, and the vendor says customized evaluations can monitor all production traffic at a fraction of the cost of a large judge model. It deploys as SaaS, into a customer VPC, or on-premises.

chunks.title: garak
chunks.text: garak (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: garak is an LLM vulnerability scanner maintained by NVIDIA. It probes models for hallucination, data leakage, prompt injection, misinformation, toxicity generation and jailbreaks across many providers including Hugging Face, OpenAI and Bedrock, run from the command line against whichever endpoint it is pointed at.

chunks.title: Gemini
chunks.text: Gemini (by Google), catalog entry under UI & API: Google's consumer Gemini chat app on the web, Android and iOS, and embedded across Google Workspace. It offers a live voice mode, Deep Research, and image and video generation, and is integrated with Search's AI Mode.

chunks.title: Gemini CLI
chunks.text: Gemini CLI (by Google), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Gemini CLI is Google's open-source terminal coding agent, bringing Gemini models into the shell for coding, debugging and task automation. It ships built-in tools for Google Search grounding, file operations, shell commands and web fetch, and extends through MCP and GEMINI.md system-prompt files.

chunks.title: Gemini CLI
chunks.text: Gemini CLI (by Google), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Since June 2026 it serves paid Gemini API keys and Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise organizations, while free individual users and Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers moved to its Antigravity CLI.

chunks.title: Gemini Embedding
chunks.text: Gemini Embedding (by Google), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Google’s embedding line on the Gemini API and Vertex AI.

chunks.title: Gemini Embedding
chunks.text: Gemini Embedding (by Google), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The head model is gemini-embedding-2, Google’s first natively multimodal embedder, which maps text, images, video, audio and PDFs into one space; gemini-embedding-001, the text-only predecessor with 100-plus languages, Matryoshka dimensions down from 3,072 and a 2,048-token input, remains available.

chunks.title: Gemini Flash
chunks.text: Gemini Flash (by Google), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Gemini Flash is Google's Flash-tier Gemini line: thinking and agentic instruct models with configurable thinking budgets that trade reasoning depth for latency, available through the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search, Antigravity, the Gemini API and enterprise products.

chunks.title: Gemini Flash
chunks.text: Gemini Flash (by Google), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Gemini 3.5 Flash opened the 3.5 generation in May 2026 and is now labeled legacy; Gemini 3.8 Flash, which Google calls its most intelligent Flash model, is the current release.

chunks.title: Gemini Pro
chunks.text: Gemini Pro (by Google), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Gemini Pro is Google DeepMind's higher-capability Gemini tier, the counterpart to Gemini Flash, taking text, image, video, audio and PDF input with a 1M-token input window and a thinking mode. The name is applied to whichever generation currently ships rather than to one fixed release.

chunks.title: Gemini Pro
chunks.text: Gemini Pro (by Google), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Weights are closed, and the tier is offered through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio and the Gemini app.

chunks.title: Gemini Robotics
chunks.text: Gemini Robotics (by Google), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Gemini Robotics is Google DeepMind's family of closed robot foundation models: Gemini Robotics 2, a vision-language-action model that turns vision and language into motor control; Gemini Robotics ER 2, an embodied-reasoning model for spatial planning offered through the Gemini API; and On-Device 2

chunks.title: Gemini Robotics
chunks.text: Gemini Robotics (by Google), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: a lightweight version that runs locally on the robot.

chunks.title: Gemma 4
chunks.text: Gemma 4 (by Google), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Gemma 4 is Google DeepMind's open-weight model family, built from the same research as Gemini 3. It spans E2B and E4B edge models, an encoder-free 12B unified model, a 26B-A4B mixture-of-experts model and a 31B dense model, all taking text and image input, with audio on the three smallest.

chunks.title: Gemma 4
chunks.text: Gemma 4 (by Google), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Context windows reach 256K tokens, and the models support more than 140 languages.

chunks.title: Geneformer
chunks.text: Geneformer (by Theodoris Lab), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Geneformer is the Theodoris lab's transformer model pretrained on human single-cell transcriptomes to make context-aware predictions in network biology.

chunks.title: Geneformer
chunks.text: Geneformer (by Theodoris Lab), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: It ships 10M, 104M, and 316M-parameter checkpoints plus a cancer-tuned variant, and the same repository carries the tokenizer, the DeepSpeed pretraining example, fine-tuning notebooks, embedding extraction, and in silico perturbation code.

chunks.title: Genesis
chunks.text: Genesis (by Genesis Embodied AI), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Genesis is a simulation platform for robotics and embodied AI that combines a multi-physics engine (rigid bodies, cloth, fluids, coupled solvers), its own photorealistic renderer Nyx alongside a ray tracer, and the Quadrants compiler, which lowers Python kernels to CUDA, ROCm, Metal, Vulkan and CPU.

chunks.title: Genesis
chunks.text: Genesis (by Genesis Embodied AI), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: It runs many heterogeneous environments in parallel and is developed by Genesis-Embodied-AI.

chunks.title: Gensim
chunks.text: Gensim (by RaRe Technologies), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Python library for topic modeling, document indexing and similarity retrieval over large text corpora, streaming data so memory use does not grow with corpus size.

chunks.title: Gensim
chunks.text: Gensim (by RaRe Technologies), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: It implements LDA, LSI, HDP and NMF topic models, word2vec, doc2vec and fastText embeddings, and similarity search, with a downloader for pretrained word vectors such as GloVe and fastText. It is in stable maintenance mode.

chunks.title: GGML
chunks.text: GGML (by ggml-org (Georgi Gerganov)), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: GGML is a low-level C tensor library for machine learning with no third-party dependencies, zero runtime memory allocations, integer quantization support, automatic differentiation, and optimizers. It runs cross-platform and is the tensor backend behind llama.cpp and whisper.cpp.

chunks.title: GGML
chunks.text: GGML (by ggml-org (Georgi Gerganov)), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It is maintained by ggml.ai, the company founded by Georgi Gerganov and now part of Hugging Face; much active development now occurs in the dependent llama.cpp and whisper.cpp repos.

chunks.title: Giskard
chunks.text: Giskard (by Giskard), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Giskard is a Python library from Giskard AI for testing and red-teaming LLM and agentic systems, rewritten for dynamic, multi-turn testing of agents. Its vulnerability scan automatically probes an application for prompt injection, harmful output and hallucination, and Giskard Checks runs scenario-based evaluations, including multi-turn agent validation.

chunks.title: Giskard
chunks.text: Giskard (by Giskard), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: The scan ships in the giskard-scan package alongside knowledge-base and RAG evaluation.

chunks.title: GitHub Copilot
chunks.text: GitHub Copilot (by GitHub (Microsoft)), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: GitHub Copilot's agent mode, which takes an assigned task and runs it as autonomous background work, planning, exploring the repository and executing changes. It orchestrates the first-party Copilot agent alongside Anthropic and OpenAI agents, and is built natively into GitHub across VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains and Neovim.

chunks.title: GitHub Copilot (IDE)
chunks.text: GitHub Copilot (IDE) (by GitHub (Microsoft)), catalog entry under UI & API: AI pair-programmer built into VS Code, JetBrains, Neovim and Visual Studio, offering inline completion, chat, agent mode and code review against OpenAI, Anthropic and Google model backends. It is distributed through GitHub with enterprise administration, and now also fronts a desktop app, a CLI and third-party agents reached over MCP.

chunks.title: GitHub MCP Server
chunks.text: GitHub MCP Server (by GitHub (Microsoft)), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: GitHub's official MCP server (Go) that lets AI agents interact with the GitHub platform in natural language, exposing 20+ toolsets - Repositories, Issues, Pull Requests, Actions, Code Security, Dependabot, Discussions, Projects, Copilot, and more. Runs locally via Docker/binary or via GitHub's remote hosted endpoint.

chunks.title: Glean Assistant
chunks.text: Glean Assistant (by Glean), catalog entry under UI & API: Glean Assistant is an enterprise AI assistant that answers questions, drafts documents and slide decks, and carries out multi-step work grounded in company data. It retrieves across a large set of enterprise connectors while enforcing each user's source-system permissions, and its Model Hub routes requests across open and proprietary LLMs.

chunks.title: Glean Assistant
chunks.text: Glean Assistant (by Glean), catalog entry under UI & API: Sub-agents, skills and actions automate work across connected systems. Glean sells it as a hosted service.

chunks.title: Glean Workplace Search AI
chunks.text: Glean Workplace Search AI (by Glean), catalog entry under UI & API: Glean Workplace Search AI is enterprise search that returns permissions-aware results and generative answers across a company's connected tools. An Enterprise Graph maps relationships across company content, and a large connector library brings in data from workplace applications. The search layer also powers Glean Assistant.

chunks.title: GLM-5.3
chunks.text: GLM-5.3 (by Z.ai), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Z.ai's flagship open-weights frontier model family, built for long-horizon agentic and coding tasks. GLM-5.3, the current release, is a post-trained update of the GLM-5.2 base: a sparse MoE of about 744B total parameters (40B active) with a 1M-token context, using the 'IndexShare' sparse attention introduced in GLM-5.2.

chunks.title: GLM-5.3
chunks.text: GLM-5.3 (by Z.ai), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: A smaller GLM-5.3-Flash ships beside it on a newly trained base with hybrid sparse and linear attention.

chunks.title: GLM-V
chunks.text: GLM-V (by Z.ai), catalog entry under Multimodal models: GLM-V is Z.ai's vision-language reasoning line, from GLM-4.1V-Thinking through GLM-4.5V to GLM-4.6V and the 9B GLM-4.6V-Flash, trained with reinforcement learning on curriculum-sampled tasks.

chunks.title: GLM-V
chunks.text: GLM-V (by Z.ai), catalog entry under Multimodal models: The models read long documents and video, ground objects with boxes, operate phone, desktop and web interfaces, and GLM-4.6V adds native function calling over images in a 128K context. The line is separate from Z.ai's GLM text models.

chunks.title: Glot500-c
chunks.text: Glot500-c (by CIS, LMU Munich), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Glot500-c is a multilingual pretraining text corpus covering 511 mostly low-resource languages, assembled from more than 150 existing monolingual and parallel datasets plus crawls of multilingual websites. The public release leaves out sources that cannot be redistributed, and each sentence records its source dataset.

chunks.title: Glot500-c
chunks.text: Glot500-c (by CIS, LMU Munich), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: LMU Munich's Center for Information and Language Processing built it to train the Glot500-m model.

chunks.title: GluonTS
chunks.text: GluonTS (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Probabilistic time-series forecasting library from AWS, focused on deep-learning models in PyTorch with older MXNet implementations. It ships estimators such as DeepAR, Temporal Fusion Transformer, PatchTST, TiDE, N-BEATS, WaveNet and DeepVAR, plus tree-based and statistical wrappers, along with dataset loaders and evaluation tools.

chunks.title: GluonTS
chunks.text: GluonTS (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: AWS's pretrained Chronos forecasters live in a separate repository.

chunks.title: GNoME
chunks.text: GNoME (by Google), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: GNoME is Google DeepMind's Graph Networks for Materials Exploration effort for inorganic-crystal discovery, released as a database of more than 520,000 materials within 1 meV per atom of the convex hull, alongside model definitions for the GNoME and NequIP architectures and Colab notebooks for exploring the data.

chunks.title: GNoME
chunks.text: GNoME (by Google), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: The repository publishes architectures and discovered structures rather than trained weights.

chunks.title: Google Cloud Run
chunks.text: Google Cloud Run (by Google), catalog entry under Deployment: Runs any OCI container image as a fully managed Google Cloud service, autoscaling from zero and billing either per request or for full instance time. Google offers individual Cloud Run instances for long-running background agents in preview, and a sandbox mode, also in preview, lets a service run untrusted or generated code in an isolated environment.

chunks.title: Google Cloud Run
chunks.text: Google Cloud Run (by Google), catalog entry under Deployment: Isolation comes from a choice of two execution environments, one built on gVisor and one on Linux microVMs.

chunks.title: Google Cloud TPU Inference
chunks.text: Google Cloud TPU Inference (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under Inference code: Google Cloud TPU Inference serves models on Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), spanning the v5e, v6e (Trillium), and Ironwood (TPU7x) generations. The Pathways distributed runtime integrates with the JetStream serving engine to partition models across multi-host TPU pods, with disaggregated serving for large language models.

chunks.title: Google Cloud TPU Inference
chunks.text: Google Cloud TPU Inference (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under Inference code: Google offers it as a managed service under AI Hypercomputer, deployed through GKE.

chunks.title: Google Cloud Vision API
chunks.text: Google Cloud Vision API (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Google Cloud's hosted image-analysis API, answering REST and RPC calls with Google's pretrained models for labels, object localization, OCR and dense document text, faces, landmarks, logos, image properties and SafeSearch ratings. It is billed per feature per image.

chunks.title: Google Cloud Vision API
chunks.text: Google Cloud Vision API (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Custom models are a separate Google Cloud product, AutoML Vision, rather than part of this API.

chunks.title: Google Coral Dev Board
chunks.text: Google Coral Dev Board (by Google), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Single-board computer from Google's Coral platform, pairing a removable system-on-module built on an NXP i.MX 8M with a baseboard carrying Google's Edge TPU. The Edge TPU delivers 4 TOPS at about 2 TOPS per watt for int8-quantized TensorFlow Lite models, running inference locally, and the module can be reused in a production design.

chunks.title: Google Dataset Search
chunks.text: Google Dataset Search (by Google), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: Google Dataset Search is a search engine for datasets hosted in thousands of repositories across the web. It indexes dataset pages whose publishers describe them with schema.org markup, and each result links back to the page where the data is kept. Repositories join by adding that markup to their own pages rather than by submitting files.

chunks.title: Google Cloud Document AI
chunks.text: Google Cloud Document AI (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Managed document-processing platform on Google Cloud built around processors - pretrained ones for forms, invoices, receipts and identity documents, and custom ones trained on a customer's own document types - that turn documents into structured entities rather than plain text.

chunks.title: Google Grounding API
chunks.text: Google Grounding API (by Google), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Grounding with Google Search is Google's managed capability for grounding Gemini model responses in real-time Google Search results, offered on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI). A companion option, Grounding with Agent Search, grounds responses in an organization's own website data or documents instead.

chunks.title: Google Grounding API
chunks.text: Google Grounding API (by Google), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: The capability is tightly integrated with the Gemini models and is the platform's search-augmented generation path.

chunks.title: Google Programmable Search
chunks.text: Google Programmable Search (by Google), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: JSON API that returns web and image search results from a Programmable Search Engine - a Google-hosted index scoped to sites the customer configures, or to the whole web. Results follow the OpenSearch 1.1 specification.

chunks.title: Goose
chunks.text: Goose (by Block), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Goose is a general-purpose on-machine AI agent, written in Rust and available as a desktop app, a CLI and an API. It connects to more than seventy extensions over the Model Context Protocol, works with over fifteen providers, and supports ACP so an existing model subscription can be used.

chunks.title: Goose
chunks.text: Goose (by Block), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Founded by Block, it is now stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation at the Linux Foundation.

chunks.title: GPQA
chunks.text: GPQA, catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Graduate-level Google-proof question answering: 448 expert-written multiple-choice questions across biology, physics and chemistry, written so that they resist quick web lookup. A 198-question Diamond subset carries the highest-agreement items and is the figure most frontier model reports cite.

chunks.title: GPT-4.1
chunks.text: GPT-4.1 (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: GPT-4.1 is an instruction-tuned language model that OpenAI released in April 2025 through its API only, aimed at coding and long-context work with a 1,047,576-token context window. OpenAI's main production line has since moved to newer GPT-5 series models, and it recommends GPT-4.1 as a lower-latency choice for tasks that do not need reasoning.

chunks.title: GPT-4o
chunks.text: GPT-4o (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: GPT-4o is OpenAI's 2024 multimodal model, taking text and image input with a 128K context window and an October 2023 knowledge cutoff. It remains a live model in OpenAI's API, without released weights, and is not deprecated there: only its first snapshot, from May 2024, is scheduled for removal, on October 23, 2026.

chunks.title: GPT-4o
chunks.text: GPT-4o (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: OpenAI withdrew GPT-4o from ChatGPT in February 2026.

chunks.title: GPT-5 line
chunks.text: GPT-5 line (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: GPT-5 is OpenAI's general-purpose model line, launched in August 2025 and continued through GPT-5.2, GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.5 (April 2026), with low-latency Instant variants and the coding-focused GPT-5.3-Codex. The models are served through the OpenAI API and ChatGPT. GPT-5.6 and the GPT-6 family have since followed.

chunks.title: GPT-6
chunks.text: GPT-6 (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: GPT-6 is OpenAI's flagship model family, released in September 2026 in three tiers: Astra, the most capable, for complex reasoning, coding and computer use; Sol, which balances capability and cost and has been updated as GPT-6.1 Sol; and Luna, for high-volume work. All three take text and image input with a context window of about one million tokens.

chunks.title: GPT-6
chunks.text: GPT-6 (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: They are served through OpenAI's API and ChatGPT, without downloadable weights.

chunks.title: GPT Image
chunks.text: GPT Image (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: GPT Image is OpenAI's line of image generation and editing models, served through the OpenAI API and inside ChatGPT. The models take text and image input, generate and edit images including inpainting and transparent backgrounds, and output custom sizes up to 4K, with quality settings that trade speed for detail.

chunks.title: gpt-oss
chunks.text: gpt-oss (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: OpenAI's open-weight reasoning models, released August 2025 in two sizes: gpt-oss-120b (117B parameters, 5.1B active) sized for a single 80GB GPU, and gpt-oss-20b (21B parameters, 3.6B active) for local and lower-latency use.

chunks.title: gpt-oss
chunks.text: gpt-oss (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Both are MoE models post-trained for reasoning, function calling and agentic tool use, with reasoning effort configurable at the prompt, and both require the harmony response format.

chunks.title: gpt-oss-safeguard
chunks.text: gpt-oss-safeguard (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: OpenAI's safety reasoning model, built on gpt-oss, with a policy-writing guide OpenAI prepared with ROOST. Rather than emitting a fixed label, it reasons over a safety policy supplied at call time and returns a reasoned decision, with low, medium or high reasoning effort. It ships in 20b and 120b sizes.

chunks.title: GPT Researcher
chunks.text: GPT Researcher (by Assaf Elovic), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Autonomous research agent that plans sub-queries, searches web and local sources, and synthesizes findings into a cited report. It is purpose-built for research rather than coding, orchestrating search, scraping and synthesis into one workflow, and ships a frontend and Docker deployment alongside the library.

chunks.title: GPT4All
chunks.text: GPT4All (by Nomic AI), catalog entry under UI & API: Cross-platform desktop app from Nomic AI for running LLMs locally on ordinary laptops, without an API key or a GPU. It bundles a chat interface, LocalDocs for retrieval over private files, an OpenAI-compatible local API server and a Python client, with Nomic Vulkan acceleration where a GPU is available.

chunks.title: GPT-QModel
chunks.text: GPT-QModel (by ModelCloud.ai), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: GPT-QModel is a quantization toolkit for large language models with hardware-accelerated kernels for NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Huawei Ascend NPUs, Intel XPUs and CPUs. Quantized checkpoints load through Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM and SGLang. It continues the GPTQ line of post-training quantization work.

chunks.title: Isaac GR00T
chunks.text: Isaac GR00T (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Isaac GR00T is NVIDIA's open foundation model line for generalist robots, from GR00T N1 to N1.7. Current releases are three-billion-parameter vision-language-action models pretrained across robot embodiments for humanoid and bimanual manipulation, published with the code to train them and a guide to fine-tuning one onto a new robot.

chunks.title: Gradio
chunks.text: Gradio (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Gradio is a Python package for quickly building web demos and applications around machine-learning models, APIs or arbitrary Python functions, without JavaScript, CSS or web-hosting knowledge. It provides the Interface, Blocks and ChatInterface classes plus built-in public sharing of demos.

chunks.title: Granite 4.0
chunks.text: Granite 4.0 (by IBM), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: IBM's enterprise foundation-model family, released October 2025 as hybrid Mamba-2/transformer models from micro (3B) through h-small (32B total, 9B active MoE).

chunks.title: Granite 4.0
chunks.text: Granite 4.0 (by IBM), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: The line targets efficient long-context inference on constrained hardware and enterprise agent workloads, and ships under Apache-2.0 with ISO 42001 certification and cryptographically signed checkpoints.

chunks.title: Granite Code Instruct
chunks.text: Granite Code Instruct (by IBM), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: IBM's enterprise code model line, fine-tuned from Granite Code Base for code instruction-following at 3B, 8B, 20B and 34B with 2K and 128K context variants. It was trained on permissively licensed code, math and natural-language instruction data, which is IBM's stated basis for offering enterprises clarity on training-data provenance.

chunks.title: Granite Embedding
chunks.text: Granite Embedding (by IBM), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Granite Embedding is IBM's retrieval model line for enterprise RAG, currently in its R2 generation. The R2 release ships two English bi-encoders on a ModernBERT backbone (47M and 149M parameters, 8192-token context), two multilingual bi-encoders (97M and 311M) and an English cross-encoder reranker.

chunks.title: Granite Embedding
chunks.text: Granite Embedding (by IBM), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: IBM's pitch is provenance as much as accuracy: the models are trained on permissively licensed open datasets plus IBM-collected data, and evaluated on enterprise-shaped retrieval - tables, long documents, conversational multi-turn and code - as well as BEIR and MTEB.

chunks.title: Granite Geospatial
chunks.text: Granite Geospatial (by IBM), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Granite Geospatial is IBM's family of Earth-observation models built on a Swin-B backbone pretrained with masked image modeling over Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery.

chunks.title: Granite Geospatial
chunks.text: Granite Geospatial (by IBM), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: The declared biomass member replaces the pretraining decoder with a UPerNet regression head and is fine-tuned against GEDI L4A lidar labels drawn from 15 biomes, predicting above-ground biomass from HLS L30 optical composites through TerraTorch.

chunks.title: Granite Guardian
chunks.text: Granite Guardian (by IBM), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: IBM's open guardrail model family for detecting risks in prompts and responses, plus RAG-specific checks. It covers harm, social bias, jailbreaking, violence, profanity and sexual content, and adds hallucination checks for retrieval pipelines (context relevance, groundedness, answer relevance).

chunks.title: Granite Speech
chunks.text: Granite Speech (by IBM), catalog entry under Speech & audio: IBM's speech models: Granite Speech 4.1 pairs a speech encoder with a Granite language model for recognition and translation in English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and Japanese, and Granite Speech 5.0 TurboCTC is a compact 470M-parameter English recognizer built for speed.

chunks.title: GraphRAG
chunks.text: GraphRAG (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Microsoft Research's graph-based RAG system. A model extracts entities and relationships from unstructured text into a knowledge graph, clusters it into hierarchical communities, generates community summaries, and answers through global, local and DRIFT search modes.

chunks.title: GraphRAG
chunks.text: GraphRAG (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: It targets corpus-wide sensemaking questions that vector retrieval alone handles poorly.

chunks.title: Grok 4.20
chunks.text: Grok 4.20 (by xAI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Grok is the family of proprietary large language models from xAI, now branded SpaceXAI, served through the xAI API, grok.com and X. The line runs from Grok 3 through the Grok 4.x releases, including a Grok 4.20 Multi-agent variant. The current flagship accepts text and image input and returns text.

chunks.title: Grok
chunks.text: Grok (by xAI), catalog entry under UI & API: xAI's consumer chat product, a standalone app at grok.com with mobile clients and integration into X, distinguished by real-time access to X content. It offers a reasoning mode, real-time search and multimodal input.

chunks.title: Grok Build
chunks.text: Grok Build (by xAI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Grok Build is a terminal coding agent that edits files, runs shell commands and searches the web from a full-screen TUI, headless scripts, or editors over the Agent Client Protocol. It adds parallel subagents, plan mode, an opt-in OS-level sandbox, MCP, skills, plugins and hooks, and can run other providers' models beside its default Grok models.

chunks.title: Grok Build
chunks.text: Grok Build (by xAI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: SpaceXAI develops it internally and publishes the source as a periodically synced mirror.

chunks.title: Groq Inference
chunks.text: Groq Inference (by Groq), catalog entry under Inference code: Groq Inference runs open models on Groq's custom Language Processing Unit (LPU) hardware, built from the ground up for AI inference rather than adapted from a general-purpose GPU. Its deterministic, statically scheduled architecture keeps model weights in on-chip SRAM rather than in off-chip memory.

chunks.title: Groq Inference
chunks.text: Groq Inference (by Groq), catalog entry under Inference code: The GroqCloud service exposes open models, including gpt-oss, Llama, and Whisper, through an OpenAI-compatible API.

chunks.title: GSM8K
chunks.text: GSM8K (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Grade School Math 8K: 8,500 grade-school math word problems, 7,473 for training and 1,319 for test, used to evaluate chain-of-thought reasoning on concise single-answer tasks. It ships main and socratic configurations and comes from the paper on training verifiers to solve math word problems.

chunks.title: GTE
chunks.text: GTE (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: GTE (General Text Embedding) covers embedding and reranking for multilingual and long-document retrieval.

chunks.title: GTE
chunks.text: GTE (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: gte-multilingual-base handles more than 70 languages at 8,192 tokens from a 305M-parameter encoder and emits sparse token weights alongside dense vectors; the ModernBERT-based embedder and cross-encoder reranker target English long documents, and the gte-Qwen2 instruct checkpoints are decoder-based variants.

chunks.title: GTE
chunks.text: GTE (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Alibaba's NLP group publishes the family.

chunks.title: GTE Reranker
chunks.text: GTE Reranker (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The reranking half of Alibaba's GTE family: two Apache-2.0 cross-encoders that score query-document pairs for a retrieval pipeline rather than emit vectors.

chunks.title: GTE Reranker
chunks.text: GTE Reranker (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: gte-reranker-modernbert-base is a 149M English model on a ModernBERT base reporting BEIR 56.19, LoCo 90.68 and CoIR 79.99 at 8,192 tokens, and gte-multilingual-reranker-base is a 306M encoder-only reranker covering more than 70 languages at the same context

chunks.title: GTE Reranker
chunks.text: GTE Reranker (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: which the mGTE paper positions as roughly ten times faster than the decoder-based alternatives of its generation.

chunks.title: Guardrails AI
chunks.text: Guardrails AI (by Guardrails AI), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Guardrails AI is a framework for input and output guards on LLM applications, with a hub of pre-built validators covering PII, toxicity, prompt injection and output format. It wraps a model call in guards that detect risks and enforce structured output, running as a self-hosted Python library.

chunks.title: gVisor
chunks.text: gVisor (by Google), catalog entry under Deployment: gVisor puts an application kernel between a container and the host, intercepting system calls in userspace and implementing a Linux-like interface in Go rather than filtering syscalls or booting a virtual machine. It ships an OCI runtime, runsc, that drops into Docker and Kubernetes tooling.

chunks.title: gVisor
chunks.text: gVisor (by Google), catalog entry under Deployment: Google develops it and runs it as the sandbox layer behind GKE Sandbox, Cloud Run and App Engine.

chunks.title: H2O-3
chunks.text: H2O-3 (by H2O.ai), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: H2O.ai's open-source, in-memory, distributed machine-learning platform, running on the JVM with Python and R clients. It offers GLM, GAM, gradient boosting, XGBoost, random forests, deep learning, SVMs, stacked ensembles, isolation forests, k-means and PCA, and H2O AutoML, which trains, tunes and stacks a set of models within a time or model budget.

chunks.title: H2O-3
chunks.text: H2O-3 (by H2O.ai), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Models export as MOJO and POJO artifacts for deployment. H2O.ai sells a commercial H2O-3 Secure edition alongside it.

chunks.title: Habitat
chunks.text: Habitat (by Meta), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Habitat is Meta's platform for embodied-AI research: Habitat-Sim, a 3D simulator that renders RGB-D and semantic camera views of scanned indoor scenes at thousands of frames per second with Bullet rigid-body physics, and Habitat-Lab, the library that defines navigation, rearrangement

chunks.title: Habitat
chunks.text: Habitat (by Meta), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: instruction-following and question-answering tasks and trains agents on them. It is the navigation and home-environment simulator of the category.

chunks.title: Hailo-10H
chunks.text: Hailo-10H (by Hailo Technologies), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Hailo's generative-AI edge accelerator, sold as an M.2 module and as a bare chip, delivering 40 TOPS at INT4 and 20 TOPS at INT8 at about 2.5W typical power. Unlike the Hailo-8 it adds a direct DDR interface, so it can run language and vision-language models on-device. It targets PCs, automotive and edge devices needing local generative AI.

chunks.title: Hailo-8
chunks.text: Hailo-8 (by Hailo Technologies), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Edge AI inference accelerator from Hailo, delivering up to 26 TOPS at roughly 2.5W typical power. It is sold in M.2, mPCIe and PCIe card form factors with integrated memory and no external DRAM, and supports TensorFlow, TensorFlow Lite, Keras, PyTorch and ONNX through the Hailo Dataflow Compiler and the HailoRT runtime.

chunks.title: Halo Record
chunks.text: Halo Record (by bkuan001), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: Halo Record keeps a tamper-evident audit trail of what an AI agent did: every tool call, model call, data access and approval becomes a record in an append-only, hash-chained log, rendered as a self-verifying report a customer can check. Checkpoints can be anchored to an outside witness or an RFC 3161 timestamp authority.

chunks.title: Halo Record
chunks.text: Halo Record (by bkuan001), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: The package is the reference implementation of an open record format.

chunks.title: HAMi
chunks.text: HAMi (by Project HAMi), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Heterogeneous GPU sharing and scheduling for Kubernetes, hosted by the CNCF. HAMi registers each accelerator in a cluster with its split count, memory limit and core limit, and its own scheduler decides which node and which devices a pod receives, recording the decision on the pod.

chunks.title: HAMi
chunks.text: HAMi (by Project HAMi), catalog entry under ML orchestration: It covers NVIDIA GPUs alongside Cambricon MLUs and other vendors' accelerators.

chunks.title: HarmBench
chunks.text: HarmBench (by Center for AI Safety), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: HarmBench is a standardized evaluation framework for automated red-teaming of large language models. It runs one pipeline that scores attack methods against target models, or models against attacks, so red-team attacks and defenses can be compared on equal terms and developed together.

chunks.title: HarmBench
chunks.text: HarmBench (by Center for AI Safety), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Its initial release covered 18 attack methods and 33 target models and defenses. It is built by the Center for AI Safety.

chunks.title: Harrier-OSS
chunks.text: Harrier-OSS (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Harrier-OSS is Microsoft's open-weight multilingual text embedding family, released by the Bing team in three sizes: 270M, 0.6B and 27B parameters.

chunks.title: Harrier-OSS
chunks.text: Harrier-OSS (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The models are decoder-only encoders with last-token pooling and L2 normalization, support more than 100 languages and a 32,768-token context, and take a one-sentence instruction on the query side.

chunks.title: Harrier-OSS
chunks.text: Harrier-OSS (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: They target retrieval, clustering, semantic similarity, classification, bitext mining and reranking, and the 27B checkpoint scores 74.3 on the Multilingual MTEB v2 benchmark.

chunks.title: Harvard Dataverse
chunks.text: Harvard Dataverse (by Institute for Quantitative Social Science), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: Harvard Dataverse is a free research data repository, open to researchers anywhere, run by Harvard's Institute for Quantitative Social Science on the open-source Dataverse software. Depositors publish datasets that are versioned under DOIs and downloadable through a web interface and an API.

chunks.title: Harvard Dataverse
chunks.text: Harvard Dataverse (by Institute for Quantitative Social Science), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: Tabular files from Stata, SPSS, R, Excel and CSV are ingested with variable-level metadata, and dataset metadata exports as Croissant, DDI and DataCite.

chunks.title: Hasher-Matcher-Actioner
chunks.text: Hasher-Matcher-Actioner (by Meta), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Hasher-Matcher-Actioner (HMA) is Meta's open-source service for finding copies of known harmful images and videos. It turns uploaded media into hashes, matches them against banks of previously identified content, and connects those banks to industry hash-sharing programs such as those run by NCMEC, GIFCT and StopNCII.

chunks.title: Hasher-Matcher-Actioner
chunks.text: Hasher-Matcher-Actioner (by Meta), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: HMA runs as a Docker container with a REST API and a PostgreSQL database, or as a Python library.

chunks.title: Haystack
chunks.text: Haystack (by deepset), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: deepset's Python orchestration framework for production LLM applications, built around composable pipelines and agent workflows with explicit control over retrieval, routing, memory and generation.

chunks.title: Haystack
chunks.text: Haystack (by deepset), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: It began as a RAG and search framework and is now a general orchestrator, shipping ready-made agents and progressive skill discovery alongside the pipeline primitives.

chunks.title: HDBSCAN
chunks.text: HDBSCAN (by scikit-learn-contrib), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Density-based clustering library implementing HDBSCAN*, which finds clusters of varying density and labels noise points, with little parameter tuning. It also provides robust single linkage, GLOSH outlier scores, soft clustering, prediction for new points and branch detection inside clusters.

chunks.title: HDBSCAN
chunks.text: HDBSCAN (by scikit-learn-contrib), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: It is a scikit-learn-contrib project with a scikit-learn interface.

chunks.title: HeDC4
chunks.text: HeDC4 (by HeNLP), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: HeDC4 (Hebrew Deduplicated and Cleaned Common Crawl Corpus) is a Hebrew pretraining corpus built by cleaning and approximately deduplicating Common Crawl text. Released as a 47.6 GB file of 910,000 documents, it was introduced to train the HeRo and LongHeRo Hebrew encoder models. HeNLP publishes it, with Vitaly Shalumov and Harel Haskey as authors.

chunks.title: Helicone
chunks.text: Helicone (by Helicone), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: LLM proxy that captures logs, costs and latency through a one-line change to the API base URL, with a dashboard for request volume, token usage, cost and error rates. It is also an AI gateway reaching more than a hundred models behind one API key, with automatic fallbacks, caching, prompt management and datasets.

chunks.title: Helicone
chunks.text: Helicone (by Helicone), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: It runs from the repository or as a hosted service.

chunks.title: HelixDB
chunks.text: HelixDB (by HelixDB), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: HelixDB is a graph database written in Rust on object storage that holds entities, relationships, embeddings and text in one transactional engine, with native vector search and BM25 full-text search. It targets knowledge graphs and agent memory.

chunks.title: HelixDB
chunks.text: HelixDB (by HelixDB), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Queries are built with SDKs for Rust, TypeScript, Python and Go and sent to a running instance as JSON requests, and it runs as a local server, embedded in a process, or on the managed Helix Cloud.

chunks.title: HellaSwag
chunks.text: HellaSwag (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Commonsense natural-language-inference and sentence-completion benchmark from 2019, holding 59,950 four-way multiple-choice examples over contexts derived from ActivityNet. It tests whether a model picks the plausible continuation of an everyday situation, and is reported in most language-model releases.

chunks.title: HELM
chunks.text: HELM (by Stanford CRFM), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models: a Python framework for reproducible evaluation of foundation models, organized around scenarios, adapters and metrics, and covering accuracy, efficiency, bias and toxicity.

chunks.title: HELM
chunks.text: HELM (by Stanford CRFM), catalog entry under Evaluation code: It ships a web leaderboard UI in the same repository and maintains boards spanning text, vision-language, text-to-image, medical and audio evaluation, plus an enterprise benchmark.

chunks.title: Hermes-4-Llama-3.1-405B
chunks.text: Hermes-4-Llama-3.1-405B (by Nous Research), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Nous Research's hybrid-mode reasoning instruct line, one post-training recipe shipped on four independent base models: ByteDance's Seed-OSS-36B, Qwen3-14B, and Meta's Llama 3.1 at 70B and 405B. A single checkpoint toggles between reasoning and non-reasoning modes.

chunks.title: Hermes 3 Dataset
chunks.text: Hermes 3 Dataset (by Nous Research), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Nous Research's release of the instruction and chat data behind Hermes 3, a mixture of curated and generated examples. A significant portion of it was retained in the Hermes 4 training data, and the Hermes 3 technical report describes how the mixture was built.

chunks.title: Hermes Agent
chunks.text: Hermes Agent (by Nous Research), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Self-improving autonomous agent from Nous Research that grows through persistent memory, auto-generated reusable skills and a built-in learning loop. It runs on a VPS or a serverless backend, is driven from Telegram and other messaging surfaces, and ships subagent delegation, natural-language scheduling, sandboxing and more than forty tools.

chunks.title: Hexabot
chunks.text: Hexabot (by Hexastack), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Automation and agent builder from Hexastack for multi-channel, multilingual conversational assistants. Flows are modeled visually or as YAML workflows with typed runtime contracts, memory and MCP integration points, and extensions add further capabilities.

chunks.title: Datasets
chunks.text: Datasets (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Datasets is a lightweight Hugging Face library providing one-line dataloaders for thousands of public datasets and efficient preprocessing for machine-learning workflows. It supports CSV, JSON, Parquet, audio, image and video formats with streaming and memory-mapping, and integrates with PyTorch, TensorFlow and JAX.

chunks.title: Datasets
chunks.text: Datasets (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It is the loading layer that feeds training and evaluation pipelines.

chunks.title: HH-RLHF (Anthropic Helpful/Harmless)
chunks.text: HH-RLHF (Anthropic Helpful/Harmless) (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Anthropic's human preference dataset for RLHF, holding about 169,000 rows of chosen-versus-rejected response pairs on helpfulness and harmlessness alongside red-teaming dialogues.

chunks.title: HH-RLHF (Anthropic Helpful/Harmless)
chunks.text: HH-RLHF (Anthropic Helpful/Harmless) (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: It was released with Anthropic's papers on training helpful and harmless assistants, and is intended for preference modeling rather than supervised dialogue training.

chunks.title: Higgs Audio
chunks.text: Higgs Audio (by Boson AI), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Boson AI's audio foundation models: Higgs TTS 3 speaks more than 100 languages with zero-shot voice cloning and conversational delivery, and the Higgs Audio v3 speech-to-text models pair a Whisper encoder with a Qwen3 decoder for transcription.

chunks.title: hnswlib
chunks.text: hnswlib (by NMSLIB project), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: hnswlib is a header-only C++ implementation of Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs for approximate nearest neighbour search, with Python bindings and support for insertions, updates and filtered queries. Several vector databases embed it as their graph index.

chunks.title: Holo
chunks.text: Holo (by H Company), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Holo is H Company's family of vision-language models for computer-use agents, fine-tuned from Qwen bases to read screens and act on web, desktop and mobile interfaces. The current Holo3.1 release comes in 0.8B, 4B, 9B and 35B-A3B sizes with native function calling and FP8, NVFP4 and GGUF builds.

chunks.title: Holo
chunks.text: Holo (by H Company), catalog entry under Multimodal models: H Company's larger Holo3-122B model is available only through its API.

chunks.title: HTCondor
chunks.text: HTCondor (by HTCondor), catalog entry under ML orchestration: High-throughput workload manager from the University of Wisconsin-Madison's Center for High Throughput Computing, and one of the schedulers large research GPU fleets run on.

chunks.title: HTCondor
chunks.text: HTCondor (by HTCondor), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Jobs declare what they need in HTCondor's own submit language - request_GPUs, require_gpus, gpus_minimum_capability, gpus_minimum_memory - and HTCondor matches each job to a machine whose advertised resources satisfy it.

chunks.title: Hugging Face Inference Providers
chunks.text: Hugging Face Inference Providers (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Inference code: Hugging Face Inference Providers routes requests for models on the Hugging Face Hub to partner inference services, among them Cerebras, Groq, Fireworks, Together and Scaleway, through one API and one Hugging Face token.

chunks.title: Hugging Face Inference Providers
chunks.text: Hugging Face Inference Providers (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Inference code: A router at router.huggingface.co exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, and requests can name a provider or let the router choose one by speed or by price. Hugging Face bills provider rates with no markup.

chunks.title: HuggingChat / chat-ui
chunks.text: HuggingChat / chat-ui (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under UI & API: Chat UI is a SvelteKit and MongoDB chat interface built and maintained by Hugging Face, and the codebase behind HuggingChat at huggingface.co/chat. It connects to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, such as Hugging Face Inference Providers, Ollama, llama.cpp or OpenRouter, and discovers the available models automatically.

chunks.title: HuggingChat / chat-ui
chunks.text: HuggingChat / chat-ui (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under UI & API: It supports MCP tool calling, image input, optional OpenID login, and an Omni router that picks a model by request type.

chunks.title: huggingface_hub
chunks.text: huggingface_hub (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: huggingface_hub is the official Python client and hf command-line tool for the Hugging Face Hub, enabling programmatic downloading and uploading of files, repository management, running inference and jobs, and search across models, datasets, and Spaces.

chunks.title: huggingface_hub
chunks.text: huggingface_hub (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It serves as the integration layer that other ML libraries use to host and retrieve content on the Hub. It is maintained by Hugging Face.

chunks.title: Hugging Face Hub
chunks.text: Hugging Face Hub (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Hosted platform at huggingface.co where any account holder publishes models, datasets and Spaces apps as Git repositories, versioned with commits, branches and tags. Full-text search indexes model and dataset cards, and an HTTP API with a published OpenAPI specification lets other tools list, create and download repositories by name.

chunks.title: Hugging Face Hub
chunks.text: Hugging Face Hub (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Hugging Face runs it with free public hosting and paid Team and Enterprise plans for private collaboration.

chunks.title: HumanEval
chunks.text: HumanEval (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: 164 hand-written Python programming problems, each with a function signature, docstring and unit tests, introduced in the Codex paper in 2021. It was the original code-generation benchmark and most code-model papers still report pass@k on it, despite its small size and Python-only scope.

chunks.title: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE)
chunks.text: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) (by Center for AI Safety), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Multimodal frontier-knowledge benchmark from the Center for AI Safety and Scale AI, built with nearly a thousand subject-matter experts across more than 500 institutions.

chunks.title: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE)
chunks.text: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) (by Center for AI Safety), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: It holds 2,500 expert-written closed-ended questions, multiple-choice and short answer with text and images, across more than a hundred subjects, each with an unambiguous answer that is not quickly findable online.

chunks.title: Humming
chunks.text: Humming (by vLLM (UC Berkeley / vLLM team)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Humming is a lightweight, JIT-compiled GEMM kernel library for quantized inference, supporting dense and MoE GEMM across FP16/BF16/FP8/FP4/INT8/INT4 activation and weight-type combinations on NVIDIA GPUs from Turing onward.

chunks.title: Hummingbird
chunks.text: Hummingbird (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Hummingbird compiles trained traditional machine learning models - decision trees, random forests and featurizers from scikit-learn, LightGBM and XGBoost - into tensor computations, so they execute on the same neural-network runtimes and hardware as deep models. Microsoft develops it.

chunks.title: Hunyuan3D
chunks.text: Hunyuan3D (by Tencent), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Hunyuan3D is Tencent's family of image-to-3D models that generate a shape with one diffusion model and paint its texture with a second. Its current release, Hunyuan3D 3.0, is served only through Tencent Cloud and the Hunyuan3D site.

chunks.title: Hunyuan3D
chunks.text: Hunyuan3D (by Tencent), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: The downloadable releases run from Hunyuan3D 2.0 and its mini and multi-view variants to Hunyuan3D 2.1, which adds a physically based material model and releases its training code.

chunks.title: HunyuanVideo
chunks.text: HunyuanVideo (by Tencent), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: HunyuanVideo is Tencent's family of diffusion-transformer video generation models. The original 13B text-to-video model and its image-to-video variant were followed by HunyuanVideo 1.5, an 8.3B model with a 3D causal VAE that generates at 480p and 720p and upscales to 1080p with a few-step super-resolution network.

chunks.title: HunyuanVideo
chunks.text: HunyuanVideo (by Tencent), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Tencent publishes the weights with inference code and, for 1.5, a full training pipeline.

chunks.title: IBM Spectrum LSF
chunks.text: IBM Spectrum LSF (by IBM), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Commercial workload manager and job scheduler for distributed high-performance computing.

chunks.title: IBM Spectrum LSF
chunks.text: IBM Spectrum LSF (by IBM), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Jobs declare what they need in LSF's own submit schema - a GPU count, mode, model and memory, or a resource requirement string naming physical GPUs and interconnect - and LSF's scheduler places each job on hosts whose advertised resources satisfy it, autoscaling onto cloud capacity where a site has configured it.

chunks.title: IBM watsonx.governance
chunks.text: IBM watsonx.governance (by IBM), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: IBM watsonx.governance is a closed AI governance product for inventorying models and agents, documenting them, assessing risk and capturing compliance evidence against policies and regulatory obligations. It is sold as SaaS on IBM Cloud and as enterprise software, and connects to IBM OpenPages for wider risk and compliance work.

chunks.title: Icelandic Dynaword
chunks.text: Icelandic Dynaword (by Danish Foundation Models), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Icelandic Dynaword is a continually updated Icelandic pretraining corpus of more than 2.6 billion tokens, gathered only from openly licensed sources: the open subcorpora of the Icelandic Gigaword Corpus, Wikipedia and its sister projects, the official state gazette and out-of-copyright books.

chunks.title: Icelandic Dynaword
chunks.text: Icelandic Dynaword (by Danish Foundation Models), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Each document carries model-generated quality and content annotations. Danish Foundation Models maintains it, applying the approach of Danish Dynaword.

chunks.title: Icelandic Gigaword Corpus
chunks.text: Icelandic Gigaword Corpus (by Árni Magnússon Institute for Icelandic Studies), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Icelandic Gigaword Corpus (IGC) is a tagged and lemmatized corpus of Icelandic drawn from news media, parliamentary speeches back to 1911, laws, court judgments, journals, social media, books and Wikipedia.

chunks.title: Icelandic Gigaword Corpus
chunks.text: Icelandic Gigaword Corpus (by Árni Magnússon Institute for Icelandic Studies), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Its 2022 version holds about 2.4 billion running words, extended by yearly releases. A JSONL release of the openly licensed subcorpora, about 1.46 billion words, serves model training. The Árni Magnússon Institute for Icelandic Studies builds it.

chunks.title: Idefics
chunks.text: Idefics (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Idefics is Hugging Face's line of open vision-language models, which take interleaved sequences of images and text and answer in text. Idefics3-8B pairs a SigLIP image encoder with Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and was built to improve OCR, document understanding and visual reasoning over Idefics2.

chunks.title: Idefics
chunks.text: Idefics (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Hugging Face trained it on open datasets it also publishes, including The Cauldron and Docmatix.

chunks.title: IFEval
chunks.text: IFEval (by Google), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Instruction-Following Eval: 541 prompts carrying about 25 types of verifiable instruction - word-count limits, keyword inclusion, format requirements - so that compliance can be scored programmatically rather than by a judge model. It is a core component of the Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard.

chunks.title: IIT Bombay English-Hindi corpus
chunks.text: IIT Bombay English-Hindi corpus (by CFILT, IIT Bombay), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The IIT Bombay English-Hindi corpus is a parallel corpus of about 1.49 million sentence pairs for machine translation, with a companion monolingual Hindi corpus.

chunks.title: IIT Bombay English-Hindi corpus
chunks.text: IIT Bombay English-Hindi corpus (by CFILT, IIT Bombay), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It compiles existing public corpora such as OPUS subsets and HindEnCorp with material the Center for Indian Language Technology collected, including Indian government websites. It has served as the English-Hindi data for the Workshop on Asian Translation shared tasks since 2016.

chunks.title: imbalanced-learn
chunks.text: imbalanced-learn (by scikit-learn-contrib), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Resampling library for classification on imbalanced data, built on the scikit-learn estimator interface. It provides over-sampling (SMOTE and its variants, ADASYN), under-sampling (NearMiss, Tomek links, edited nearest neighbours), combined methods and imbalance-aware ensembles such as balanced random forests and RUSBoost.

chunks.title: imbalanced-learn
chunks.text: imbalanced-learn (by scikit-learn-contrib), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: It is a scikit-learn-contrib project run by volunteer maintainers.

chunks.title: INCLUDE
chunks.text: INCLUDE (by Cohere), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: INCLUDE is a multilingual knowledge and reasoning benchmark of four-option multiple-choice questions taken from local academic, professional and licensing exams in 44 languages.
