Because the questions come from each region's own exams rather than translated English tests, many probe regional knowledge. A smaller lite subset covers the same languages.

chunks.title: INCLUDE
chunks.text: INCLUDE (by Cohere), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It was built by EPFL and Cohere Labs researchers.

chunks.title: IndicAlign
chunks.text: IndicAlign (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: IndicAlign is an instruction-tuning and safety-alignment collection of about 74.7 million prompt-response pairs in 14 Indic languages.

chunks.title: IndicAlign
chunks.text: IndicAlign (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It pools translated and romanized English sets such as Dolly and OpenAssistant, instruction pairs built from IndoWordNet entries, crowd-sourced Anudesh prompts, Wikipedia-grounded conversations generated with Llama 2, and toxic prompts paired with refusals. AI4Bharat released it with Sangraha as part of IndicLLMSuite.

chunks.title: IndicCorp v2
chunks.text: IndicCorp v2 (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: IndicCorp v2 is a monolingual pretraining text corpus of about 20.9 billion tokens in 24 languages from four language families, reaching low-resource languages such as Bodo, Khasi and Santali.

chunks.title: IndicCorp v2
chunks.text: IndicCorp v2 (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: AI4Bharat curated it to train its IndicBERT v2 encoder models, and released it with IndicXTREME, a human-supervised benchmark of nine language-understanding tasks.

chunks.title: IndicGenBench
chunks.text: IndicGenBench (by Google Research), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: IndicGenBench is a benchmark of generation tasks for large language models in 29 Indic languages across 13 scripts, covering cross-lingual summarization, machine translation, and multilingual and cross-lingual question answering.

chunks.title: IndicGenBench
chunks.text: IndicGenBench (by Google Research), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It extends CrossSum, FLORES, XQuAD and XorQA by having people translate their English examples into each target language, which makes the test data multi-way parallel. Google Research releases it as four task sets.

chunks.title: IndicVoices
chunks.text: IndicVoices (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: IndicVoices is a speech corpus of read, extempore and conversational audio in all 22 scheduled Indian languages, recorded from about 51,000 speakers in more than 400 districts. More than 23,000 hours have been recorded, and about half of them transcribed by people under published guidelines.

chunks.title: IndicVoices
chunks.text: IndicVoices (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: AI4Bharat collected it with its open Kathbath and Shoonya tools and trained its 22-language IndicASR model on it.

chunks.title: IndicVoices-R
chunks.text: IndicVoices-R (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: IndicVoices-R is a text-to-speech corpus of 1,704 hours from 10,496 speakers across the 22 scheduled Indian languages. AI4Bharat built it by restoring recordings from the IndicVoices speech recognition collection with demixing, dereverberation and enhancement models, then filtering for clarity.

chunks.title: IndicVoices-R
chunks.text: IndicVoices-R (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Each 48 kHz clip carries verbatim and normalized transcripts and speaker metadata, and a benchmark tests speaker generalization.

chunks.title: IndicXTREME
chunks.text: IndicXTREME (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: IndicXTREME is a natural language understanding benchmark of nine tasks across 20 Indian languages, grouping 105 evaluation sets for classification, structure prediction, question answering and sentence retrieval.

chunks.title: IndicXTREME
chunks.text: IndicXTREME (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: AI4Bharat created new sets, among them IndicCOPA, IndicQA, IndicXParaphrase and IndicSentiment, and folded in Naamapadam, IndicXNLI, MASSIVE and FLORES. It was released with IndicBERT v2 to test zero-shot multilingual transfer.

chunks.title: IndoNLU
chunks.text: IndoNLU (by IndoNLP), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: IndoNLU is a benchmark for Indonesian natural language understanding with twelve tasks, from emotion and sentiment classification to part-of-speech tagging, named-entity recognition, keyphrase extraction, textual entailment and extractive QA.

chunks.title: IndoNLU
chunks.text: IndoNLU (by IndoNLP), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The task data comes from social media, reviews, news and Wikipedia, some of it labeled by Indonesian linguists. It shipped with the Indo4B pretraining corpus and the IndoBERT models, from a collaboration including Institut Teknologi Bandung, Universitas Indonesia, Gojek and Prosa.AI.

chunks.title: Infinity
chunks.text: Infinity (by InfiniFlow), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Infinity is a database built for LLM applications that indexes dense vectors, sparse vectors, tensors and full text in one engine and fuses them into a single hybrid query. Results can be reranked with reciprocal rank fusion, weighted sum or ColBERT-style tensor rerankers, and structured data is queried in the same system. It is self-hosted.

chunks.title: Inflection 3.0
chunks.text: Inflection 3.0 (by Inflection AI), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Inflection AI's foundation model, powering the Pi assistant and the company's enterprise tier. Inflection 3.0, released October 2024, pairs a Pi conversational model with a Productivity model and runs on Intel Gaudi 3 hardware with on-premises or cloud deployment.

chunks.title: Inflection 3.0
chunks.text: Inflection 3.0 (by Inflection AI), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Most of the original research team moved to Microsoft in 2024, after which the company pivoted to enterprise work.

chunks.title: Inkling
chunks.text: Inkling (by Thinking Machines Lab), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Inkling, released July 15, 2026, is Thinking Machines Lab's first open-weight foundation model, a natively multimodal mixture of experts with 975 billion total and 41 billion active parameters.

chunks.title: Inkling
chunks.text: Inkling (by Thinking Machines Lab), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Each token is routed to six of 256 experts plus two shared ones, with hybrid local and global attention, a one-million-token context and 45 trillion training tokens. A 276B Small sibling with 12B active parameters is part of the same family.

chunks.title: Inkuba-Instruct
chunks.text: Inkuba-Instruct (by Lelapa AI), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Inkuba-Instruct is an instruction-tuning dataset for Hausa, Yoruba, Swahili, isiZulu and isiXhosa, built by recasting existing task datasets such as MAFAND-MT, MasakhaNER, MasakhaPOS, AfriQA, SIB-200, MasakhaNEWS and AfriSenti into instruction, input and output records.

chunks.title: Inkuba-Instruct
chunks.text: Inkuba-Instruct (by Lelapa AI), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It spans translation, named-entity recognition, part-of-speech tagging, question answering, topic classification and sentiment. Lelapa AI released it with the InkubaLM paper.

chunks.title: Inkuba-Mono
chunks.text: Inkuba-Mono (by Lelapa AI), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Inkuba-Mono is a monolingual text corpus for Hausa, Yoruba, Swahili, isiZulu and isiXhosa, about 1.7 billion tokens compiled from public repositories on Hugging Face, GitHub and Zenodo. Swahili contributes about a billion tokens and Yoruba the fewest. Lelapa AI assembled it to pretrain its InkubaLM small language model.

chunks.title: InsightFace
chunks.text: InsightFace (by DeepInsight), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Open-source face-analysis project covering face detection, alignment, recognition and attributes, known for the ArcFace recognition loss and the RetinaFace and SCRFD detectors.

chunks.title: InsightFace
chunks.text: InsightFace (by DeepInsight), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: The insightface Python package runs its pretrained model packs through ONNX Runtime and downloads the default buffalo_l pack on first use; the repository also holds training code for detection and recognition.

chunks.title: InsightFace
chunks.text: InsightFace (by DeepInsight), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: The library code is MIT-licensed, and the pretrained models are for non-commercial research, with commercial model licenses sold separately.

chunks.title: Inspect AI
chunks.text: Inspect AI (by UK AI Security Institute), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Frontier-AI evaluation framework from the UK AI Security Institute with Meridian Labs, offering one interface over lab APIs, cloud APIs and local vLLM, Ollama and llama.cpp backends.

chunks.title: Inspect AI
chunks.text: Inspect AI (by UK AI Security Institute), catalog entry under Evaluation code: It ships built-in components for prompt engineering, tool use, multi-turn dialogue and model-graded scoring, alongside a collection of more than 200 pre-built evaluations.

chunks.title: Intel Neural Compressor
chunks.text: Intel Neural Compressor (by Intel), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Intel Neural Compressor is a Python library that applies model-compression techniques across PyTorch, TensorFlow and JAX, covering static and dynamic quantization, SmoothQuant, weight-only quantization, quantization-aware training and mixed precision.

chunks.title: Intel Neural Compressor
chunks.text: Intel Neural Compressor (by Intel), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Low-bit formats including the MX and NVFP4 families are supported experimentally, with an auto-tune workflow.

chunks.title: InternData-A1
chunks.text: InternData-A1 (by Shanghai AI Laboratory), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: InternData-A1 is a simulated robot manipulation dataset from Shanghai AI Laboratory: over 630k trajectories and 7,433 hours across four single- and dual-arm embodiments (Franka, AgileX Split ALOHA, ARX Lift-2 and an AgiBot robot), 70 tasks and 227 scenes

chunks.title: InternData-A1
chunks.text: InternData-A1 (by Shanghai AI Laboratory), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: generated by a physics-validated motion-planning pipeline and published in LeRobot format for pretraining vision-language-action policies.

chunks.title: InternLM 2.5
chunks.text: InternLM 2.5 (by Shanghai AI Laboratory), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Shanghai AI Lab's open-weights model family. The InternLM 2.5 generation at 7B and 20B reaches a one-million-token context through dynamic NTK interpolation. It was superseded by InternLM3 in January 2025, an 8B model trained on four trillion tokens with an integrated deep-thinking chain-of-thought mode.

chunks.title: InternVL
chunks.text: InternVL (by Shanghai AI Laboratory), catalog entry under Multimodal models: InternVL is Shanghai AI Laboratory's open vision-language model family, released by OpenGVLab from InternVL 1.5 through InternVL3.5 in sizes from 1B to 241B. InternVL3.5 handles single and multi-image input, documents and video, and adds GUI interaction and embodied-agent tasks, with a Flash variant for faster inference.

chunks.title: InternVL
chunks.text: InternVL (by Shanghai AI Laboratory), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Its multimodal preference data and reinforcement-learning code are published alongside the weights.

chunks.title: invisible-watermark
chunks.text: invisible-watermark (by ShieldMnt), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: invisible-watermark is a Python library and command-line tool that embeds and decodes invisible watermarks in images using frequency-domain methods (DWT-DCT and DWT-DCT-SVD) or the RivaGAN neural encoder. The fast default method suits embedding on the fly, while the other two are several times slower on a CPU.

chunks.title: invisible-watermark
chunks.text: invisible-watermark (by ShieldMnt), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: The maintainers describe it as experimental and warn that decoding is not guaranteed.

chunks.title: InvokeAI
chunks.text: InvokeAI (by Invoke), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: InvokeAI is a locally run image-generation application with a unified canvas, a gallery and a node-based workflow editor. It runs the Stable Diffusion, FLUX, Qwen-Image, Z-Image and other image families on the user's own hardware and can call a few hosted models through their APIs.

chunks.title: InvokeAI
chunks.text: InvokeAI (by Invoke), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: The project is now maintained by its community after the company behind it closed its hosted service.

chunks.title: IREE
chunks.text: IREE (by LF AI & Data (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: IREE is an MLIR-based compiler and runtime that lowers machine learning models to a unified intermediate representation, targeting datacenter hardware at one end and mobile and edge constraints at the other. Input comes from PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow and ONNX; output targets include CPU, CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan and SPIR-V.

chunks.title: IREE
chunks.text: IREE (by LF AI & Data (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: The project is hosted by the LF AI & Data Foundation.

chunks.title: Isaac Lab
chunks.text: Isaac Lab (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Isaac Lab is NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated framework for robot learning, covering reinforcement learning, imitation learning and motion planning.

chunks.title: Isaac Lab
chunks.text: Isaac Lab (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: It ships more than thirty ready-to-train environments wired to RL libraries such as RSL RL, SKRL and Stable Baselines, runs on Isaac Sim's PhysX physics and RTX rendering, and is adding the open Newton engine as a second physics backend.

chunks.title: Jamba 1.5 Large
chunks.text: Jamba 1.5 Large (by AI21 Labs), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Jamba 1.5 Large is a hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts chat model from AI21 Labs, with 398B total and 94B active parameters and a 256K-token context window. It is instruction-tuned for chat and agentic use, with tool use, grounded generation and JSON mode.

chunks.title: Jamba 1.5 Large
chunks.text: Jamba 1.5 Large (by AI21 Labs), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: AI21 announced it in August 2024, and its Hugging Face card lists Jamba-Large-1.7 as the newer version.

chunks.title: Jan
chunks.text: Jan (by Jan), catalog entry under UI & API: Jan is a cross-platform desktop app for running open-weights models entirely offline, with a chat interface, custom assistants, Projects with indexed files and MCP connectors. It also connects to cloud providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic, and serves a local OpenAI-compatible API on localhost:1337. Menlo Research builds it.

chunks.title: Janus
chunks.text: Janus (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Janus is DeepSeek's family of unified models that both understand images and generate them from text in one autoregressive transformer. It separates visual encoding for the two jobs, SigLIP for understanding and a discrete image tokenizer for generation.

chunks.title: Janus
chunks.text: Janus (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Janus-Pro comes in 1B and 7B sizes on DeepSeek-LLM bases, and JanusFlow swaps in rectified flow for generation.

chunks.title: JAX
chunks.text: JAX (by Google), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: JAX is a Python library for accelerator-oriented array computation and program transformation, combining NumPy-style arrays with composable function transforms: automatic differentiation, just-in-time compilation through XLA, and automatic vectorization.

chunks.title: JAX
chunks.text: JAX (by Google), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It is developed by the jax-ml organization, having originated at Google, and targets high-performance numerical computing and large-scale ML research.

chunks.title: Jina Embeddings
chunks.text: Jina Embeddings (by Jina AI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Jina AI's text embedding line, from the v2 English and bilingual encoders through v3's task-LoRA multilingual model to the v5-text family released in early 2026.

chunks.title: Jina Embeddings
chunks.text: Jina Embeddings (by Jina AI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: v5-text-small is a 677M Qwen3-0.6B-Base distillation of Qwen3-Embedding-4B scoring 67.7 on MMTEB across 119+ languages at 32K tokens, with retrieval, text-matching, clustering and classification adapters shipped separately for vLLM and ONNX. The weights are published on the Hub, but the current generation is non-commercial.

chunks.title: Jina Reader
chunks.text: Jina Reader (by Jina AI), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Jina Reader is a service and open-source codebase that converts a web page into markdown for language models when a URL is prefixed with r.jina.ai. It reads HTML, PDF and Microsoft Office documents and captions images. A companion endpoint, s.jina.ai, searches the web and returns the results as markdown.

chunks.title: Jina Reranker
chunks.text: Jina Reranker (by Jina AI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Jina AI's reranker line, from the v1 turbo and tiny English cross-encoders through v2-base-multilingual to the v3 and v3.5 listwise rerankers. v3 is a 0.6B Qwen3-derived model with a "last but not late interaction" architecture that attends across query and up to 64 documents inside one 131K-token window, reporting 61.94 nDCG@10 on BEIR.

chunks.title: Jina Reranker
chunks.text: Jina Reranker (by Jina AI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The weights are published on the Hub, but under a non-commercial licence.

chunks.title: Jojajovai
chunks.text: Jojajovai (by PLN group, Universidad de la República), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Jojajovai is a Guarani-Spanish parallel corpus of about 30,000 sentence pairs gathered from eight sources, among them news, blogs, books and the AmericasNLP data, each split into training, development and test sets.

chunks.title: Jojajovai
chunks.text: Jojajovai (by PLN group, Universidad de la República), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Native speakers annotated a test sample for Guarani dialect, including Jopara, and for translation correctness. Researchers at Universidad de la República in Uruguay built it with partners in Paraguay, Brazil and Spain.

chunks.title: JuiceFS
chunks.text: JuiceFS (by Juicedata), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: JuiceFS is a POSIX-compatible distributed file system that stores file data in object storage such as Amazon S3 while keeping metadata in a separate database engine - Redis, MySQL or TiKV among them. Training and analytics jobs mount it and read cloud storage as files without code changes. Juicedata develops it.

chunks.title: K2
chunks.text: K2 (by LLM360), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: LLM360 and MBZUAI's K2 model line. K2-V2, a 70B dense model released in December 2025 as a reasoning-enhanced LLM the project calls 360-open, ships its weights alongside the complete TxT360 pretraining, mid-training and SFT data, the training code and intermediate checkpoints, so the run is reproducible; it superseded the 65B K2 Chat.

chunks.title: K2
chunks.text: K2 (by LLM360), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: K2 Horizon, released in September 2026 under Apache-2.0 in sizes up to a 375B-parameter mixture of experts with 23B active, is the current flagship.

chunks.title: Kaggle Datasets
chunks.text: Kaggle Datasets (by Kaggle), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: Kaggle Datasets is the public dataset catalog on Kaggle, Google's data science platform. Users and organizations publish datasets with per-file descriptions and column schemas, add new versions, and choose a license.

chunks.title: Kaggle Datasets
chunks.text: Kaggle Datasets (by Kaggle), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: The catalog is searchable by file type, license, tag and size, and the Kaggle CLI and the kagglehub library download a dataset by owner and name or load a file straight into a dataframe.

chunks.title: Kaggle Models
chunks.text: Kaggle Models (by Kaggle), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Model hub inside Kaggle, Google's data science platform, where users and organizations publish models as variations per framework and size, each variation versioned as file snapshots. Models are private until published, searchable and sortable by downloads or votes, and downloadable by handle through the kagglehub library and the Kaggle CLI.

chunks.title: Kaggle Models
chunks.text: Kaggle Models (by Kaggle), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: TensorFlow Hub moved here in 2023, and tfhub.dev links redirect to it.

chunks.title: Kagi Search API
chunks.text: Kagi Search API (by Kagi), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Search API over Kagi's own index. The v1 API has two paths - `/search`, which returns ranked references, and `/extract`, which returns page markdown - and `/search` can run the extraction inline so one call returns results with their page content.

chunks.title: KAI Scheduler
chunks.text: KAI Scheduler (by KAI Scheduler), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Kubernetes-native scheduler for AI workloads at large scale. It schedules whole PodGroups rather than individual pods, supports hierarchical queues with fair-share over time, bin-packing and spread placement, topology-aware scheduling, and separates workload priority from preemptibility.

chunks.title: KAI Scheduler
chunks.text: KAI Scheduler (by KAI Scheduler), catalog entry under ML orchestration: It runs alongside other schedulers on the same cluster rather than replacing them.

chunks.title: Kata Containers
chunks.text: Kata Containers (by OpenInfra Foundation), catalog entry under Deployment: Kata Containers runs each container inside its own lightweight virtual machine, so workloads keep container ergonomics while gaining hardware-backed isolation of kernel, memory, network and I/O.

chunks.title: Kata Containers
chunks.text: Kata Containers (by OpenInfra Foundation), catalog entry under Deployment: A containerd shimv2 runtime and an in-VM agent plug it into Kubernetes through a RuntimeClass, and the hypervisor is pluggable across QEMU, Cloud Hypervisor, Firecracker, Dragonball and StratoVirt. The OpenInfra Foundation stewards the project.

chunks.title: Kathbath
chunks.text: Kathbath (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Kathbath is a speech recognition corpus of 1,684 hours of labeled speech in 12 Indian languages, recorded by 1,218 contributors in 203 districts. Contributors read aloud sentences drawn from IndicCorp text, collected through the Karya crowdsourcing platform, and the corpus includes clean and noisy test sets.

chunks.title: Kathbath
chunks.text: Kathbath (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: AI4Bharat built it as the data behind IndicSUPERB, its benchmark of six speech tasks.

chunks.title: Kubeflow Katib
chunks.text: Kubeflow Katib (by Kubeflow), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Kubernetes-native hyperparameter tuning and neural architecture search. An Experiment declares the search space, objective and algorithm; Katib's controllers create Trials, run them in parallel up to a declared limit, collect the objective metric from each and stop the Experiment when the goal or the trial budget is reached.

chunks.title: Kubeflow Katib
chunks.text: Kubeflow Katib (by Kubeflow), catalog entry under ML orchestration: It is framework-agnostic and tunes whatever the trial runs.

chunks.title: Kazakh Speech Corpus 2
chunks.text: Kazakh Speech Corpus 2 (by Institute of Smart Systems and Artificial Intelligence, Nazarbayev University), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Kazakh Speech Corpus 2 (KSC2) provides about 1,200 hours of transcribed Kazakh speech in over 600,000 utterances for speech recognition.

chunks.title: Kazakh Speech Corpus 2
chunks.text: Kazakh Speech Corpus 2 (by Institute of Smart Systems and Artificial Intelligence, Nazarbayev University), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It merges the earlier Kazakh Speech Corpus and Kazakh Text-To-Speech 2 with recordings from TV, radio, the Senate, and podcasts, and includes Kazakh-Russian code-switching.

chunks.title: Kazakh Speech Corpus 2
chunks.text: Kazakh Speech Corpus 2 (by Institute of Smart Systems and Artificial Intelligence, Nazarbayev University), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Institute of Smart Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ISSAI) at Nazarbayev University releases it with an ESPnet training recipe.

chunks.title: KazMMLU
chunks.text: KazMMLU (by Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: KazMMLU tests language models on 23,000 multiple-choice questions in Kazakh and Russian, 10,969 and 12,031 respectively, reflecting Kazakhstan's bilingual education system.

chunks.title: KazMMLU
chunks.text: KazMMLU (by Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The questions cover STEM, humanities, and social sciences in high-school and university material, sourced from authentic educational materials and manually validated by native speakers and educators. MBZUAI researchers built it.

chunks.title: Kencorpus
chunks.text: Kencorpus (by Kencorpus), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Kencorpus is a text and speech corpus for Swahili, Dholuo and Luhya (Lumarachi, Logooli and Lubukusu), gathered from communities, schools, media and publishers: 4,442 texts of about 5.6 million words and 177 hours of spontaneous speech.

chunks.title: Kencorpus
chunks.text: Kencorpus (by Kencorpus), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Companion sets add part-of-speech tags, Swahili question answering, translation into Swahili and a Swahili speech recognition set. The Kencorpus project publishes it.

chunks.title: Keras
chunks.text: Keras (by Google), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Keras is a high-level deep learning framework tagged "Deep Learning for humans"; Keras 3 is multi-backend, running on JAX, TensorFlow, PyTorch, and OpenVINO (inference only). It provides an accessible API for building and training models while letting users choose the underlying backend. It is maintained by the keras-team organization.

chunks.title: Khadas Edge2
chunks.text: Khadas Edge2 (by Khadas (Shenzhen Wesion)), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Credit-card-sized single-board computer built around the Rockchip RK3588S2, an 8nm eight-core 64-bit Arm SoC with a Mali-G610 MP4 GPU and a built-in NPU rated at 6 TOPS.

chunks.title: Khadas Edge2
chunks.text: Khadas Edge2 (by Khadas (Shenzhen Wesion)), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: It ships in Basic and Pro configurations with 8GB or 16GB of memory and 32GB or 64GB of eMMC in a compact fanless design, running Ubuntu and Android with mainline Armbian support.

chunks.title: Khayyam Challenge
chunks.text: Khayyam Challenge (by Raia Center), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Khayyam Challenge, also called PersianMMLU, tests language models on 20,192 four-choice questions in Persian from 38 tasks drawn from Persian examinations, from lower primary to upper secondary school.

chunks.title: Khayyam Challenge
chunks.text: Khayyam Challenge (by Raia Center), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The questions are original rather than translated and carry metadata such as human response rates, difficulty ratings, and descriptive answers. The RAIA Center publishes it.

chunks.title: Khmer ASR Cultural Dataset
chunks.text: Khmer ASR Cultural Dataset (by Digital Divide Data), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Khmer ASR Cultural Dataset is a speech corpus of about 728 hours of Khmer read by native speakers, paired with transcripts, for training speech recognition and related models.

chunks.title: Khmer ASR Cultural Dataset
chunks.text: Khmer ASR Cultural Dataset (by Digital Divide Data), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Twelve speakers from Cambodia (five women, seven men) recorded sentences written around 61 cultural topics and 1,749 subtopics, averaging eight seconds per clip, with speaker gender, age group and origin city attached. Digital Divide Data built and published it.

chunks.title: Khoj
chunks.text: Khoj (by Khoj AI), catalog entry under UI & API: Khoj is a personal assistant that answers over the user's own documents and the web, run on infrastructure the operator controls. It chats with cloud or local models, runs semantic search over PDF, Markdown, org-mode, Word and Notion content, builds custom agents, schedules automations and performs deep research.

chunks.title: Khoj
chunks.text: Khoj (by Khoj AI), catalog entry under UI & API: Clients cover the browser, Obsidian, Emacs and a desktop app.

chunks.title: Kimi K3
chunks.text: Kimi K3 (by Moonshot AI), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Kimi K3 is Moonshot AI's flagship mixture-of-experts model, announced July 16, 2026, with 2.8 trillion total parameters activating sixteen of 896 experts, native vision and a one-million-token context. It is built on Kimi Delta Attention and attention residuals, and runs on kimi.com, Kimi Work, Kimi Code and the Kimi API.

chunks.title: Kimi Code CLI
chunks.text: Kimi Code CLI (by Moonshot AI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Kimi Code CLI is a terminal coding agent that reads and edits code, runs shell commands, searches files and fetches web pages.

chunks.title: Kimi Code CLI
chunks.text: Kimi Code CLI (by Moonshot AI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: It uses Moonshot AI's Kimi models by default and can be pointed at Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible and Gemini providers, dispatches coder, explore and plan sub-agents, and works inside Zed and JetBrains over the Agent Client Protocol. Moonshot AI builds it in TypeScript as the successor to its Python Kimi CLI.

chunks.title: Kimi-VL
chunks.text: Kimi-VL (by Moonshot AI), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Kimi-VL is Moonshot AI's mixture-of-experts vision-language model, activating 2.8B parameters in its language decoder behind the native-resolution MoonViT encoder. It reads images, documents, multi-image sets and long video in a 128K context, and locates and operates interface elements on screen.

chunks.title: Kimi-VL
chunks.text: Kimi-VL (by Moonshot AI), catalog entry under Multimodal models: The Thinking variants add long chain-of-thought reasoning; the line is separate from the general Kimi models.

chunks.title: Klavis AI
chunks.text: Klavis AI (by Klavis AI), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: MCP integration platform: a hosted catalogue of more than a hundred prebuilt servers with OAuth handled for the end user, plus Strata, an open-source aggregator that puts many tools behind one MCP server.

chunks.title: Kokoro
chunks.text: Kokoro (by hexgrad), catalog entry under Speech & audio: An 82-million-parameter open-weight text-to-speech model with dozens of preset voices across English, Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Brazilian Portuguese and Mandarin. Small enough to run on a CPU, it is widely deployed in local apps and commercial APIs.

chunks.title: Kornia
chunks.text: Kornia (by Kornia), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Differentiable computer-vision library for PyTorch, with operators for geometry and camera models, feature detection and matching, filtering, color, augmentation and losses that run batched on GPUs inside training graphs.

chunks.title: Kornia
chunks.text: Kornia (by Kornia), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: It also ships builders for ported pretrained models such as LoFTR, LightGlue, DISK, SAM, YuNet and RT-DETR, a zoo now frozen for expansion. It is a non-profit project funded by sponsorship.

chunks.title: Korpus Malti
chunks.text: Korpus Malti (by Maltese Language Resource Server, University of Malta), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Korpus Malti is a general corpus of written Maltese spanning 19 genres, from parliamentary debates, court proceedings and laws to the press, blogs, theses, literature and Wikipedia. Version 4.0, the data used to train the BERTu model, holds about 466 million tokens in 20.8 million sentences.

chunks.title: Korpus Malti
chunks.text: Korpus Malti (by Maltese Language Resource Server, University of Malta), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Maltese Language Resource Server team at the University of Malta curates it.

chunks.title: KTransformers
chunks.text: KTransformers (by KVCache.AI), catalog entry under Inference code: KTransformers runs very large language models on limited hardware by splitting inference between CPU and GPU, keeping routed experts in DRAM with AMX- and AVX-optimized kernels while the GPU handles the rest.

chunks.title: KTransformers
chunks.text: KTransformers (by KVCache.AI), catalog entry under Inference code: It made DeepSeek-R1 671B runnable on a single 24GB GPU with 382GB of DRAM, supports NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and Ascend backends, and its kt-kernel is being integrated into SGLang. LoRA and full fine-tuning of MoE models through LLaMA-Factory sit alongside the inference path.

chunks.title: Kubeflow Hub (Model Registry)
chunks.text: Kubeflow Hub (Model Registry) (by Kubeflow), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Kubeflow component, formerly called Model Registry, where teams register models, model versions and their artifacts through a REST API and Python client and track them from experimentation to production.

chunks.title: Kubeflow Hub (Model Registry)
chunks.text: Kubeflow Hub (Model Registry) (by Kubeflow), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: The registry stores metadata and the URI of each artifact in S3 or an OCI registry, and its client can upload a local model and register it in one call. A companion catalog lets users browse models from external sources such as Hugging Face before registering them. The component is still marked alpha.

chunks.title: Kubeflow Pipelines
chunks.text: Kubeflow Pipelines (by Kubeflow), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Platform for building and running portable machine-learning workflows on Kubernetes. A pipeline is composed in Python from components whose inputs and outputs are typed ML artifacts - Model, Dataset, Metrics, ClassificationMetrics - and each component runs as a container step with an accelerator type and limit set on it.

chunks.title: Kubeflow Pipelines
chunks.text: Kubeflow Pipelines (by Kubeflow), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Runs, their artifacts and their lineage are tracked in ML Metadata.

chunks.title: Kubeflow Trainer
chunks.text: Kubeflow Trainer (by Kubeflow), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Kubernetes operator for distributed model training and LLM fine-tuning. A TrainJob is a first-class resource describing the trainer, its dataset and model initializers and the number of nodes, and the operator materializes it as a JobSet of pods across the cluster. Runtimes ship for PyTorch, DeepSpeed and MPI-based training.

chunks.title: Kueue
chunks.text: Kueue (by Kubernetes), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Kubernetes-native job queueing from the Kubernetes SIG, deciding when a job waits, when it is admitted so its pods may be created, and when it is preempted. Quotas and fair sharing are expressed per tenant over ResourceFlavors that describe heterogeneous hardware, and Topology-Aware Scheduling can pin a whole PodSet to nodes inside one rack or block.

chunks.title: L3Cube-MahaCorpus
chunks.text: L3Cube-MahaCorpus (by L3Cube Pune), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: L3Cube-MahaCorpus is a Marathi monolingual text corpus of 24.8 million sentences and 289 million tokens scraped from news and other websites. Combined with existing sources it forms a 752-million-token Marathi corpus, on which L3Cube Pune trained its MahaBERT, MahaAlBERT and MahaRoBERTa models and MahaFT word embeddings.

chunks.title: L3Cube-MahaCorpus
chunks.text: L3Cube-MahaCorpus (by L3Cube Pune), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Both versions are Google Drive downloads linked from the MarathiNLP repository.

chunks.title: Lahaja
chunks.text: Lahaja (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Lahaja is a Hindi speech recognition benchmark of 12.5 hours of read and extempore speech from 132 speakers across 83 districts of India, built to test models on regional accents. Each clip carries verbatim and normalized transcripts with the speaker's native language, district and occupation.

chunks.title: Lahaja
chunks.text: Lahaja (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: AI4Bharat built it and released four NeMo baseline models with it.

chunks.title: lakeFS
chunks.text: lakeFS (by Treeverse), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: lakeFS turns an object store into a Git-like repository, giving a data lake branches, commits and atomic merges without copying the underlying objects. It exposes an S3-compatible API over AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage and Google Cloud Storage, so Spark, Hive and similar frameworks read and write versioned data unchanged. Treeverse develops it.

chunks.title: Lakera Guard
chunks.text: Lakera Guard (by Lakera), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Lakera Guard is a real-time API that screens LLM application and agent traffic for prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage, harmful content and off-policy tool use. Check Point, which acquired Lakera, now sells it as AI Guardrails, the runtime layer of its AI Agent Security product, alongside workforce-AI security and red teaming.

chunks.title: Lakera Guard
chunks.text: Lakera Guard (by Lakera), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: It runs as a hosted service or a licensed self-hosted container.

chunks.title: LakeSoul
chunks.text: LakeSoul (by LakeSoul), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: LakeSoul is a cloud-native lakehouse table format and storage framework with a Rust-native metadata and file-IO core, ACID transactions, upsert semantics, schema evolution, automated compaction and fine-grained access control, shared identically across Spark, Flink, Presto, Ray, Daft and PyArrow bindings.

chunks.title: LakeSoul
chunks.text: LakeSoul (by LakeSoul), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Its Vortex file format can store multimodal data and vector embeddings alongside tabular data.

chunks.title: Laminar
chunks.text: Laminar (by Laminar AI), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Observability platform built for AI agents, providing tracing, evaluation and analytics for agentic workflows with an emphasis on debugging multi-step runs. It has a Rust backend and a TypeScript UI, deploys from the repository's docker-compose files, and makes traces, spans, metrics and events queryable with SQL.

chunks.title: LaminDB
chunks.text: LaminDB (by Lamin Labs), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: LaminDB is an open-source data management library for traceable, multimodal AI and life-sciences data. It queries, traces and governs datasets across diverse storage formats and locations through a Django-ORM registry, tracking lineage, branching and versioning over files, tables and arrays without a separate server.

chunks.title: Lamini
chunks.text: Lamini (by AMD), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Lamini is an enterprise fine-tuning and inference platform built around Mixture of Memory Experts (MoME), a technique that trains many LoRA-style memory experts per model to target hallucinations.

chunks.title: Lamini
chunks.text: Lamini (by AMD), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: It ships as an on-demand or reserved hosted service, or as a self-managed deployment on a customer's own GPUs, with a Python client library as the entry point to the tuning engine in every tier.

chunks.title: Lance
chunks.text: Lance (by Lance Format project), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Lance is a columnar table format for multimodal data that keeps random access fast enough to train and query directly against stored rows, rather than requiring a scan-oriented layout. Vector indexes, full-text indexes and dataset versioning are part of the format, and it interoperates with Pandas, DuckDB, Polars, PyArrow, Ray and Spark.

chunks.title: LanceDB
chunks.text: LanceDB (by LanceDB), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: LanceDB is an embedded retrieval database for multimodal data, storing vectors, full text and the underlying records together on top of the Lance columnar format. It runs in the application process with no separate server, indexes on GPU as well as CPU, and reads and writes directly against object storage.

chunks.title: LanceDB
chunks.text: LanceDB (by LanceDB), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Python, TypeScript and Rust bindings ship from the same repository.

chunks.title: LangChain
chunks.text: LangChain (by LangChain), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Framework for building applications over language models, composing chains, agents, memory and a large ecosystem of integrations across model providers, vector stores and tools. It provides the primitives that LangGraph and the surrounding LangChain tooling build on, and is distributed as a set of Python packages.

chunks.title: Langflow
chunks.text: Langflow (by Langflow (DataStax)), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Low-code visual builder for AI agents and RAG workflows. Components are wired on a drag-and-drop canvas and flows are then exposed as APIs or run as agents. Against the code-first frameworks its differentiator is the visual editor with hundreds of pre-built components, while staying model-agnostic and extensible in Python.

chunks.title: Langfuse
chunks.text: Langfuse (by Langfuse), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: LLM engineering platform providing tracing, prompt management, evaluations, cost tracking and datasets, deployable on self-managed infrastructure or as a hosted service. It instruments applications through OpenTelemetry and through direct integrations with LangChain, the OpenAI SDK and LiteLLM.

chunks.title: LangGraph
chunks.text: LangGraph (by LangChain), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Low-level orchestration framework from LangChain for stateful, multi-actor agent applications.

chunks.title: LangGraph
chunks.text: LangGraph (by LangChain), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: It exposes an explicit graph and state-machine model - nodes, edges, persistence and human-in-the-loop checkpoints - rather than a higher-level abstraction, which is what makes fine-grained control over loops, branching and durable resumable execution possible.

chunks.title: LangSmith
chunks.text: LangSmith (by LangChain), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Observability and testing platform from the LangChain team, providing tracing, datasets, evaluations, a prompt hub and annotation queues, alongside deployment and sandbox infrastructure for agents.

chunks.title: LangSmith
chunks.text: LangSmith (by LangChain), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: It integrates tightly with the LangChain ecosystem and instruments any application through OpenTelemetry SDKs, and is offered as managed cloud, a customer-managed cloud (BYOC) option, or a self-hosted enterprise deployment.

chunks.title: Langtrace
chunks.text: Langtrace (by Scale3 Labs), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: OpenTelemetry-based end-to-end observability tool for LLM applications, providing real-time tracing, evaluations and metrics across model providers, frameworks and vector databases, with TypeScript and Python SDKs. It is distinguished by strict OTel compliance and vector-database tracing, and deploys from the repository's docker-compose file.

chunks.title: languagebench
chunks.text: languagebench (by FAIR Forward / Datenlabor BMZ (GIZ)), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Languagebench is an auto-updating multilingual leaderboard and harness that tracks frontier language models across the world's languages, with a deliberate focus on low-resource ones.

chunks.title: languagebench
chunks.text: languagebench (by FAIR Forward / Datenlabor BMZ (GIZ)), catalog entry under Evaluation code: It runs seven tasks - bidirectional translation, classification, MMLU, ARC, TruthfulQA and MGSM - over about forty models via OpenRouter, drawing on FLORES+, Global-MMLU, AfriMMLU, AfriMGSM and Uhura-TruthfulQA and machine-translating English-only sets where none exists.

chunks.title: languagebench
chunks.text: languagebench (by FAIR Forward / Datenlabor BMZ (GIZ)), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Results publish to a Hugging Face Space with a global proficiency map, plus two datasets of aggregated and per-sample tables.

chunks.title: LangWatch
chunks.text: LangWatch (by LangWatch), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Platform for LLM evaluation and agent testing with production monitoring, combining observability traces with automated quality checks and guardrails and dashboards for cost, latency and quality. It runs end-to-end agent simulations against a full stack before release, so evaluation and production observability sit in one loop.

chunks.title: LaoBench
chunks.text: LaoBench (by Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI)), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: LaoBench is a benchmark for testing language models in Lao, with more than 17,000 expert-curated items across three areas: culturally grounded knowledge, K-12 curriculum questions, and translation among Lao, Chinese and English. Experts wrote the items, and an agent-assisted pipeline verified them.

chunks.title: LaoBench
chunks.text: LaoBench (by Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI)), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It comes in an open subset and a held-out subset scored through a controlled service. BAAI publishes it.

chunks.title: LatentSync
chunks.text: LatentSync (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: LatentSync is ByteDance's audio-conditioned latent diffusion model for lip-sync: given a video of a face and a speech track, it regenerates the mouth region so the lips match the audio, supervised by a SyncNet model released with it. The current release, LatentSync 1.6, is trained on 512x512 video.

chunks.title: Latitude
chunks.text: Latitude (by Latitude), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Self-healing AI agent platform providing telemetry-based tracing of multi-turn sessions, tool calls and execution paths, automatic clustering of failing traces into tracked signals, coding-agent dispatch that writes and opens a fix from sample failures, and regression replay against real failing traces to verify the fix held.

chunks.title: Latitude
chunks.text: Latitude (by Latitude), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Self-hostable at any scale on Docker Compose, a Kubernetes Helm chart, or Railway, alongside a hosted cloud with usage-based billing.

chunks.title: Latxa Corpus
chunks.text: Latxa Corpus (by HiTZ Center, University of the Basque Country), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Latxa Corpus is a deduplicated monolingual Basque collection for language model pretraining, combining the EusCrawl web crawl, official gazettes, Basque Parliament transcripts, academic journals, Wikipedia and the Basque portions of CulturaX, HPLT, FineWeb2 and Colossal OSCAR.

chunks.title: Latxa Corpus
chunks.text: Latxa Corpus (by HiTZ Center, University of the Basque Country), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The version behind the first Latxa models held 4.2 billion tokens in 4.3 million documents. HiTZ and the IXA group at the University of the Basque Country build it.

chunks.title: Le Chat
chunks.text: Le Chat (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under UI & API: Le Chat is Mistral's assistant at chat.mistral.ai for individuals, teams and enterprises, offering web search with citations, deep research across the web and connected tools, file and canvas handling for documents, spreadsheets and presentations, image generation and voice input.

chunks.title: Le Chat
chunks.text: Le Chat (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under UI & API: Enterprise customers can deploy it on-premises, in a private cloud or on Mistral Cloud.

chunks.title: LeKiwi
chunks.text: LeKiwi (by SIGRobotics UIUC), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: LeKiwi is a low-cost, 3D-printable mobile manipulator: an SO-101 arm on a three-wheel omnidirectional base with a Raspberry Pi 5 and cameras, designed by SIGRobotics at the University of Illinois with Hugging Face contributors and driven by the LeRobot library.

chunks.title: LeKiwi
chunks.text: LeKiwi (by SIGRobotics UIUC), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: The repository publishes STL files, a URDF and a bill of materials, about $480 for the full robot, and Seeed Studio sells a kit.

chunks.title: Lemonade
chunks.text: Lemonade (by Lemonade SDK), catalog entry under Inference code: Lemonade is a local AI server that runs chat, coding, speech and image models on the user's own NPU and GPU, exposing OpenAI-, Anthropic- and Ollama-compatible APIs that hundreds of apps can connect to. It installs on Windows, macOS and Linux with GGUF and ONNX backends, and an embeddable binary packages the same runtime into other applications.

chunks.title: Lemonade
chunks.text: Lemonade (by Lemonade SDK), catalog entry under Inference code: The community builds it with optimizations from AMD engineers for Ryzen AI, Radeon and Strix Halo PCs.

chunks.title: LeRobot
chunks.text: LeRobot (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: LeRobot is Hugging Face's PyTorch library for learning robot policies from real-world data.

chunks.title: LeRobot
chunks.text: LeRobot (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: It records teleoperated demonstrations into a standard dataset format hosted on the Hugging Face Hub, trains imitation-learning, reinforcement-learning and vision-language-action policies such as ACT, Diffusion Policy, SmolVLA, pi0 and GR00T, and drives low-cost arms through to humanoids.

chunks.title: Letta
chunks.text: Letta (by Letta), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Agent harness for long-lived agents that keep persistent memory and rewrite their own memory blocks, skills and prompts as they work. Letta Code runs as a terminal interface, a desktop app and an App Server that applications reach through the Letta Agent SDK, and its agents can run on schedules, call subagents and answer in Slack, Telegram or Discord.

chunks.title: Letta
chunks.text: Letta (by Letta), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Letta, the team behind MemGPT, builds it.

chunks.title: LettuceDetect
chunks.text: LettuceDetect (by KR Labs), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: LettuceDetect checks whether an AI answer is supported by the source material it was given and marks the exact passages that are not. Small encoder models run locally for fast checks, and a 2B generative model also labels each unsupported passage by type.

chunks.title: LettuceDetect
chunks.text: LettuceDetect (by KR Labs), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: It covers retrieval-augmented answers, coding-agent responses and tool output, and KR Labs publishes it as a Python package with an optional web API.

chunks.title: LFM-VL
chunks.text: LFM-VL (by Liquid AI), catalog entry under Multimodal models: LFM-VL is Liquid AI's family of small vision-language models for on-device use, from 450M to 3B parameters, built on its LFM2 hybrid language models. The models read text and images, including several images at once, and handle OCR, document comprehension, object grounding and screen understanding.

chunks.title: LFM-VL
chunks.text: LFM-VL (by Liquid AI), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Liquid AI ships them with GGUF, ONNX and MLX builds for local inference.

chunks.title: LibreChat
chunks.text: LibreChat (by LibreChat), catalog entry under UI & API: LibreChat is a self-hosted web chat application that puts models from providers such as Anthropic, AWS, OpenAI and Azure behind one interface. It adds agents with MCP tool support, a sandboxed code interpreter, artifacts, web search and multi-user sign-in through OAuth2, SAML or LDAP. ClickHouse acquired the project in 2025 and now stewards it.

chunks.title: Liger Kernel
chunks.text: Liger Kernel (by LinkedIn), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Liger Kernel is a set of Triton kernels for large language model training, replacing fused operations such as RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU and cross-entropy, and adding memory-efficient post-training loss functions for DPO and ORPO. It patches into Hugging Face model classes so existing training scripts pick it up without restructuring.

chunks.title: Liger Kernel
chunks.text: Liger Kernel (by LinkedIn), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: LinkedIn develops it.

chunks.title: lighteval
chunks.text: lighteval (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Evaluation toolkit from Hugging Face's Leaderboard and Evals team, supporting inspect-ai, vLLM, SGLang, transformers and endpoint backends with a focus on speed and easy custom metric authoring. It ships more than a thousand evaluation tasks in the package.

chunks.title: LightGBM
chunks.text: LightGBM (by LightGBM), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Gradient-boosted decision tree library built for speed and memory efficiency, with histogram-based tree learning, leaf-wise growth, GPU training and distributed learning. It handles regression, classification and learning-to-rank from Python, R, C and a command line.

chunks.title: LightGBM
chunks.text: LightGBM (by LightGBM), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Created at Microsoft, it moved in March 2026 to the lightgbm-org account under the same maintainers.

chunks.title: LightLLM
chunks.text: LightLLM (by ModelTC), catalog entry under Inference code: LightLLM is a Python-based LLM inference and serving framework built for a lightweight design and horizontal scalability, drawing on implementations including FasterTransformer, Text Generation Inference, vLLM and FlashAttention.

chunks.title: LightOnOCR
chunks.text: LightOnOCR (by LightOn), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Compact vision-language OCR model from LightOn, released at around one billion parameters and trained end-to-end to turn page images into markdown-formatted text. Its argument is throughput: it targets the accuracy of far larger document models at a fraction of the inference cost.

chunks.title: Lightpanda
chunks.text: Lightpanda (by Lightpanda), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Headless browser written in Zig for agent and automation workloads, implementing the DOM and a JavaScript runtime through V8 without rendering pixels, so pages are executed rather than drawn. Speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol, so Playwright and Puppeteer clients drive it in place of Chrome.

chunks.title: LightRAG
chunks.text: LightRAG (by HKU Data Science Lab), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Lightweight graph-based RAG framework from HKU's Data Science Lab that combines a knowledge graph with vector embeddings through dual-level retrieval. It drops GraphRAG's expensive community-report step and supports incremental updates, so new data can be added without rebuilding the global index.

chunks.title: LightRAG
chunks.text: LightRAG (by HKU Data Science Lab), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: It ships naive, local, global and hybrid query modes, pluggable storage, an API server and a web UI.

chunks.title: Linkup
chunks.text: Linkup (by Linkup), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Web search API for agents. One `/search` route takes a natural-language query and returns, at the caller's election, ranked sources with content snippets, a cited natural-language answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema; `/fetch` renders a named URL to markdown and `/research` runs the same pipeline asynchronously for long-form questions.

chunks.title: LiteLLM
chunks.text: LiteLLM (by BerriAI), catalog entry under UI & API: Python SDK and proxy server exposing one OpenAI-format API across a large set of LLM providers including Bedrock, Azure, Vertex, Anthropic, Cohere and vLLM. The proxy translates calls to the chat-completions and responses endpoints and adds routing, fallbacks, virtual keys, guardrails and spend tracking, which is what makes it usable as an organization-wide gateway.

chunks.title: LiteRT-LM
chunks.text: LiteRT-LM (by Google), catalog entry under Inference code: LiteRT-LM is Google's orchestration layer for running language models with LiteRT on edge devices, engineered for cross-platform on-device execution rather than datacenter serving. It is distributed as a command-line tool and as prebuilt C API shared libraries.

chunks.title: LitGPT
chunks.text: LitGPT (by Lightning AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: LitGPT is a library of 20+ from-scratch implementations of open LLMs, including Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Phi, and Qwen, with recipes for pretraining, fine-tuning (full, LoRA, QLoRA, Adapter/Adapter v2), and deployment. Each model is a single file with no abstraction layer, extending nanoGPT and Lit-LLaMA.

chunks.title: LitGPT
chunks.text: LitGPT (by Lightning AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Lightning AI builds it on Lightning Fabric, with Flash Attention, FSDP across 1 to 1,000+ GPUs or TPUs, and 4/8-bit quantization.

chunks.title: LiveBench
chunks.text: LiveBench (by LiveBench), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Contamination-limited language-model benchmark with objective ground-truth answers and automatic scoring rather than judge models, spanning math, coding, reasoning, language, instruction following and data analysis. New questions are released monthly and older ones retired to limit contamination.

chunks.title: LiveBench
chunks.text: LiveBench (by LiveBench), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Built by Abacus.AI with NYU, Nvidia, UMD and USC, and published as an ICLR 2025 spotlight.

chunks.title: LiveCodeBench
chunks.text: LiveCodeBench (by LiveCodeBench Team), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Continuously updated coding benchmark that collects fresh problems from LeetCode, Codeforces and AtCoder after a model's training cutoff, so evaluation stays contamination-free. It covers code generation, self-repair, execution and test-output prediction, and ships release-versioned snapshots with hidden test cases bundled.

chunks.title: LivePortrait
chunks.text: LivePortrait (by Kuaishou), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: LivePortrait is a portrait-animation model from Kuaishou's Kling research team that turns a single still image of a face, human or animal, into video driven by the expressions and head pose of a reference clip.

chunks.title: LivePortrait
chunks.text: LivePortrait (by Kuaishou), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: It uses implicit keypoints with stitching and retargeting control rather than diffusion, which makes it fast enough for real-time use, and supports video-to-video editing and regional control.

chunks.title: Llama 4 Scout / Maverick
chunks.text: Llama 4 Scout / Maverick (by Meta), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Llama 4 is Meta's natively multimodal mixture-of-experts family, released in April 2025. Scout has 17B active and 109B total parameters with a 10M-token context, and Maverick has 17B active and 400B total parameters with a 1M-token context. The larger Behemoth model has not been released.

chunks.title: llama.cpp
chunks.text: llama.cpp (by ggml-org (Georgi Gerganov)), catalog entry under Inference code: llama.cpp runs LLM and VLM inference in portable, dependency-free C/C++, across CPUs and GPU backends including CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, SYCL, and HIP. It supports 1.5-bit through 8-bit integer quantization and the GGUF format used widely for local model distribution, from servers down to Android phones.

chunks.title: llama.cpp
chunks.text: llama.cpp (by ggml-org (Georgi Gerganov)), catalog entry under Inference code: The ggml-org organization maintains it, and its ggml.ai team joined Hugging Face in February 2026.

chunks.title: LlamaFactory
chunks.text: LlamaFactory, catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: LlamaFactory is a toolkit for fine-tuning 100+ open LLM and vision-language architectures, including LLaMA, Qwen, DeepSeek, Gemma, and GLM. It covers continued pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, reward modeling, and preference or RL methods such as PPO, DPO, KTO, and ORPO, across full, LoRA, and QLoRA tuning.

chunks.title: LlamaFactory
chunks.text: LlamaFactory, catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: A CLI and the Gradio-based LLaMA Board web UI run the same pipeline without custom code, and the project appeared as an ACL 2024 paper.

chunks.title: Llama Guard
chunks.text: Llama Guard (by Meta), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Meta's input and output safety classifier built on Llama 3.1 8B. It labels both prompts and responses across fourteen hazard categories aligned to the MLCommons taxonomy - violent crime, child exploitation, hate, self-harm, code-interpreter abuse and others - in eight languages.

chunks.title: LlamaIndex
chunks.text: LlamaIndex (by LlamaIndex), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Data framework in Python and TypeScript for building LLM applications over private data. It provides connectors across APIs, PDFs, documents and SQL, indices, retrievers, query engines and reranking, and an agent and workflows orchestration layer.

chunks.title: LlamaIndex
chunks.text: LlamaIndex (by LlamaIndex), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Its depth is in retrieval and ingestion - document agents, many-format parsing and structured extraction.

chunks.title: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
chunks.text: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (by Meta), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is an instruction-tuned 8-billion-parameter Llama 3.1 model for chat and assistant workflows, post-trained with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with human feedback on Meta's Llama 3.1 base. It supports a 128K-token context window.

chunks.title: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
chunks.text: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (by Meta), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Weights are gated behind a manual access request rather than an open download.

chunks.title: Llama Prompt Guard 2
chunks.text: Llama Prompt Guard 2 (by Meta), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Llama Prompt Guard 2 is Meta's compact classifier for prompt injection and jailbreaks, labeling prompts as benign or malicious. It is part of LlamaFirewall and was evaluated in eight languages.

chunks.title: Llama Prompt Guard 2
chunks.text: Llama Prompt Guard 2 (by Meta), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Of its two sizes, the 86M model classifies a 512-token prompt in about 92 ms on an A100, and the 22M model cuts latency by about three quarters at some cost in recall.

chunks.title: Llamacha monolingual Quechua corpus
chunks.text: Llamacha monolingual Quechua corpus (by Llamacha), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Monolingual-Quechua-IIC is a Southern Quechua text corpus for training language models, collected mainly from the southern region of Peru and combined with the Quechua portions of Wikipedia and OSCAR.

chunks.title: Llamacha monolingual Quechua corpus
chunks.text: Llamacha monolingual Quechua corpus (by Llamacha), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Its authors used it to train QuBERT, a BERT model for Quechua, and tested that on named-entity recognition and part-of-speech tagging. The Llamacha group released it.

chunks.title: llamafile
chunks.text: llamafile (by Mozilla AI), catalog entry under Inference code: llamafile packages a large language model and the software to run it into a single cross-platform executable that runs without installation on macOS, Linux, BSD, and Windows. It combines llama.cpp with Cosmopolitan Libc to produce one file that works across operating systems and CPU architectures.

chunks.title: llamafile
chunks.text: llamafile (by Mozilla AI), catalog entry under Inference code: Originally a Mozilla Builders project, it is now maintained by Mozilla.ai and ships a companion single-file speech-to-text tool, whisperfile.

chunks.title: LlamaFirewall
chunks.text: LlamaFirewall (by Meta), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Meta's open, system-level guardrail framework for AI agents (part of PurpleLlama). It composes layered defenses: Prompt Guard 2 (jailbreak/injection detection), Agent Alignment Checks (detecting goal hijacking), and CodeShield (filtering insecure generated code), into a real-time firewall around agent execution.

chunks.title: LLaVA
chunks.text: LLaVA (by LMMs-Lab), catalog entry under Multimodal models: LLaVA is the open vision-language model line that began with visual instruction tuning and continued through LLaVA-NeXT and LLaVA-OneVision. The current LLaVA-OneVision-2 is an 8B model on a Qwen3 base that handles single images, multi-image sets and long video, and is released with its data, vision encoders, training code and logs.

chunks.title: LLaVA
chunks.text: LLaVA (by LMMs-Lab), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Hugging Face maintains transformers conversions of the earlier releases.

chunks.title: LLM (Datasette)
chunks.text: LLM (Datasette) (by Datasette), catalog entry under UI & API: Command-line tool and Python library for prompting large language models. It provides one CLI and API across remote providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini and across local models, with a plugin architecture for new backends. Prompts and responses are logged to a local SQLite database, and it supports embeddings and templated prompts.

chunks.title: LLM (Datasette)
chunks.text: LLM (Datasette) (by Datasette), catalog entry under UI & API: Part of Simon Willison's Datasette ecosystem.

chunks.title: LLM Compressor
chunks.text: LLM Compressor (by vLLM (UC Berkeley / vLLM team)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: LLM Compressor applies quantization and pruning to large language models for deployment with vLLM, covering weight, activation, KV-cache and attention quantization along with algorithms such as SmoothQuant and GPTQ.

chunks.title: LLM Compressor
chunks.text: LLM Compressor (by vLLM (UC Berkeley / vLLM team)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: It reads and writes Hugging Face models, saves in the compressed-tensors format vLLM loads, and supports distributed and disk-offloaded compression of models too large for one device.

chunks.title: llm-d
chunks.text: llm-d (by llm-d project), catalog entry under Inference code: llm-d is a distributed inference serving stack for Kubernetes, built above model servers like vLLM to serve production traffic across accelerators.

chunks.title: llm-d
chunks.text: llm-d (by llm-d project), catalog entry under Inference code: It routes requests on prefix cache and load signals, tiers KV cache to CPU and disk, disaggregates prefill and decode, and autoscales against latency objectives, shipping as benchmarked Helm-based well-lit paths. It is a CNCF Sandbox project founded by Red Hat, Google Cloud, IBM Research, CoreWeave and NVIDIA.

chunks.title: LLM Guard
chunks.text: LLM Guard (by Protect AI), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: LLM Guard is a security toolkit for LLM interactions from Protect AI, providing input and output scanners for prompt injection, PII and data leakage, secrets, toxicity, bias and harmful content, with detection and sanitization. It runs as a self-hosted Python library or is deployed as an API.

chunks.title: lm-evaluation-harness
chunks.text: lm-evaluation-harness (by EleutherAI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Unified framework for evaluating language models across more than 60 academic benchmarks with hundreds of subtasks, including MMLU, ARC, GSM8K and HellaSwag, driven by a single config-based CLI. It was the backend behind the Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard and has been used in hundreds of papers to report reproducible benchmark numbers.

chunks.title: LM Studio
chunks.text: LM Studio (by LM Studio), catalog entry under UI & API: LM Studio is a desktop application for discovering, downloading and running large language models locally on macOS, Windows and Linux. It provides a chat interface, a Hugging Face model browser, an OpenAI-compatible local server, an MCP client, and llama.cpp and Apple MLX runtimes.

chunks.title: LM Studio
chunks.text: LM Studio (by LM Studio), catalog entry under UI & API: The same core ships as llmster, a headless daemon for servers and continuous integration, alongside TypeScript and Python SDKs and the lms command-line tool. Element Labs builds it.

chunks.title: LMDeploy
chunks.text: LMDeploy (by Shanghai AI Laboratory), catalog entry under Inference code: LMDeploy is a toolkit for compressing, deploying, and serving large language models, built by the InternLM team at Shanghai AI Laboratory. It provides two inference engines: TurboMind, which pairs persistent batching with a blocked KV cache and custom CUDA kernels, and a pure-Python PyTorch engine.

chunks.title: LMDeploy
chunks.text: LMDeploy (by Shanghai AI Laboratory), catalog entry under Inference code: Both support weight-only and KV-cache quantization, across families including Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, and vision-language models such as InternVL.

chunks.title: lmms-eval
chunks.text: lmms-eval (by LMMs-Lab), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Multimodal counterpart to lm-evaluation-harness, evaluating vision, video and audio language models across 100+ tasks and 30+ model families through the same config-driven CLI. EleutherAI's harness README points multimodal users here, and recent releases added an HTTP eval server, agentic task evaluation and audio benchmarks.

chunks.title: Lobe Chat
chunks.text: Lobe Chat (by LobeHub), catalog entry under UI & API: Chat framework supporting OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Ollama, Azure and DeepSeek among others, with knowledge bases, vision and text-to-speech, an MCP skill marketplace, agent groups and memory. It offers one-click deployment for self-hosting alongside a hosted tier. The repository has been rebranded from lobe-chat to lobehub.

chunks.title: LocalAI
chunks.text: LocalAI (by Mudler (LocalAI)), catalog entry under Inference code: LocalAI is a self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible inference engine that runs LLMs plus vision, image, audio, and video models on commodity hardware, with no GPU required. Dozens of backends, including llama.cpp, vLLM, whisper.cpp, diffusers, and MLX, sit behind one unified API, with built-in agents, RAG, and Model Context Protocol support.

chunks.title: LocalAI
chunks.text: LocalAI (by Mudler (LocalAI)), catalog entry under Inference code: Ettore Di Giacinto created it; the LocalAI team now maintains it.

chunks.title: Pydantic Logfire
chunks.text: Pydantic Logfire (by Pydantic), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: AI and application observability platform from the Pydantic team, built on OpenTelemetry, providing agent and LLM tracing, prompt management with versioning and rollout, live evaluations, datasets and experiments, and SQL querying over recorded traces, metrics and logs.

chunks.title: Pydantic Logfire
chunks.text: Pydantic Logfire (by Pydantic), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: The Python, TypeScript and Rust SDKs are open source and can export to any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend; the Logfire platform itself - the UI and the server that records and displays the data - is closed source, with self-hosting available only under a purchased enterprise license.

chunks.title: Lovable
chunks.text: Lovable (by Lovable), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Agentic app and website builder driven from a chat interface, taking a prototype through to a deployed application. It covers file generation, design, a managed cloud backend, testing, security, connectors, git sync and a managed npm registry. It was formerly called GPT Engineer.

chunks.title: LTX
chunks.text: LTX (by Lightricks), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: LTX is Lightricks' family of diffusion-transformer video models. The current LTX-2 line, up to the 22B LTX-2.5, generates synchronized video and audio in one model from text, image, video or audio input, with native output at 1024 by 1536 and a 4K upscaling path; the earlier LTX-Video models were built for speed.

chunks.title: LTX
chunks.text: LTX (by Lightricks), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Lightricks also publishes a trainer for LoRA and full fine-tuning.

chunks.title: Lucie 7B
chunks.text: Lucie 7B (by Linagora), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Linagora and OpenLLM-France's fully open multilingual 7B foundation model on the Llama 3.1 architecture, trained on roughly three trillion tokens with about equal French and English shares plus German, Spanish, Italian and code.

chunks.title: Lucie 7B
chunks.text: Lucie 7B (by Linagora), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: The weights ship with the Lucie Training Dataset, the Megatron-DeepSpeed training code and intermediate checkpoints as repository branches.

chunks.title: Luciole
chunks.text: Luciole (by Linagora), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Luciole is Linagora and OpenLLM-France's fully open French-English model family and the successor to Lucie, released at 1B, 8B and 23B in base and instruct forms. The weights ship with a 4.65-trillion-token training dataset drawn from openly licensed corpora, the training pipeline and training checkpoints.

chunks.title: Luciole
chunks.text: Luciole (by Linagora), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Base models are pretrained on about 5 trillion tokens, roughly 42 percent English and 30 percent French alongside six other languages.

chunks.title: Proton Lumo
chunks.text: Proton Lumo (by Proton), catalog entry under UI & API: Privacy-focused AI assistant from Proton with zero-access encryption, a no-logs policy and a ghost mode that discards conversations on close. It runs open-weights models in Proton's European data centers rather than sending prompts to third-party providers, and requires no account.

chunks.title: Lyria
chunks.text: Lyria (by Google), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Lyria is Google DeepMind's music generation model line, which produces full-length songs with vocals and instrumental clips from text prompts. It is served through the Gemini API and in Google products including Gemini, YouTube Shorts and Flow, alongside a real-time variant for interactive generation.

chunks.title: MACE
chunks.text: MACE (by ACEsuit), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: MACE is ACEsuit's equivariant message-passing framework for machine-learning interatomic potentials, shipping a full data-preprocessing, training, and fine-tuning pipeline alongside a series of pretrained foundation models covering 89 elements.

chunks.title: MACE
chunks.text: MACE (by ACEsuit), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: The foundation checkpoints span inorganic materials, organic molecules, electrostatics, and cross-domain models, and are released under different licences from the code.

chunks.title: MADLAD-400
chunks.text: MADLAD-400 (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Document-level multilingual web corpus derived from Common Crawl and covering 419 languages, built by Google researchers and hosted by the Allen Institute for AI.

chunks.title: MADLAD-400
chunks.text: MADLAD-400 (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: It ships in a noisy variant filtered only by language identification and a clean quality-filtered variant of roughly 3 trillion tokens, with a focus on low-resource languages. It underpins the MADLAD-400 machine-translation models.

chunks.title: Magistral
chunks.text: Magistral (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Mistral's reasoning model line, launched June 2025 in two tiers: the open-weight Magistral Small, a 24B model distilled from Magistral Medium traces with RL on top, and the API-only Magistral Medium. The current Small 1.2 adds a vision encoder and reasons in a dedicated thinking block, and fits on a single consumer GPU once quantized.

chunks.title: ManiSkill
chunks.text: ManiSkill (by ManiSkill), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: ManiSkill is a GPU-parallel robot simulation and training framework built on the SAPIEN engine.

chunks.title: ManiSkill
chunks.text: ManiSkill (by ManiSkill), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: It renders RGB-D and segmentation observations at tens of thousands of frames per second on one GPU, lets every parallel environment hold a different scene, and ships manipulation, mobile-manipulation and humanoid tasks with real-to-sim environments for evaluating real-world policies.

chunks.title: Maple AI
chunks.text: Maple AI (by OpenSecret), catalog entry under UI & API: End-to-end encrypted AI chat assistant. Conversations are encrypted on the device and processed inside hardware-isolated Trusted Execution Environments, so the operator cannot read them; remote attestation lets users check the running build against published source.

chunks.title: Maple AI
chunks.text: Maple AI (by OpenSecret), catalog entry under UI & API: It serves open-weights models and ships as apps for major platforms, built on the OpenSecret confidential-computing platform.

chunks.title: Marin
chunks.text: Marin (by Stanford CRFM), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Marin is a fully open foundation-model line (Marin 8B Base and Instruct, Marin 32B Base) trained in JAX with the Levanter framework, with bit-for-bit reproducible training. Code, data mixtures, experiments, hyperparameters and training logs are published alongside the weights, and every experiment is tracked as a public GitHub issue.

chunks.title: Marin
chunks.text: Marin (by Stanford CRFM), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: The project began at Stanford CRFM and is now primarily developed by Open Athena.

chunks.title: Marin (framework)
chunks.text: Marin (framework) (by Stanford CRFM), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Open framework for reproducible foundation-model development that tracks every step from raw data to final model: data curation, transformation, filtering, tokenization, training, evaluation, and experiment/mixture orchestration. Distinct from the Marin model it produces.

chunks.title: Marker
