chunks.text: Marker (by Datalab), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Document conversion pipeline that turns PDFs, images, Office documents and EPUB into Markdown, JSON and HTML, running layout analysis, table and equation recognition and OCR through a stack of purpose-trained models. Published by Datalab alongside a hosted API and an on-premises offering.

chunks.title: MarkItDown
chunks.text: MarkItDown (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Lightweight Python utility from Microsoft for converting files and office documents - PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images (OCR), audio (transcription), HTML, CSV/JSON/XML, ZIP, EPub, even YouTube URLs - into Markdown optimized for LLMs and agents.

chunks.title: MarkItDown
chunks.text: MarkItDown (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Offers CLI, Python API, Docker, and a plugin system, with optional Azure Document Intelligence and LLM-vision for image descriptions.

chunks.title: Masader
chunks.text: Masader (by ARBML), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: Masader is a public catalog of Arabic text and speech datasets, describing each with more than two dozen attributes such as dialect, domain, source, annotation method and license, and linking to where its publisher hosts it. New entries are submitted through a form and added by the maintainers.

chunks.title: Masader
chunks.text: Masader (by ARBML), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: It began in the BigScience workshop and is maintained by the ARBML community.

chunks.title: Mastra
chunks.text: Mastra (by Mastra), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: TypeScript-native framework for building agents and agentic applications. It covers agents with tools and instructions, graph-based workflows with explicit control flow, conversation memory with semantic recall, model routing across many providers, and built-in evaluations, tracing and human-in-the-loop.

chunks.title: Mastra
chunks.text: Mastra (by Mastra), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: It runs on Node.js, integrates with React and Next.js, or deploys as a standalone server.

chunks.title: MATH
chunks.text: MATH (by Hendrycks et al. (UC Berkeley)), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Benchmark of 12,500 competition mathematics problems, split into 7,500 training and 5,000 test problems, each with a full step-by-step solution. It accompanies the paper Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset.

chunks.title: Mathpix
chunks.text: Mathpix (by Mathpix), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Document-conversion service specialising in scientific and mathematical content. It converts PDFs, images and handwriting into LaTeX, Markdown, DOCX and HTML, and is the reference tool for documents whose value is in the equations rather than the prose.

chunks.title: MatrixHub
chunks.text: MatrixHub (by DaoCloud), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Self-hosted model registry that works as a drop-in private replacement for Hugging Face Hub in inference infrastructure. Pointing HF_ENDPOINT at it lets the hf CLI, vLLM, SGLang and Dynamo download and upload models, and repositories are reachable over Git, Git LFS and HTTP with project-scoped permissions and version management.

chunks.title: MatrixHub
chunks.text: MatrixHub (by DaoCloud), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: It can cache public Hugging Face models on first request, on local or NFS storage. Most of its maintainers work at DaoCloud, and the project describes itself as community-led.

chunks.title: MatterGen
chunks.text: MatterGen (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: MatterGen is Microsoft's diffusion model for generating inorganic crystal structures across the periodic table. It ships an unconditional base model and property-conditioned adaptations, along with training data, preprocessing code, a full training pipeline, and evaluation tooling for novelty and predicted stability.

chunks.title: MatterSim
chunks.text: MatterSim (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: MatterSim is Microsoft's deep-learning atomistic model for bulk materials, acting as a machine-learning force field across the periodic table for temperatures from 0 to 5000 K and pressures up to 1000 GPa.

chunks.title: MatterSim
chunks.text: MatterSim (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: It ships 1M- and 5M-parameter M3GNet checkpoints in the repository, with a fine-tuning script for adapting the model to a custom dataset or a higher level of theory.

chunks.title: MAX
chunks.text: MAX (by Modular), catalog entry under Inference code: MAX is an inference engine built on the Mojo programming language that serves LLMs and other models across NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple GPUs plus CPUs from a single codebase. A graph compiler optimizes model execution for the target hardware, and it serves PyTorch and Hugging Face models through OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

chunks.title: MAX
chunks.text: MAX (by Modular), catalog entry under Inference code: Modular, the company founded by LLVM and Swift creator Chris Lattner, develops and distributes it.

chunks.title: MBPP
chunks.text: MBPP (by Google Research), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Mostly Basic Python Problems: 974 crowd-sourced Python tasks solvable by an entry-level programmer, each with a task description, a reference solution and three automated test cases, plus a 427-problem hand-verified subset.

chunks.title: MBPP
chunks.text: MBPP (by Google Research), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Where HumanEval tests function-level generation from a detailed docstring, MBPP tests natural-language-to-code translation across a broader difficulty range.

chunks.title: MCP Apps
chunks.text: MCP Apps (by Model Context Protocol project), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: An extension to the Model Context Protocol, with its own dated specification and SDK, letting a tool declare a `ui://` resource carrying an HTML interface that the host renders in a sandboxed iframe and communicates with bidirectionally.

chunks.title: MCP C# SDK
chunks.text: MCP C# SDK (by Model Context Protocol project), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: The official C# SDK for the Model Context Protocol, maintained in collaboration with Microsoft. Client and server, all three primitives, and stdio, Streamable HTTP and legacy SSE transports.

chunks.title: MCP Go
chunks.text: MCP Go (by Mark III Labs), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: MCP Go is a Go implementation of the Model Context Protocol, letting developers build servers and clients that expose resources, tools and prompts to LLM applications.

chunks.title: MCP Go
chunks.text: MCP Go (by Mark III Labs), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: It handles protocol compliance and message routing, supports stdio, SSE and streamable HTTP transports plus OAuth-protected resources, and implements an earlier revision of the Model Context Protocol specification, with backward compatibility to an even earlier revision. Maintained by Mark III Labs.

chunks.title: MCP Go SDK (official)
chunks.text: MCP Go SDK (official) (by Model Context Protocol project), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: The official Go SDK for the Model Context Protocol, maintained in collaboration with Google. Implements client and server, all three primitives and every standard transport, against the current specification revision.

chunks.title: MCP Inspector
chunks.text: MCP Inspector (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: MCP Inspector is a developer tool for testing and debugging MCP servers. One npm package and one binary run three clients, a React web UI with a Node backend, a scriptable CLI for automation and CI, and an Ink terminal UI. It handles OAuth and stores client secrets in the OS keychain where one is available.

chunks.title: MCP Java SDK
chunks.text: MCP Java SDK (by Model Context Protocol project), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: The official Java SDK for the Model Context Protocol, maintained in collaboration with Spring AI. Synchronous and asynchronous client and server over stdio, Server-Sent Events and Streamable HTTP, validated against the MCP conformance suite.

chunks.title: MCP Kotlin SDK
chunks.text: MCP Kotlin SDK (by Model Context Protocol project), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: The official Kotlin SDK for the Model Context Protocol, maintained in collaboration with JetBrains. Client and server, all three primitives, and four transports including WebSocket.

chunks.title: MCP PHP SDK
chunks.text: MCP PHP SDK (by Model Context Protocol project), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: The official PHP SDK for the Model Context Protocol, maintained with The PHP Foundation. Framework-agnostic client and server covering tools, resources and prompts over stdio and HTTP, measured weekly against the MCP conformance suite.

chunks.title: MCP Python SDK
chunks.text: MCP Python SDK (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: Official Python implementation of the Model Context Protocol for building MCP clients and servers that give LLMs standardized access to tools, resources, and prompts. Speaks every standard transport - stdio, Streamable HTTP and SSE - and ships an `mcp` CLI for developing, running and installing servers.

chunks.title: Official MCP Registry
chunks.text: Official MCP Registry (by Model Context Protocol project), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: The Model Context Protocol's own catalogue of MCP servers - an API and a hosted service that lists what servers exist and how to reach them, with a publishing flow for server authors. Run by the protocol's maintainers rather than a vendor.

chunks.title: MCP Rust SDK
chunks.text: MCP Rust SDK (by Model Context Protocol project), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: The official Rust SDK for the Model Context Protocol, published as the `rmcp` crate. Implements client and server against the current specification revision, with a deliberate decision not to ship the legacy two-endpoint HTTP+SSE transport.

chunks.title: MCP Swift SDK
chunks.text: MCP Swift SDK (by Model Context Protocol project), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: The official Swift SDK for the Model Context Protocol. Client and server across tools, resources and prompts, with stdio, Streamable HTTP and in-process transports, implemented against an earlier specification revision rather than the current one.

chunks.title: MCP TypeScript SDK
chunks.text: MCP TypeScript SDK (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: Official TypeScript SDK for the Model Context Protocol, running on Node.js, Bun and Deno. It publishes separate server and client packages covering tools, resources and prompts, Streamable HTTP and stdio transports and auth helpers, plus thin middleware packages for Express, Fastify, Hono and Node.js HTTP.

chunks.title: MCP Bundles
chunks.text: MCP Bundles (by Model Context Protocol project), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: A packaging format for local MCP servers: a zip archive carrying the server and a manifest describing it, so a desktop application can install one in a single click. Ships the bundle specification, a CLI that builds bundles, and the loader desktop clients use to verify them.

chunks.title: MediaPipe
chunks.text: MediaPipe (by Google), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Google's framework and ready-made solutions for on-device machine learning on Android, iOS, the web and Python.

chunks.title: MediaPipe
chunks.text: MediaPipe (by Google), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Its Tasks APIs run pretrained models for face detection and landmarks, hand and pose landmarks, gesture recognition, holistic tracking, object detection, image classification, embedding and segmentation, interactive segmentation, audio and text classification and language detection, and it adds on-device LLM inference.

chunks.title: MediaPipe
chunks.text: MediaPipe (by Google), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Some solutions can be retrained with the Model Maker tool, which is no longer actively maintained.

chunks.title: MediaWiki Search API
chunks.text: MediaWiki Search API (by Wikimedia Foundation), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: The search surface of the MediaWiki Action API, served at the `api.php` endpoint of every MediaWiki site, including Wikipedia and Wikinews, which answer it for anonymous callers.

chunks.title: MediaWiki Search API
chunks.text: MediaWiki Search API (by Wikimedia Foundation), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Its `list=search` module returns ranked page titles with highlighted snippets and page metadata, and can run as a generator that passes its results to the TextExtracts module, which returns plain-text extracts of the pages found. On Wikimedia's wikis it is backed by the CirrusSearch extension over an OpenSearch index.

chunks.title: Megatron-LM
chunks.text: Megatron-LM (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Megatron-LM trains transformer models across large GPU clusters, pairing pre-configured training scripts with Megatron Core, a composable library of GPU-optimized building blocks.

chunks.title: Megatron-LM
chunks.text: Megatron-LM (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Megatron Core supplies tensor, pipeline, data, expert, and context parallelism, mixed-precision training, and distributed checkpointing for teams building their own training frameworks. NVIDIA develops both in the open, alongside a Megatron Bridge converter for Hugging Face checkpoints.

chunks.title: Meilisearch
chunks.text: Meilisearch (by Meili SAS), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Meilisearch is a search engine exposed as an HTTP API, offering typo-tolerant full-text search with faceting, filtering and geosearch, and semantic and hybrid search over embeddings produced by third-party embedding models it calls. It is written in Rust and runs as a single binary or on the vendor's hosted service. Meili SAS develops it.

chunks.title: MeloTTS
chunks.text: MeloTTS (by MyShell), catalog entry under Speech & audio: A multilingual text-to-speech library from MyShell and MIT, with voices for several English accents, Spanish, French, Chinese mixed with English, Japanese and Korean, fast enough for real-time synthesis on a CPU.

chunks.title: MemryX MX3
chunks.text: MemryX MX3 (by MemryX), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Edge AI accelerator from MemryX in the United States, built on a dataflow architecture where each MX3 chip provides about 6 TOPS and an M.2 2280 M-key module packs four of them for up to 24 TOPS at roughly 6 to 8 watts with passive cooling. It connects over PCIe Gen3 and supports 4, 8 and 16-bit weights alongside BFloat16, with no model-zoo lock-in.

chunks.title: Meshy
chunks.text: Meshy (by Meshy), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Meshy is a hosted 3D generation service that turns text descriptions, images and conversational prompts into textured, game-ready 3D models, with remeshing, texturing, rigging and animation tools. It is used through the Meshy web app and plugins and through a REST API that exposes every generation capability to developers.

chunks.title: Meta AI
chunks.text: Meta AI (by Meta), catalog entry under UI & API: Meta's consumer AI assistant, embedded in WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger alongside a standalone web app at meta.ai and native mobile apps. It plans multi-step tasks, connects to email and calendar apps and creates slides. Meta builds and operates the service.

chunks.title: Metaflow
chunks.text: Metaflow (by Netflix), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Python framework from Netflix for building and operating machine-learning and AI systems. A flow is a class of steps; decorators attach resources, retries and checkpoints to each step, and @batch or @kubernetes send that step to AWS Batch or a Kubernetes cluster to run.

chunks.title: Metaflow
chunks.text: Metaflow (by Netflix), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Metaflow tracks every run, its artifacts and its models, and can resume a failed flow from the step that failed.

chunks.title: Microsoft Copilot
chunks.text: Microsoft Copilot (by Microsoft), catalog entry under UI & API: Microsoft's Copilot chat surface on Windows, the web and mobile, and embedded across Microsoft 365 in Word, Excel, Teams and Outlook. It runs over models from Microsoft and, in licensed Microsoft 365 experiences, Anthropic, and grounds answers in Microsoft Graph content across those applications.

chunks.title: Midjourney
chunks.text: Midjourney (by Midjourney), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Midjourney is an independent research lab's image generation service, used through its website and Discord. Its models generate images from text and image prompts with style and mood references, and the service adds image editing and an image-to-video mode that animates still images into short clips.

chunks.title: Mila Suicide Prevention Guardrail
chunks.text: Mila Suicide Prevention Guardrail (by Mila), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Mila Suicide Prevention Guardrail is a BERT-based classifier that reads a chatbot's reply and flags it when the reply enables, encourages or endorses suicide, self-injury or disordered eating, following the MLCommons AILuminate definition of that harm.

chunks.title: Mila Suicide Prevention Guardrail
chunks.text: Mila Suicide Prevention Guardrail (by Mila), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: It checks English assistant responses one at a time, not user messages, and is small enough to run on a CPU. Mila's AI Safety Studio built it with ROOST.

chunks.title: Miles
chunks.text: Miles (by RadixArk), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Miles is a reinforcement learning framework for post-training large language and vision-language models. It pairs SGLang for rollout generation with Megatron-LM for training and offers a PyTorch FSDP2 backend as an alternative, with rollout and training workers decoupled so runs can be fully asynchronous. It is a fork of slime, maintained by RadixArk.

chunks.title: MILU
chunks.text: MILU (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: MILU (Multi-task Indic Language Understanding Benchmark) is an evaluation set of about 80,000 multiple-choice questions in 10 Indic languages and English, spanning 8 domains and 41 subjects.

chunks.title: MILU
chunks.text: MILU (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Its questions come largely from regional and state examinations, about a quarter of them translated, and cover India-specific topics such as local history, arts and law. AI4Bharat publishes it with an lm-evaluation-harness setup for running it.

chunks.title: Milvus
chunks.text: Milvus (by Zilliz), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Milvus is a distributed vector database for approximate nearest-neighbor search over billions of vectors. Hybrid search combines vector similarity with scalar filtering and BM25 full-text search, over index types from HNSW to DiskANN. The project belongs to the LF AI & Data Foundation, and Zilliz, its main contributor, runs the managed Zilliz Cloud service.

chunks.title: MiMo-V2.6-Pro
chunks.text: MiMo-V2.6-Pro (by Xiaomi), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: MiMo-V2.6-Pro is Xiaomi's flagship mixture-of-experts model, with about 1.02 trillion total and 42 billion active parameters. Xiaomi publishes the weights under MIT, along with a fork of verl that reproduces its agentic RL recipe on a distilled 9B model, and a dataset of RL environments for code, cybersecurity, general, visual and music tasks.

chunks.title: MinerU
chunks.text: MinerU (by Shanghai AI Laboratory), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Document extraction pipeline that converts PDFs and Office documents into LLM-ready Markdown and JSON, preserving reading order and handling multi-column layouts, tables, formulas and scanned pages through OCR. Published by OpenDataLab and distributed as a Python package, a Docker image and a hosted web application.

chunks.title: MiniCPM
chunks.text: MiniCPM (by OpenBMB), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: OpenBMB's on-device model family, spanning MiniCPM3-4B through the MiniCPM4/4.1 8B hybrid-reasoning generation to the current MiniCPM5-1B. The line pairs small dense models with efficiency research — trainable sparse attention (InfLLM-V2), quantized end-side inference — to run capable models on phones and edge hardware.

chunks.title: MiniCPM-o
chunks.text: MiniCPM-o (by OpenBMB), catalog entry under Multimodal models: MiniCPM-o is OpenBMB's omni-modal model line for live, full-duplex interaction on phones and other devices. MiniCPM-o 4.5, a 9B model built from SigLIP2, Whisper-medium, CosyVoice2 and Qwen3-8B, watches video and listens to audio at the same time as it answers in text and speech, and can clone a voice from a short reference clip.

chunks.title: MiniCPM-o
chunks.text: MiniCPM-o (by OpenBMB), catalog entry under Multimodal models: It shares a repository with MiniCPM-V.

chunks.title: MiniCPM-V
chunks.text: MiniCPM-V (by OpenBMB), catalog entry under Multimodal models: MiniCPM-V is OpenBMB's line of small vision-language models built to run on phones and other edge devices. The models read single images, several images at once and video, and the current MiniCPM-V 4.6 pairs a SigLIP2-400M encoder with a Qwen3.5-0.8B language model and supports tool calling.

chunks.title: MiniCPM-V
chunks.text: MiniCPM-V (by OpenBMB), catalog entry under Multimodal models: The line is separate from OpenBMB's text MiniCPM models and shares its repository with the omni-modal MiniCPM-o.

chunks.title: MiniMax M3
chunks.text: MiniMax M3 (by MiniMax), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: MiniMax-M3 is MiniMax's flagship model, launched on June 1, 2026, with MiniMax Sparse Attention, a one-million-token context and native multimodality. It was API-first at launch, with weights subsequently published on Hugging Face alongside vLLM and SGLang deployment guides.

chunks.title: MiniMax Hailuo
chunks.text: MiniMax Hailuo (by MiniMax), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: MiniMax Hailuo is MiniMax's video generation line. Its downloadable model, MiniMax H3, is a 33B single-stream transformer that generates 4 to 15 second clips with 32 kHz stereo audio from text, first and last frames, or up to nine reference images, three video clips and three audio clips.

chunks.title: MiniMax Hailuo
chunks.text: MiniMax Hailuo (by MiniMax), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: The Hailuo 02 and 2.3 models, and the H3 2K regeneration and context modules, are served only through MiniMax's app and API.

chunks.title: MIOpen
chunks.text: MIOpen (by AMD), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: MIOpen is AMD's library of high-performance machine learning primitives for ROCm, covering convolution, RNN, pooling, batch normalization and related deep learning kernels - the same role cuDNN plays for NVIDIA.

chunks.title: MIOpen
chunks.text: MIOpen (by AMD), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: AMD develops it as part of the ROCm stack; the project is being folded into the consolidated ROCm/rocm-libraries monorepo, and this repository is kept as a retired, read-only mirror during that migration.

chunks.title: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
chunks.text: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 is an instruction-tuned 7B chat model with a 32K context window, fine-tuned from the Mistral-7B-v0.2 base model and prompted with [INST] tags. Mistral describes it as a quick demonstration that the base model can be fine-tuned easily, and the card notes it has no moderation mechanisms.

chunks.title: Mistral Embed
chunks.text: Mistral Embed (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Mistral AI’s general-purpose text embedding endpoint, mistral-embed-2312: a 1,024-dimension text embedder with an 8k context, sold on La Plateforme at $0.10 per million tokens through /v1/embeddings and the batch API. It is distinct from codestral-embed, Mistral’s later code-specialized embedder.

chunks.title: Mistral Fine-Tuning API
chunks.text: Mistral Fine-Tuning API (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Mistral Fine-Tuning API is Mistral's managed service for training custom versions of its own models, offering LoRA-based supervised fine-tuning for text and vision models plus a Classifier Factory for classification tasks. Supported base models include Mistral Small, Mistral Large, Codestral, Mistral NeMo, Ministral and Pixtral.

chunks.title: Mistral Fine-Tuning API
chunks.text: Mistral Fine-Tuning API (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Mistral's documentation files the service under deprecated, legacy features. A separate open-source SDK, mistral-finetune, covers self-hosted training.

chunks.title: Mistral Large 3
chunks.text: Mistral Large 3 (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Mistral Large 3 is Mistral AI's first mixture-of-experts model since Mixtral, with 41B active and 675B total parameters, a 256K context window and native text-and-image input.

chunks.title: Mistral Large 3
chunks.text: Mistral Large 3 (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Trained from scratch on 3,000 H200 GPUs and released in December 2025 in base and instruct form, it sits alongside the smaller dense Ministral 3 models and succeeds Mistral Large 2. A reasoning variant announced at launch has not been released.

chunks.title: Mistral Medium
chunks.text: Mistral Medium (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Mistral AI's flagship open-weight model. Mistral Medium 3.5 is a dense 128-billion-parameter model that handles instruction following, reasoning and coding in one set of weights, with a 256k-token context window, image input and reasoning effort set per request.

chunks.title: Mistral Medium
chunks.text: Mistral Medium (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: It replaced Magistral and Mistral Medium 3.1 in Le Chat and Devstral 2 in the Vibe coding agent.

chunks.title: Mistral OCR
chunks.text: Mistral OCR (by Mistral AI (API)), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Document-understanding API from Mistral that converts PDFs and images into ordered markdown with images, tables and equations preserved as structured elements, and returns them in a form intended to be fed straight into a model's context.

chunks.title: mistral.rs
chunks.text: mistral.rs (by Eric Buehler), catalog entry under Inference code: mistral.rs is an LLM inference engine written in Rust, exposing OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible endpoints from one binary. It carries paged attention, prefix caching, ISQ and UQFF quantization and multimodal support. It is not affiliated with Mistral AI.

chunks.title: Mistral Small
chunks.text: Mistral Small (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Mistral Small is a line of open-weight models from Mistral AI. Mistral Small 4 is a 119-billion-parameter mixture of experts with about 6.5 billion parameters active per token.

chunks.title: Mistral Small
chunks.text: Mistral Small (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: It merges Mistral's instruct, reasoning (previously Magistral) and Devstral coding models into one, with reasoning switched on per request, image input and a 256k-token context window.

chunks.title: Mistral Studio
chunks.text: Mistral Studio (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Inference code: Mistral Studio, formerly La Plateforme, is Mistral AI's platform for running its models through an API. The API reference covers chat completion, fill-in-the-middle code completion, embeddings, classifiers, OCR, speech transcription and synthesis, and batch jobs, alongside endpoints for agents, workflows and observability.

chunks.title: Mistral Studio
chunks.text: Mistral Studio (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Inference code: Beyond the hosted API, Mistral sells hybrid, dedicated and self-hosted deployments of the platform.

chunks.title: Mistral Vibe
chunks.text: Mistral Vibe (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Mistral Vibe is a terminal coding agent that reads and edits files, runs shell commands, searches code and delegates work to subagents. It runs interactively, as a non-interactive command for scripts, or inside editors through the Agent Client Protocol, and extends through MCP servers, skills and hooks.

chunks.title: Mistral Vibe
chunks.text: Mistral Vibe (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Mistral's hosted models are the default, though local models and other compatible API keys also work. Mistral AI develops it.

chunks.title: mxbai-rerank
chunks.text: mxbai-rerank (by Mixedbread), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Mixedbread's cross-encoder reranking line, distinct from their mxbai-embed bi-encoders.

chunks.title: mxbai-rerank
chunks.text: mxbai-rerank (by Mixedbread), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The v2 generation (base 0.5B, large 1.5B) is trained with a three-step GRPO, contrastive and preference-learning recipe, covers 100-plus languages and 8K-token documents, and reports 57.49 BEIR average for large-v2; the v1 generation (xsmall, base, large) predates it and still carries most of the line's downloads.

chunks.title: MLC LLM
chunks.text: MLC LLM (by MLC AI), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: MLC LLM compiles large language models for native execution across a wide range of consumer and server hardware, then runs them on its own MLCEngine. Compilation targets Vulkan, CUDA, ROCm, Metal, OpenCL, WebGPU and WASM, covering Linux, Windows, macOS, iOS, Android and the browser.

chunks.title: MLC LLM
chunks.text: MLC LLM (by MLC AI), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: The project builds on the MLC fork of Apache TVM's compilation stack.

chunks.title: MLE-bench
chunks.text: MLE-bench (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Benchmark measuring how well AI agents perform machine learning engineering, built from 75 Kaggle competitions. OpenAI ships the preparation and grading code plus new train/test splits, and the raw competition data is downloaded from Kaggle under each competition's own rules.

chunks.title: MLE-bench
chunks.text: MLE-bench (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: A public leaderboard tracks agent submissions, though new submissions are paused as of April 2026.

chunks.title: MLflow
chunks.text: MLflow (by Databricks), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: AI engineering platform covering the machine-learning and LLM lifecycle in one tool, combining distributed tracing of agents and model calls, automated evaluation, a prompt registry and an AI gateway with the experiment tracking and model registry it began as. Databricks Managed MLflow is sold beside it as hosting rather than as a paid tier.

chunks.title: MLRun
chunks.text: MLRun (by MLRun), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Open-source MLOps platform for building and running continuous machine-learning and generative-AI applications. Functions are declared in Python and executed as jobs on Kubernetes, with pipelines, a feature store, artifact and model tracking, and real-time serving graphs over the same objects. It is the open core beneath Iguazio's commercial platform.

chunks.title: mLSTM Kernels
chunks.text: mLSTM Kernels (by NXAI), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: mLSTM Kernels (Tiled Flash Linear Attention) provides fast, chunkwise-parallel Triton kernels for the mLSTM used in xLSTM, with JAX and PyTorch native implementations and Triton integrations for both. NXAI, the xLSTM team's company, distributes it under its own restrictive community license rather than an OSI-approved one.

chunks.title: MLTE
chunks.text: MLTE (by MLTE), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: MLTE (Machine Learning Test and Evaluation) is a framework and Python package for testing ML models against requirements agreed with stakeholders. Teams record requirements, collect evidence from measurements, and assemble it into reports, with an optional web interface and backend that store the artifacts.

chunks.title: MLTE
chunks.text: MLTE (by MLTE), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: Its authors describe the framework in a 2023 IEEE/ACM paper.

chunks.title: MLX
chunks.text: MLX (by Apple), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: MLX is an array framework for machine learning on Apple silicon, from Apple machine learning research.

chunks.title: MLX
chunks.text: MLX (by Apple), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It offers a NumPy-like Python API plus C++, C and Swift APIs, higher-level mlx.nn and mlx.optimizers packages following PyTorch conventions, composable function transformations for automatic differentiation and vectorization, lazy evaluation, dynamic graph construction and a unified memory model across CPU and GPU.

chunks.title: MLX LM
chunks.text: MLX LM (by Apple), catalog entry under Inference code: MLX LM generates text with large language models on Apple silicon using MLX, pulling any of thousands of compatible models from the Hugging Face Hub. It ships CLI commands for generation, chat, a server and quantized model conversion, with prompt caching, a rotating KV cache and distributed inference and fine-tuning through mx.distributed.

chunks.title: MLX LM
chunks.text: MLX LM (by Apple), catalog entry under Inference code: Apple's ml-explore organization maintains it as the LM layer split out of the core mlx repo.

chunks.title: MLX-VLM
chunks.text: MLX-VLM (by Blaizzy (Prince Canuma)), catalog entry under Inference code: MLX-VLM runs vision-language and omni models locally on Apple silicon using MLX, taking image, audio and video inputs alongside text. It ships a CLI and a FastAPI server with continuous batching, automatic prefix caching, KV-cache quantization and speculative decoding, and converts and quantizes Hugging Face models for local use.

chunks.title: MLX-VLM
chunks.text: MLX-VLM (by Blaizzy (Prince Canuma)), catalog entry under Inference code: Fine-tuning with LoRA and QLoRA is included but the package is inference-first.

chunks.title: MMAudio
chunks.text: MMAudio (by hkchengrex), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: MMAudio generates sound effects and ambient audio synchronized to a video clip, a text prompt, or both, trained jointly on audio-visual and audio-text data. The model is small (157M parameters in the paper) and produces an eight-second clip in about a second.

chunks.title: MMAudio
chunks.text: MMAudio (by hkchengrex), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: It came out of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign with Sony AI and was presented at CVPR 2025.

chunks.title: MMLU
chunks.text: MMLU (by Hendrycks et al. (UC Berkeley)), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Massive Multitask Language Understanding: 14,042 four-option multiple-choice test questions across 57 subjects spanning humanities, social sciences, STEM and professional domains, designed to measure broad knowledge and reasoning. An auxiliary training split brings the repository to roughly 231,400 rows.

chunks.title: MMLU-Pro
chunks.text: MMLU-Pro (by TIGER-Lab), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Harder successor to MMLU with about 12,032 questions across 14 disciplines, expanding the choice set from four options to ten and removing trivial and noisy items. It is expert-reviewed and contamination-hardened, and ships a 12,000-question test split with a small validation set.

chunks.title: MMMU
chunks.text: MMMU, catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding: about 11,550 college-level questions combining images and text across 30 subjects and 183 subfields, using 30 image types, drawn from college exams, quizzes and textbooks. It splits into a 150-question dev set, a 900-question validation set and a 10,500-question test set.

chunks.title: MMS (Massively Multilingual Speech)
chunks.text: MMS (Massively Multilingual Speech) (by Meta), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Meta's Massively Multilingual Speech models: one wav2vec 2.0 recognizer with per-language adapters for over 1,100 languages, language identification across about 4,000, and a separate text-to-speech voice for each of more than 1,100 languages.

chunks.title: MMS-lab data
chunks.text: MMS-lab data (by Meta), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: MMS-lab is Meta's labeled speech corpus of New Testament readings in 1,107 languages, built for the Massively Multilingual Speech project. Recordings from Faith Comes By Hearing, goto.bible and bible.com were force-aligned with their texts chapter by chapter and filtered for quality, and nearly every recording has a single speaker.

chunks.title: MMS-lab data
chunks.text: MMS-lab data (by Meta), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Meta trained its MMS recognition and synthesis models on it.

chunks.title: Mochi
chunks.text: Mochi (by Genmo), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Mochi 1 is Genmo's 10B-parameter text-to-video diffusion model, built on its Asymmetric Diffusion Transformer architecture and trained from scratch. It generates 480p clips and is tuned for photorealistic rather than animated styles.

chunks.title: Mochi
chunks.text: Mochi (by Genmo), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Genmo publishes an inference harness with context parallelism and a LoRA fine-tuning trainer that runs on a single 80 GB GPU.

chunks.title: Modal Sandboxes
chunks.text: Modal Sandboxes (by Modal Labs), catalog entry under Deployment: Modal Sandboxes runs untrusted or agent-generated code in gVisor-isolated containers on Modal's serverless cloud, created at runtime from the Python, JavaScript or Go SDK. A sandbox can be built from an arbitrary container image, looked up later by name, given GPUs, and held open for anything from the five-minute default to twenty-four hours.

chunks.title: Modal Sandboxes
chunks.text: Modal Sandboxes (by Modal Labs), catalog entry under Deployment: Compute is billed by the core-second.

chunks.title: Model Context Protocol
chunks.text: Model Context Protocol (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: Model Context Protocol is an open standard for connecting AI agents to external tools and data sources, defining how an agent discovers, authenticates with and invokes a tool over JSON-RPC. Anthropic announced it in November 2024 and donated it to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation in December 2025.

chunks.title: Model Context Protocol
chunks.text: Model Context Protocol (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: The specification, schema and documentation live in one repository, with official SDKs in separate repositories for languages including Python, TypeScript, C#, Java, Go, Rust and Ruby.

chunks.title: OpenSSF Model Signing
chunks.text: OpenSSF Model Signing (by Sigstore), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: OpenSSF Model Signing signs machine-learning models and verifies those signatures, so a user can check a model's integrity and provenance for themselves rather than trusting whoever trained it.

chunks.title: OpenSSF Model Signing
chunks.text: OpenSSF Model Signing (by Sigstore), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: It signs with Sigstore's keyless flow, with public keys or certificates, or through PKCS #11 devices, and emits a Sigstore bundle following the OpenSSF Model Signing specification. It is developed under the Sigstore project.

chunks.title: ModelScope
chunks.text: ModelScope (by ModelScope (Alibaba)), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Alibaba's hosted model community at modelscope.cn, with an international edition at modelscope.ai. Account holders publish models, datasets and Studio apps into repositories with public, internal or private visibility, versioned by branch, tag and commit.

chunks.title: ModelScope
chunks.text: ModelScope (by ModelScope (Alibaba)), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: The hub serves downloads over git and an OpenAPI surface that the official modelscope-hub client and CLI wrap.

chunks.title: ModernVBERT
chunks.text: ModernVBERT (by ModernVBERT), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: ModernVBERT is a 250M-parameter vision-language encoder built for document retrieval rather than repurposed from a generative decoder.

chunks.title: ModernVBERT
chunks.text: ModernVBERT (by ModernVBERT), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The paper walks the whole training pipeline - attention masking, image resolution, modality-alignment data regime, late-interaction contrastive objective - and the resulting ColModernVBERT checkpoint matches visual-document retrievers ten times its size while running query encoding on CPU.

chunks.title: ModernVBERT
chunks.text: ModernVBERT (by ModernVBERT), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The suite also ships a bi-encoder variant, the aligned base model and the intermediate checkpoints.

chunks.title: Molmo
chunks.text: Molmo (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Molmo is Ai2's family of open vision-language models, released with their training data and code. Molmo2 understands single images, several images and video, and answers by pointing at objects or tracking them across frames as well as in text.

chunks.title: Molmo
chunks.text: Molmo (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Its checkpoints pair Qwen3 or OLMo language models with a SigLIP 2 vision encoder, and every dataset was built without distilling from closed models.

chunks.title: MONAI
chunks.text: MONAI (by Project MONAI), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: PyTorch framework for deep learning on medical images, part of the PyTorch Ecosystem.

chunks.title: MONAI
chunks.text: MONAI (by Project MONAI), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: It supplies medical-imaging transforms, losses and metrics, a large set of network architectures (UNet, UNETR, SwinUNETR, SegResNet, VISTA3D and more), training workflows and model bundles, and Auto3DSeg, which analyzes a dataset, trains several segmentation algorithms and ensembles them with minimal user input.

chunks.title: MONAI
chunks.text: MONAI (by Project MONAI), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: It began at NVIDIA and King's College London and is steered by an advisory board drawn from its member institutions.

chunks.title: MONAI Model Zoo
chunks.text: MONAI Model Zoo (by Project MONAI), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Collection of medical imaging models packaged as MONAI Bundles, each bundling weights, training configuration and inference code under its own license.

chunks.title: MONAI Model Zoo
chunks.text: MONAI Model Zoo (by Project MONAI), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Researchers and institutions contribute bundles by reviewed pull request, every bundle version is archived and indexed, and monai.bundle.download fetches a named bundle from Project MONAI's hosting on NGC or Hugging Face. Project MONAI, started by NVIDIA and King's College London, maintains it.

chunks.title: Monocle
chunks.text: Monocle (by Monocle2AI), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: OpenTelemetry-native tracing SDK for GenAI applications and agents, built under the Linux Foundation AI & Data umbrella.

chunks.title: Monocle
chunks.text: Monocle (by Monocle2AI), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: It ships a metamodel mapping agents, prompts, tools and vector operations to standardized OTLP span attributes, framework adapters for LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack and Google ADK, and a companion trace-assertion testing library, monocle-test-tools. Traces export as OTLP to any collector or backend, with no hosted service of its own.

chunks.title: Moondream
chunks.text: Moondream (by M87 Labs), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Moondream is M87 Labs' small vision-language model line, built to run quickly on local hardware. Moondream 3.1, a 9B mixture-of-experts model with 2B active parameters, answers questions, writes captions, and returns points and bounding boxes as structured output, with an optional reasoning mode. The earlier Moondream 2 is a 2B model.

chunks.title: Moonshine
chunks.text: Moonshine (by Moonshine AI), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Moonshine AI's on-device speech recognition models and toolkit: small streaming recognizers, from 34M to 245M parameters, built for live transcription on phones, laptops, Raspberry Pi boards and the browser, with one library for Python, JavaScript, iOS, Android and desktop.

chunks.title: Morphic
chunks.text: Morphic (by Morphic), catalog entry under UI & API: Answer engine with a generative interface: answers render source-credited inline components such as images, grids and headings from a streamed JSON specification rather than plain markdown. It supports several model providers and search backends, with chat history, shareable result URLs, file upload and guest mode, and deploys with Docker.

chunks.title: Mosaic AI Model Training
chunks.text: Mosaic AI Model Training (by Databricks), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Mosaic AI Model Training was Databricks' managed service for full fine-tuning and continued pre-training of Meta Llama 3.1 to 3.3 models, driven from the databricks_genai SDK or a web UI. Training jobs read data from Unity Catalog and registered the resulting weights back to it, so customers kept the trained checkpoint.

chunks.title: Mosaic AI Model Training
chunks.text: Mosaic AI Model Training (by Databricks), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Databricks has ended support for the service and recommends its AI Runtime environment instead.

chunks.title: Moshi
chunks.text: Moshi (by Kyutai), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Kyutai's speech-text foundation model and full-duplex spoken dialogue system: it listens and speaks at the same time, with about 200 ms of practical latency, using the Mimi streaming audio codec. Released as the Moshiko and Moshika voices for PyTorch, MLX and Rust.

chunks.title: MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize
chunks.text: MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize (by OpenMOSS), catalog entry under Speech & audio: OpenMOSS's end-to-end model for long multi-speaker recordings: in one pass over up to 90 minutes of audio it transcribes, labels who spoke when, and adds timestamps and acoustic events, in more than 50 languages. It pairs a Whisper-style encoder with a small Qwen3-style decoder.

chunks.title: MS MARCO Cross-Encoders
chunks.text: MS MARCO Cross-Encoders (by UKP Lab (TU Darmstadt)), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The `cross-encoder/ms-marco-*` family of BERT and MiniLM cross-encoders trained on MS MARCO Passage Ranking and published alongside SentenceTransformers.

chunks.title: MS MARCO Cross-Encoders
chunks.text: MS MARCO Cross-Encoders (by UKP Lab (TU Darmstadt)), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Each checkpoint takes a (query, passage) pair and returns a single relevance logit, and the family spans TinyBERT-L2 through MiniLM-L12 so a deployment can trade throughput against NDCG. It is the default self-hosted reranker in most retrieve-and-rerank stacks.

chunks.title: MT-Bench
chunks.text: MT-Bench (by SGLang (LMSYS / UC Berkeley)), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Multi-turn open-ended benchmark of 80 questions for instruction-following and conversational ability, scored by a strong model acting as judge. Created by LMSYS, it ships inside FastChat with both the questions and GPT-4 reference answers published, and was introduced in the NeurIPS 2023 paper on judging with language models.

chunks.title: MuJoCo
chunks.text: MuJoCo (by Google), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: MuJoCo (Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact) is Google DeepMind's physics engine for articulated bodies in contact, used throughout robotics and reinforcement-learning research.

chunks.title: MuJoCo
chunks.text: MuJoCo (by Google), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: The C core runs on the CPU with an OpenGL viewer and Python bindings, and the product line includes MJX, a JAX reimplementation, and MuJoCo Warp, a GPU build maintained with NVIDIA, for batched simulation on accelerators.

chunks.title: MultiPL-E
chunks.text: MultiPL-E (by Northeastern University / Brown / Wellesley), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Translation of HumanEval's 161 problems and MBPP's 397 into 22 to 23 programming languages including Ada, C++, C#, Go, Haskell, Java, JavaScript, Lua, OCaml, PHP, R, Ruby, Rust, Scala, Shell, Swift and TypeScript.

chunks.title: MultiPL-E
chunks.text: MultiPL-E (by Northeastern University / Brown / Wellesley), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: It lets code-generation performance be compared across languages rather than in Python alone, and is integrated into the BigCode evaluation harness.

chunks.title: Muse Glimmer
chunks.text: Muse Glimmer (by Meta Superintelligence Labs), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Muse Glimmer is a 30-billion-parameter open-weight model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, distilled from Muse Spark and built to run agentic tasks locally on consumer hardware.

chunks.title: Muse Glimmer
chunks.text: Muse Glimmer (by Meta Superintelligence Labs), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: A dense transformer with a 1.8-billion-parameter vision encoder, it reads text and images, writes text, holds a 131k-token context and takes a reasoning strength set per request. Meta also publishes 4-bit GGUF and ExecuTorch builds and a speculative-decoding drafter.

chunks.title: Muse Spark
chunks.text: Muse Spark (by Meta Superintelligence Labs), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Muse Spark is a multimodal language model line from Meta Superintelligence Labs, launched on April 8, 2026 as the first in the Muse series. The hosted releases, currently Muse Spark 1.3, power the Meta AI app and website and Meta's other apps and AI glasses, and reach developers through the Meta Model API.

chunks.title: Muse Spark
chunks.text: Muse Spark (by Meta Superintelligence Labs), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: On October 15, 2026 Meta published Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 42 billion active parameters that shares Muse Spark 1.3's base model, as downloadable weights under the Muse Model License.

chunks.title: MusicGen
chunks.text: MusicGen (by Meta), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: MusicGen is Meta's transformer model that generates instrumental music from a text description, and in its melody variants from a text description guided by a reference melody. It comes in 300M, 1.5B and 3.3B sizes with mono and stereo builds, plus style-conditioned and stem-separated variants, and runs through Meta's AudioCraft library.

chunks.title: mxbai-embed
chunks.text: mxbai-embed (by Mixedbread), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: mxbai-embed is Mixedbread's open-weight English sentence embedding line, headed by mxbai-embed-large-v1, a BERT-large bi-encoder with a 512-token window, released in March 2024. The family also includes a 2D-Matryoshka variant, an xsmall checkpoint and a German model built with deepset.

chunks.title: mxbai-embed
chunks.text: mxbai-embed (by Mixedbread), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: All of them support Matryoshka truncation and binary quantization, which is the line's distinguishing feature: a 1024-dimension float vector can be cut to a fraction of its storage cost with most of its retrieval quality intact.

chunks.title: n8n
chunks.text: n8n (by n8n), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Workflow automation platform with native AI and agent capabilities. It pairs a visual node-based canvas with drop-in JavaScript and Python, several hundred integrations, and LangChain-based nodes for building agents and AI workflows. It is a general automation platform first, with AI as a native layer, and runs self-hosted or on the vendor's cloud.

chunks.title: naab
chunks.text: naab (by Speech and Language Processing Lab, Sharif University of Technology), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: naab is a cleaned Farsi text corpus for pretraining language models, with about 130 GB, 250 million paragraphs, and 15 billion words.

chunks.title: naab
chunks.text: naab (by Speech and Language Processing Lab, Sharif University of Technology), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It merges existing Persian corpora, OSCAR-fa, the formerly private AGP corpus, Telegram channels, and LSCP, and a raw version (naab-raw) and the preprocessing code are published beside it. Sharif University of Technology's Speech and Language Processing Lab builds it.

chunks.title: NaijaVoices
chunks.text: NaijaVoices (by NaijaVoices), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: NaijaVoices is a speech dataset of about 1,800 hours of speech paired with expert-curated text in Igbo, Hausa and Yoruba, roughly 600 hours per language, from more than 5,000 speakers with a balanced age range. Each row carries the audio, transcript, language, speaker ID, gender and age bracket.

chunks.title: NaijaVoices
chunks.text: NaijaVoices (by NaijaVoices), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The NaijaVoices community project collected it and also publishes a compressed copy of the same data.

chunks.title: Nano Banana (Gemini Image)
chunks.text: Nano Banana (Gemini Image) (by Google), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Nano Banana is Google's name for Gemini's native image generation and editing models, served through the Gemini app, Google products and the Gemini API.

chunks.title: Nano Banana (Gemini Image)
chunks.text: Nano Banana (Gemini Image) (by Google), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: The line spans a premium Pro model, a general Flash model with 4K output and a low-cost Lite model, and it generates and edits images conversationally from text, image or video input.

chunks.title: nano-graphrag
chunks.text: nano-graphrag (by gusye1234), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Small, hackable reimplementation of GraphRAG in roughly eleven hundred lines, written because the official implementation is hard to read or modify. It is portable, fully asynchronous and typed, with swappable graph, vector and model backends, and is meant as a reference and customization base rather than a production system.

chunks.title: Nanonets OCR
chunks.text: Nanonets OCR (by Nanonets), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Document-parsing models from Nanonets released as open weights alongside the company's hosted intelligent-document-processing platform. The models convert documents to structured markdown, recognising tables, equations, signatures, checkboxes and watermarks as tagged elements rather than flattening them into text.

chunks.title: NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model
chunks.text: NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model (by NASA IMPACT), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: A ViT-B encoder-decoder pretrained from scratch on SomBench, roughly two million co-registered lunar tile bundles spanning 11 modalities at two spatial scales, LROC NAC at about 1 m/px and LROC WAC at about 100 m/px.

chunks.title: NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model
chunks.text: NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model (by NASA IMPACT), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: It adapts TerraMind's masked-token recipe to the Moon by tokenizing acquisition geometry as explicit context and training both resolution families in one mixed-batch loop, and downstream adaptation runs through TerraTorch with runnable configs for crater detection, Irregular Mare Patch segmentation and ice prospectivity.

chunks.title: NCHLT named-entity corpora
chunks.text: NCHLT named-entity corpora (by Centre for Text Technology, North-West University), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The NCHLT text corpora are foundational text resources for South African languages: monolingual corpora with subsets annotated for tokenization, morphology and part of speech, used to build tokenizers, lemmatizers and taggers.

chunks.title: NCHLT named-entity corpora
chunks.text: NCHLT named-entity corpora (by Centre for Text Technology, North-West University), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Hugging Face entry loads the named-entity annotated corpora for nine languages, from Afrikaans to isiZulu, from the SADiLaR repository. A North-West University curator maintains the entry.

chunks.title: ncnn
chunks.text: ncnn (by Tencent), catalog entry under Inference code: ncnn is a neural network inference runtime optimized for mobile, embedded and desktop deployment, with no third-party dependency in its core. It ships pnnx for converting PyTorch and ONNX models into its own format, and targets general neural network inference rather than LLM serving specifically.

chunks.title: NEBULA
chunks.text: NEBULA (by CyberDataLab), catalog entry under Federated learning: NEBULA is a platform for decentralized federated learning, formerly called Fedstellar, developed at the University of Murcia with armasuisse and the University of Zurich.

chunks.title: NEBULA
chunks.text: NEBULA (by CyberDataLab), catalog entry under Federated learning: A web frontend and a controller set up a federation on star, ring, mesh or custom topologies and deploy it as local processes, Docker containers or physical devices, with a core running on each participant. It adds differential privacy through Opacus, simulated attacks with reputation-based defenses, and trustworthiness metrics.

chunks.title: NVIDIA NeMo Speech
chunks.text: NVIDIA NeMo Speech (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Speech & audio: NVIDIA's PyTorch toolkit for training, fine-tuning and serving speech models: recognition, synthesis, speaker tasks and speech LLMs. It is the framework behind NVIDIA's Parakeet, Canary and Magpie TTS models and installs as nemo-toolkit.

chunks.title: NeMo Curator
chunks.text: NeMo Curator (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: GPU-accelerated toolkit for curating LLM training data across text, image, video, and audio: extraction, language ID, exact/fuzzy/substring deduplication, quality classification, and synthetic data generation. NVIDIA uses it for the Nemotron-4 pretraining data (8+ trillion tokens of multilingual web data) and the Nemotron-CC curation pipeline.

chunks.title: NVIDIA NeMo Data Designer
chunks.text: NVIDIA NeMo Data Designer (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Generates synthetic datasets from scratch or from seed data using statistical samplers, dependency-aware generation across correlated fields, Python, SQL and custom validators, and judge-model scoring. The data-designer library runs locally, and the NeMo Platform runs the same configurations as a managed service.

chunks.title: NeMo Guardrails
chunks.text: NeMo Guardrails (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: NVIDIA's toolkit for adding programmable guardrails around LLM applications. It wraps input and output moderation, dialog control, retrieval filtering and tool-use control in a small policy language called Colang, works across multiple model providers, and deploys as a Python library, a CLI, a Docker image or a standalone server.

chunks.title: NeMo-RL
chunks.text: NeMo-RL (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: NeMo-RL is NVIDIA's library for reinforcement-learning post-training of language and vision-language models, re-architected from the earlier NeMo Aligner. It implements GRPO, GSPO, DAPO, PPO, DPO, SFT, on-policy distillation and reward modeling on DTensor or Megatron Core backends, and runs from a single GPU to multi-node clusters.

chunks.title: NeMo-RL
chunks.text: NeMo-RL (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: NeMo Customizer is a separate managed fine-tuning microservice alongside it.

chunks.title: Nemotron 3
chunks.text: Nemotron 3 (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Nemotron 3 is NVIDIA's open-weight family of instruction-tuned models for agentic reasoning, post-trained with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning on Nemotron base models.

chunks.title: Nemotron 3
chunks.text: Nemotron 3 (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: It spans Nano (30B total, 3B active), Super (120B total, 12B active) and Ultra (550B total, 55B active) mixture-of-experts models, with a 1M-token context window on Super and Ultra. NVIDIA publishes training data and recipes with the weights, and the line is its reference for NeMo and NIM, tuned for NVIDIA hardware.

chunks.title: Nemotron-CC
chunks.text: Nemotron-CC (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: NVIDIA's Common Crawl-derived pretraining corpus family, spanning trillions of tokens with synthetic rephrasing across general, math, code and specialized sets. It backs the Nemotron model line and is a documented component of Marin 8B.

chunks.title: Nemotron Embed
chunks.text: Nemotron Embed (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Nemotron Embed is NVIDIA's text embedding line for retrieval-augmented generation, now in its third generation.

chunks.title: Nemotron Embed
chunks.text: Nemotron Embed (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The current Nemotron-3-Embed release ships 1B and 8B bidirectional encoders with average pooling and 2048-dimension output, in BF16 and NVFP4 builds; the preceding generation - llama-embed-nemotron-8b and llama-nemotron-embed-1b-v2 - is still distributed.

chunks.title: Nemotron Embed
chunks.text: Nemotron Embed (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The line is tuned for multilingual and cross-lingual retrieval and evaluated on RTEB, MMTEB retrieval and the text split of ViDoRe-V3.

chunks.title: Nemotron Nano Omni
chunks.text: Nemotron Nano Omni (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Nemotron Nano Omni is NVIDIA's omni-modal reasoning model, a 30B-total, 3B-active mixture-of-experts that understands video, audio, images and text and answers in text. It reads video with its soundtrack, transcribes speech with word-level timestamps, parses long documents and drives computer interfaces, with tool calling in a 256K context.

chunks.title: Nemotron Nano Omni
chunks.text: Nemotron Nano Omni (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Multimodal models: NVIDIA ships BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 builds.

chunks.title: Llama Nemotron Rerank
chunks.text: Llama Nemotron Rerank (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: NVIDIA's NeMo Retriever reranking model, a 1B cross-encoder fine-tuned from Llama-3.2-1B with bidirectional attention and a binary relevance head.

chunks.title: Llama Nemotron Rerank
chunks.text: Llama Nemotron Rerank (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: It supports 8,192-token documents and was evaluated across 26 languages on MIRACL, MLQA and MLDR, and it is the reranking stage NVIDIA ships as a NIM microservice alongside its llama-nemotron embedding model. A vision-language sibling, llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2, extends it to visual documents.

chunks.title: Nemotron Nano VL
chunks.text: Nemotron Nano VL (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Nemotron Nano VL is NVIDIA's vision-language model line for document intelligence, image question answering and video understanding. The current Nemotron Nano 12B v2 VL reads up to four document images at 1k by 2k resolution and samples video at up to 128 frames in a 128K context. The earlier Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Nano-VL-8B is built on Llama 3.1.

chunks.title: Nepali Text Corpus
chunks.text: Nepali Text Corpus (by Institute for Research and Innovation in Intelligent Systems (IRIIS)), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Nepali Text Corpus is a monolingual Nepali pretraining corpus of about 6.4 million articles, 27.5 GB as CSV, collected from Nepali news websites, blogs and other online sources.

chunks.title: Nepali Text Corpus
chunks.text: Nepali Text Corpus (by Institute for Research and Innovation in Intelligent Systems (IRIIS)), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: IRIIS Research assembled it to pretrain Nepali BERT, RoBERTa and GPT-2 models, and its paper puts it at about 2.4 times the size of earlier Nepali corpora.

chunks.title: NeuralGCM
chunks.text: NeuralGCM (by Google), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: NeuralGCM is a hybrid machine-learning and physics atmospheric model from Google Research that couples learned parameterizations to the Dinosaur dynamical core. It runs weather forecasts and multi-decade climate simulations from ERA5 states, and ships deterministic checkpoints at three horizontal resolutions plus a stochastic one.

chunks.title: New Relic AI Monitoring
chunks.text: New Relic AI Monitoring (by New Relic), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Enterprise AI/LLM monitoring integrated into the New Relic observability platform. Traces LLM interactions, tracks token usage and costs, monitors model performance and error rates. Supports OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, and other providers.

chunks.title: New Relic AI Monitoring
chunks.text: New Relic AI Monitoring (by New Relic), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: For organizations already on New Relic who want AI observability unified with their existing APM, infrastructure, and log monitoring.

chunks.title: Newton
chunks.text: Newton (by Newton Physics), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Newton is a GPU-accelerated, differentiable physics engine for robotics simulation, built on NVIDIA Warp with MuJoCo Warp as its primary backend and further solvers for articulated bodies, cloth, soft bodies and granular material. It loads URDF, MJCF and USD models and renders ray-traced camera images across many parallel worlds.

chunks.title: Newton
chunks.text: Newton (by Newton Physics), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Newton was initiated by Disney Research, Google DeepMind and NVIDIA and is a Linux Foundation project.

chunks.title: NextChat
chunks.text: NextChat (by NextChat), catalog entry under UI & API: Lightweight cross-platform chat client for OpenAI, Gemini and Claude, packaged as a single Next.js app that deploys to Vercel in one click. It runs on the web, desktop and mobile, supports plugins, vision, MCP and artifacts, and offers an Enterprise Edition that adds permissions, team management and an internal knowledge base.

chunks.title: NLTK
chunks.text: NLTK (by NLTK Project), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: The Natural Language Toolkit, a suite of Python modules for tokenization, stemming, tagging, chunking, parsing, classification, language modeling and semantic reasoning, with interfaces to more than 50 corpora and lexical resources such as WordNet.

chunks.title: NLTK
chunks.text: NLTK (by NLTK Project), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: It supports research and development in natural language processing, and is a community project led by Steven Bird since 2001.

chunks.title: Nomic Embed
chunks.text: Nomic Embed (by Nomic AI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Nomic Embed produces long-context text embeddings for search and retrieval-augmented generation. The v1 and v1.5 encoders accept up to 8,192 tokens, and v1.5 is trained with Matryoshka representations so a vector can be truncated to 64 dimensions with graded loss of quality.

chunks.title: Nomic Embed
chunks.text: Nomic Embed (by Nomic AI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Version 2 is a mixture-of-experts encoder covering roughly 100 languages at a 512-token limit. Nomic AI publishes weights, training data and the contrastors training pipeline together.

chunks.title: nono
chunks.text: nono (by nolabs), catalog entry under Deployment: nono runs AI coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenCode inside a least-privilege sandbox on macOS, Linux and Windows, isolating at the kernel rather than in a container or VM. Tools the agent calls get their own child sandboxes with separate filesystem, network and credential policy.

chunks.title: nono
chunks.text: nono (by nolabs), catalog entry under Deployment: nolabs-ai, founded by members of the Sigstore team, writes it in Rust and ships bindings for Python, TypeScript and Go plus a public profile registry.

chunks.title: North Micro Vision
chunks.text: North Micro Vision (by Cohere), catalog entry under Multimodal models: North Micro Vision is Cohere's 2.4B-parameter vision-language model, part of its North family of purpose-built models. It reads interleaved text and images at native resolution and handles question answering, captioning, grounding, OCR, charts and documents in several languages.

chunks.title: North Micro Vision
chunks.text: North Micro Vision (by Cohere), catalog entry under Multimodal models: The vision encoder is trained from SigLIP 2 and the language model is Cohere's own.

chunks.title: Northflank Sandboxes
chunks.text: Northflank Sandboxes (by Northflank), catalog entry under Deployment: Runs untrusted and AI-generated code in microVM-backed sandboxes isolated with Kata Containers and gVisor, booting in under a second with no forced session time limit. Sandboxes sit inside Northflank's wider runtime platform alongside services, jobs, databases and GPU workloads, and can run on Northflank's cloud or inside a customer VPC.

chunks.title: Northflank Sandboxes
chunks.text: Northflank Sandboxes (by Northflank), catalog entry under Deployment: Northflank Ltd operates it as a commercial managed service.

chunks.title: Norwegian Colossal Corpus
chunks.text: Norwegian Colossal Corpus (by National Library of Norway AI Lab), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Norwegian Colossal Corpus (NCC) is a Norwegian pretraining corpus, mainly Bokmål and Nynorsk, drawn from books and newspapers digitized by the National Library, government reports, parliament collections, public-sector websites and Wikipedia, with each document tagged by source type and year.

chunks.title: Norwegian Colossal Corpus
chunks.text: Norwegian Colossal Corpus (by National Library of Norway AI Lab), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Newspapers distributed under the Språkbank agreement were withdrawn at the request of media houses, leaving about 4.6 billion words. The National Library of Norway AI Lab builds it.

chunks.title: Notion MCP Server
chunks.text: Notion MCP Server (by Notion), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Notion's official MCP server, written in TypeScript, exposing the Notion API to agents: searching a workspace, querying, retrieving, creating and updating data sources, reading and writing pages and blocks, and managing properties and comments, with token-optimized responses and Markdown page editing.

chunks.title: Notion MCP Server
chunks.text: Notion MCP Server (by Notion), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: It targets the API version in which data sources rather than databases are the primary abstraction, and installs over standard OAuth.

chunks.title: Nunchaku
chunks.text: Nunchaku (by nunchux-ai), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Nunchaku is an inference engine for diffusion models quantized to 4-bit weights and activations with SVDQuant, a low-rank method that keeps image quality close to the full-precision model while cutting memory several times over.

chunks.title: Nunchaku
chunks.text: Nunchaku (by nunchux-ai), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: It runs INT4 and NVFP4 builds of FLUX.1, Qwen-Image, SANA, Z-Image and PixArt, and plugs into ComfyUI through a companion node pack. It began in MIT HAN Lab.

chunks.title: NVIDIA FLARE
chunks.text: NVIDIA FLARE (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Federated learning: NVIDIA's federated learning runtime and SDK.

chunks.title: NVIDIA FLARE
chunks.text: NVIDIA FLARE (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Federated learning: A provisioned server and client sites run jobs that keep each site's data local; it ships a simulator for research, Kubernetes and Slurm launchers for production and HPC sites, a mobile SDK for Android and iOS devices, homomorphic encryption, differential privacy and confidential-computing options, and federated fine-tuning of large language models.

chunks.title: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin
chunks.text: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: NVIDIA's high-end edge-AI system-on-module, delivering up to 275 sparse INT8 TOPS from a 2048-core Ampere GPU with 64 tensor cores alongside a 12-core Arm Cortex-A78AE CPU. It ships in 32GB and 64GB LPDDR5 variants on a 699-pin module and is the top of the Jetson Orin family, aimed at robotics and autonomous machines.

chunks.title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit
chunks.text: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Entry-level edge-AI developer kit pairing an 8GB Jetson Orin Nano module with a carrier board, where the Super mode raises throughput to 67 sparse INT8 TOPS.

chunks.title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit
chunks.text: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: It uses an Ampere GPU with 1024 CUDA cores and 32 tensor cores, a 6-core Arm Cortex-A78AE CPU and 8GB of LPDDR5, and runs small language and vision-language models locally.

chunks.title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX
chunks.text: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Compact mid-range edge-AI system-on-module in a 260-pin SO-DIMM form factor, delivering up to 157 TOPS from a 1792-core Ampere GPU with 56 tensor cores and an 8-core Arm Cortex-A78AE CPU. It ships in 8GB and 16GB LPDDR5 variants and sits between the Orin Nano and AGX Orin, used in drones, cameras and compact robotics.

chunks.title: NVIDIA Model Optimizer
chunks.text: NVIDIA Model Optimizer (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: NVIDIA Model Optimizer is a library of model-optimization techniques - quantization, pruning, neural architecture search, distillation, sparsity and speculative decoding - composed through Python APIs.

chunks.title: NVIDIA Model Optimizer
chunks.text: NVIDIA Model Optimizer (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: It takes Hugging Face, PyTorch or ONNX models and exports optimized checkpoints for downstream deployment stacks including TensorRT-LLM, TensorRT and vLLM.

chunks.title: NVIDIA NGC Catalog
chunks.text: NVIDIA NGC Catalog (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: NVIDIA's curated catalog of GPU-optimized containers, pretrained models, Helm charts and resources, published by NVIDIA and admitted third-party vendors such as Meta, Google and Mistral AI. Public entries download without sign-in through the web catalog, the NGC CLI or the API, as numbered versions.

chunks.title: NVIDIA NGC Catalog
chunks.text: NVIDIA NGC Catalog (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: DGX and NVIDIA AI Enterprise customers also get a private registry for their own models.

chunks.title: NVIDIA Physical AI Dataset
chunks.text: NVIDIA Physical AI Dataset (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: NVIDIA's GR00T X-Embodiment Sim dataset, the most downloaded release in its Physical AI robotics collection, holds simulated trajectories used to post-train GR00T N1: bimanual Panda arms, the GR1 humanoid at tabletop tasks, single-arm kitchen manipulation and Unitree G1 loco-manipulation, published on the Hugging Face Hub.

chunks.title: NVIDIA Run:ai
chunks.text: NVIDIA Run:ai (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Enterprise platform for AI workloads and GPU orchestration. It pools GPU capacity across public clouds, private clouds, hybrid environments and on-premise data centres, allocates it dynamically including fractionally, and places AI workloads against quotas set per team.

chunks.title: TensorIR
chunks.text: TensorIR (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: TensorIR is NVIDIA's lightweight MLIR compiler frontend for expressing tensor computations, lowering to CUDA Tile IR for code generation on NVIDIA GPUs. NVIDIA is releasing it early for community evaluation and feedback ahead of a production-performance commitment.

chunks.title: NVIDIA Attestation SDK (nvTrust)
chunks.text: NVIDIA Attestation SDK (nvTrust) (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: NVIDIA's attestation tooling for confidential computing on its GPUs and NVSwitches. It collects hardware evidence from a GPU running in confidential-computing mode and verifies it, locally or through NVIDIA's remote attestation service, so a relying party can confirm what hardware and firmware ran a workload.

chunks.title: NVIDIA Attestation SDK (nvTrust)
chunks.text: NVIDIA Attestation SDK (nvTrust) (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: The C++ SDK and nvattest CLI (NVAT) succeed the Python guest tools of the original nvTrust repository.

chunks.title: NXP i.MX 8M Plus
chunks.text: NXP i.MX 8M Plus (by NXP Semiconductors), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: NXP applications processor family with up to a quad Arm Cortex-A53 at 1.8 GHz, an 800 MHz Cortex-M7 real-time core and an integrated NPU delivering up to 2.3 TOPS for on-device machine learning and vision.

chunks.title: NXP i.MX 8M Plus
chunks.text: NXP i.MX 8M Plus (by NXP Semiconductors), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: It carries dual image signal processors and two camera inputs, and targets smart home, building, city and industrial applications, with module options from ADLINK, Toradex and SolidRun.

chunks.title: o3 / o4-mini
chunks.text: o3 / o4-mini (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: OpenAI's o3 and o4-mini are reasoning models that work through an extended chain of thought before answering: o3 is the full-scale model and o4-mini the cost-efficient one.

chunks.title: o3 / o4-mini
chunks.text: o3 / o4-mini (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Both are still served through OpenAI's API, without downloadable weights, but are deprecated there, with GPT-5 and GPT-5 Mini named as their successors; o4-mini is scheduled for removal on October 23, 2026 and o3 on December 11, 2026. Both have left ChatGPT.

chunks.title: OpenAssistant Conversations (OASST1)
chunks.text: OpenAssistant Conversations (OASST1) (by OpenAssistant), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Crowdsourced human dialogue corpus from the 2023 OpenAssistant project, holding about 161,000 messages across 35 languages contributed by the LAION community. It remains a staple human-data ingredient in open post-training mixes, from Guanaco through Tulu 3 to OLMo 3's Dolci.

chunks.title: Octo
