chunks.text: Octo (by Octo Model Team), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Octo is an open generalist robot policy from UC Berkeley's Robotic AI and Learning Lab and collaborators: a transformer diffusion policy trained on 800k trajectories from Open X-Embodiment.

chunks.title: Octo
chunks.text: Octo (by Octo Model Team), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: It accepts several camera views and either a language instruction or a goal image, and its modular attention lets it be fine-tuned to new sensors, action spaces and robot bodies with a small dataset.

chunks.title: Off Grid AI
chunks.text: Off Grid AI (by Off Grid AI), catalog entry under UI & API: Off Grid AI is an on-device assistant for iPhone and Mac. It runs GGUF language models locally with vision input, Whisper speech recognition and image generation, and adds retrieval over local files and MCP tool access. A paid Pro tier adds on-device text-to-speech, custom personas, approval-gated actions and cross-device sync.

chunks.title: OGX
chunks.text: OGX (by Meta), catalog entry under UI & API: Open agentic API server from Meta, launched as Llama Stack in 2024 and rebranded in 2026 as OGX. It is not an inference engine: it composes and routes to inference backends such as vLLM, Ollama and Bedrock, alongside vector stores, safety, tools and file storage, behind OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs, with unified interfaces for agents, fine-tuning and evaluation.

chunks.title: OLDI Seed
chunks.text: OLDI Seed (by Open Language Data Initiative), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: OLDI Seed is a parallel corpus of 6,193 English Wikipedia sentences translated into several dozen low-resource languages, meant to kick-start machine translation where no large training set exists. It extends the NLLB-Seed data that Meta commissioned from professional translators for No Language Left Behind.

chunks.title: OLDI Seed
chunks.text: OLDI Seed (by Open Language Data Initiative), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Open Language Data Initiative now maintains it and adds community translations.

chunks.title: Ollama
chunks.text: Ollama (by Ollama), catalog entry under Deployment: Ollama runs open models locally through a Docker-like CLI (ollama pull, ollama run) and a local REST API with an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, handling model download, quantization and GPU/CPU routing itself. A curated library covers Llama, Qwen, Gemma, DeepSeek and gpt-oss, and the CLI launches coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenCode against them.

chunks.title: Ollama
chunks.text: Ollama (by Ollama), catalog entry under Deployment: The Go engine installs from a platform installer or the official Docker image; Ollama also sells hosted cloud inference.

chunks.title: Ollama Library
chunks.text: Ollama Library (by Ollama), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: The model registry at ollama.com that the Ollama runner pulls from and pushes to. Ollama curates the official library namespace, and any account holder who registers a public key can push models to a namespace of their own.

chunks.title: Ollama Library
chunks.text: Ollama Library (by Ollama), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Models are addressed as namespace/model:tag, with each tag naming a specific version, and pull counts and tag lists are shown per model.

chunks.title: OLMES
chunks.text: OLMES (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Ai2's evaluation system behind the OLMo and Tülu releases, built on lm-evaluation-harness with deeper task configuration, instance-level prediction logging and external results storage for faithful reproduction of published numbers. It packages the OLMES standard for evaluating base and instruction-tuned models.

chunks.title: OLMo 3
chunks.text: OLMo 3 (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Ai2's OLMo 3 family at 7B and 32B in Base, Think, Instruct and RL-Zero variants, released November 2025 with a December update. The weights ship with the 9.3-trillion-token Dolma 3 corpus, the training code, the data recipes and intermediate checkpoints, so the whole run can be inspected and modified. It supersedes OLMo 2.

chunks.title: OLMo 3 Instruct
chunks.text: OLMo 3 Instruct (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Instruction-tuned chat releases of Ai2's OLMo 3 family at 7B and 32B, post-trained on the fully open OLMo 3 base with the open Tulu and OLMo recipe. Every stage, checkpoint, dataset and dependency needed to recreate or modify them is published. It supersedes OLMo 2 Instruct.

chunks.title: olmOCR
chunks.text: olmOCR (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Converts PDFs and images to clean markdown/text using a 7B vision-language model, handling equations, tables, and handwriting. Emits Dolma-format documents; used in the Dolma 3 PDF-extraction path.

chunks.title: OLMoE Instruct
chunks.text: OLMoE Instruct (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Ai2's fully open mixture-of-experts instruct model, with roughly 1 billion active parameters out of 6.9 billion total, post-trained with supervised fine-tuning and DPO. It was released with its pretraining data, post-training data, training code, logs and 244 intermediate checkpoints.

chunks.title: OmniVoice
chunks.text: OmniVoice (by k2-fsa (Next-gen Kaldi)), catalog entry under Speech & audio: A massively multilingual zero-shot text-to-speech model from the k2-fsa (Next-gen Kaldi) project: it clones a voice or designs one from a description in more than 600 languages, at up to 40 times faster than real time.

chunks.title: oneDNN
chunks.text: oneDNN (by UXL Foundation), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: oneDNN is a cross-platform performance library of deep-learning building blocks - convolutions, matrix multiplications, normalizations and fused primitives - implementing the oneAPI specification for the component. It is optimized for x86-64, AMD64 and 64-bit Arm CPUs and for Intel GPUs, and frameworks call it as their CPU kernel layer.

chunks.title: oneDNN
chunks.text: oneDNN (by UXL Foundation), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: The UXL Foundation hosts the project.

chunks.title: oneMath
chunks.text: oneMath (by UXL Foundation), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: oneMath is the UXL Foundation's open implementation of the oneMath specification, a cross-vendor math library exposing one interface for BLAS, LAPACK, FFT, RNG and sparse routines and dispatching to a vendor backend - oneMKL, NVIDIA cuBLAS, AMD rocBLAS and others - per target device.

chunks.title: oneMath
chunks.text: oneMath (by UXL Foundation), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: It began as oneMKL Interfaces before the UXL Foundation renamed the project.

chunks.title: OneTrainer
chunks.text: OneTrainer (by Nerogar), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: OneTrainer is a training application for diffusion models, supporting full fine-tuning, LoRA and embeddings across Stable Diffusion 1.5 through 3.5, SDXL, FLUX.1, FLUX.2, Qwen Image, PixArt, Sana and Hunyuan Video. It includes masked training, EMA, aspect-ratio bucketing and multi-resolution training, and runs from either a GUI or a CLI.

chunks.title: ONNX
chunks.text: ONNX (by LF AI & Data (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: ONNX (Open Neural Network Exchange) is an open standard format and specification for representing machine learning models, defining an extensible computation graph model plus built-in operators and standard data types. It enables interoperability so models can move between frameworks, tools, runtimes and compilers.

chunks.title: ONNX
chunks.text: ONNX (by LF AI & Data (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It is governed under the Linux Foundation as part of LF AI & Data.

chunks.title: ONNX Runtime
chunks.text: ONNX Runtime (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Inference code: ONNX Runtime is a cross-platform accelerator for machine learning inference and training, running models exported from PyTorch, TensorFlow/Keras, and classical ML libraries via the ONNX interchange format.

chunks.title: ONNX Runtime
chunks.text: ONNX Runtime (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Inference code: It executes on CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, and custom accelerators through hardware-specific execution providers that target NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Qualcomm, and Apple silicon. Microsoft develops it and uses it in production across Windows, Office, and Azure.

chunks.title: ONNX Simplifier
chunks.text: ONNX Simplifier (by ONNX Simplifier project), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: ONNX Simplifier rewrites an ONNX graph into an equivalent, smaller one by folding constant subgraphs and removing the redundant operations exporters emit. It runs as a command-line tool or a Python call and ships npm and Rust bindings beside the Python package.

chunks.title: OpenConnector
chunks.text: OpenConnector (by OOMOL), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Open-source connector gateway: connect a user's app accounts once, then expose a shared catalogue of over a thousand providers and their prebuilt actions to agents over SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP or OpenAPI, with credential encryption and token refresh behind the runtime boundary.

chunks.title: Open LLM Leaderboard
chunks.text: Open LLM Leaderboard (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Hugging Face's public leaderboard for comparing open language models on a fixed, reproducible benchmark suite run on a shared cluster. Its second version raised difficulty with IFEval, BBH, MATH Level 5, GPQA, MuSR and MMLU-Pro, replacing the original six-benchmark suite.

chunks.title: Open-Sora
chunks.text: Open-Sora (by HPC-AI Tech), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Open-Sora is HPC-AI Tech's open video-generation model family. The current release, Open-Sora 2.0, is an 11B-parameter model for text-to-video and image-to-video at up to 768px, trained for about USD 200K with the checkpoints and training code both published.

chunks.title: Open-Sora
chunks.text: Open-Sora (by HPC-AI Tech), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Its own configs generate text-to-video directly, and an optional text-to-image-to-video pipeline uses FLUX.1 [dev] for the first frame.

chunks.title: Open WebUI
chunks.text: Open WebUI (by Open WebUI), catalog entry under UI & API: Open WebUI is an extensible web interface for chatting with Ollama models or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, deployed on infrastructure the operator runs.

chunks.title: Open WebUI
chunks.text: Open WebUI (by Open WebUI), catalog entry under UI & API: It includes retrieval-augmented generation over a choice of vector databases, voice and image handling, plugin support through Pipelines, tools, MCP and OpenAPI servers, and enterprise access control through RBAC, LDAP, SCIM and SSO.

chunks.title: Open X-Embodiment
chunks.text: Open X-Embodiment (by Google), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Open X-Embodiment is a pooled robot-learning dataset assembled in a collaboration of 21 institutions and published by Google DeepMind: more than a million real robot trajectories from 22 robot embodiments, from single arms to bimanual robots, covering 527 skills.

chunks.title: Open X-Embodiment
chunks.text: Open X-Embodiment (by Google), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Every constituent dataset is converted to the RLDS episode format and served through TensorFlow Datasets and a public Cloud Storage bucket.

chunks.title: OpenAI Agents SDK
chunks.text: OpenAI Agents SDK (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Python framework for building agents and multi-agent workflows, in which agents carry instructions, tools and guardrails and hand tasks to one another. It adds sessions that keep conversation history, human-in-the-loop approvals, tracing, sandbox agents that work inside an isolated workspace, and realtime and voice agents.

chunks.title: OpenAI Agents SDK
chunks.text: OpenAI Agents SDK (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Models can come from the OpenAI APIs or from other providers. OpenAI builds it, alongside a separate JavaScript and TypeScript version.

chunks.title: OpenAI Code Interpreter
chunks.text: OpenAI Code Interpreter (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Deployment: Writes and runs Python inside an OpenAI-managed sandbox container, exposed as a tool on the Responses, Chat Completions and Assistants APIs so a model can compute, analyze attached files, and retry code that fails. Containers come in 1, 4, 16 and 64 GB memory tiers, are billed per 20-minute session, and expire after 20 minutes without use.

chunks.title: OpenAI Code Interpreter
chunks.text: OpenAI Code Interpreter (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Deployment: OpenAI describes each container only as a sandboxed virtual machine, naming no isolation technology, and distributes no runtime.

chunks.title: OpenAI Text Embeddings
chunks.text: OpenAI Text Embeddings (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: OpenAI's general-purpose text embedding models, text-embedding-3-small and text-embedding-3-large, reached only through the /v1/embeddings endpoint.

chunks.title: OpenAI Text Embeddings
chunks.text: OpenAI Text Embeddings (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Both accept 8,192 tokens, default to 1,536 and 3,072 dimensions, and were trained with Matryoshka-style shortening so a caller can trade dimensions for storage through the `dimensions` parameter.

chunks.title: OpenAI Evals
chunks.text: OpenAI Evals (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Framework for evaluating language models and the systems built on them, published in 2023 with a registry of community-contributed benchmarks as an early open framework for eval-driven development. It supports custom eval authoring and model-graded grading, and runs against private data as well as the bundled registry.

chunks.title: OpenAI Evals API & Dashboard
chunks.text: OpenAI Evals API & Dashboard (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Managed evaluation product inside the OpenAI platform: an Evals API and a dashboard that let developers define eval datasets, run them against OpenAI models, grade with built-in or custom graders, and inspect results across versions.

chunks.title: OpenAI Fine-Tuning API
chunks.text: OpenAI Fine-Tuning API (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: The OpenAI Fine-Tuning API trains custom versions of OpenAI's hosted models on OpenAI's own infrastructure, covering supervised fine-tuning, vision fine-tuning, direct preference optimization and reinforcement fine-tuning for reasoning models. Jobs run against gpt-4.1, gpt-4o and o4-mini snapshots.

chunks.title: OpenAI Fine-Tuning API
chunks.text: OpenAI Fine-Tuning API (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: OpenAI is winding the platform down: new sign-ups have stopped, job creation ends in January 2027, and fine-tuned models serve until their base models are deprecated.

chunks.title: OpenAI Internal Evals
chunks.text: OpenAI Internal Evals (by OpenAI (Internal)), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: OpenAI's internal evaluation suites, used in model development and in safety assessment under its Preparedness Framework. They cover harder coding challenges, agentic task completion and cybersecurity-related tests, and are referenced in system cards and safety reports under the framework's tracked categories.

chunks.title: OpenAI Moderation API
chunks.text: OpenAI Moderation API (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: OpenAI's Moderation API is a free hosted endpoint that classifies text and images against OpenAI's content-policy categories, including hate, harassment, self-harm, sexual content and violence. It does not classify audio.

chunks.title: OpenAI Moderation API
chunks.text: OpenAI Moderation API (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Moderation scores can also be requested inline with a Responses or Chat Completions generation instead of through a separate call.

chunks.title: OpenAI speech models
chunks.text: OpenAI speech models (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Speech & audio: OpenAI's hosted speech models: gpt-transcribe and the gpt-4o transcription models (including a diarizing variant) for recognition, gpt-4o-mini-tts for instructable text-to-speech, and whisper-1 for timestamps and translation, all through the Audio API.

chunks.title: OpenAI Web Search
chunks.text: OpenAI Web Search (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Built-in tool in the OpenAI Responses API that lets a model search the live web during a call and return an answer with inline citations to the pages it used.

chunks.title: OpenAlex
chunks.text: OpenAlex (by OurResearch), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Free catalog of the world's scholarly research, run by the nonprofit OurResearch, covering hundreds of millions of works with their authors, institutions, sources and funders.

chunks.title: OpenAlex
chunks.text: OpenAlex (by OurResearch), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Its REST API searches works by keyword or by meaning, sorts them by relevance, and links each open-access work it holds a copy of to the full text as a PDF and as structured XML. The data is released under CC0, and the whole database can be downloaded as a free snapshot.

chunks.title: OpenArm
chunks.text: OpenArm (by Enactic), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: OpenArm is an open-source seven-degree-of-freedom humanoid arm for physical AI research in contact-rich settings, sold as a complete bimanual system for about $6.5k or built from the published design. Enactic, a Tokyo robotics company, publishes the CAD alongside CAN control, ROS 2, teleoperation, MuJoCo and Isaac Lab packages and a dataset toolkit.

chunks.title: OpenClaw
chunks.text: OpenClaw (by OpenClaw Foundation), catalog entry under UI & API: Local-first personal AI assistant that runs an agent gateway answering on the messaging channels people already use, including WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Signal, iMessage, Teams and Matrix. Companion apps cover macOS, iOS, Android, Windows and Linux, a browser Control UI handles chat and configuration, and skills and plugins extend the agent.

chunks.title: OpenClaw
chunks.text: OpenClaw (by OpenClaw Foundation), catalog entry under UI & API: The gateway is model-agnostic and routes to hosted, subscription-backed or local LLM backends.

chunks.title: OpenCLIP
chunks.text: OpenCLIP (by LAION), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: OpenCLIP is the open reimplementation of CLIP: a full contrastive pretraining pipeline plus a family of image-text checkpoints trained on LAION's published corpora rather than on a private crawl.

chunks.title: OpenCLIP
chunks.text: OpenCLIP (by LAION), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Because both halves are in the open, it is the line that made CLIP-style scaling reproducible - the ViT-bigG/14 checkpoint reaches 80.1% zero-shot ImageNet, above anything OpenAI released - and it is the reference implementation almost every later CLIP variant is trained and evaluated with.

chunks.title: OpenCode
chunks.text: OpenCode (by SST / Anomaly), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Terminal coding agent from the Anomaly team, deliberately provider-agnostic across more than seventy model providers including hosted and local models. It offers a native terminal interface with multi-session parallel agents, shareable session links, automatic LSP loading, and a client/server architecture.

chunks.title: OpenCompass
chunks.text: OpenCompass (by OpenCompass Community), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Evaluation platform covering more than a hundred datasets across open and API models, with both objective scoring and subjective arena-style comparison. Its dataset list includes many Chinese-language benchmarks, and multimodal evaluation runs through the integrated VLMEvalKit. The project is developed at Shanghai AI Laboratory.

chunks.title: OpenCV
chunks.text: OpenCV (by OpenCV), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Open Source Computer Vision Library: C++ image and video processing, feature detection, camera calibration, stereo, stitching and object detection routines with Python, Java and JavaScript bindings, plus a dnn module that runs ONNX, TensorFlow and TFLite networks. The opencv-python wheels on PyPI are built from a separate packaging repository.

chunks.title: OpenCV
chunks.text: OpenCV (by OpenCV), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Maintained by the non-profit Open Source Vision Foundation.

chunks.title: OpenFn
chunks.text: OpenFn (by Open Function Group (OpenFn)), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Workflow automation and data-integration platform used by governments and NGOs to orchestrate service workflows across legacy systems, web APIs, databases and model-backed tools. Its Lightning platform is built in Elixir and Phoenix and ships with an adaptor library as the connector layer.

chunks.title: OpenFn
chunks.text: OpenFn (by Open Function Group (OpenFn)), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: It is a verified Digital Public Good, maintained by a public benefit corporation since 2014.

chunks.title: OpenFold
chunks.text: OpenFold (by AlQuraishi Laboratory), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: OpenFold is a trainable PyTorch reproduction of AlphaFold from the AQLab consortium. Unlike the reference implementation it ships training as well as inference code, its own from-scratch trained parameters, and OpenProteinSet, some 400,000 MSAs and PDB70 template hit files hosted on the Registry of Open Data on AWS.

chunks.title: OpenFold
chunks.text: OpenFold (by AlQuraishi Laboratory), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: OpenFold3 extends the line to an all-atom AlphaFold 3-class model.

chunks.title: OpenGuardrails
chunks.text: OpenGuardrails (by OpenGuardrails), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: OpenGuardrails publishes an open safety and manipulation-detection model, a 3.3B quantized LLM covering content safety, prompt injection, jailbreak, code-interpreter abuse and data leakage across 119 languages.

chunks.title: OpenGuardrails
chunks.text: OpenGuardrails (by OpenGuardrails), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: The project also maintains OGR, an Apache-2.0 vendor-neutral protocol for agent safety with reference runtimes, Python and JavaScript SDKs, gateway and sandbox integrations, and a detector benchmark. The same team sells a commercial runtime built on the protocol, as SaaS or a licensed private deployment.

chunks.title: OpenHands
chunks.text: OpenHands (by All Hands AI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Autonomous coding agent, formerly OpenDevin, that writes code, runs commands, browses the web and calls APIs to complete software-engineering tasks end to end. It executes inside a sandboxed runtime, works with many model providers by letting users supply their own API key, and ships an SDK for building on the agent directly.

chunks.title: OpenHermes 2.5
chunks.text: OpenHermes 2.5 (by Teknium), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Synthetic instruction-following dataset of roughly a million conversational examples, compiled and generated primarily from GPT-4 outputs across math, code, roleplay and general-knowledge tasks.

chunks.title: OpenHermes 2.5
chunks.text: OpenHermes 2.5 (by Teknium), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Created by Teknium as an expansion of OpenHermes 1, it trained the OpenHermes 2.5 fine-tunes and is used as a base supervised-tuning mix by open instruction models.

chunks.title: OpenLake
chunks.text: OpenLake (by OpenLake project), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: OpenLake is a distributed storage engine for LLM inference and GPU training, built in Rust on io_uring and aimed at small-I/O throughput and sub-millisecond reads. Two surfaces sit on the same engine: an offload pool that spills KV cache off GPU nodes, and a petabyte-scale S3-compatible object store. A vLLM connector ships in the repository.

chunks.title: OpenLIT
chunks.text: OpenLIT (by OpenLIT), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: OpenTelemetry-native AI engineering platform covering LLM observability, GPU monitoring, guardrails, evaluations, and prompt management. Integrates with 50+ LLM providers, vector databases, and agent frameworks. Vault for managing API keys, plus a rule engine and a playground.

chunks.title: OpenLIT
chunks.text: OpenLIT (by OpenLIT), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Differentiated by breadth of integrations and GPU-level monitoring, and self-hostable from the repository's docker-compose file.

chunks.title: OpenLLMetry
chunks.text: OpenLLMetry (by Traceloop), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation library for LLM applications. It automatically instruments applications built with LangChain, LlamaIndex, the OpenAI SDK, and other popular frameworks, and exports telemetry data to any OTel-compatible backend, such as Jaeger, Grafana or Datadog.

chunks.title: OpenLLMetry
chunks.text: OpenLLMetry (by Traceloop), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: The 'OpenTelemetry for LLMs' approach is standards-based and vendor-neutral, shipping standard OTel instrumentations for LLM providers and vector databases alongside the Traceloop SDK.

chunks.title: OpenManus
chunks.text: OpenManus (by FoundationAgents), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: OpenManus is an open reimplementation of the Manus autonomous agent, built by members of the MetaGPT team as a general agent that needs no invite code. It performs tasks through tools and browser automation, supports MCP, and adds a data-analysis agent. It is framed as a product run from a clone rather than a reusable library.

chunks.title: OpenML
chunks.text: OpenML (by OpenML), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: OpenML is an open platform for sharing machine learning datasets together with the tasks, pipelines and experiment runs built on them. Anyone can upload a dataset from a dataframe; OpenML stores it in a uniform format under an ID and version, computes its data characteristics, and serves it to Python, R and Java clients.

chunks.title: OpenML
chunks.text: OpenML (by OpenML), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: It is run as a community project represented by the not-for-profit Open Machine Learning Foundation.

chunks.title: OpenMLDB
chunks.text: OpenMLDB (by 4Paradigm), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: OpenMLDB is a machine learning database that computes SQL-defined features consistently between offline training and online, low-latency inference. It ships as a distributed, highly-available cluster with an online and offline execution engine sharing the same feature definitions.

chunks.title: OpenPAI
chunks.text: OpenPAI (by Microsoft), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Cluster management and resource scheduling platform for AI, originally from Microsoft Research.

chunks.title: OpenPAI
chunks.text: OpenPAI (by Microsoft), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Users submit deep-learning jobs to a shared GPU cluster; OpenPAI schedules them with HiveD, a scheduler extender that models each tenant as a virtual cluster and guarantees not just a GPU count but the topology those GPUs sit in, so an eight-GPU job that must run inside one node gets a placement that satisfies it.

chunks.title: OpenPCC
chunks.text: OpenPCC (by Confident Security), catalog entry under Deployment: OpenPCC is a standard and reference implementation for verifiably private AI inference, modeled on Apple's Private Cloud Compute but vendor-neutral and self-deployable. Each request is encrypted end to end, the serving node attests its TPM and GPU beforehand, and Oblivious HTTP keeps the provider from linking requests to a user.

chunks.title: OpenPCC
chunks.text: OpenPCC (by Confident Security), catalog entry under Deployment: Confident Security maintains the Go client, a C library behind the Python and JavaScript clients, and a separate compute-node repository.

chunks.title: OpenPipe
chunks.text: OpenPipe (by OpenPipe), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: OpenPipe ships the Agent Reinforcement Trainer (ART), a library for post-training agentic LLMs with reinforcement learning (GRPO) and supervised fine-tuning. ART's client-server split lets training run on a self-hosted GPU or through a hosted backend, and OpenPipe sells a managed training and serving platform layered on the library.

chunks.title: OpenRAG
chunks.text: OpenRAG (by Linagora), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Linagora's modular retrieval-augmented generation framework, packaged as a self-hostable application stack rather than a bare library. It ingests PDFs, documents, audio and images with AI captioning, organizes knowledge into partitions, and runs hybrid semantic and keyword search with multilingual reranking.

chunks.title: OpenRAG
chunks.text: OpenRAG (by Linagora), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: A bundled chat interface, an admin UI and an OpenAI-compatible REST API sit in front, with Ray for distribution across machines and GPUs.

chunks.title: OpenRLHF
chunks.text: OpenRLHF (by OpenRLHF), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: OpenRLHF is a Ray-based distributed RLHF and agentic-RL framework that separates Actor, Reward, Reference, and Critic models across GPUs for training at 70B+ parameters.

chunks.title: OpenRLHF
chunks.text: OpenRLHF (by OpenRLHF), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: It combines Ray for scheduling, vLLM for fast rollout generation, and DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 for memory-efficient training, and supports PPO, REINFORCE++, GRPO, RLOO, and DAPO-style dynamic filtering. A published design paper (arXiv:2405.11143) documents the architecture.

chunks.title: OpenRouter
chunks.text: OpenRouter (by OpenRouter), catalog entry under UI & API: Commercial API gateway exposing models from many providers behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with automatic failover, routing and unified billing across them. It runs as a hosted service and is a routing gateway rather than a chat interface.

chunks.title: OpenSandbox
chunks.text: OpenSandbox (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Deployment: OpenSandbox is a general-purpose sandbox platform for AI agents that defines a Sandbox Protocol of lifecycle and execution APIs and implements it over Docker and Kubernetes runtimes.

chunks.title: OpenSandbox
chunks.text: OpenSandbox (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Deployment: SDKs for Python, Java/Kotlin, JavaScript, C#/.NET and Go sit on top, alongside an osb CLI and an MCP server, with built-in command, filesystem and code-interpreter environments. Operators can back a sandbox with runc, gVisor, Kata Containers or Firecracker. Alibaba originated the project.

chunks.title: OpenThoughts-114k
chunks.text: OpenThoughts-114k (by Open Thoughts), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Synthetic reasoning dataset of roughly 114,000 examples spanning math, science, code and puzzles, built by curating problem sets, generating reasoning traces with DeepSeek-R1 and then verifying correctness. It was created by the Open Thoughts team and used to train the OpenThinker 7B and 32B models.

chunks.title: OpenTinker
chunks.text: OpenTinker (by OpenTinker), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: OpenTinker trains language-model agents with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning as a service: a client defines environments and objectives, and a server-side scheduler runs jobs on shared GPUs, with many LoRA adapters sharing one base model.

chunks.title: OpenTinker
chunks.text: OpenTinker (by OpenTinker), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Training runs on verl, with examples for math, vision-language geometry, ALFWorld, Android World and Gomoku agents. It was built at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, independently of Thinking Machines, whose closed Tinker API its paper cites as motivation.

chunks.title: OpenVINO
chunks.text: OpenVINO (by Intel), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: OpenVINO is a toolkit for optimizing and deploying AI inference across computer vision, speech, NLP and generative AI. It converts models from PyTorch, TensorFlow and ONNX and deploys across x86 and Arm CPUs, Intel integrated and discrete GPUs and Intel NPUs, with a GenAI API for LLM pipelines.

chunks.title: OpenVINO
chunks.text: OpenVINO (by Intel), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It is developed by Intel and integrates with Hugging Face Optimum Intel and vLLM.

chunks.title: OpenVLA
chunks.text: OpenVLA (by OpenVLA), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: OpenVLA is a seven-billion-parameter open vision-language-action model. It fine-tunes the Prismatic VLM (DINOv2 and SigLIP vision encoders with a Llama 2 language model) on 970k manipulation episodes from Open X-Embodiment, and controls robot arms seen in that mixture from a camera image and a language instruction.

chunks.title: OpenWebMath
chunks.text: OpenWebMath (by OpenWebMath project), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Corpus of 14.7 billion tokens of mathematical web text extracted from Common Crawl with LaTeX preserved, released by researchers at the University of Toronto and collaborators. It appears in Proof-Pile-2 behind Llemma, and in OLMoE, Nemotron 3 and StarCoder2's math supplements.

chunks.title: Opik
chunks.text: Opik (by Comet ML), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Platform for debugging, evaluating and monitoring LLM applications, RAG systems and agentic workflows, providing tracing, automated evaluations and production dashboards. Built by Comet ML, its server, web application and evaluation components run on self-managed infrastructure, with Comet's cloud offered as optional managed hosting.

chunks.title: Optimum
chunks.text: Optimum (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Optimum is an extension of Transformers, Diffusers, TIMM, and Sentence-Transformers that provides tools to optimize training and inference on targeted hardware. It supports accelerators and runtimes including ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO, Intel Gaudi, AWS Trainium/Inferentia, and NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, and handles model export and quantization.

chunks.title: Optimum
chunks.text: Optimum (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It is maintained by Hugging Face.

chunks.title: Orama
chunks.text: Orama (by OramaSearch), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Orama is a full-text, vector and hybrid search engine that runs embedded in the browser, on a server, or at the edge, in under 2KB of core JavaScript. It indexes and stores documents itself rather than talking to a separate server, with no native dependencies.

chunks.title: Orange Pi 5
chunks.text: Orange Pi 5 (by Orange Pi (Shenzhen Xunlong)), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Single-board computer built around the Rockchip RK3588S, an eight-core 64-bit Arm processor pairing four Cortex-A76 with four Cortex-A55, a Mali-G610 GPU and a built-in NPU rated at 6 TOPS. It ships in 4GB, 8GB and 16GB LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X configurations and runs Android, Debian, Ubuntu and Orange Pi OS.

chunks.title: Orange Pi 5
chunks.text: Orange Pi 5 (by Orange Pi (Shenzhen Xunlong)), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Orange Pi, trading as Shenzhen Xunlong, makes it.

chunks.title: Orb
chunks.text: Orb (by Orbital Materials), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Orb is Orbital Materials' family of pretrained interatomic potentials for atomic simulations, covering inorganic crystals through the orb-v2 and orb-v3 series and molecular systems through OrbMol.

chunks.title: Orb
chunks.text: Orb (by Orbital Materials), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: The models predict energies, forces and stresses, expose a per-atom confidence head, integrate with ASE and TorchSim, and can be finetuned on a custom dataset with the packaged script.

chunks.title: Ornith 1.0 9B
chunks.text: Ornith 1.0 9B (by DeepReinforce), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: DeepReinforce's open-weights agentic coding model, a 9B dense model built on the Qwen 3.5 architecture, with explicit <think> reasoning and tool-calling for terminal-based software-engineering tasks. Optimized for single-GPU deployment (~19GB in bf16).

chunks.title: OSCAR-2301
chunks.text: OSCAR-2301 (by OSCAR Project), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: OSCAR-2301 is a multilingual web corpus extracted from the November/December 2022 Common Crawl snapshot and distributed by language in original and deduplicated versions, covering 151 languages. Its documents carry KenLM-based adult content detection and precomputed locality-sensitive hashes for near deduplication.

chunks.title: OSCAR-2301
chunks.text: OSCAR-2301 (by OSCAR Project), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: The OSCAR project publishes it.

chunks.title: Osprey
chunks.text: Osprey (by ROOST), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Safety rules engine for real-time abuse mitigation, originally built at Discord and donated to ROOST. It evaluates events and their properties in real time using a Python-based rules DSL called SML, ingesting signals including machine-learning classifier outputs to detect and action spam, abuse and policy violations.

chunks.title: Osprey
chunks.text: Osprey (by ROOST), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: It is Trust and Safety operational infrastructure rather than an AI guardrail model.

chunks.title: OSWorld
chunks.text: OSWorld (by XLang AI Lab), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Real-computer environment and execution-based harness for benchmarking multimodal computer-use agents on 369 open-ended tasks across Ubuntu, Windows and macOS. Agents drive a virtual desktop and are scored by 134 execution-based evaluation functions against full trajectories, running under VMware, VirtualBox or Docker with KVM.

chunks.title: Otari
chunks.text: Otari (by Mozilla AI), catalog entry under UI & API: Open, self-hosted OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway from Mozilla AI. It puts one endpoint in front of many providers with virtual API keys, budget enforcement and usage tracking, and ships server-side model-agnostic tools including sandboxed code execution in a Docker-isolated Python REPL. Built on Mozilla AI's any-llm, with a hosted platform running on the same core.

chunks.title: OWASP AIBOM Generator
chunks.text: OWASP AIBOM Generator (by OWASP), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: The OWASP AIBOM Generator produces AI Bills of Materials in CycloneDX 1.6 JSON for models hosted on Hugging Face, extracting metadata from model cards, configurations and repository files. It scores how complete each bill of materials is and suggests what is missing, and is listed in the CycloneDX Tool Center.

chunks.title: OWASP AIBOM Generator
chunks.text: OWASP AIBOM Generator (by OWASP), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: It runs under the OWASP GenAI Security Project, with a hosted instance for trying it.

chunks.title: Oxen
chunks.text: Oxen (by Oxen.ai), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Oxen is a data version control system built for large repositories of files, from training data and model weights to game assets. It mirrors git's workflow (init, add, commit, push, pull) while handling millions of files and terabytes of data, with a Rust core (`liboxen`), a CLI, Python bindings, and a self-hostable Oxen Server for remotes.

chunks.title: P2PFL
chunks.text: P2PFL (by P2PFL), catalog entry under Federated learning: P2PFL is a Python library for decentralized federated learning, in which peers exchange model updates over a peer-to-peer network with gossip protocols instead of reporting to a central server. The same code runs as an in-memory or Ray simulation or across machines over gRPC, where mutual TLS admits only nodes holding certificates from a shared authority.

chunks.title: P2PFL
chunks.text: P2PFL (by P2PFL), catalog entry under Federated learning: It trains PyTorch, TensorFlow/Keras and JAX models and can add local differential privacy to outgoing updates.

chunks.title: PaddlePaddle
chunks.text: PaddlePaddle (by PaddlePaddle), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: PaddlePaddle is a deep learning framework developed by Baidu, covering training and inference in one codebase.

chunks.title: PaddlePaddle
chunks.text: PaddlePaddle (by PaddlePaddle), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Release 3.2 unifies dynamic and static graphs with automatic parallelism, deriving a distributed strategy from tensor partitioning annotations written against a single-device configuration, and adds high-order differentiation for scientific computing.

chunks.title: PaddleOCR
chunks.text: PaddleOCR (by PaddlePaddle), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: OCR and document-parsing toolkit from Baidu's PaddlePaddle project, covering text detection and recognition in more than a hundred languages plus table, formula and seal recognition, and a document-parsing pipeline that emits Markdown and JSON. PaddleOCR-VL is its vision-language parsing model.

chunks.title: Alibaba Cloud PAI-DLC
chunks.text: Alibaba Cloud PAI-DLC (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Managed distributed training service in Alibaba Cloud's Platform for AI. Jobs are submitted as typed distributed training workloads - PyTorch, TensorFlow and others - onto resource quotas backed by GPU instances, and the service manages their queued, running and terminal states for the life of the run.

chunks.title: PaliGemma
chunks.text: PaliGemma (by Google), catalog entry under Multimodal models: PaliGemma is Google's vision-language model built from the SigLIP vision encoder and Gemma language models, designed to be fine-tuned for specific tasks. PaliGemma 2 comes in 3B, 10B and 28B sizes at 224 to 896 pixel resolution and outputs captions, answers, text read from images, bounding boxes and segmentation codes.

chunks.title: PaliGemma
chunks.text: PaliGemma (by Google), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Google releases pretrained, task-transfer and mixed-task checkpoints.

chunks.title: Pangu-Weather
chunks.text: Pangu-Weather (by Huawei), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Pangu-Weather is Huawei Cloud's 3D transformer for medium-range global weather forecasting, released as four ONNX checkpoints with lead times of 1, 3, 6, and 24 hours that are chained to build longer forecasts. The repository provides inference scripts and algorithm pseudocode; ECMWF has run the published models in its own charts.

chunks.title: ParadeDB
chunks.text: ParadeDB (by ParadeDB), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: ParadeDB is a Postgres extension that adds a custom index for full-text search with BM25 scoring, vector search, filtering and aggregations directly inside Postgres, so application data and search live in one database rather than two systems kept in sync.

chunks.title: Parakeet
chunks.text: Parakeet (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Speech & audio: NVIDIA's FastConformer transducer and CTC speech recognition models. The current Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 transcribes 25 European languages with word-level timestamps and runs thousands of times faster than real time on a GPU; earlier checkpoints are English-only.

chunks.title: Parallel Search API
chunks.text: Parallel Search API (by Parallel Web Systems), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Search API that takes a natural-language objective rather than keywords and returns ranked URLs with compressed excerpts of their content, sized for a model's context. One of six separately priced APIs Parallel Web Systems sells.

chunks.title: Pathway
chunks.text: Pathway (by Pathway), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Python stream-processing and ETL framework on a Rust dataflow engine, unifying batch and streaming under one API with live connectors and production RAG templates. Unlike glue-layer frameworks it is an incremental dataflow engine, keeping vector indexes continuously synced with changing data instead of re-indexing in batches.

chunks.title: Pathway
chunks.text: Pathway (by Pathway), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: It runs from a single node to Kubernetes.

chunks.title: Patronus Evaluation Platform
chunks.text: Patronus Evaluation Platform (by Patronus AI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Managed evaluation platform built around in-house judge models: Lynx for hallucination detection, GLIDER for explainable rubric judging and Percival for analyzing agent execution traces.

chunks.title: Patronus Evaluation Platform
chunks.text: Patronus Evaluation Platform (by Patronus AI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: It runs experiments for A/B testing, real-time production monitoring with tracing and alerts, and red-teaming, reached through Python and TypeScript SDKs.

chunks.title: PEFT
chunks.text: PEFT (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: PEFT (Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning) is a Hugging Face library that adapts large pretrained models by training a small set of extra parameters instead of the full model. It implements LoRA and its DoRA and QLoRA variants, plus AdaLoRA, IA3, prompt tuning, and prefix tuning, attached to a base model through get_peft_model or Transformers' add_adapter.

chunks.title: PEFT
chunks.text: PEFT (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: PEFT also integrates with Diffusers and Accelerate, and TRL applies it to RLHF training.

chunks.title: Perception LM
chunks.text: Perception LM (by Meta), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Perception LM (PLM) is Meta FAIR's family of vision-language models for detailed image and video understanding, in 1B, 3B and 8B sizes that pair the Perception Encoder with Llama 3.2 and Llama 3.1 language models.

chunks.title: Perception LM
chunks.text: Perception LM (by Meta), catalog entry under Multimodal models: It answers questions about images, documents, charts and video, including fine-grained and spatio-temporally grounded questions about what happens in a clip. Meta released it with its human-labeled video training data and the PLM-VideoBench benchmark.

chunks.title: Vane
chunks.text: Vane (by ItzCrazyKns), catalog entry under UI & API: Answer engine that returns answers with citations, pairing a bundled SearXNG metasearch layer with local or cloud models so queries stay on the machine the operator runs. It works with Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and offers web, academic, discussion, image and video search modes plus file-upload retrieval.

chunks.title: Perplexity
chunks.text: Perplexity (by Perplexity AI), catalog entry under UI & API: Search-grounded consumer chat product that answers questions with cited sources. It routes over models from several providers including OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, and adds guided deep research, a voice mode, and an assistant that drafts messages and makes bookings. It ships as a mobile app that syncs across devices, distinct from the Perplexity API.

chunks.title: Perplexity Sonar API
chunks.text: Perplexity Sonar API (by Perplexity AI), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Perplexity's Sonar API is a search-augmented LLM API that combines real-time web search with model reasoning to produce answers with citations. Where a search API returns raw results, Sonar returns a synthesized, cited answer, and Perplexity's developer platform also offers a separate Search API for raw ranked results.

chunks.title: Perplexity Sonar API
chunks.text: Perplexity Sonar API (by Perplexity AI), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: It is offered alongside Perplexity's consumer product.

chunks.title: PersonaHub
chunks.text: PersonaHub (by Tencent AI Lab), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Persona-driven synthetic data resource from Tencent AI Lab, backed by the paper "Scaling Synthetic Data Creation with 1,000,000,000 Personas".

chunks.title: PersonaHub
chunks.text: PersonaHub (by Tencent AI Lab), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: It releases a large set of distilled personas - a 200,000-persona preview alongside roughly 370 million elite personas - plus seed synthetic samples including 50,000 math problems, 50,000 logical-reasoning problems and 50,000 instructions.

chunks.title: PersonaPlex
chunks.text: PersonaPlex (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Speech & audio: NVIDIA's full-duplex speech-to-speech conversation model, fine-tuned from Kyutai's Moshi: it listens and speaks at the same time, handling interruptions and fast turn-taking, and takes a text role prompt and a voice sample to set its persona. English only.

chunks.title: Perspective API
chunks.text: Perspective API (by Jigsaw), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Jigsaw's free hosted API for scoring the toxicity of text and related attributes such as insult, threat and identity attack. It has been used for comment moderation since 2017. Jigsaw has announced that the service is sunsetting and will be out of operation after 2026.

chunks.title: peS2o
chunks.text: peS2o (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Ai2's corpus of roughly 40 million cleaned academic papers derived from S2ORC on Semantic Scholar. It is a standard open scientific-text component, documented in the pretraining mixes for OLMoE, Marin and NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.

chunks.title: pfl-research
chunks.text: pfl-research (by Apple), catalog entry under Federated learning: Apple's Python framework for private federated learning simulations. Researchers run fast simulations across processes, GPUs and machines, with local and central differential privacy mechanisms built in and benchmark suites over realistic datasets.

chunks.title: PFLlib
chunks.text: PFLlib (by TsingZ0), catalog entry under Federated learning: Personalized federated learning library and benchmark, built to be beginner-friendly. It implements traditional and personalized federated algorithms over heterogeneous-data scenarios, simulates hundreds of clients on a single GPU, includes privacy-evaluation attacks, and maintains a public leaderboard.

chunks.title: pgvector
chunks.text: pgvector (by pgvector project), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: pgvector is a Postgres extension that adds vector types and similarity search to the database, supporting exact and approximate nearest neighbour queries over single-precision, half-precision, binary and sparse vectors with L2, inner-product, cosine, L1, Hamming and Jaccard distances.

chunks.title: pgvector
chunks.text: pgvector (by pgvector project), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Vectors live in ordinary tables, so joins, transactions and point-in-time recovery apply to them.

chunks.title: pgvectorscale
chunks.text: pgvectorscale (by Tiger Data), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: pgvectorscale is a Postgres extension that complements pgvector with a StreamingDiskANN index, inspired by Microsoft's DiskANN research, and a statistical binary quantization scheme for cost-efficient storage at scale. It also adds label-based filtered vector search, combining similarity search with metadata filtering in a single index.

chunks.title: pgvectorscale
chunks.text: pgvectorscale (by Tiger Data), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Written in Rust using the PGRX framework and developed by Tiger Data (formerly Timescale).

chunks.title: Phi-4
chunks.text: Phi-4 (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Phi-4 is Microsoft's 14B dense small language model, announced in December 2024 and fully released the following month. It was trained on 9.8 trillion tokens of heavily curated and synthetic data, with a recipe that centers on data quality and uses synthetic data throughout training.

chunks.title: Phi-4
chunks.text: Phi-4 (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: The line has since been extended with mini, multimodal, reasoning and reasoning-vision variants.

chunks.title: Phi-4-mini-instruct
chunks.text: Phi-4-mini-instruct (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Phi-4-mini-instruct is a 3.8B-parameter dense decoder-only language model with a 128K-token context window, tuned for chat and instruction following through supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization. Microsoft positions it for memory-constrained and latency-bound settings.

chunks.title: Phi-4-mini-instruct
chunks.text: Phi-4-mini-instruct (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: It belongs to the Phi-4 family, alongside reasoning and multimodal variants.

chunks.title: Phoenix
chunks.text: Phoenix (by Arize AI), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Phoenix is an AI observability and evaluation toolkit from Arize AI that provides tracing, datasets and experiments, prompt management with a playground, and LLM evaluation. It instruments applications through OpenTelemetry, with integrations for LlamaIndex and LangChain, and deploys via Docker or a Helm chart.

chunks.title: PhysioNet
chunks.text: PhysioNet (by MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: PhysioNet is a publishing platform for de-identified biomedical and clinical data, run by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology with NIH funding. Researchers submit databases, software and models that content editors review before publication.

chunks.title: PhysioNet
chunks.text: PhysioNet (by MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: Each published version is fixed, most data is open while sensitive clinical records need credentialed access, and files download by versioned path over the web or from S3.

chunks.title: Pi
chunks.text: Pi (by Earendil), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Pi is a terminal coding agent built as a minimal, extensible harness. It ships read, write, edit and bash tools, works across many model providers with mid-session switching, and runs interactively, in print or JSON mode, over RPC or through a TypeScript SDK.

chunks.title: Pi
chunks.text: Pi (by Earendil), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Sub-agents, plan mode and permission controls are left to extensions, skills and installable Pi packages. Mario Zechner created Pi, and Earendil now owns and develops it.

chunks.title: π0 (openpi)
chunks.text: π0 (openpi) (by Physical Intelligence), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: π0 is Physical Intelligence's line of vision-language-action models, released with training and inference code in the openpi repository. It spans π0, a flow-matching VLA, π0-FAST, an autoregressive variant using the FAST action tokenizer, and π0.5, which generalizes better to new environments.

chunks.title: π0 (openpi)
chunks.text: π0 (openpi) (by Physical Intelligence), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Base checkpoints are pretrained on over ten thousand hours of robot data.

chunks.title: Pinecone
chunks.text: Pinecone (by Pinecone), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Pinecone is a fully managed vector database offered as a serverless cloud service, with sparse-dense hybrid search built in. It is used through an API rather than installed, and a BYOC option runs its data plane inside a customer's own cloud account.

chunks.title: Pipedream Connect
chunks.text: Pipedream Connect (by Pipedream), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Managed authentication and tool-calling for agents: Pipedream runs the OAuth flow, stores and refreshes the tokens, and injects them per user on every request across roughly 3,000 APIs and 10,000 prebuilt tools.

chunks.title: Piper
chunks.text: Piper (by Open Home Foundation), catalog entry under Speech & audio: A fast, local neural text-to-speech engine that embeds espeak-ng for phonemization, with a large catalog of downloadable voices and documented voice training. Its README lists Home Assistant and the NVDA screen reader among its users.

chunks.title: Pixeltable
chunks.text: Pixeltable (by Pixeltable), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Pixeltable is a unified multimodal backend for AI data apps. It stores images, video, audio, documents and structured data in one table interface, indexes embeddings, and runs models and transformations from computed columns declared on insert, in place of separately gluing together blob storage, a vector database and an orchestrator.

chunks.title: Plato
chunks.text: Plato (by TL-System), catalog entry under Federated learning: Research framework for federated learning. Experiments run from a configuration file on one machine or in Docker, and the server can also be deployed on a public cloud behind HTTPS with clients connecting from elsewhere. It includes LoRA fine-tuning of Hugging Face language models and a homomorphic-encryption secure-aggregation example.

chunks.title: Playwright MCP
chunks.text: Playwright MCP (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: MCP server that gives agents browser automation through Playwright: navigating pages, clicking elements, filling forms, taking screenshots and extracting structured data. It works from structured accessibility snapshots rather than screenshots, so the agent reads a page as a tree rather than as pixels.

chunks.title: Playwright MCP
chunks.text: Playwright MCP (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: It is backed by Microsoft and integrated with VS Code and Copilot.

chunks.title: pmdarima
chunks.text: pmdarima (by alkaline-ml), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Python equivalent of R's auto.arima, which searches ARIMA and seasonal ARIMA orders for a time series automatically. Around that search it adds stationarity and seasonality tests, differencing, Box-Cox and Fourier transformers, pipelines and time-series cross-validation, with a scikit-learn-style interface over statsmodels.

chunks.title: Poe
chunks.text: Poe (by Quora), catalog entry under UI & API: Multi-model chat aggregator from Quora, giving access to many providers' models plus image, video and audio generators from one interface, on a points-based unified pricing model. Alongside the providers' own assistants it carries bots that users build and publish themselves, which is what distinguishes it from a single-vendor chat surface.

chunks.title: PolicyLM
chunks.text: PolicyLM (by Musubi), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: PolicyLM is Musubi's 1.7B-parameter moderation classifier: given a message and a policy written as short plain-language categories, it returns a score from 0 to 1 for every category in one pass, without generating text. A built-in mode scores against NVIDIA's 23-category Aegis 2.0 taxonomy instead.

chunks.title: PolicyLM
chunks.text: PolicyLM (by Musubi), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: It is meant for user content such as chat messages and posts, was evaluated in 19 languages, and runs on a single 24 GB GPU or a CPU.

chunks.title: Polyaxon
chunks.text: Polyaxon (by Polyaxon), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Platform for running and tracking machine-learning workloads on Kubernetes. Operations are submitted to queues that route them to an agent managing a namespace or a whole cluster, with quotas, priorities and concurrency limits applied on the way.

chunks.title: Polyaxon
chunks.text: Polyaxon (by Polyaxon), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Polyaxon Community Edition carries the core platform; queues, RBAC and retention are part of the commercial editions.

chunks.title: Postgres MCP Pro
chunks.text: Postgres MCP Pro (by Crystal DBA), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Actively maintained PostgreSQL MCP server (Python) by Crystal DBA, 'Postgres MCP Pro', that goes beyond read-only querying to database performance and health tooling for agents: schema/object inspection, execute_sql with access modes, EXPLAIN with hypothetical-index simulation, slow-query analysis, index advising, and health checks.

chunks.title: Pralekha
chunks.text: Pralekha (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Pralekha is a parallel corpus and benchmark of whole documents covering 11 Indic languages and English, with more than 3 million aligned document pairs, 1.5 million of them English-Indic.

chunks.title: Pralekha
chunks.text: Pralekha (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The documents are Press Information Bureau releases and Mann Ki Baat radio scripts, and unalignable documents sampled from Sangraha are mixed in to test cross-lingual document alignment. AI4Bharat built it, with train, dev and test splits for translating whole documents.

chunks.title: Predibase
chunks.text: Predibase (by Predibase), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Predibase is a managed platform for fine-tuning and serving language models, offering supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement fine-tuning with GRPO, and continued pretraining. It deploys as SaaS or inside a customer's own VPC and serves models through LoRAX, the multi-LoRA inference engine its founders publish alongside Ludwig, a declarative ML framework.

chunks.title: Predibase
chunks.text: Predibase (by Predibase), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Rubrik acquired Predibase in June 2025 and runs it within its AI Agent Operations platform.

chunks.title: Presto
chunks.text: Presto (by NASA Harvest), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Presto, the Pretrained Remote Sensing Transformer, is a lightweight self-supervised model from NASA Harvest for remote-sensing pixel timeseries.

chunks.title: Presto
chunks.text: Presto (by NASA Harvest), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: It consumes between one and twenty-four monthly timesteps of Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, ERA5 meteorology, SRTM topography, Dynamic World classes, and latitude and longitude, and exposes an encoder whose pooled embeddings are fine-tuned for downstream classification and regression.

chunks.title: prime-rl
chunks.text: prime-rl (by Prime Intellect), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: prime-rl is a framework for asynchronous reinforcement learning on language models at large scale, using FSDP2 for training and vLLM for inference.

chunks.title: prime-rl
chunks.text: prime-rl (by Prime Intellect), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: It covers SFT, RL and evaluation in one stack, trains on multi-turn and agentic tasks written as verifiers environments, and is designed to train mixture-of-experts models above a trillion parameters across more than 1,000 GPUs under Slurm. Prime Intellect develops it.

chunks.title: Prithvi-EO
chunks.text: Prithvi-EO (by NASA IMPACT), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Prithvi-EO is an Earth-observation foundation-model family jointly developed by NASA and IBM.

chunks.title: Prithvi-EO
chunks.text: Prithvi-EO (by NASA IMPACT), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Its spatiotemporal vision transformer consumes Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel imagery together with location and acquisition-time metadata, and the release includes several model sizes plus configurations and notebooks for downstream remote-sensing tasks.

chunks.title: Prithvi WxC
chunks.text: Prithvi WxC (by NASA IMPACT), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Prithvi WxC is a NASA-IBM weather and climate foundation model trained on 160 MERRA-2 variables. Its 2.3-billion-parameter architecture combines masked reconstruction with forecasting, accepts flexible time intervals, and has separate base and rollout checkpoints plus downstream adaptations for regional forecasting and climate processes.

chunks.title: PrivateGPT
chunks.text: PrivateGPT (by Zylon), catalog entry under UI & API: PrivateGPT is an API layer for building private AI applications against local or self-hosted models.

chunks.title: PrivateGPT
chunks.text: PrivateGPT (by Zylon), catalog entry under UI & API: It exposes a messages API with streaming and token counting, file and artifact ingestion, retrieval with citations and agentic RAG, built-in tools mirroring the Claude API, custom tools and MCP connectors, structured access to databases and CSV files, and embeddings. It works with any OpenAI-compatible model server.

chunks.title: Privatemode
chunks.text: Privatemode (by Edgeless Systems), catalog entry under UI & API: Confidential-computing AI inference service from Edgeless Systems. Prompts are encrypted on the device and processed inside hardware-based Trusted Execution Environments on confidential VMs with Nvidia GPUs, so data stays encrypted during inference and the provider cannot read it; end-to-end remote attestation makes the guarantee checkable.

chunks.title: Privatemode
chunks.text: Privatemode (by Edgeless Systems), catalog entry under UI & API: It serves third-party open-weights models behind a chat interface and an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API, aimed at regulated industries.

chunks.title: promptfoo
chunks.text: promptfoo (by promptfoo), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Declarative CLI and Node library that tests prompts, models and RAG pipelines from a YAML config, comparing model outputs side by side and running the same checks in CI. It also ships a red-teaming mode that scans an application for vulnerabilities.

chunks.title: PromptLayer
chunks.text: PromptLayer (by PromptLayer), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: PromptLayer is a prompt management and monitoring platform that logs LLM API requests with their prompts, responses, cost and latency. It provides a prompt registry with versioning and a no-code editor, traces including OpenTelemetry ingestion, and evaluations over datasets.

chunks.title: PromptLayer
chunks.text: PromptLayer (by PromptLayer), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: It is reached over an API key, with an open-source client library and a self-hosted option on the Enterprise plan.

chunks.title: Prophet
chunks.text: Prophet (by Meta), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Time-series forecasting procedure from Meta's Core Data Science team that fits an additive model of non-linear trend, yearly, weekly and daily seasonality and holiday effects, in R and Python over a shared Stan core. It produces automated forecasts with uncertainty intervals that analysts can tune by hand.

chunks.title: Prophet
chunks.text: Prophet (by Meta), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Since v1.4.0 it is in maintenance mode, taking bug fixes but no new features.

chunks.title: Public AI Inference Utility
chunks.text: Public AI Inference Utility (by Public AI Inference Utility), catalog entry under Inference code: The Public AI Inference Utility is a nonprofit hosted inference service that gives developers an OpenAI-compatible API to open models from public institutions, among them Switzerland's Apertus, AI Singapore's SEA-LION and Poland's Bielik.

chunks.title: Public AI Inference Utility
chunks.text: Public AI Inference Utility (by Public AI Inference Utility), catalog entry under Inference code: A gateway routes each request to vLLM servers running on compute donated by partners such as AWS, Exoscale and the Jülich Supercomputing Centre. The same models are offered through Hugging Face as an inference provider, and the developer portal and gateway code are published under the MIT license.

chunks.title: Puppeteer
chunks.text: Puppeteer (by Puppeteer), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: JavaScript library that drives Chrome or Firefox over the DevTools Protocol or WebDriver BiDi. It serves as the browser-control layer that several higher-level agent automation tools are built on top of.

chunks.title: pyannote.audio
chunks.text: pyannote.audio (by pyannote), catalog entry under Speech & audio: An open-source PyTorch toolkit for speaker diarization: who spoke when. It bundles pretrained segmentation, embedding and clustering pipelines, the open community-1 pipeline among them, and a client for pyannoteAI's paid premium pipeline.

chunks.title: PyBullet
chunks.text: PyBullet (by Bullet Physics), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: PyBullet is the Python interface to the Bullet Physics SDK, a real-time collision-detection and rigid-body simulation library used for robotics, reinforcement learning and VR. It loads robots from URDF, ships example gym-style environments and robot models, and renders through a basic OpenGL viewer.

chunks.title: PyBullet
chunks.text: PyBullet (by Bullet Physics), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: The C++ SDK is maintained by Erwin Coumans in the bullet3 repository.

chunks.title: PyCaret
chunks.text: PyCaret (by PyCaret), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Low-code machine-learning library that wraps scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost and other libraries behind a few calls.

chunks.title: PyCaret
chunks.text: PyCaret (by PyCaret), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: After a setup step it trains and ranks every applicable model with one function, then tunes, blends, evaluates and deploys the chosen pipeline, for classification, regression, clustering, anomaly detection and time-series forecasting. The 4.0 line in development adds a web control plane and moves the engine to the Functional Source License.

chunks.title: PydanticAI
chunks.text: PydanticAI (by Pydantic), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Python agent framework from the Pydantic team that brings type safety to production agents: structured outputs validated as they stream, typed dependency injection, tools and dynamic instructions, MCP and UI event streams, human-in-the-loop and graph support. It is model-agnostic across providers.

chunks.title: PyOD
chunks.text: PyOD (by yzhao062), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Outlier and anomaly detection library with more than sixty detectors behind one fit/predict API, covering tabular data, time series, graphs and, through foundation-model embeddings, text, images and audio.

chunks.title: PyOD
chunks.text: PyOD (by yzhao062), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Version 3 adds ADEngine, which profiles a dataset, picks and runs detectors and assesses the results, and an agent skill and MCP server that drive it from natural-language requests. It is led by Yue Zhao with an advisory committee.

chunks.title: PyRIT
chunks.text: PyRIT (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: The Python Risk Identification Tool (PyRIT) is an open framework from the Microsoft AI Red Team that automates red-teaming of generative AI systems. It orchestrates adversarial prompts, single- and multi-turn attack strategies and scoring to surface harms and vulnerabilities at scale, against targets from hosted model APIs to custom HTTP endpoints.

chunks.title: PyRIT
chunks.text: PyRIT (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: A command-line scanner and a local GUI sit alongside the Python library.

chunks.title: Syft / PySyft
chunks.text: Syft / PySyft (by OpenMined), catalog entry under Federated learning: PySyft is OpenMined's library for privacy-preserving data science on data that stays with its owner.

chunks.title: Syft / PySyft
chunks.text: Syft / PySyft (by OpenMined), catalog entry under Federated learning: A data scientist submits computations that the data owner approves and runs on private data, over cloud storage the organizations already use, such as Google Drive, with sandboxed job execution, per-collaborator approval and an optional Trusted Execution Environment package.

chunks.title: Pythia
chunks.text: Pythia (by EleutherAI), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: EleutherAI's suite of sixteen models from 70M to 12B parameters, eight sizes trained twice on The Pile and its deduplicated variant, in the same data order, with 154 intermediate checkpoints released for each.

chunks.title: Pythia
chunks.text: Pythia (by EleutherAI), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: It is a research tool for studying how language models learn rather than a production family, and the dataloader tooling makes the exact token order reconstructable.

chunks.title: PyTorch
chunks.text: PyTorch (by PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: PyTorch is a Python package for tensor computation with GPU acceleration and for deep neural networks built on a tape-based autograd system. It works alongside Python libraries such as NumPy, SciPy and Cython, and provides distributed training across multiple GPUs and machines.

chunks.title: PyTorch Hub
chunks.text: PyTorch Hub (by PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Index of pretrained PyTorch models at pytorch.org/hub.

chunks.title: PyTorch Hub
chunks.text: PyTorch Hub (by PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: A publisher adds a hubconf.py to its own GitHub repository and opens a pull request to pytorch/hub with a model page; once merged, the model is listed on the site and torch.hub.load fetches the code from the publisher's repository and the weights from wherever the publisher hosts them.

chunks.title: PyTorch Hub
chunks.text: PyTorch Hub (by PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: The hub stores no weights itself. It is listed on the PyTorch Foundation's pytorch.org, and the loader ships inside PyTorch.

chunks.title: PyTorch Lightning
chunks.text: PyTorch Lightning (by Lightning AI), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: PyTorch Lightning is a training abstraction over PyTorch. Its Trainer and Fabric interfaces move the same model code between CPU, CUDA and Apple Silicon GPUs, TPUs, multi-GPU and multi-node runs without changing the model, and expose distributed strategies including DDP, FSDP and DeepSpeed together with mixed precision.

chunks.title: Qdrant
chunks.text: Qdrant (by Qdrant), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Qdrant is a vector database and similarity search engine written in Rust. It stores vectors with JSON payloads that queries can filter on, and supports dense, sparse and multivector search, hybrid queries and quantization. Teams run it self-hosted from a Docker image or use the managed Qdrant Cloud service.

chunks.title: Qualcomm AI Engine Direct
chunks.text: Qualcomm AI Engine Direct (by Qualcomm), catalog entry under Inference code: Qualcomm AI Engine Direct, also called the Qualcomm AI Runtime (QAIRT or QNN), is an on-device inference SDK for Snapdragon processors, distributed as a separate SDK download from Qualcomm. It exposes a unified low-level API over the Hexagon NPU/HTP, Adreno GPU, and Kryo CPU.

chunks.title: Qualcomm AI Engine Direct
chunks.text: Qualcomm AI Engine Direct (by Qualcomm), catalog entry under Inference code: LiteRT, ONNX Runtime, and ExecuTorch delegate to it as their Qualcomm NPU backend. Qualcomm's qai-appbuilder, formerly ai-engine-direct-helper, wraps it in a convenience API on GitHub.

chunks.title: Qualcomm AI Hub Models
chunks.text: Qualcomm AI Hub Models (by Qualcomm), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Qualcomm's catalog of machine learning models optimized for Snapdragon and other Qualcomm devices, browsable at aihub.qualcomm.com and installable as the qai-hub-models package. A CLI and Python API browse the catalog and fetch deployable assets per runtime and precision, and demos run locally in PyTorch.

chunks.title: Qualcomm AI Hub Models
chunks.text: Qualcomm AI Hub Models (by Qualcomm), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Compiling and profiling on real devices goes through the hosted Qualcomm AI Hub Workbench.

chunks.title: Qualcomm Dragonwing RB3 Gen 2 Development Kit
chunks.text: Qualcomm Dragonwing RB3 Gen 2 Development Kit (by Qualcomm), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Qualcomm edge AI and IoT development kit built around the QCS6490 SoC, pairing a Kryo 670 CPU, an Adreno 643L GPU and a Hexagon NPU rated at 12 TOPS. It follows the modular 96Boards form factor and ships with a Qualcomm Linux and Android SDK stack, with support in Qualcomm AI Hub and Edge Impulse.

chunks.title: Qualcomm Dragonwing RB3 Gen 2 Development Kit
chunks.text: Qualcomm Dragonwing RB3 Gen 2 Development Kit (by Qualcomm), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: It is a reference platform for prototyping commercial edge-AI products.

chunks.title: Quilt
chunks.text: Quilt (by Quilt Data), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Quilt is a scientific data management platform on AWS that packages data with metadata, documentation and version history for reuse.

chunks.title: Quilt
chunks.text: Quilt (by Quilt Data), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: It ships a Python SDK and CLI for creating and installing versioned data packages on S3, and a self-deployed catalog stack (web UI, Lambda indexing services, and a search cluster) for browsing, searching and visualizing them.

chunks.title: Qwen Base
chunks.text: Qwen Base (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Alibaba's pretrained Qwen base models, published for fine-tuning and research rather than chat. The current base generation is Qwen3.5, released in February 2026 in five sizes from 0.8B to a 35B mixture of experts with 3B active parameters.

chunks.title: Qwen Base
chunks.text: Qwen Base (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Qwen has published no base checkpoints for Qwen 3.6 or 3.8, whose open-weight models ship post-trained only.

chunks.title: Qwen3-ASR
chunks.text: Qwen3-ASR (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Alibaba's Qwen3-ASR speech recognition models (1.7B and 0.6B), built on the Qwen3 audio stack. They identify the language and transcribe 30 languages and 22 Chinese dialects, and a companion forced-alignment model predicts timestamps.

chunks.title: Qwen Code
chunks.text: Qwen Code (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Qwen Code is a coding agent from Alibaba's Qwen team that runs in the terminal and through editor plugins, a desktop app, a browser UI and chat apps. It works with the OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen APIs or a local model, and ships sub-agents, agent teams, MCP, plan mode and SDKs for three languages.

chunks.title: Qwen Code
chunks.text: Qwen Code (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: The project began as a fork of Google's Gemini CLI and now develops on its own.

chunks.title: Qwen3-Coder
chunks.text: Qwen3-Coder (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct is a mixture-of-experts model with 480 billion total and 35 billion active parameters across 160 experts, tuned for non-thinking instruction-following and agentic coding. It supports a native context window of 256K tokens, extendable to 1M tokens with Yarn.

chunks.title: Qwen-Image
chunks.text: Qwen-Image (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Qwen-Image is Alibaba's Qwen family of image generation and editing models, designed for complex text rendering and precise editing. Its current release, Qwen-Image 3.0, is served only through Alibaba Cloud Model Studio.

chunks.title: Qwen-Image
