chunks.text: Qwen-Image (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: The downloadable line runs from the original 20B Qwen-Image and its Edit, Layered and 2512 updates to Qwen-Image-2.1, a unified generation-and-editing model that takes up to ten reference images.

chunks.title: Qwen 3.8
chunks.text: Qwen 3.8 (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Alibaba's post-trained Qwen chat models.

chunks.title: Qwen 3.8
chunks.text: Qwen 3.8 (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: The current release, Qwen 3.8 from August 2026, ships three open-weight models that think by default and can answer directly on request: a dense 27B under Apache-2.0, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a 125B mixture of experts with 6B active parameters, and the 2.4-trillion-parameter Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, which is also the base of the hosted Qwen3.8-Max.

chunks.title: Qwen 3.8
chunks.text: Qwen 3.8 (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: From Qwen 3.5 on, Alibaba publishes its chat checkpoints under the plain release name rather than as Instruct models.

chunks.title: Qwen-Omni
chunks.text: Qwen-Omni (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Qwen-Omni is Alibaba's omni-modal model line, which takes text, images, audio and video as input and answers in text or in streaming natural speech. Its current release, Qwen3.5-Omni, is served only through Alibaba Cloud's API.

chunks.title: Qwen-Omni
chunks.text: Qwen-Omni (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Multimodal models: The earlier Qwen3-Omni, a mixture-of-experts Thinker-Talker model with Instruct, Thinking and audio Captioner checkpoints, and Qwen2.5-Omni before it remain downloadable.

chunks.title: Qwen3-TTS
chunks.text: Qwen3-TTS (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Alibaba's Qwen3-TTS open text-to-speech models (1.7B and 0.6B) built on a 12 Hz speech tokenizer: three-second voice cloning, preset custom voices and voice design from a text description, in 10 languages.

chunks.title: Qwen-VL
chunks.text: Qwen-VL (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Qwen-VL is Alibaba's vision-language model line, from Qwen-VL and Qwen2-VL through Qwen2.5-VL to Qwen3-VL, released in dense and mixture-of-experts sizes with Instruct and Thinking editions.

chunks.title: Qwen-VL
chunks.text: Qwen-VL (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Multimodal models: Qwen3-VL reads images, documents in 32 OCR languages and hours-long video in a 256K context, grounds objects in 2D and 3D, and operates desktop and phone interfaces. Its successor is the natively multimodal Qwen3.5 family.

chunks.title: Qwen3-Embedding
chunks.text: Qwen3-Embedding (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Qwen3-Embedding is Alibaba's text embedding family built on the Qwen3 dense base models and shipped in 0.6B, 4B and 8B sizes. The models cover 100+ natural and programming languages at a 32k context, support Matryoshka output dimensions from 32 up to 4096, and take a task instruction on the query side.

chunks.title: Qwen3-Embedding
chunks.text: Qwen3-Embedding (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: They are released alongside a matching Qwen3-Reranker line, so a retrieval stack can use the same family for both the bi-encoder and the cross-encoder stage.

chunks.title: Qwen3 Reranker
chunks.text: Qwen3 Reranker (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Alibaba's Qwen3 reranking line, the cross-encoder half of the Qwen3 Embedding series. The text models (0.6B, 4B, 8B) score a query-document pair over 100-plus languages at 32K context and accept a task instruction.

chunks.title: Qwen3 Reranker
chunks.text: Qwen3 Reranker (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Qwen ships Qwen3-VL-Reranker models that extend the same interface to images and video, but this product is scoped to the text cross-encoders: the category treats a vision-language line as a separate product from the text line, for a vendor's reranker and its embedder alike.

chunks.title: Qwen3Guard
chunks.text: Qwen3Guard (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Qwen3Guard is Alibaba's family of safety moderation models built on Qwen3, in 0.6B, 4B and 8B sizes, that classify prompts and responses as safe, controversial or unsafe across 119 languages. A streaming variant classifies each token as it is generated, for real-time moderation. The models run on vLLM, SGLang and Hugging Face Transformers.

chunks.title: QwenPaw
chunks.text: QwenPaw (by AgentScope), catalog entry under UI & API: QwenPaw is a self-hosted personal assistant from the AgentScope team. It connects to multiple chat channels, supports MCP tools and plugins, keeps persistent memory across conversations, and offers a terminal UI alongside a desktop application.

chunks.title: QwenPaw
chunks.text: QwenPaw (by AgentScope), catalog entry under UI & API: It installs from PyPI, a shell script, Docker, or a hosted deployment on Alibaba Cloud, the AgentScope platform or ModelScope.

chunks.title: Radxa ROCK 5B
chunks.text: Radxa ROCK 5B (by Radxa), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Single-board computer built on the Rockchip RK3588, pairing a quad-core Cortex-A76 at up to 2.4 GHz with a quad-core Cortex-A55 and a built-in 6 TOPS NPU, in a 100 by 75 millimetre form factor. It is offered with 4GB to 16GB of LPDDR4X, and up to 32GB of LPDDR5 on the Plus variant.

chunks.title: RagaAI Catalyst
chunks.text: RagaAI Catalyst (by RagaAI), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Python client for RagaAI's hosted LLM observability and evaluation platform, providing project, dataset and prompt management, agentic trace recording, metric-based evaluation, synthetic data generation and guardrail management.

chunks.title: RagaAI Catalyst
chunks.text: RagaAI Catalyst (by RagaAI), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Every operation authenticates against the hosted catalyst.raga.ai service; the repository ships no server, dashboard or self-host path of its own.

chunks.title: Ragas
chunks.text: Ragas (by Exploding Gradients), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Evaluation framework for RAG and LLM applications, with about thirty metrics covering retrieval quality, generation faithfulness and answer relevance, plus automatic test-set generation. It integrates with LangChain.

chunks.title: RAGFlow
chunks.text: RAGFlow (by InfiniFlow), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: RAGFlow is a RAG engine built around deep document understanding, with template-based chunking and layout-aware parsing of complex PDFs, tables, figures and scans, producing answers with visible citations.

chunks.title: RAGFlow
chunks.text: RAGFlow (by InfiniFlow), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Unlike a general orchestration framework it is a batteries-included RAG server deployed with Docker Compose, and it includes agent workflows and MCP support.

chunks.title: Rasa
chunks.text: Rasa (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Rasa is an expressive text-to-speech corpus covering the 22 officially recognized languages of India, with a female and a male voice per language and about 1,145 hours in total. Its 48 kHz recordings mix neutral Wikipedia readings, speech in the six Ekman emotions, voice-assistant style commands, conversation, news reading and book narration.

chunks.title: Rasa
chunks.text: Rasa (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: AI4Bharat built it, and the method appeared at Interspeech 2024.

chunks.title: Raspberry Pi 5
chunks.text: Raspberry Pi 5 (by Raspberry Pi), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Credit-card-sized single-board computer built on the Broadcom BCM2712, with a 2.4 GHz quad-core Arm Cortex-A76 and a VideoCore VII GPU, offered with 1GB to 16GB of LPDDR4X. It carries no dedicated NPU, so on-device inference runs on the CPU and GPU or through an add-on accelerator such as the AI HAT+.

chunks.title: Raspberry Pi AI HAT+
chunks.text: Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ (by Raspberry Pi), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Accelerator add-on board for the Raspberry Pi 5 that integrates a Hailo neural-network accelerator, in a 13 TOPS Hailo-8L variant and a 26 TOPS Hailo-8 variant. It conforms to the Raspberry Pi HAT+ specification, connects over PCIe and integrates with the Pi camera stack for object detection and segmentation.

chunks.title: Raspberry Pi AI HAT+
chunks.text: Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ (by Raspberry Pi), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Raspberry Pi makes the board; Hailo supplies the silicon.

chunks.title: Ray
chunks.text: Ray (by Anyscale), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Framework for building and serving AI and ML applications across distributed compute, scheduling work over many machines and mixed CPU and GPU resources.

chunks.title: Ray
chunks.text: Ray (by Anyscale), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Ray Core provides task and actor primitives; the libraries above it - Data, Train, Tune, Serve and RLlib - cover batch inference, model serving, distributed training, hyperparameter tuning and feature engineering. Applications deploy as Ray clusters on virtual machines or Kubernetes, and the project is governed by the PyTorch Foundation.

chunks.title: RDT (Robotics Diffusion Transformer)
chunks.text: RDT (Robotics Diffusion Transformer) (by Tsinghua Machine Learning Group), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: RDT is Tsinghua University's line of bimanual robot foundation models.

chunks.title: RDT (Robotics Diffusion Transformer)
chunks.text: RDT (Robotics Diffusion Transformer) (by Tsinghua Machine Learning Group), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: RDT-1B is a one-billion-parameter diffusion transformer pretrained on more than a million multi-robot episodes; RDT2 adapts Qwen2.5-VL-7B into a vision-language-action model trained on over ten thousand hours of data from a handheld gripper

chunks.title: RDT (Robotics Diffusion Transformer)
chunks.text: RDT (Robotics Diffusion Transformer) (by Tsinghua Machine Learning Group), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: and deploys zero-shot on bimanual UR5e and Franka arms it was not trained on.

chunks.title: Reachy Mini
chunks.text: Reachy Mini (by Pollen Robotics), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Reachy Mini is an expressive desktop robot for building and testing AI apps. Its head rides on a six-degree-of-freedom Stewart platform above a rotating body, with two moving antennas, a wide-angle camera, a four-microphone array and a speaker, and it has no arm or gripper.

chunks.title: Reachy Mini
chunks.text: Reachy Mini (by Pollen Robotics), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Pollen Robotics sells it as a kit in a Wireless version with an onboard Raspberry Pi CM4 and a Lite version driven over USB from a computer, programmed through Python and JavaScript SDKs.

chunks.title: RediSearch
chunks.text: RediSearch (by Redis), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: RediSearch is Redis's own query and indexing module, adding secondary indexing, full-text search, vector similarity search and aggregations on top of Redis. It ships as a loadable Redis module built from this repository rather than a separate service, inheriting Redis's storage and clustering.

chunks.title: RedPajama-Data
chunks.text: RedPajama-Data (by Together AI), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: The RedPajama construction and quality-signal pipeline: quality classifiers, per-document quality/toxicity/importance annotations, and exact + fuzzy deduplication. Produced RedPajama-Data-v2 (30T tokens, 5 languages).

chunks.title: RedPajama-Data-v2
chunks.text: RedPajama-Data-v2 (by Together AI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Large open web dataset built from Common Crawl by Together Computer, holding more than 100 billion text documents, of which around 30 billion carry quality-signal annotations and about 20 billion are deduplicated. It is published raw and unfiltered so downstream users apply their own filtering.

chunks.title: Reducto Parse
chunks.text: Reducto Parse (by Reducto), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Document-ingestion API aimed at retrieval pipelines. It parses PDFs, images, spreadsheets and Office documents into layout-aware JSON and into chunks sized and bounded for embedding, so the output is shaped for a retrieval index rather than for a human reader.

chunks.title: RefinedWeb
chunks.text: RefinedWeb (by Technology Innovation Institute), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: English web dataset of roughly 968 million rows and about 2.8TB, built by the Technology Innovation Institute through stringent filtering and exact-plus-fuzzy deduplication of Common Crawl. The public release is an extract of the larger corpus used to train the Falcon 7B and 40B models.

chunks.title: Registry of Open Data on AWS
chunks.text: Registry of Open Data on AWS (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: The Registry of Open Data on AWS is a catalog of public datasets that government agencies, researchers and companies make available in AWS storage. Data providers propose entries as YAML files by pull request, and AWS's open data team decides what is listed.

chunks.title: Registry of Open Data on AWS
chunks.text: Registry of Open Data on AWS (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: Each entry names the S3 buckets or other resources that hold the data, which anyone can read without an AWS account, and the Open Data Sponsorship Program pays storage costs for sponsored datasets.

chunks.title: Reka Core
chunks.text: Reka Core (by Reka AI), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: Reka AI's multimodal foundation model, announced April 2024, natively processing text, images, video and audio with a 128K context and delivered through an API or on-premises and on-device deployment. Reka has since extended the stack with an open-weights Flash release and a multi-agent product, while Core itself remains the closed flagship.

chunks.title: Replit Agent
chunks.text: Replit Agent (by Replit), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Cloud development agent embedded in Replit's online IDE that builds applications from a natural-language description, scaffolding projects, installing packages, writing code, configuring databases and deploying to production. It runs entirely in the hosted environment, with plan mode, agent skills, a task board and end-to-end publishing.

chunks.title: Replit Agent / Code Execution API
chunks.text: Replit Agent / Code Execution API (by Replit), catalog entry under Deployment: Runs untrusted and model-generated code, primarily Python, through a stateless API on Replit's cloud development platform. Each call executes inside an ephemeral unprivileged container created on Replit Autoscale Deployments and sandboxed by omegajail, returning whatever the code prints.

chunks.title: RewardBench
chunks.text: RewardBench (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Benchmark for evaluating reward models, pairing prompts with chosen and rejected responses across chat, reasoning and safety subsets. RewardBench 2 extends it with harder, unseen human prompts, and both versions publish their datasets, results and a public leaderboard.

chunks.title: RewardBench
chunks.text: RewardBench (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: The repository provides a common inference format for scoring most open reward models.

chunks.title: RF-DETR
chunks.text: RF-DETR (by Roboflow), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Real-time transformer object detector from Roboflow, released in sizes from Nano to 2XL with instance-segmentation and keypoint variants. The published sizes were found by neural architecture search, and the detection and segmentation heads were pretrained on Objects365 pseudo-labeled with SAM2.

chunks.title: RF-DETR
chunks.text: RF-DETR (by Roboflow), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: The rfdetr package fine-tunes and runs the checkpoints, and the two largest detection sizes ship separately under Roboflow's platform license.

chunks.title: RFdiffusion
chunks.text: RFdiffusion (by Rosetta Commons), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: RFdiffusion is a diffusion model for de novo protein design from the Institute for Protein Design, built on RoseTTAFold's architecture and trained parameters.

chunks.title: RFdiffusion
chunks.text: RFdiffusion (by Rosetta Commons), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: It generates unconditional monomers, scaffolds functional motifs, designs binders against a target with specified hotspot residues, builds symmetric oligomers, and partially rediffuses an existing backbone to diversify it.

chunks.title: Rhino Federated Computing Platform
chunks.text: Rhino Federated Computing Platform (by Rhino Federated Computing), catalog entry under Federated learning: Rhino Federated Computing's platform for federated statistics, federated learning and federated inference on data that stays behind each custodian's firewall.

chunks.title: Rhino Federated Computing Platform
chunks.text: Rhino Federated Computing Platform (by Rhino Federated Computing), catalog entry under Federated learning: Custodians connect data across clouds and on-premises sites; custom code runs next to the data in secure containers under role-based access control, with differential privacy, k-anonymization, homomorphic encryption, customer-managed keys and audit logs.

chunks.title: RisuAI
chunks.text: RisuAI (by Kwaroran), catalog entry under UI & API: RisuAI is cross-platform software for character-based chat and LLM roleplay. It supports character cards, persistent memory, plugins, speech synthesis and image generation, and runs in a browser, as a desktop build or through Docker.

chunks.title: River
chunks.text: River (by online-ml), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Python library for online machine learning, where models learn from one observation at a time on streaming data instead of from a fixed dataset.

chunks.title: River
chunks.text: River (by online-ml), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: It covers linear models, trees and forests, naive Bayes, nearest neighbors, clustering, anomaly and drift detection, recommendation, time-series forecasting, bandits and ensembles, with streaming metrics and preprocessing. It came from the merger of creme and scikit-multiflow.

chunks.title: BRIA RMBG
chunks.text: BRIA RMBG (by BRIA AI), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Background-removal model line from BRIA AI. RMBG-2.0, the current still-image model, is built on the BiRefNet architecture and trained on images BRIA licensed, a dataset it presents as safe for commercial deployment.

chunks.title: BRIA RMBG
chunks.text: BRIA RMBG (by BRIA AI), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: The weights are published for non-commercial use, and commercial use goes through a BRIA agreement or its paid background-removal API.

chunks.title: Roblox PII Classifier
chunks.text: Roblox PII Classifier (by Roblox), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Roblox PII Classifier flags chat messages that ask for or share personal information, such as phone numbers, social media handles and credentials, and messages that try to move a user to another platform.

chunks.title: Roblox PII Classifier
chunks.text: Roblox PII Classifier (by Roblox), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Version 2 reads each message together with the surrounding multi-user conversation, which helps it catch bypass attempts like phonetic spelling and implicit references. Roblox built it by fine-tuning the 560M-parameter XLM-RoBERTa-Large encoder for its own chat moderation.

chunks.title: Roblox Sentinel
chunks.text: Roblox Sentinel (by Roblox), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Roblox Sentinel is a Python library for detecting very rare kinds of harmful text, such as grooming, across a run of messages from one source rather than one message at a time.

chunks.title: Roblox Sentinel
chunks.text: Roblox Sentinel (by Roblox), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: It compares each message with small sets of harmful and ordinary examples by embedding similarity, then combines the results for that source, by default with skewness, to surface candidates for human review. Roblox built it for its own chat moderation.

chunks.title: Roblox Voice Safety Classifier
chunks.text: Roblox Voice Safety Classifier (by Roblox), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Roblox Voice Safety Classifier scores short voice-chat clips for policy violations, working on the audio itself rather than a transcript.

chunks.title: Roblox Voice Safety Classifier
chunks.text: Roblox Voice Safety Classifier (by Roblox), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Version 3 takes 16 kHz clips of up to 30 seconds and scores eight categories, including harassment, discrimination, sexual content, profanity, requests for personal information and disruptive audio, in 30 languages. It is a 320M-parameter transformer distilled from a larger model Roblox trained on its own voice chat.

chunks.title: RoboMIND
chunks.text: RoboMIND (by X-Humanoid), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: RoboMIND is a real-world robot manipulation dataset from the Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics (X-Humanoid), recorded by teleoperation on several robot bodies.

chunks.title: RoboMIND
chunks.text: RoboMIND (by X-Humanoid), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: Version 1 has about 107k trajectories on a Franka arm, a UR5e arm, an AgileX dual-arm robot and the Tien Kung humanoid; RoboMIND 2.0 scales to 310k trajectories and over 1,000 hours on six embodiments, with tactile and mobile-manipulation data.

chunks.title: robosuite
chunks.text: robosuite (by ARISE Initiative), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: robosuite is a modular simulation framework and benchmark for robot learning built on the MuJoCo physics engine. It provides manipulation tasks, a range of robot embodiments including humanoids, composite and whole-body controllers, and teleoperation devices for collecting demonstrations.

chunks.title: robosuite
chunks.text: robosuite (by ARISE Initiative), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: It comes from Stanford's SVL and is maintained with UT Austin and NVIDIA under the ARISE Initiative.

chunks.title: Rockchip RK3588
chunks.text: Rockchip RK3588 (by Rockchip), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Application-processor SoC from Fuzhou Rockchip rather than a board. It is an octa-core Arm design pairing four Cortex-A76 with four Cortex-A55, a Mali-G610 MC4 GPU and a 6 TOPS triple-core NPU supporting INT4, INT8, INT16, FP16, BF16 and TF32, with up to 32GB of LPDDR4X or LPDDR5 and PCIe 3.0.

chunks.title: Rockchip RK3588
chunks.text: Rockchip RK3588 (by Rockchip), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: It is the silicon behind boards including Orange Pi 5, Radxa Rock 5B and Khadas Edge2.

chunks.title: RT-DETR
chunks.text: RT-DETR (by lyuwenyu), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Real-time end-to-end object detector family built on the DETR transformer design, which removes the non-maximum-suppression step that YOLO-style detectors need.

chunks.title: RT-DETR
chunks.text: RT-DETR (by lyuwenyu), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: The line began with RT-DETR and RT-DETRv2, published from the lyuwenyu repository; RT-DETRv4, the newest member, distills features from a DINOv3 vision foundation model into small detectors. Checkpoints are trained on COCO, some pretrained on Objects365, and full training code ships for each version.

chunks.title: RTP-LLM
chunks.text: RTP-LLM (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Inference code: RTP-LLM is an LLM inference acceleration engine developed by Alibaba's Foundation Model Inference Team, built on work from the FasterTransformer project.

chunks.title: RWKV
chunks.text: RWKV (by RWKV Project), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: RWKV is an open-weights model family whose architecture runs as a recurrent network at inference yet trains in parallel like a transformer, giving linear-time inference, constant memory with no KV cache and effectively unbounded context.

chunks.title: RWKV
chunks.text: RWKV (by RWKV Project), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: The RWKV-7 Goose generation, which includes the G1 models, adds dynamic state evolution that its paper argues gives it more expressive power than standard attention.

chunks.title: Northern Sámi web corpus
chunks.text: Northern Sámi web corpus (by Language Technology Group, University of Oslo), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Northern Sámi web corpus is a crawl of about 33,000 web documents in Northern Sámi, seeded from the external links of the Sámi Wikipedia and continued breadth-first through pages that GlotLID identified as Northern Sámi and whose robots.txt allowed crawling.

chunks.title: Northern Sámi web corpus
chunks.text: Northern Sámi web corpus (by Language Technology Group, University of Oslo), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Text was extracted with Trafilatura and fuzzy-deduplicated document by document. The Language Technology Group at the University of Oslo publishes it.

chunks.title: Safetensors
chunks.text: Safetensors (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Safetensors is a file format and library for storing and loading tensors safely, designed as an alternative to Python pickle that avoids arbitrary code execution and supports fast zero-copy loading. It is implemented in Rust with Python bindings and provides loaders for PyTorch, TensorFlow, Flax, NumPy and PaddlePaddle.

chunks.title: Safetensors
chunks.text: Safetensors (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Hugging Face maintains it.

chunks.title: SageAttention
chunks.text: SageAttention (by Tsinghua Machine Learning Group), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: SageAttention is a quantized attention implementation that replaces the attention operator with 8-bit and INT4 arithmetic, using outlier smoothing and per-thread quantization to hold accuracy.

chunks.title: SageAttention
chunks.text: SageAttention (by Tsinghua Machine Learning Group), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: It is applied as a drop-in substitution in language, image and video models, and the repository carries the SageAttention, SageAttention2 and SageAttention2++ implementations described in the papers.

chunks.title: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
chunks.text: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Model catalog in Amazon SageMaker AI that onboards publicly available and proprietary foundation models from third-party providers and partners, alongside built-in algorithms. Models can be fine-tuned, evaluated and deployed to SageMaker endpoints from Studio or the Python SDK.

chunks.title: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
chunks.text: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Administrators create private hubs that curate a subset of the public catalog and add their own versioned models, notebooks and datasets.

chunks.title: Amazon SageMaker AI Pipelines
chunks.text: Amazon SageMaker AI Pipelines (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Managed workflow orchestration service for machine learning on AWS. A pipeline is built from typed steps - training, processing, tuning, model registration - authored in the SageMaker Python SDK or a visual editor, and each step names the instance type it runs on.

chunks.title: Amazon SageMaker AI Pipelines
chunks.text: Amazon SageMaker AI Pipelines (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under ML orchestration: SageMaker provisions, scales and shuts down the compute for the pipeline and for the jobs it orchestrates.

chunks.title: SambaNova Cloud
chunks.text: SambaNova Cloud (by SambaNova Systems), catalog entry under Inference code: SambaNova Cloud is an inference service running on SambaNova's custom Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit (RDU) chips, the SN40L. Its three-tier memory system pairs on-chip SRAM for hot local work with HBM to stream model weights and DDR DRAM for prompt caching and multi-model workloads.

chunks.title: SambaNova Cloud
chunks.text: SambaNova Cloud (by SambaNova Systems), catalog entry under Inference code: It serves open-weight models through OpenAI-compatible endpoints as SambaCloud, with SambaStack offered for on-premise deployment.

chunks.title: Samvaad-Hi
chunks.text: Samvaad-Hi (by Sarvam AI), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Samvaad-Hi is an instruction-tuning dataset of about 100,000 multi-turn conversations in English, Hindi and Hinglish written with an Indian context. Each record is a list of user and assistant messages in chat format. Sarvam AI publishes it, and its one-line card does not say how the conversations were produced.

chunks.title: sandbox-runtime
chunks.text: sandbox-runtime (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Deployment: The Anthropic Sandbox Runtime enforces filesystem, network and unix-socket restrictions on arbitrary local processes without a container. It uses bubblewrap on Linux and sandbox-exec on macOS, with an alpha Windows backend that runs processes under a dedicated restricted account, and routes network traffic through a filtering proxy.

chunks.title: sandbox-runtime
chunks.text: sandbox-runtime (by Anthropic), catalog entry under Deployment: A CLI named srt and a matching library apply it to agents, local MCP servers and shell commands. Anthropic develops it for Claude Code and ships it as a research preview.

chunks.title: Sangraha
chunks.text: Sangraha (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Sangraha is a pretraining text corpus of about 251 billion tokens across 22 Indic languages and English.

chunks.title: Sangraha
chunks.text: Sangraha (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It joins three parts: text from human-verified websites, OCR of Indic PDFs and transcribed videos and podcasts; perplexity-filtered text from existing multilingual corpora; and English Wikimedia machine-translated into 14 languages and romanized. AI4Bharat built it with Setu, its open cleaning and deduplication pipeline.

chunks.title: Sarvam-2T
chunks.text: Sarvam-2T (by Sarvam AI), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Sarvam-2T is Sarvam AI's Indic pretraining corpus of about 2 trillion tokens across ten Indian languages: Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Oriya, Punjabi, Tamil and Telugu. Most of it was produced with synthetic data generation rather than web crawling, and the languages are split almost evenly except for Hindi.

chunks.title: Sarvam-2T
chunks.text: Sarvam-2T (by Sarvam AI), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Sarvam used it to train its Sarvam-1 model.

chunks.title: Scale Evaluation
chunks.text: Scale Evaluation (by Scale AI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Enterprise evaluation and red-teaming service combining automated scoring, expert human raters and private benchmark suites, deployable into a customer's own cloud. Scale runs the SEAL leaderboards on proprietary datasets that stay private and unpublished, launching with coding, instruction following, math and multilinguality.

chunks.title: Scale SEAL Leaderboard
chunks.text: Scale SEAL Leaderboard (by Scale AI), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Scale AI's private evaluation sets behind its SEAL leaderboards, covering domains including instruction-following, math, coding and multilinguality. Problems are held private to prevent contamination and are scored by expert annotators, and the leaderboards rank frontier models rather than publishing the prompts.

chunks.title: scGPT
chunks.text: scGPT (by Wang Lab), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: scGPT is the Wang lab's generative transformer pretrained on 33 million human cells for single-cell multi-omic analysis.

chunks.title: scGPT
chunks.text: scGPT (by Wang Lab), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: It publishes a whole-human checkpoint alongside brain, blood, heart, lung, kidney, and pan-cancer checkpoints, with fine-tuning examples and tutorials for batch integration, cell-type annotation, genetic perturbation prediction, and gene regulatory network inference.

chunks.title: scikit-image
chunks.text: scikit-image (by scikit-image), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Image-processing library for Python built on NumPy and SciPy, covering color conversion, exposure, filtering, morphology, feature detection, segmentation, geometric transforms, registration, restoration and measurement. It is a consensus-based community project governed by a steering council, widely used in scientific imaging.

chunks.title: scikit-learn
chunks.text: scikit-learn (by scikit-learn), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Python library of classical machine-learning estimators - linear and kernel models, support vector machines, trees and ensembles including gradient boosting, nearest neighbors, clustering, decomposition and outlier detection - under one fit and predict interface, with pipelines, model selection, metrics and preprocessing around them.

chunks.title: scikit-learn
chunks.text: scikit-learn (by scikit-learn), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: A consensus-governed community project, first released by INRIA researchers in 2010.

chunks.title: SEA-HELM
chunks.text: SEA-HELM (by AI Singapore), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: SEA-HELM (Southeast Asian Holistic Evaluation of Language Models) is AI Singapore's evaluation suite for large language models in Southeast Asian languages. It groups tasks under five pillars: classic NLP tasks, LLM-specific tasks such as instruction following and multi-turn chat, linguistic diagnostics, culture, and safety.

chunks.title: SEA-HELM
chunks.text: SEA-HELM (by AI Singapore), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Test sets combine native datasets, human translations and new handcrafted sets such as Kalahi. The suite absorbed the earlier BHASA benchmark and feeds the SEA-HELM leaderboard.

chunks.title: SEA-Instruct
chunks.text: SEA-Instruct (by AI Singapore), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: SEA-Instruct is an instruction-tuning dataset from AI Singapore for Southeast Asian languages and contexts, pairing prompts filtered from open data and AI Singapore's own synthetic prompts with model-generated responses.

chunks.title: SEA-Instruct
chunks.text: SEA-Instruct (by AI Singapore), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Qwen3 models tagged prompts and drafted answers and DeepSeek-V3.1 revised them, and the release keeps only prompts rated excellent, coherent and natural. It spans English, Chinese and ten regional languages, each row tagged for domain, task, complexity and cultural knowledge.

chunks.title: SEA-LION
chunks.text: SEA-LION (by AI Singapore), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: SEA-LION (Southeast Asian Languages In One Network) is AI Singapore's family of language models for Southeast Asia, funded by the National Research Foundation Singapore.

chunks.title: SEA-LION
chunks.text: SEA-LION (by AI Singapore), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: The current release, SEA-LION v4.8, adapts NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 models to English and seven regional languages, from Burmese and Tamil to Thai and Vietnamese, through continued pretraining and post-training, in 30B and 120B mixture-of-experts sizes. Earlier v4 releases were built on Qwen3 32B and Gemma 3 27B.

chunks.title: SEA-PILE
chunks.text: SEA-PILE (by AI Singapore), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: SEA-PILE is AI Singapore's pretraining corpus for Southeast Asian languages.

chunks.title: SEA-PILE
chunks.text: SEA-PILE (by AI Singapore), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Its v2 release holds about 120 billion tokens of web text in Vietnamese, Indonesian, Tamil, Malay, Thai, Tagalog, Khmer, Lao and Burmese, extracted from 24 CommonCrawl snapshots, deduplicated per snapshot and filtered with heuristics and perplexity scoring developed with native speakers.

chunks.title: SEA-PILE
chunks.text: SEA-PILE (by AI Singapore), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The earlier v1 release is the cleaned mC4 portion of the data behind the first SEA-LION models.

chunks.title: SEACrowd
chunks.text: SEACrowd (by SEACrowd), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: SEACrowd collects and standardizes datasets for Southeast Asian languages behind one Python library, `seacrowd`, whose dataloaders return text, speech and vision-language corpora in shared schemas with license and citation metadata attached.

chunks.title: SEACrowd
chunks.text: SEACrowd (by SEACrowd), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The hub covers nearly 1,000 languages of the region across three modalities and ships benchmark bundles such as SEACrowd-VL. It is a grassroots research community effort modeled on NusaCrowd.

chunks.title: SeaExam
chunks.text: SeaExam (by Alibaba DAMO Academy), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: SeaExam is a multiple-choice benchmark from DAMO-NLP-SG, the group behind SeaLLMs, for testing language models in Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese, Chinese and English. It combines real human exam questions adapted from M3Exam, standardized to four shuffled options, with 2,850 MMLU questions machine-translated using Google Translate.

chunks.title: SeaExam
chunks.text: SeaExam (by Alibaba DAMO Academy), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Its companion SeaBench adds open-ended multi-turn and instruction-following questions in Indonesian, Thai and Vietnamese, and both feed the SeaExam leaderboard.

chunks.title: SeamlessM4T
chunks.text: SeamlessM4T (by Meta), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Meta's multilingual speech translation model: one model translates speech to speech, speech to text and text to speech, and transcribes, with speech input in about 100 languages and speech output in 35. The v2 release adds a streaming variant for simultaneous translation.

chunks.title: SearXNG
chunks.text: SearXNG (by SearXNG), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: SearXNG is a privacy-respecting metasearch engine that aggregates results from many search services without tracking or profiling users, and a community-run successor to the older searx project. It predates the LLM era and does no inference itself, but exposes a JSON API and runs on self-hosted infrastructure.

chunks.title: SearXNG
chunks.text: SearXNG (by SearXNG), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Answer engines and RAG stacks such as Open WebUI, Perplexica, Morphic and LibreChat integrate it as a web-search provider.

chunks.title: Seed-OSS
chunks.text: Seed-OSS (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: ByteDance Seed's open-weight model line, released August 2025 as 36B base and instruct checkpoints trained on 12T tokens. The instruct model targets long-context, reasoning and agentic use with a controllable thinking budget, and the base ships in with- and without-synthetic-data variants aimed at fine-tuning research.

chunks.title: Seedance
chunks.text: Seedance (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Seedance is ByteDance Seed's video generation model line, which generates video and synchronized audio in one pass from text, image, audio and video references. It is served in ByteDance's Jimeng and Doubao apps and through the BytePlus ModelArk API, with multi-shot storytelling and editing of existing clips.

chunks.title: Segment Anything (SAM)
chunks.text: Segment Anything (SAM) (by Meta), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Meta's promptable segmentation model line for images and video. SAM 3, the current generation, detects, segments and tracks every instance of a concept named by a short text phrase or shown by an example, as well as objects picked with points, boxes and masks; SAM 3.1 adds faster multi-object tracking.

chunks.title: Segment Anything (SAM)
chunks.text: Segment Anything (SAM) (by Meta), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: The earlier SAM and SAM 2 releases, Apache-licensed, segment from visual prompts only.

chunks.title: Selenium
chunks.text: Selenium (by Selenium), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Browser automation framework built around the W3C WebDriver specification, with language bindings for Python, Java, Ruby, Rust and .NET driving every major browser.

chunks.title: Semantic Kernel
chunks.text: Semantic Kernel (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Microsoft's SDK for building AI agents and integrating models into C#, Python or Java code. It exposes application code as model-callable plugins, often through OpenAPI, with connectors to AI services and vector stores, telemetry and responsible-AI hooks.

chunks.title: Semantic Kernel
chunks.text: Semantic Kernel (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Its first-class multi-language support distinguishes it from the Python-first frameworks.

chunks.title: SentencePiece
chunks.text: SentencePiece (by Google), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: SentencePiece is an unsupervised text tokenizer and detokenizer that implements subword units (Byte-Pair Encoding and unigram language model) directly from raw text, without language-specific pre-tokenization.

chunks.title: SentencePiece
chunks.text: SentencePiece (by Google), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It treats input as a stream of Unicode characters, enabling a language-independent, end-to-end pipeline useful for languages without clear word boundaries. The project is hosted under Google's GitHub organization and describes itself as not an official Google product.

chunks.title: SerpApi
chunks.text: SerpApi (by SerpApi), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Scrapes search engine results pages and returns them as structured JSON. One metered product covers roughly 130 engines - Google, Bing, Baidu, DuckDuckGo, Amazon, Walmart, Yandex, YouTube and the rest - with organic results, answer boxes, knowledge graph, local packs and ads parsed into fields.

chunks.title: Serper
chunks.text: Serper (by Serper), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Serper is a Google Search API for developers that returns structured search-results-page data, including organic results, the knowledge graph and related searches. Besides web search it covers images, news, maps, places, videos, shopping, scholar, patents and autocomplete, and it is sold on per-query pricing and response speed.

chunks.title: CSM (Conversational Speech Model)
chunks.text: CSM (Conversational Speech Model) (by Sesame), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Sesame's Conversational Speech Model: a speech generator with a Llama backbone and a small audio decoder producing Mimi codes, which conditions on the preceding conversation, text and audio, to speak with context-appropriate prosody. The released CSM-1B is a base model without a fixed voice.

chunks.title: SGLang
chunks.text: SGLang (by SGLang (LMSYS / UC Berkeley)), catalog entry under Inference code: SGLang is a serving engine for large language and multimodal models, built around RadixAttention for automatic prefix-KV cache reuse.

chunks.title: SGLang
chunks.text: SGLang (by SGLang (LMSYS / UC Berkeley)), catalog entry under Inference code: It adds zero-overhead scheduling, speculative decoding, structured-output generation, disaggregated prefill, and quantization, and runs across NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and TPU hardware from a single GPU to distributed clusters. The LMSYS non-profit hosts it, and it sits in the PyTorch ecosystem.

chunks.title: sherpa-onnx
chunks.text: sherpa-onnx (by k2-fsa (Next-gen Kaldi)), catalog entry under Speech & audio: The Next-gen Kaldi project's ONNX Runtime engine for offline speech: streaming and non-streaming recognition, synthesis, speaker diarization and identification, voice activity detection and more, on Linux, Windows, macOS, Android, iOS, HarmonyOS, embedded boards and WebAssembly, with bindings for a dozen programming languages.

chunks.title: ShieldGemma
chunks.text: ShieldGemma (by Google), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Google DeepMind's content-safety classifier built on Gemma 2, shipped in 2B, 9B and 27B sizes. It predicts policy violations in English across four harm categories (sexually explicit, dangerous content, hate, harassment) for both prompts and responses, answering yes or no.

chunks.title: Shieldstral
chunks.text: Shieldstral (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Mistral AI's 3B-parameter multimodal safety classifier, built on Ministral 3 3B with a Pixtral vision encoder.

chunks.title: Shieldstral
chunks.text: Shieldstral (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Rather than predicting a fixed set of moderation categories, it answers one yes-or-no question written in natural language about a prompt, a response, a prompt-response pair or an image, and returns a continuous safety score from a single forward pass. It covers twelve languages and fits on a single 16GB GPU.

chunks.title: Shrutilipi
chunks.text: Shrutilipi (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Shrutilipi is a labeled speech recognition corpus of more than 6,400 hours in 12 Indian languages, from Bengali and Hindi to Sanskrit and Urdu. Its audio and sentence transcripts were mined from All India Radio news bulletins by aligning broadcast audio with the published bulletin text.

chunks.title: Shrutilipi
chunks.text: Shrutilipi (by AI4Bharat), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: AI4Bharat built it, and the paper reports 4.95 million sentences.

chunks.title: SIB-200
chunks.text: SIB-200 (by David Adelani), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: SIB-200 is a topic classification benchmark in 205 languages and dialects, built by labeling the English FLORES-200 sentences with seven topics such as science, travel and politics and carrying the labels across to every aligned translation. Train, validation and test splits exist for every language.

chunks.title: SIB-200
chunks.text: SIB-200 (by David Adelani), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It was created by David Adelani and colleagues, with annotators recruited through Masakhane.

chunks.title: SigLIP
chunks.text: SigLIP (by Google), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: SigLIP replaces CLIP's softmax contrastive loss with a pairwise sigmoid loss, which needs no global view of the batch and so trains well at both very large and quite small batch sizes.

chunks.title: SigLIP
chunks.text: SigLIP (by Google), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: SigLIP 2 folds captioning pretraining, self-distillation, masked prediction and online data curation into the same recipe and adds multilingual coverage and native-aspect-ratio variants. The checkpoints serve two audiences at once: image-text retrieval in their own right, and the default frozen vision tower for a large share of current open VLMs.

chunks.title: Silero VAD
chunks.text: Silero VAD (by Silero), catalog entry under Speech & audio: A small pretrained voice activity detector that processes a 30 ms audio chunk in under a millisecond on one CPU thread. It ships as PyTorch and ONNX models with a Python package and runs wherever ONNX Runtime does, including the browser.

chunks.title: SillyTavern
chunks.text: SillyTavern (by SillyTavern), catalog entry under UI & API: Self-hosted chat front end for character and roleplay use, forked from TavernAI in 2023. It runs on Node.js and connects to many backends including KoboldAI, OpenAI, Claude and Mistral, with deep prompt engineering, lorebooks, group chats, image generation, text-to-speech, extensions and a visual-novel mode.

chunks.title: simple-evals
chunks.text: simple-evals (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: OpenAI's lightweight reference library for evaluating language models, open sourced for transparency about the accuracy numbers it publishes alongside new models.

chunks.title: simple-evals
chunks.text: simple-evals (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: It bundles implementations of MMLU, MATH, GPQA, DROP, MGSM, HumanEval, SimpleQA, BrowseComp and HealthBench, emphasizing the zero-shot, chain-of-thought setting, each with its upstream license listed. The library is deprecated and will no longer be updated for new models or benchmark results.

chunks.title: SimpleAudit
chunks.text: SimpleAudit (by Simula Research Laboratory), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Local-first framework for multilingual auditing and red-teaming of AI systems through adversarial probing, developed by Simula and SimulaMet in Norway with the Norwegian Directorate of Health.

chunks.title: SimpleAudit
chunks.text: SimpleAudit (by Simula Research Laboratory), catalog entry under Evaluation code: It runs open models locally so prompts, transcripts and policies stay inside the deployment environment, and ships scenario packs for safety, RAG, healthcare and broken-premise testing. It is a verified Digital Public Good.

chunks.title: Sipeed MaixCAM
chunks.text: Sipeed MaixCAM (by Sipeed), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Compact AI vision and audio development board built around the SOPHGO SG2002, pairing a 1 GHz RISC-V C906 core with a 700 MHz companion core and a 1 TOPS INT8 NPU that also runs BF16 models. It carries 256MB of DDR3, a 2.3-inch IPS touchscreen and dual MIPI-CSI camera inputs, and is programmed through the MaixPy and MaixCDK SDKs.

chunks.title: sktime
chunks.text: sktime (by sktime), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Python library with one scikit-learn-style interface across time-series learning tasks - forecasting, classification, regression, clustering, anomaly and changepoint detection - and tools for pipelining, ensembling, tuning and reduction between them. It interfaces statsmodels, Prophet, PyOD and other libraries alongside its own estimators.

chunks.title: sktime
chunks.text: sktime (by sktime), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: A consensus-governed community project, with support services sold by a separate company.

chunks.title: SkyPilot
chunks.text: SkyPilot (by SkyPilot), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Framework for running AI workloads on whatever compute is available - Kubernetes, Slurm, more than twenty clouds, or on-premise machines - behind one interface.

chunks.title: SkyPilot
chunks.text: SkyPilot (by SkyPilot), catalog entry under ML orchestration: A task declares its accelerators and how many nodes it needs; SkyPilot finds capacity that satisfies it, provisions the cluster, reserves the nodes for the job and exposes their ranks and addresses to the running code.

chunks.title: SkyRL
chunks.text: SkyRL (by NovaSky), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: SkyRL is a modular reinforcement-learning library for post-training language models and agents. Its unified skyrl package runs PPO, GRPO and related algorithms over FSDP or Megatron training with vLLM or SGLang rollout, and implements the Tinker API so Tinker training scripts run on local GPUs.

chunks.title: SkyRL
chunks.text: SkyRL (by NovaSky), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Alongside it ship skyrl-gym, a set of tool-use environments, and skyrl-agent for long-horizon agents. NovaSky at the Berkeley Sky Computing Lab builds it with Anyscale.

chunks.title: Slack MCP Server
chunks.text: Slack MCP Server (by Dmitry Korotovsky), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Actively maintained community Slack MCP server (Go) connecting AI agents to Slack workspaces over stdio/SSE/HTTP, with a 'stealth mode' needing no bot install or workspace permissions plus an OAuth mode. Exposes 18 tools (history, search, posting, reactions, channel/user management).

chunks.title: Slurm
chunks.text: Slurm (by SchedMD), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Workload manager for Linux clusters, and a long-standing scheduler for HPC and GPU training. Jobs request generic resources with --gres or --gpus, and Slurm's controller allocates whole nodes or specific GPUs to a job, enforces the allocation, and runs the job's steps inside it.

chunks.title: Slurm
chunks.text: Slurm (by SchedMD), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Multi-node allocations are granted together, which is what all-or-nothing training jobs need.

chunks.title: smallpond
chunks.text: smallpond (by DeepSeek), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Lightweight distributed data-processing framework built on DuckDB and DeepSeek's 3FS, aimed at PB-scale preprocessing.

chunks.title: SMOL
chunks.text: SMOL (by Google), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: SMOL is a Google suite of professionally translated training data for machine translation into more than 200 low-resource languages. It combines SmolSent, sentences picked for broad vocabulary coverage; SmolDoc, whole documents chosen for topic coverage, with factuality ratings; and the GATITOS word and phrase lexicon.

chunks.title: SMOL
chunks.text: SMOL (by Google), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Volunteers have added translations for further languages since the first release.

chunks.title: smolagents
chunks.text: smolagents (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Minimal code-first agent framework from Hugging Face, whose CodeAgent writes actions as executable Python rather than JSON tool calls. The core is about a thousand lines. It runs actions in a sandbox, is model-agnostic across hosted and local providers, and imports tools over MCP and from LangChain.

chunks.title: SmolLM3
chunks.text: SmolLM3 (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: SmolLM3 is Hugging Face's fully open 3B small language model, released in base and instruct form in July 2025. Trained on about 11 trillion tokens, it supports a 128K context window, six languages and dual-mode reasoning.

chunks.title: SmolLM3
chunks.text: SmolLM3 (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: The full engineering blueprint, covering architecture, data mixtures and the training and post-training recipe, is published, and the line supersedes SmolLM2.

chunks.title: SmolTalk
chunks.text: SmolTalk (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Hugging Face's supervised fine-tuning mixture behind the SmolLM instruct models, combining new synthetic sets such as Smol-Magpie-Ultra with established public datasets. Marin 8B Instruct also trains on it. The record covers both SmolTalk and its successor SmolTalk2.

chunks.title: SmolVLA
chunks.text: SmolVLA (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: SmolVLA is Hugging Face's compact vision-language-action model, about 450 million parameters, trained on community-collected datasets from affordable robot arms.

chunks.title: SmolVLA
chunks.text: SmolVLA (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: It takes multi-view images, robot state and an optional instruction and outputs continuous action chunks by flow matching, trains on a single GPU, and runs on consumer GPUs or CPUs through the LeRobot library.

chunks.title: SmolVLM
chunks.text: SmolVLM (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Multimodal models: SmolVLM is Hugging Face's family of small vision-language models, from 256M to 2.2B parameters, built on the Idefics3 architecture for on-device use. The models caption, answer questions about and transcribe text from interleaved images, and SmolVLM2 adds video. Hugging Face publishes the training code in its smollm repository.

chunks.title: SMUGRI data
chunks.text: SMUGRI data (by TartuNLP, University of Tartu), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: SMUGRI data is a news-based monolingual text collection for seven low-resource Finno-Ugric languages: Komi, Udmurt, Moksha, Erzya, Mansi, Khanty and Livvi Karelian, about 130,000 rows in all.

chunks.title: SMUGRI data
chunks.text: SMUGRI data (by TartuNLP, University of Tartu), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It accompanies a paper on machine translation for these languages presented at the 24th Nordic Conference on Computational Linguistics. TartuNLP at the University of Tartu publishes it.

chunks.title: Snorkel AI Data Development Platform
chunks.text: Snorkel AI Data Development Platform (by Snorkel AI), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Snorkel AI's commercial data-development platform: programmatic labeling and weak supervision through heuristic and model-generated labeling functions, plus curation, slicing, filtering and fine-tuning and evaluation data workflows.

chunks.title: Snorkel AI Data Development Platform
chunks.text: Snorkel AI Data Development Platform (by Snorkel AI), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: The customer deploys it rather than consuming it as a service, and the documentation carries an administrator guide covering installation, users, roles and permissions.

chunks.title: Snowflake Cortex Fine-Tuning
chunks.text: Snowflake Cortex Fine-Tuning (by Snowflake), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Snowflake Cortex Fine-Tuning is a fully managed function inside Snowflake Cortex AI that applies parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) to a short, fixed list of supported base models, such as Llama 3.1 8B.

chunks.title: Snowflake Cortex Fine-Tuning
chunks.text: Snowflake Cortex Fine-Tuning (by Snowflake), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Training data comes from tables in the customer's account, and both training and inference run on Snowflake compute rather than a third-party platform, billed per token in credits.

chunks.title: SO-101 arm
chunks.text: SO-101 arm (by The Robot Studio), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: SO-101 is a low-cost, 3D-printable six-degree-of-freedom robot arm designed by The Robot Studio with Hugging Face, sold as a leader and follower pair for teleoperated data collection with the LeRobot library.

chunks.title: SO-101 arm
chunks.text: SO-101 arm (by The Robot Studio), catalog entry under Robotics & embodied AI: The repository publishes STEP and STL files for every part, and a two-arm kit costs about $230 in parts or ships ready-made from several vendors.

chunks.title: SOLD (Sinhala Offensive Language Dataset)
chunks.text: SOLD (Sinhala Offensive Language Dataset) (by Sinhala NLP), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: SOLD is a Sinhala offensive language dataset of 10,000 Twitter posts labeled by hand as offensive or not, with rationales marking the words behind each offensive label. Its companion SemiSOLD adds more than 145,000 Sinhala tweets scored by classifiers trained on SOLD.

chunks.title: SOLD (Sinhala Offensive Language Dataset)
chunks.text: SOLD (Sinhala Offensive Language Dataset) (by Sinhala NLP), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Sinhala-NLP group released both with an experiment codebase.

chunks.title: Sonar
chunks.text: Sonar (by Dphn AI), catalog entry under Inference code: Sonar is an inference engine for Hugging Face-compatible language and multimodal models, providing continuous batching, paged KV-cache management, optimized kernels, quantization, speculative decoding and distributed serving. It is based on vLLM.

chunks.title: Spaces
chunks.text: Spaces (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Deployment: Spaces hosts interactive machine-learning apps on Hugging Face infrastructure, built with the Gradio or Streamlit SDKs, an arbitrary Dockerfile, or static HTML and JavaScript. Hardware runs from a free CPU tier through a shared ZeroGPU pool to hourly dedicated GPUs, alongside persistent storage and an SSH dev mode.

chunks.title: Spaces
chunks.text: Spaces (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Deployment: Hub integration deploys a Space from a model card, and a Space can be exposed as an MCP server or API endpoint.

chunks.title: spaCy
chunks.text: spaCy (by Explosion), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Python and Cython library for production natural language processing, running pipelines for tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, dependency parsing, named entity recognition, text classification, lemmatization and entity linking across more than 70 languages. It ships trained pipelines, a training system for custom ones and transformer support.

chunks.title: spaCy
chunks.text: spaCy (by Explosion), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Built by Explosion, which sells the separate Prodigy annotation tool and consulting.

chunks.title: Spec Kit
chunks.text: Spec Kit (by GitHub (Microsoft)), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: GitHub's toolkit for spec-driven development, which works with coding agents rather than being one. A structured specify, plan, tasks and implement workflow produces Markdown artifacts that feed each phase, giving an agent structured context instead of ad-hoc prompts. Its CLI scaffolds those files and orchestrates more than thirty agents.

chunks.title: SpeechBrain
chunks.text: SpeechBrain (by SpeechBrain), catalog entry under Speech & audio: An open-source PyTorch toolkit for training and running speech models, with more than 200 training recipes across about 20 tasks: recognition, synthesis, speaker recognition, diarization, voice activity detection, enhancement, separation, translation and more, and over 100 pretrained models on the Hub.

chunks.title: SPRING-INX
chunks.text: SPRING-INX (by SPRING Lab, IIT Madras), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: SPRING-INX is a speech recognition corpus of about 2,000 hours of manually transcribed speech in ten Indian languages, from Assamese and Bengali to Punjabi and Tamil. Agencies recorded monologues and mock conversations across at least ten domains under common guidelines, and a KL University team checked quality.

chunks.title: SPRING-INX
chunks.text: SPRING-INX (by SPRING Lab, IIT Madras), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: SPRING Lab at IIT Madras releases it per language, with ESPnet baseline recipes.

chunks.title: SPTAG
chunks.text: SPTAG (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: SPTAG (Space Partition Tree And Graph) is a Microsoft Research and Bing library for large-scale approximate nearest neighbour search, combining kd-tree or balanced k-means tree partitioning with a relative neighbourhood graph. It supports online insertion and deletion and a distributed search mode across machines.

chunks.title: Stable Audio
chunks.text: Stable Audio (by Stability AI), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Stable Audio is Stability AI's family of diffusion models that generate music and sound effects from text. The Stable Audio 3 generation ships Small Music, Small SFX and Medium models that produce clips of up to two and six minutes and support editing and continuation, alongside the earlier Stable Audio Open models.

chunks.title: Stable Audio
chunks.text: Stable Audio (by Stability AI), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: The largest Stable Audio 3 model is not publicly downloadable; Stability offers it through its API and enterprise self-hosting.

chunks.title: Stable Diffusion
chunks.text: Stable Diffusion (by Stability AI), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Stable Diffusion is Stability AI's line of latent diffusion models for text-to-image generation, from SDXL and its Turbo distillations to the multimodal-diffusion-transformer Stable Diffusion 3 and 3.5 models in Medium, Large and Large Turbo sizes.

chunks.title: Stable Diffusion
chunks.text: Stable Diffusion (by Stability AI), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Stability's newer Stable Image Core and Ultra models are offered through its API and Amazon Bedrock.

chunks.title: stable-diffusion.cpp
chunks.text: stable-diffusion.cpp (by leejet), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: stable-diffusion.cpp is a C and C++ inference engine for diffusion image and video models, built on the ggml tensor library and run from a command line or an embedded web interface. It reads safetensors and GGUF weights and targets CPUs and CUDA, Vulkan, Metal, OpenCL and SYCL devices.

chunks.title: stable-diffusion.cpp
chunks.text: stable-diffusion.cpp (by leejet), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Supported models range from the Stable Diffusion line through FLUX and Qwen-Image to the Wan, LTX and HunyuanVideo video models.

chunks.title: Stable Diffusion web UI (AUTOMATIC1111)
chunks.text: Stable Diffusion web UI (AUTOMATIC1111) (by AUTOMATIC1111), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Stable Diffusion web UI is a browser interface for generating and editing images with Stable Diffusion models, built on the Gradio library and known by its author's handle, AUTOMATIC1111.

chunks.title: Stable Diffusion web UI (AUTOMATIC1111)
chunks.text: Stable Diffusion web UI (AUTOMATIC1111) (by AUTOMATIC1111), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: It covers text-to-image and image-to-image, inpainting and outpainting, LoRA and embedding loading, checkpoint merging and upscaling, and is extended through a large ecosystem of third-party extensions.

chunks.title: Stable Video Diffusion
chunks.text: Stable Video Diffusion (by Stability AI), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Stable Video Diffusion is Stability AI's latent diffusion model that turns a single still image into a short video clip. The original SVD generates 14 frames and SVD-XT 25 frames at 576x1024; SVD-XT 1.1, released in February 2024, is a fine-tune of SVD-XT for more consistent output.

chunks.title: Stack-Edu
chunks.text: Stack-Edu (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Hugging Face's education-filtered slice of StarCoder2Data, about 125 billion tokens of code scored by an educational-value classifier. It is a documented component of SmolLM3 and of the Dolma 3 pool behind OLMo 3.

chunks.title: Stanza
chunks.text: Stanza (by Stanford NLP), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: The Stanford NLP Group's Python library for linguistic analysis in many languages.

chunks.title: Stanza
chunks.text: Stanza (by Stanford NLP), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Its neural pipeline does tokenization, multi-word token expansion, lemmatization, part-of-speech and morphological tagging, dependency and constituency parsing, named-entity recognition, sentiment and coreference, with pretrained models for about 80 languages trained on Universal Dependencies treebanks.

chunks.title: Stanza
chunks.text: Stanza (by Stanford NLP), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Every module can be retrained on the user's data, and it also gives Python access to the Java CoreNLP toolkit.

chunks.title: StarCoder2
chunks.text: StarCoder2 (by BigCode Project), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: BigCode's self-aligned instruct release of StarCoder2 at 16B, trained with a fully transparent pipeline and evaluated on EvalPlus, LiveCodeBench and DS-1000. The base StarCoder2-15B it builds on was trained on The Stack v2 and belongs to the base_pretrained shelf.

chunks.title: StarCoderData
chunks.text: StarCoderData (by BigCode Project), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: BigCode's filtered code corpus of roughly 250 billion tokens drawn from The Stack v1, covering source files alongside issues and notebooks, used to train StarCoder. It became a standard open code-pretraining component, documented in TinyLlama, IBM Granite Code, ALIA, Apertus, Marin and OLMoE.

chunks.title: StatsForecast
chunks.text: StatsForecast (by Nixtla), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Nixtla's library of fast statistical forecasting models, compiled with numba and able to fit millions of series on Spark, Dask or Ray. It implements automatic ARIMA, ETS, CES and Theta selection, MSTL and TBATS for multiple seasonalities, GARCH, intermittent-demand models such as Croston and ADIDA, and baselines, about 35 models in all.

chunks.title: StatsForecast
chunks.text: StatsForecast (by Nixtla), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Nixtla's closed TimeGPT forecasting service is a separate product.

chunks.title: statsmodels
chunks.text: statsmodels (by statsmodels), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Python library for statistical modeling and inference: linear, generalized linear, mixed and robust regression, discrete-choice models, survival analysis, multivariate methods and a large time-series suite from ARIMA and SARIMAX to state-space, VAR and Markov-switching models.

chunks.title: statsmodels
chunks.text: statsmodels (by statsmodels), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: It reports standard errors, tests and diagnostics alongside every fit. Maintained by the statsmodels developers.

chunks.title: Steel Browser
chunks.text: Steel Browser (by Steel), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Open-source browser API for agents: a batteries-included sandbox that manages sessions, pages and browser processes behind an HTTP API, self-hostable with Docker or run as Steel Cloud.

chunks.title: Suna
chunks.text: Suna (by Kortix AI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Generalist AI agent positioned as an autonomous operating system for a company. It browses the web, writes and executes code, manages files, calls APIs and completes multi-step business tasks, running specialist agents in isolated sandboxes behind a web interface with a large connector library. It is now branded Kortix.

chunks.title: Suno
chunks.text: Suno (by Suno), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Suno is a hosted music generation service that writes and produces complete songs, vocals and lyrics included, from a text prompt, with editing tools for working on the result. Its current model generation was developed with record-label partners including Warner Music Group, and paid plans grant commercial rights to the songs.

chunks.title: supervision
chunks.text: supervision (by Roboflow), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Roboflow's model-agnostic toolkit for working with computer-vision results.

chunks.title: supervision
chunks.text: supervision (by Roboflow), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: It converts detections and segmentations from Ultralytics, Transformers, MMDetection, Roboflow Inference and other libraries into one format, then draws annotations, filters and tracks detections, counts objects in zones, slices large images for inference, loads and converts datasets and computes metrics.

chunks.title: SurfSense
chunks.text: SurfSense (by SurfSense), catalog entry under UI & API: Desktop app that answers questions over a user's own documents, with cited hybrid retrieval, and turns them into summaries, slide decks, reports, flashcards, quizzes and podcasts. Parsing, indexing and generation run on the user's machine with a local model or any OpenAI-compatible API.

chunks.title: SurfSense
chunks.text: SurfSense (by SurfSense), catalog entry under UI & API: The repository also holds the earlier Docker web stack, now community-supported. It is positioned as a local alternative to NotebookLM.

chunks.title: Surya
chunks.text: Surya (by Datalab), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: OCR, layout analysis and reading-order engine from Datalab covering more than ninety languages. It detects text lines, classifies layout blocks, orders them for reading, and recognises tables - and it is the engine underneath the same team's Marker document pipeline rather than a competing end-to-end converter.

chunks.title: Surya
chunks.text: Surya (by NASA IMPACT), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Surya is a NASA-IBM heliophysics foundation model trained on aligned observations from the Solar Dynamics Observatory's AIA and HMI instruments.

chunks.title: Surya
chunks.text: Surya (by NASA IMPACT), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Its spatiotemporal transformer works at the instruments' native image resolution and supports solar forecasting, segmentation, solar-wind prediction, spectral modeling, and parameter-efficient downstream adaptation.

chunks.title: SWE-agent
chunks.text: SWE-agent (by Princeton NLP), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Research coding agent from Princeton NLP that takes a GitHub issue and attempts to fix it autonomously, and also runs offensive-security and competitive-programming tasks. It was published at NeurIPS 2024, and its agent-computer-interface scaffold became a reference architecture for later agents.

chunks.title: SWE-bench
chunks.text: SWE-bench (by Princeton NLP), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Docker-based evaluation harness that benchmarks coding agents on 2,294 real GitHub issues drawn from twelve Python repositories, generating patches and grading them by running each repository's own tests. It documents Verified, Lite and Multimodal splits, and offers cloud execution as an alternative to local Docker.

chunks.title: SWE-bench Verified
chunks.text: SWE-bench Verified (by Princeton NLP / OpenAI), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: 500 human-validated instances drawn from the wider SWE-bench dataset, each pairing a real GitHub issue with a test-verified solution patch and the fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass test lists that grade it. It was curated by OpenAI from the SWE-bench test set to reduce noise in the original 2,294-instance set.

chunks.title: SWIFT
chunks.text: SWIFT (by ModelScope (Alibaba)), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: SWIFT, packaged as ms-swift, covers the full lifecycle of 600+ text and 400+ multimodal models: pre-training, fine-tuning, alignment, inference, evaluation, quantization, and deployment.

chunks.title: SWIFT
chunks.text: SWIFT (by ModelScope (Alibaba)), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Tuning spans full-parameter, LoRA/QLoRA/DoRA, the GRPO family of RL algorithms, and preference methods such as DPO and KTO, reached through a CLI, a Python API, or a web UI. Alibaba's DAMO ModelScope team maintains it, and an AAAI 2025 paper describes the design.

chunks.title: Syft Space
chunks.text: Syft Space (by OpenMined), catalog entry under Federated learning: Syft Space is an application a data owner runs to make a document collection answerable without handing it over. It indexes the documents in a local or remote vector database, pairs them with a model from OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, vLLM or another provider, and serves the pair as an endpoint with its own access rules, rate limits and pricing.

chunks.title: Syft Space
chunks.text: Syft Space (by OpenMined), catalog entry under Federated learning: Endpoints can be listed on SyftHub, and only answers leave the owner's machine. OpenMined builds it.

chunks.title: SyftHub
chunks.text: SyftHub (by OpenMined), catalog entry under Federated learning: SyftHub is a registry where people publish AI models and data sources as endpoints, and others find them, see what each one costs and requires, and query them from a web app, a Python SDK or an MCP server.

chunks.title: SyftHub
chunks.text: SyftHub (by OpenMined), catalog entry under Federated learning: Its retrieval aggregator sends a question to each chosen source on its owner's own Syft Space node and combines only the passages that come back into one answer. OpenMined builds it.

chunks.title: SYNTH
chunks.text: SYNTH (by PleIAs), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Large synthetic dataset from PleIAs, released with the AI Alliance, designed for training small reasoning models end to end.

chunks.title: SYNTH
chunks.text: SYNTH (by PleIAs), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: It holds tens of millions of samples amplifying content from tens of thousands of Wikipedia articles, Wikibooks and internal documents, across exercise types including arithmetic, creative writing, RAG and information extraction. Samples carry reasoning traces and seed attribution, and roughly a fifth covers non-English European languages.

chunks.title: SynthID-Text
chunks.text: SynthID-Text (by Google), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: SynthID-Text is Google DeepMind's reference implementation of the text watermarking method published in Nature: it biases token sampling during generation so the output carries a statistical watermark, and detects it with a weighted-mean or a trained Bayesian detector.

chunks.title: SynthID-Text
chunks.text: SynthID-Text (by Google), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: It integrates with Hugging Face Transformers for Gemma and GPT-2 models, and the authors state it is not intended for production use.

chunks.title: TabICL
chunks.text: TabICL (by Inria SODA), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Tabular foundation model from Inria's Soda team that classifies and regresses on a new table by in-context learning, with no training or tuning step and a scikit-learn interface. TabICLv2 is pretrained on millions of synthetic datasets, and the repository releases the synthetic data generator and the pretraining code alongside inference.

chunks.title: TabICL
chunks.text: TabICL (by Inria SODA), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Published at ICML 2026.

chunks.title: TabPFN
chunks.text: TabPFN (by Prior Labs), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Tabular foundation model from Prior Labs that predicts on a new classification or regression table in a single forward pass, with no training or hyperparameter search: the fitted dataset is read in context. It is pretrained only on synthetic tables drawn from a prior.

chunks.title: TabPFN
chunks.text: TabPFN (by Prior Labs), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: The tabpfn package runs the checkpoints locally and adds fine-tuning, and a hosted API and enterprise edition are sold separately.

chunks.title: TACO
chunks.text: TACO (by TACO (MIT CSAIL / Adobe)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: TACO (the Tensor Algebra Compiler) is a C++ library and code generator, developed at MIT CSAIL and Adobe, that compiles sparse and dense tensor algebra expressions into native code competitive with hand-optimized kernels, using novel sparse iteration-space compiler techniques.

chunks.title: τ-Bench
chunks.text: τ-Bench (by Sierra), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Benchmark for tool-using conversational agents that must coordinate with a simulated human user under domain policy, across airline, retail, telecom and banking-knowledge domains. Tasks, domain data and the evaluation harness ship together in the repository, with a public leaderboard at taubench.com.

chunks.title: τ-Bench
chunks.text: τ-Bench (by Sierra), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: The current release, τ³-bench, adds voice and knowledge-retrieval evaluation on top of the τ² task set.

chunks.title: Tavily Search API
