chunks.text: Tavily Search API (by Tavily), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Tavily Search API is a hosted search service for AI agents and retrieval-augmented generation workflows, returning structured results through search, extract, crawl, map and research endpoints. Its documentation lists integrations with frameworks such as LangChain and CrewAI.

chunks.title: Te Hiku Media te reo Māori corpus
chunks.text: Te Hiku Media te reo Māori corpus (by Te Hiku Media), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Te Hiku Media's te reo Māori corpus is a labeled speech collection that the iwi broadcaster uses to build Māori speech recognition. It combines decades of archived radio interviews with native speakers, many now deceased, and sentences read aloud by the public through the Kōrero Māori site.

chunks.title: Te Hiku Media te reo Māori corpus
chunks.text: Te Hiku Media te reo Māori corpus (by Te Hiku Media), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Te Hiku Media keeps the data under Māori stewardship.

chunks.title: TensorFlow
chunks.text: TensorFlow (by Google), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: TensorFlow is an end-to-end machine learning platform with Python APIs for building, training and deploying models across CPUs, GPUs and TPUs, including mobile and edge devices. It was originally developed by the Google Brain team.

chunks.title: TensorFlow Federated
chunks.text: TensorFlow Federated (by Google), catalog entry under Federated learning: Google's open framework for machine learning and other computations on decentralized data. It provides a language for expressing federated computations, a Federated Learning API with aggregators, and a single-machine simulation runtime for experiments.

chunks.title: TensorFlow Serving
chunks.text: TensorFlow Serving (by Google), catalog entry under Inference code: TensorFlow Serving is a serving system for machine learning models in production, handling the inference side of the lifecycle with a batching scheduler and gRPC and HTTP endpoints. It integrates with TensorFlow models out of the box and can be extended to serve other model types.

chunks.title: Tensorlake Sandbox
chunks.text: Tensorlake Sandbox (by Tensorlake), catalog entry under Deployment: Tensorlake runs agent code in Firecracker microVMs, giving each harness or tool call its own machine with a shell, packages and processes, and putting it to sleep when idle.

chunks.title: Tensorlake Sandbox
chunks.text: Tensorlake Sandbox (by Tensorlake), catalog entry under Deployment: Around that sit a versioned POSIX filesystem that mounts like a disk, hosted Git that serves repositories without a clone, and durable serverless functions with queues, timers and retries. The company repositioned from document ingestion to this sandbox-native cloud.

chunks.title: TensorRT
chunks.text: TensorRT (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: TensorRT is NVIDIA's SDK for compiling trained networks into optimized inference engines for NVIDIA GPUs, applying layer fusion and explicit quantization. This repository holds the open-source components, the ONNX parser, the plugin library, the Python bindings and samples.

chunks.title: TensorRT
chunks.text: TensorRT (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: The optimizing builder itself ships as a prebuilt binary release that the repository links against.

chunks.title: TensorRT-LLM
chunks.text: TensorRT-LLM (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Inference code: TensorRT-LLM is NVIDIA's inference library for optimizing and serving LLMs on NVIDIA GPUs, using custom kernels, in-flight batching, FP8/INT4 quantization, speculative decoding, and multi-GPU tensor parallelism. It exposes a PyTorch-native Python API for defining and compiling models and integrates with Triton Inference Server and NVIDIA Dynamo.

chunks.title: TensorRT-LLM
chunks.text: TensorRT-LLM (by NVIDIA), catalog entry under Inference code: Being built on CUDA, it is tightly coupled to NVIDIA hardware.

chunks.title: Terminal-Bench
chunks.text: Terminal-Bench (by Laude Institute), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Benchmark of difficult, hand-vetted tasks that agents must complete in a real terminal, from compiling and debugging code to system administration. It runs as a continuous benchmark with tagged releases (2.0, 2.1, 3.0) mirrored on Hugging Face and executed through the Harbor framework, with an audited leaderboard at tbench.ai.

chunks.title: Terminal-Bench
chunks.text: Terminal-Bench (by Laude Institute), catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: Frontier agent builders use it to track progress on long-horizon terminal work.

chunks.title: TerraMind
chunks.text: TerraMind (by IBM), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: TerraMind is an any-to-any generative Earth-observation model developed by IBM, ESA Phi-Lab, and Forschungszentrum Juelich. It processes six satellite and terrain modalities, learns both pixel- and token-scale representations, and can generate missing modalities or supply embeddings for fine-tuned downstream models through TerraTorch.

chunks.title: Tesseract OCR
chunks.text: Tesseract OCR (by Tesseract OCR), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Long-standing open-source OCR engine, originally developed at HP and maintained since 2006 with Google's support. It recognises text in over a hundred languages with an LSTM-based engine, and outputs plain text, hOCR, ALTO, TSV and PDF.

chunks.title: Tesseract OCR
chunks.text: Tesseract OCR (by Tesseract OCR), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: It remains the default OCR dependency for a large amount of other software rather than a document-conversion product in its own right.

chunks.title: Text Embeddings Inference
chunks.text: Text Embeddings Inference (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Inference code: Text Embeddings Inference (TEI) is Hugging Face's Rust server for deploying open embedding, reranking and sequence-classification models such as Qwen3-Embedding, GTE, E5 and BGE.

chunks.title: Text Embeddings Inference
chunks.text: Text Embeddings Inference (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Inference code: It batches requests dynamically by token count, runs optimized model code built on Flash Attention, Candle and cuBLASLt, loads Safetensors and ONNX weights, and exposes HTTP and gRPC APIs with OpenTelemetry tracing and Prometheus metrics.

chunks.title: Text Embeddings Inference
chunks.text: Text Embeddings Inference (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Inference code: It ships as Docker images for CPUs and recent NVIDIA GPU generations, with AMD Instinct and Apple Silicon builds as well.

chunks.title: Text Generation Inference
chunks.text: Text Generation Inference (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Inference code: Text Generation Inference (TGI) is Hugging Face's LLM serving toolkit, a Rust, Python, and gRPC server purpose-built for the HF model ecosystem. It supports continuous batching, tensor parallelism, Flash Attention, token streaming, and quantization (GPTQ, AWQ, EETQ), and has powered Hugging Face's Inference Endpoints and Hugging Chat.

chunks.title: Text Generation Inference
chunks.text: Text Generation Inference (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Inference code: Its final release was v3.3.7 (2025-12-19) and the repository was archived 2026-03-21, with Hugging Face pointing new deployments to vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and MLX.

chunks.title: TextBlob
chunks.text: TextBlob (by sloria), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Python library with a simple API for common text-processing tasks - noun-phrase extraction, part-of-speech tagging, sentiment analysis, classification, tokenization, n-grams, inflection, lemmatization, spelling correction and WordNet lookup.

chunks.title: TextBlob
chunks.text: TextBlob (by sloria), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: It builds on NLTK and on parts of the pattern library, and its classifiers wrap NLTK's naive Bayes and decision-tree learners.

chunks.title: Amazon Textract
chunks.text: Amazon Textract (by Amazon Web Services), catalog entry under Document conversion & OCR: Managed document-analysis service from AWS that extracts text, handwriting, tables, forms and key-value pairs from scanned documents, with query-based extraction that answers a natural-language question against a document rather than returning the whole page.

chunks.title: tf2onnx
chunks.text: tf2onnx (by LF AI & Data (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: tf2onnx converts TensorFlow, Keras, TensorFlow.js and TFLite models into ONNX, from the command line or a Python API, mapping framework operations onto ONNX operator sets. It is the ONNX project's TensorFlow-side converter and sits under the ONNX organization.

chunks.title: ThaiExam
chunks.text: ThaiExam (by SCB 10X), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: ThaiExam is a Thai knowledge benchmark of multiple-choice questions taken from real examinations in Thailand: the grade-12 O-NET, the Investment Consultant licensing exam, TGAT, TPAT-1 and A-Level. It holds 590 questions in total, and each exam includes five worked examples for few-shot prompting.

chunks.title: ThaiExam
chunks.text: ThaiExam (by SCB 10X), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Typhoon team built it to evaluate the Typhoon Thai language models.

chunks.title: The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA)
chunks.text: The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA) (by National Cancer Institute), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA) de-identifies and publishes cancer-related medical images, mostly in DICOM, together with supporting clinical data, annotations and analysis results.

chunks.title: The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA)
chunks.text: The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA) (by National Cancer Institute), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: Research groups apply to publish collections, which an advisory group reviews before TCIA's team curates and releases them, each with a DataCite DOI and a version history. The National Cancer Institute funds it, and the Frederick National Laboratory for Cancer Research manages it.

chunks.title: The Pile
chunks.text: The Pile (by EleutherAI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: EleutherAI's 825 GiB English pretraining corpus from 2020, drawn from 22 sources spanning web text, academic papers, code, books and forums. It set the template for documented open pretraining data and trained Pythia, GPT-NeoX-20B, GPT-J and Cerebras-GPT among others.

chunks.title: The Pile (pipeline)
chunks.text: The Pile (pipeline) (by EleutherAI), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: The original documented-corpus construction pipeline: downloads, combines, weights/upsamples, and formats 22 components into The Pile. Distinct from the released Pile dataset.

chunks.title: The Stack v2
chunks.text: The Stack v2 (by BigCode Project), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Source-code dataset of 3.28 billion unique files, 67.53TB uncompressed, drawn from 104.2 million GitHub repositories across 658 programming languages and sourced through Software Heritage. It was created by the BigCode project and used to train the StarCoder2 models.

chunks.title: Thunderbolt
chunks.text: Thunderbolt (by MZLA Technologies), catalog entry under UI & API: Thunderbolt is an AI client for web, desktop and mobile that offers chat, search, research and reusable automations, with support for MCP servers and Agent Client Protocol agents.

chunks.title: Thunderbolt
chunks.text: Thunderbolt (by MZLA Technologies), catalog entry under UI & API: It connects to Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral, Fireworks or any OpenAI-compatible model, including local Ollama and llama.cpp, and organizations run it on their own infrastructure. MZLA Technologies, the Mozilla Foundation subsidiary behind Thunderbird, builds it as a sovereign alternative to hosted enterprise assistants.

chunks.title: ThunderKittens
chunks.text: ThunderKittens (by Hazy Research (Stanford)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: ThunderKittens is a CUDA-embedded framework of tile primitives for writing deep-learning kernels, built on the premise that kernels expressed over register and shared-memory tiles reach hand-written performance.

chunks.title: ThunderKittens
chunks.text: ThunderKittens (by Hazy Research (Stanford)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Because it embeds in CUDA rather than replacing it, authors can drop to raw CUDA where the abstraction runs out. Stanford's Hazy Research group develops it.

chunks.title: Texas Instruments AM67A
chunks.text: Texas Instruments AM67A (by Texas Instruments), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: Texas Instruments' edge-AI vision SoC, built on a 16nm FinFET process, pairs a quad Arm Cortex-A53 at 1.4 GHz with dual C7x DSP cores and matrix multiply accelerators delivering 4 TOPS.

chunks.title: Texas Instruments AM67A
chunks.text: Texas Instruments AM67A (by Texas Instruments), catalog entry under Edge AI hardware: It integrates a multi-camera image signal processor with up to four CSI-2 inputs, PCIe Gen3 and Gigabit Ethernet with TSN, and supports up to 8GB of LPDDR4. It is the silicon behind the BeagleY-AI board.

chunks.title: timm (PyTorch Image Models)
chunks.text: timm (PyTorch Image Models) (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: PyTorch library of image models, layers, optimizers, schedulers, augmentations and reference training and validation scripts, spanning more than 100 architecture families from ResNet and EfficientNet to ViT, ConvNeXt and MobileNetV4, with over 700 pretrained weights.

chunks.title: timm (PyTorch Image Models)
chunks.text: timm (PyTorch Image Models) (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Created by Ross Wightman and maintained under Hugging Face.

chunks.title: Tinker
chunks.text: Tinker (by Thinking Machines Lab), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Tinker is Thinking Machines Lab's managed training API for researchers, launched October 1, 2025. It lets teams control the training loop through four primitives (forward_backward, optim_step, sample, and save_state) while Thinking Machines runs the distributed infrastructure underneath.

chunks.title: Tinker
chunks.text: Tinker (by Thinking Machines Lab), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: The API covers LoRA fine-tuning and RL sampling on open-weight models from several vendors, including large mixture-of-experts checkpoints, alongside Thinking Machines' own Inkling models.

chunks.title: TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0
chunks.text: TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 (by TinyLlama), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 is a 1.1B-parameter chat model that uses the Llama 2 architecture and tokenizer. It was fine-tuned on UltraChat and aligned with DPO on UltraFeedback, starting from a TinyLlama base pretrained on three trillion tokens.

chunks.title: Amazon Titan Text Embeddings
chunks.text: Amazon Titan Text Embeddings (by Amazon), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Amazon’s text embedding model on Bedrock, currently Titan Text Embeddings V2 (amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0): an 8,000-token text embedder with configurable output dimensions defaulting to 1,024, invoked through the Bedrock runtime and used as the default embedder for Bedrock Knowledge Bases.

chunks.title: TituLM Bangla corpus
chunks.text: TituLM Bangla corpus (by Hishab), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The TituLM Bangla corpus is a Bangla pretraining text corpus of about 20 billion tokens in 31 million documents. Most of it is Common Crawl text extracted with Trafilatura and filtered on 20 quality signals, and the rest is English news machine-translated into Bangla plus romanized Bangla, both produced with a fine-tuned NLLB model.

chunks.title: TituLM Bangla corpus
chunks.text: TituLM Bangla corpus (by Hishab), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Hishab released it alongside its TituLLMs Bangla language models.

chunks.title: Together Fine-Tuning
chunks.text: Together Fine-Tuning (by Together AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Together Fine-Tuning adapts open-weight models, including Llama, Mistral, Qwen, and DeepSeek, on Together AI's infrastructure, with LoRA and full-parameter fine-tuning plus supervised, preference (DPO), function-calling, reasoning, and vision-language methods.

chunks.title: Together Fine-Tuning
chunks.text: Together Fine-Tuning (by Together AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: It LoRA-tunes models above 100B parameters, including DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen3-235B, and runs the pipeline from data upload through training to a dedicated endpoint; the finished checkpoint can also be downloaded.

chunks.title: Together Inference Engine
chunks.text: Together Inference Engine (by Together AI), catalog entry under Inference code: Together Inference Engine is a serving stack that runs open models with FlashAttention, adaptive speculative decoding (ATLAS), and custom CUDA kernels. It offers serverless endpoints across a large catalog of open models alongside dedicated instances that reserve GPU capacity for a single model.

chunks.title: Together Inference Engine
chunks.text: Together Inference Engine (by Together AI), catalog entry under Inference code: Together AI builds it, and its team also publishes open kernel research including FlashAttention and ThunderKittens.

chunks.title: Tokenizers
chunks.text: Tokenizers (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Tokenizers is a library providing fast implementations of modern tokenization algorithms including Byte-Pair Encoding, WordPiece, and Unigram. It is written in Rust with bindings for Python and Node.js, and emphasizes high-throughput training and inference.

chunks.title: Tokenizers
chunks.text: Tokenizers (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Maintained by Hugging Face, it is a direct dependency of the Transformers library.

chunks.title: Torch-TensorRT
chunks.text: Torch-TensorRT (by PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: Torch-TensorRT is PyTorch's official compiler that lowers PyTorch, TorchScript and FX models into NVIDIA TensorRT engines, accelerating inference on NVIDIA GPUs while staying inside the PyTorch runtime.

chunks.title: TorchAO
chunks.text: TorchAO (by PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: TorchAO is PyTorch's native architecture-optimization library, applying quantization to models for both training and serving. It covers float8 and MX-format training, quantization-aware training, and int4 and int8 post-training quantization with dtype extensions that compose with torch.compile.

chunks.title: torchtune
chunks.text: torchtune (by PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: torchtune is a PyTorch-native library of training recipes for post-training language models: supervised fine-tuning, knowledge distillation, DPO, PPO, GRPO, and quantization-aware training.

chunks.title: torchtune
chunks.text: torchtune (by PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: It bundles implementations of open models such as Llama, Gemma, Mistral, Phi, and Qwen, scales from one device to multi-node via FSDP2, and integrates with Hugging Face Hub and Weights & Biases. Meta built it; development wound down in 2025 and it is no longer maintained.

chunks.title: torchvision
chunks.text: torchvision (by PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: PyTorch's computer-vision library, with popular datasets, image and video transforms, vision operators, and model architectures with pretrained weights for classification, semantic and instance segmentation, object detection, keypoint detection, video classification and optical flow.

chunks.title: torchvision
chunks.text: torchvision (by PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation)), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Reference training scripts reproduce each model. It is part of the PyTorch project under the PyTorch Foundation.

chunks.title: Traccia
chunks.text: Traccia (by Traccia), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Traccia is an open-source Python SDK for OpenTelemetry-based tracing, evaluation and governance across AI agents and LLM applications, with automatic instrumentation for OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini, guardrail detection, and EU AI Act and HIPAA-oriented evidence records.

chunks.title: Traccia
chunks.text: Traccia (by Traccia), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: It exports traces as OTLP to any collector with no account required, while its prompt registry and persisted evaluation features connect to the separate, commercial Traccia platform at app.traccia.ai.

chunks.title: Transformers
chunks.text: Transformers (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Transformers is a model-definition framework for machine learning across text, vision, audio, video and multimodal models, covering both inference and training.

chunks.title: Transformers
chunks.text: Transformers (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: It provides a unified API to load and run pretrained checkpoints from the Hugging Face Hub, and its model definitions are reused by training frameworks, inference engines and adjacent libraries such as llama.cpp and mlx. Hugging Face maintains it.

chunks.title: TRELLIS
chunks.text: TRELLIS (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: TRELLIS is Microsoft's family of 3D asset generation models built on structured 3D latents.

chunks.title: TRELLIS
chunks.text: TRELLIS (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: The original models turn a text or image prompt into radiance fields, 3D Gaussians or textured meshes; TRELLIS.2, a 4B model, generates meshes with PBR materials from a single image at voxel resolutions up to 1536 cubed and can texture an existing mesh from a reference image.

chunks.title: TripoSG
chunks.text: TripoSG (by VAST), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: TripoSG is VAST's 1.5B-parameter rectified-flow transformer that generates a 3D mesh from a single image, decoding a signed distance field trained on two million curated image-SDF pairs. A distilled TripoSG-scribble variant generates shapes from a sketch and a text prompt for quick prototyping.

chunks.title: TripoSR
chunks.text: TripoSR (by VAST), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: TripoSR is a feed-forward transformer that reconstructs a textured 3D mesh from a single image in under a second, built on the Large Reconstruction Model design. VAST (Tripo AI) developed it with Stability AI and trained it on a curated subset of Objaverse.

chunks.title: Triton
chunks.text: Triton (by Triton (triton-lang)), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Triton is a Python-embedded language and compiler for writing efficient custom GPU kernels, aiming for higher productivity than CUDA with more flexibility than other domain-specific languages. It compiles through MLIR and targets NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, with CPU support in progress.

chunks.title: Triton
chunks.text: Triton (by Triton (triton-lang)), catalog entry under Core ML frameworks & libraries: Created by Philippe Tillet at OpenAI, it is now developed under the triton-lang organization and serves as the kernel backend for PyTorch's inductor.

chunks.title: TRL
chunks.text: TRL (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: TRL (Transformers Reinforcement Learning) post-trains language models through Trainer classes covering supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization (DPO, KTO, ORPO, CPO), online methods (GRPO, RLOO, PPO), reward modeling, and knowledge distillation.

chunks.title: TRL
chunks.text: TRL (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Built on Hugging Face Transformers, it scales through Accelerate with DDP, DeepSpeed ZeRO, and FSDP, and integrates PEFT for LoRA and QLoRA training. A trl command-line interface runs the same methods without Python code. Hugging Face maintains it.

chunks.title: TruLens
chunks.text: TruLens (by Snowflake), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Library for evaluation and tracing of LLM applications and agents.

chunks.title: TruLens
chunks.text: TruLens (by Snowflake), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Its differentiator is feedback functions, programmatic evaluators including the RAG triad of groundedness, context relevance and answer relevance alongside toxicity and others, combined with application instrumentation and tracing, which makes it more evaluation-first than the gateway and observability-first tools around it.

chunks.title: TrustMark
chunks.text: TrustMark (by Adobe), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: TrustMark is Adobe's open-source image watermarking method for the Content Authenticity Initiative: it hides an identifier in an image of any resolution that survives resharing, screenshots and JPEG compression, and decodes or removes it again.

chunks.title: TrustMark
chunks.text: TrustMark (by Adobe), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: The identifier can point to a C2PA manifest kept elsewhere, and the method is on the C2PA list of approved watermarks. Implementations exist in Python, JavaScript and Rust.

chunks.title: TruthfulQA
chunks.text: TruthfulQA, catalog entry under Benchmark / eval datasets: 817 questions across 38 categories, written to elicit imitative falsehoods - the misconceptions a model picks up from its training text rather than errors of reasoning. It ships generation and multiple-choice configurations and dates from 2021.

chunks.title: Tulu 3
chunks.text: Tulu 3 (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Ai2's open post-training model family at 8B, 70B and 405B, applying a fully reproducible recipe on top of Meta's Llama 3.1 base: open supervised and preference data, the open-instruct training code, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. The evaluation framework is released alongside it.

chunks.title: Tulu 3 SFT Mixture
chunks.text: Tulu 3 SFT Mixture (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Supervised fine-tuning dataset of roughly 939,000 samples combining 18 data sources, created by the Allen Institute for AI for its Tulu 3 post-training recipe. It covers conversation, instruction-following, math, code, safety and multilingual data across more than 70 languages, and underpins the Tulu 3 model family.

chunks.title: TurkishMMLU
chunks.text: TurkishMMLU (by Arda Yüksel), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: TurkishMMLU tests language models on multiple-choice questions from Turkish high-school curricula, covering nine subjects in natural sciences, mathematics, Turkish language and literature, and social sciences and humanities. Curriculum experts wrote the more than 10,000 questions, and each carries a correctness ratio as a difficulty signal.

chunks.title: TurkishMMLU
chunks.text: TurkishMMLU (by Arda Yüksel), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Arda Yüksel, Abdullatif Köksal and colleagues publish it with evaluation code.

chunks.title: TxT360
chunks.text: TxT360 (by LLM360), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: LLM360's globally deduplicated pretraining corpus, combining 99 Common Crawl snapshots with 14 curated sources including FreeLaw, PG-19, arXiv, Wikipedia and StackExchange. It holds about 5 trillion deduplicated tokens and supports a recipe reaching beyond 15 trillion, and trains K2-V2 together with its mid-training and SFT extensions.

chunks.title: TxT360 (pipeline)
chunks.text: TxT360 (pipeline) (by LLM360), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Construction pipeline for the TxT360 open pretraining corpus: global deduplication and source processing across 99 Common Crawl snapshots and 14 curated sources. Distinct from the released TxT360 dataset.

chunks.title: Typesense
chunks.text: Typesense (by Typesense), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Typesense is an in-memory search engine offering typo-tolerant full-text search with faceting, filtering, geosearch and vector and hybrid search, positioned as a self-hostable alternative to hosted search APIs. It is written in C++ and runs as a single binary or clustered, with a hosted service and paid support sold beside it.

chunks.title: Typhoon-S sovereign capability dataset
chunks.text: Typhoon-S sovereign capability dataset (by SCB 10X), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Typhoon-S sovereign capability dataset holds the Thai training and test files behind the region-specific part of the Typhoon-S post-training study.

chunks.title: Typhoon-S sovereign capability dataset
chunks.text: Typhoon-S sovereign capability dataset (by SCB 10X), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Legal-domain files derive from NitiBench and WangchanX-Legal-ThaiCCL-RAG, split into reinforcement-learning, pretraining, supervised and agent sets, and general-domain files derive from MIRAGE. The release totals about 30,000 rows in Thai and English and comes from the Typhoon team.

chunks.title: UberText
chunks.text: UberText (by lang-uk), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: UberText 2.0 is a corpus of modern Ukrainian of about 3.27 billion tokens in 8.59 million texts, spanning news from 38 websites, fiction, public Telegram channels, the Ukrainian Wikipedia and Supreme Court decisions. It is offered for direct download in several processing layers, from cleaned text to sentence-split and tokenized files.

chunks.title: UberText
chunks.text: UberText (by lang-uk), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Dmytro Chaplynskyi and the lang-uk community build it.

chunks.title: UCE
chunks.text: UCE (by Stanford SNAP), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: UCE is the Stanford SNAP lab's universal cell embedding model, a self-supervised transformer that maps single-cell transcriptomes from many tissues and species into one latent space. It ships 4-layer and 33-layer pretrained checkpoints and an evaluation script that embeds an AnnData dataset directly, with no labeling, training, or fine-tuning step.

chunks.title: UCI Machine Learning Repository
chunks.text: UCI Machine Learning Repository (by University of California, Irvine), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: The UCI Machine Learning Repository is the University of California, Irvine's collection of datasets donated for machine learning research, kept since 1987. Librarians approve each donation, which then receives a DOI and a CC BY 4.0 license, and datasets from elsewhere can be linked.

chunks.title: UCI Machine Learning Repository
chunks.text: UCI Machine Learning Repository (by University of California, Irvine), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: A public JSON API and the ucimlrepo Python package fetch a dataset by ID or name into pandas with its variable descriptions.

chunks.title: UI-TARS
chunks.text: UI-TARS (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under Multimodal models: UI-TARS is ByteDance Seed's GUI agent model, which takes screenshots as its only input and returns mouse, keyboard and touch actions for desktop, browser and phone interfaces. The released checkpoints are the 2B, 7B and 72B SFT and DPO models and UI-TARS-1.5-7B, built on a Qwen2.5-VL base.

chunks.title: UI-TARS
chunks.text: UI-TARS (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under Multimodal models: The UI-TARS-desktop application that drives it is a separate project.

chunks.title: UltraChat 200k
chunks.text: UltraChat 200k (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Hugging Face H4's filtered 200,000-dialogue slice of the ChatGPT-distilled UltraChat corpus, prepared for supervised fine-tuning of chat models. It anchored the Zephyr recipe and is also used by TinyLlama-Chat, and remains a common starting point for open chat alignment work.

chunks.title: UltraFeedback
chunks.text: UltraFeedback (by OpenBMB), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: GPT-4-annotated preference dataset of roughly 64,000 prompts, 256,000 responses and 380,000 fine-grained feedback annotations across instruction-following, truthfulness, honesty and helpfulness. Prompts are drawn from six public datasets with responses from 17 different models.

chunks.title: UltraFeedback
chunks.text: UltraFeedback (by OpenBMB), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Built by OpenBMB, it is used to train reward and critic models in open RLHF and DPO pipelines.

chunks.title: Ultralytics YOLO
chunks.text: Ultralytics YOLO (by Ultralytics), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Python package and CLI for training, validating and deploying the YOLO family of real-time vision models - YOLOv8, YOLO11 and YOLO26 - across detection, instance and semantic segmentation, depth estimation, classification, pose, oriented boxes and tracking.

chunks.title: Ultralytics YOLO
chunks.text: Ultralytics YOLO (by Ultralytics), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: The same package downloads the pretrained checkpoints and exports them to deployment formats. Built by Ultralytics, which also sells an enterprise license and a hosted platform.

chunks.title: UMA
chunks.text: UMA (by Meta), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: UMA is Meta FAIR's family of Universal Models for Atoms, trained on roughly half a billion DFT structures compiled from five chemical-domain datasets and routed at inference by a task embedding covering molecules, inorganic materials, catalysis, MOFs, and molecular crystals.

chunks.title: UMA
chunks.text: UMA (by Meta), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: Weights are distributed through a gated Hugging Face repository and run through the fairchem library's ASE calculator and multi-GPU simulation interfaces.

chunks.title: UMAP
chunks.text: UMAP (by lmcinnes), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection, a non-linear dimension reduction method used for visualization in the way t-SNE is and for general embedding of high-dimensional data.

chunks.title: UMAP
chunks.text: UMAP (by lmcinnes), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: The umap-learn package implements it with a scikit-learn interface and adds supervised and semi-supervised embedding, densMAP, AlignedUMAP for data that changes over time, and Parametric UMAP, which trains a neural network to learn the mapping.

chunks.title: Ungoliant
chunks.text: Ungoliant (by OSCAR Project), catalog entry under Dataset Processing Tools: Rust pipeline that generates the OSCAR corpus from Common Crawl WET files: language identification, filtering, and metadata annotation. The official OSCAR / Colossal-OSCAR construction pipeline.

chunks.title: Union.ai
chunks.text: Union.ai (by Union.ai), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Commercial AI runtime built on Flyte, deployed into the customer's own cloud rather than hosted by the vendor. It runs the same typed Python workflows Flyte does, adds managed control-plane services around them, and keeps data and models inside the customer's infrastructure.

chunks.title: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)
chunks.text: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) (by Universal Commerce Protocol project), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: The Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) is an open standard for agentic commerce, giving AI agents and apps, businesses and payment providers one language for catalog search, carts, checkout, identity linking and orders.

chunks.title: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)
chunks.text: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) (by Universal Commerce Protocol project), catalog entry under Agent protocols & SDKs: A business declares the capabilities it supports in a profile that platforms discover, and serves them over REST, MCP or A2A. Google and Shopify founded it, and a council of member companies governs it.

chunks.title: Unsloth
chunks.text: Unsloth (by Unsloth AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Unsloth is a fine-tuning library that trains language, diffusion, speech and embedding models with custom Triton kernels for faster training and lower VRAM use. Supported methods include LoRA, QLoRA, full fine-tuning, pretraining, GRPO reinforcement learning and DPO preference tuning, and trained models export to formats including GGUF.

chunks.title: Unsloth
chunks.text: Unsloth (by Unsloth AI), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Unsloth runs as code through Unsloth Core, or through the Unsloth Studio web UI and a desktop app.

chunks.title: Updesh
chunks.text: Updesh (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Updesh is a synthetic instruction-tuning dataset of about 9.5 million examples in 13 Indian languages and English. Its reasoning part translates Orca-AgentInstruct and OrcaMath tasks with Llama 3.1 405B, and its generative part builds multi-hop questions, dialogues, summaries and similar tasks from language-specific Wikipedia with Qwen3-235B.

chunks.title: Updesh
chunks.text: Updesh (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Microsoft Research built it to post-train smaller models for Indian languages.

chunks.title: UrduSpeech
chunks.text: UrduSpeech (by ASLP Lab), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: UrduSpeech is an Urdu speech corpus of 156 hours in 71,792 utterances, split into standard Pakistani Urdu, Urdu-English code-switching and Pakistani-accented English.

chunks.title: UrduSpeech
chunks.text: UrduSpeech (by ASLP Lab), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Audio comes from YouTube and Pakistan Television archives across 12 categories such as news, drama and poetry, then transcribed and tagged with 12 paralinguistic attributes through an LLM pipeline built on Gemini 2.5 Pro. ASLP-lab built it, with a separate 9-hour benchmark corrected by native speakers.

chunks.title: USearch
chunks.text: USearch (by Unum), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: USearch is a single-file similarity search and clustering engine implementing HNSW over user-defined metrics, including spatial, binary and probabilistic distances. The C++ header compiles into bindings for a dozen languages and runs on desktop, mobile, WebAssembly and inside SQLite. Unum develops it.

chunks.title: Uzu
chunks.text: Uzu (by Mirai Tech), catalog entry under Inference code: Uzu is a high-performance on-device inference engine for Apple platforms, running models locally on iOS and macOS against unified memory so that inference needs no network round trip and no per-token cost. It ships Python, TypeScript and Swift bindings in-repo.

chunks.title: v0
chunks.text: v0 (by Vercel), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Generative UI and full-stack development agent from Vercel that builds web applications from natural-language prompts. It generates React and Next.js components, assembles pages, manages state, connects to databases and iterates on visual feedback, planning and creating its own tasks as it builds.

chunks.title: v0
chunks.text: v0 (by Vercel), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: It ships on the web and iOS with one-click deployment to Vercel.

chunks.title: Project Vaani
chunks.text: Project Vaani (by ARTPARK, Indian Institute of Science), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Project Vaani is a speech corpus of spontaneous, image-prompted speech from about 156,000 speakers in 165 Indian districts, spanning some 105 languages. It holds over 31,000 hours of audio, about 2,000 hours of it transcribed, together with the roughly 289,000 prompt images.

chunks.title: Project Vaani
chunks.text: Project Vaani (by ARTPARK, Indian Institute of Science), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: IISc Bangalore and ARTPARK run the project with funding from Google, and also publish a transcribed-only subset and a Hindi speech-recognition benchmark.

chunks.title: ValidMind Library
chunks.text: ValidMind Library (by ValidMind), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: The ValidMind Library is a Python toolkit that runs validation tests on models and automates model documentation for risk and compliance review. It works with any Python model and sends its test results and documentation artifacts to the ValidMind Platform, a cloud-hosted service where validators review them.

chunks.title: ValidMind Library
chunks.text: ValidMind Library (by ValidMind), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: Optional PII detection keeps sensitive data out of logged results.

chunks.title: Vals AI
chunks.text: Vals AI (by Vals AI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Independent benchmarking service that runs evaluations over finance, law, healthcare, coding, math, education, cybersecurity and games, and publishes composite indices alongside a leaderboard of frontier models.

chunks.title: Vals AI
chunks.text: Vals AI (by Vals AI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Vals says its scores are based on privately held test sets, kept private so models cannot be trained to them, and it has open sourced the infrastructure that runs the evaluations.

chunks.title: vantage6
chunks.text: vantage6 (by vantage6), catalog entry under Federated learning: Privacy-preserving federated analysis infrastructure from IKNL. A central HQ server, an authentication service, an algorithm store and a web UI coordinate nodes that each data holder runs in Docker beside its own data; algorithms travel to the nodes as containers, and the network runs federated learning, federated statistics or MPC algorithms.

chunks.title: Vearch
chunks.text: Vearch (by Vearch project), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Vearch is a distributed vector database for similarity search over embeddings, combining vector retrieval with scalar filtering in hybrid queries. It deploys as a cluster with separate master, router and partition-server roles.

chunks.title: Vellum
chunks.text: Vellum (by Vellum), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Personal AI assistant across web, macOS, iOS and a CLI, with episodic, semantic and procedural memory, that takes actions on the user's behalf across channels including Slack and Telegram. It runs proactive check-ins and isolates credentials out of process. The company pivoted to it in 2026 from an LLMops platform, which remains available.

chunks.title: Venturalitica SDK
chunks.text: Venturalitica SDK (by Venturalitica), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: The Venturalitica SDK brings compliance checks into model training: it maps controls to EU AI Act articles 9 to 15, gathers evidence such as data lineage, metrics and a bill of materials during a run, and writes it as OSCAL. Checks run locally by default, with an optional strict mode for CI pipelines.

chunks.title: Venturalitica SDK
chunks.text: Venturalitica SDK (by Venturalitica), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: It accompanies a 2026 preprint on machine-readable compliance evidence.

chunks.title: Veo
chunks.text: Veo (by Google), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Veo is Google DeepMind's video generation model line, which generates video with native audio from text and image prompts. It is served through the Gemini API and Google's Flow filmmaking tool in standard, Fast and Lite tiers, with 4K output and portrait formats.

chunks.title: Vercel Sandbox
chunks.text: Vercel Sandbox (by Vercel), catalog entry under Deployment: Vercel Sandbox runs untrusted or agent-generated code in a Firecracker microVM with its own filesystem and network, started from a Vercel-managed Linux image or a custom OCI image in the Vercel Container Registry.

chunks.title: Vercel Sandbox
chunks.text: Vercel Sandbox (by Vercel), catalog entry under Deployment: Sandboxes persist by default, resuming where they stopped, and can be snapshotted, given root and system privileges, or split per agent by Linux user. JavaScript and Python SDKs and a CLI drive it, and each sandbox runs in a Vercel region the caller chooses.

chunks.title: VerifyWise
chunks.text: VerifyWise (by BlueWave Labs), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: VerifyWise is a self-hostable AI governance platform for keeping the records an organization needs under frameworks such as the EU AI Act and ISO 42001: an inventory of AI systems, risk assessments, policies, vendor reviews and audit evidence.

chunks.title: VerifyWise
chunks.text: VerifyWise (by BlueWave Labs), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: BlueWave Labs publishes it under the Business Source License and sells an enterprise license for hosting it for others.

chunks.title: verl
chunks.text: verl (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: verl (Volcano Engine Reinforcement Learning) is a post-training library for large language models, built on the HybridFlow hybrid-controller architecture. It targets RLHF and reasoning RL on math and code tasks, implements PPO, GRPO, RLOO, GSPO, and DAPO, and runs on FSDP or Megatron-LM with vLLM and SGLang rollout.

chunks.title: verl
chunks.text: verl (by ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: ByteDance Seed started the project; the verl community maintains it.

chunks.title: Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation Service
chunks.text: Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation Service (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Google Cloud's managed service for scoring generative-AI outputs, part of the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, using adaptive rubrics that generate per-prompt pass/fail tests, static rubrics, computation-based metrics such as ROUGE and BLEU, and custom Python function metrics.

chunks.title: Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation Service
chunks.text: Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation Service (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under Evaluation code: It covers models and agents, works with any model callable through LiteLLM, and builds evaluation datasets from uploaded files, production logs or synthetic data.

chunks.title: Model Garden (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform)
chunks.text: Model Garden (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Google Cloud's model catalog on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI, listing Google's own models, partner models such as Anthropic's Claude, and open models including Gemma, Llama, Mistral and popular Hugging Face repositories.

chunks.title: Model Garden (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform)
chunks.text: Model Garden (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under Model hubs & registries: Each entry can be tested, tuned and deployed to a managed endpoint in one click or through the SDK, CLI or REST API, and customers can deploy their own weights into their project.

chunks.title: Vertex AI Model Observability
chunks.text: Vertex AI Model Observability (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Google Cloud's production monitoring surface for generative AI on Vertex AI: a predefined Cloud Monitoring dashboard tracking usage, throughput, token consumption, latency and error rates, including capacity errors, for Gemini and other Model Garden foundation models.

chunks.title: Vertex AI Model Observability
chunks.text: Vertex AI Model Observability (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Vertex AI Agent Builder extends it with sessions, traces, logs, agent performance dashboards, multi-turn auto-raters, online evaluation against live traffic and a unified trace viewer for debugging agent reasoning.

chunks.title: Vertex AI Pipelines
chunks.text: Vertex AI Pipelines (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Serverless managed service for running machine-learning pipelines on Google Cloud. Pipelines are defined with the Kubeflow Pipelines or TFX SDK and executed without the user managing orchestration infrastructure, with runs schedulable on a recurring basis and artifact lineage tracked in ML Metadata.

chunks.title: Vertex AI Tuning
chunks.text: Vertex AI Tuning (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Vertex AI Tuning is Google Cloud's managed tuning service for Gemini models, offering supervised fine-tuning, preference tuning from human feedback, and a preview reinforcement fine-tuning method, with continuous tuning, checkpoints and function-calling tuning. Datasets can be as small as about 100 examples.

chunks.title: Vertex AI Tuning
chunks.text: Vertex AI Tuning (by Google Cloud), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: Tuned models stay on Google Cloud, since Google does not release Gemini weights.

chunks.title: Vespa
chunks.text: Vespa (by Vespa.ai), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Vespa is a serving platform that stores, indexes and retrieves vectors, tensors, text and structured data in one system, and evaluates ranking models over the results at query time. Retrieval combines approximate nearest neighbour search with lexical matching and filtering, and inference runs inside the serving path rather than beside it.

chunks.title: Vespa
chunks.text: Vespa (by Vespa.ai), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: The repository builds and runs the whole system.

chunks.title: VibeThinker-3B
chunks.text: VibeThinker-3B (by WeiboAI), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: WeiboAI's VibeThinker-3B is a 3B-parameter reasoning model fine-tuned from Qwen2.5-Coder-3B and specialized for verifiable math, coding and STEM problems. Its model card claims scores in the range of top frontier reasoning models on verifiable benchmarks, and it is not intended for tool calling or agentic use.

chunks.title: VibeVoice
chunks.text: VibeVoice (by Microsoft), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Microsoft Research's speech models: VibeVoice-ASR transcribes up to an hour of audio in one pass with speaker labels and timestamps in more than 50 languages, with streaming and CPU variants, and the TTS models generate long multi-speaker conversations or stream speech in real time.

chunks.title: VideoLLaMA
chunks.text: VideoLLaMA (by Alibaba DAMO Academy), catalog entry under Multimodal models: VideoLLaMA is Alibaba DAMO Academy's video-language model line, which answers questions about video and images in text. VideoLLaMA3 builds on Qwen2.5 language models in 2B and 7B sizes, samples video at a configurable frame rate and is trained in four stages from vision-encoder adaptation to video-centric fine-tuning.

chunks.title: VideoLLaMA
chunks.text: VideoLLaMA (by Alibaba DAMO Academy), catalog entry under Multimodal models: VideoLLaMA2.1-AV adds audio-visual input.

chunks.title: Vietnamese Curated Dataset
chunks.text: Vietnamese Curated Dataset (by VTS NLP (Viettel)), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Vietnamese Curated Dataset is a pretraining text corpus of about 12.2 million Vietnamese documents assembled from existing open sources: the Vietnamese subsets of C4 and OSCAR 23.01, Vietnamese Wikipedia and the Binhvq news corpus.

chunks.title: Vietnamese Curated Dataset
chunks.text: Vietnamese Curated Dataset (by VTS NLP (Viettel)), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Viettel Solutions cleaned it with NVIDIA NeMo Curator, applying Unicode normalization, exact deduplication, and heuristic and classifier-based quality filtering.

chunks.title: Vuk'uzenzele isiXhosa Speech Dataset (ViXSD)
chunks.text: Vuk'uzenzele isiXhosa Speech Dataset (ViXSD) (by Lelapa AI), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Vuk'uzenzele isiXhosa Speech Dataset (ViXSD) is about 10 hours of read isiXhosa speech in which eight native speakers, four men and four women, narrate articles from the Vuk'uzenzele corpus. Each of its 395 recordings comes with a transcript and speaker metadata on age, accent and linguistic background.

chunks.title: Vuk'uzenzele isiXhosa Speech Dataset (ViXSD)
chunks.text: Vuk'uzenzele isiXhosa Speech Dataset (ViXSD) (by Lelapa AI), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Lelapa AI released it as the proof of concept for its community-centered Esethu Framework and license.

chunks.title: vLLM
chunks.text: vLLM (by vLLM (UC Berkeley / vLLM team)), catalog entry under Inference code: vLLM is a serving engine for large language models built on PagedAttention, which manages the KV cache as virtual memory pages to reduce memory waste during batched inference.

chunks.title: vLLM
chunks.text: vLLM (by vLLM (UC Berkeley / vLLM team)), catalog entry under Inference code: It supports continuous batching, tensor and pipeline parallelism, speculative decoding, and quantization, exposing an OpenAI-compatible API server for self-hosted deployment. It originated in the Sky Computing Lab at UC Berkeley and is community-governed under vllm-project.

chunks.title: VLMEvalKit
chunks.text: VLMEvalKit (by OpenCompass Community), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Evaluation toolkit for large vision-language models that runs 220+ models over 80+ multimodal benchmarks with one command and generation-based scoring. It produces the numbers behind the OpenVLM Leaderboard, the reference leaderboard for open multimodal models, and is installed from source rather than a package registry.

chunks.title: VMLU
chunks.text: VMLU (by Zalo AI), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: VMLU is a Vietnamese benchmark suite for language models from Zalo AI and JAIST. Its core multiple-choice set has 10,880 questions across 58 subjects in STEM, humanities, social sciences and professional fields, drawn from school, university and national graduation examinations, spanning elementary school to professional study.

chunks.title: VMLU
chunks.text: VMLU (by Zalo AI), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The suite also adds reading-comprehension, discrete-reasoning and dialogue sets, and scores submissions on a public leaderboard at vmlu.ai.

chunks.title: Volcano
chunks.text: Volcano (by Volcano), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Batch scheduling system for Kubernetes, hosted by the CNCF, aimed at AI, machine learning and big-data workloads that Kubernetes' default scheduler handles poorly.

chunks.title: Volcano
chunks.text: Volcano (by Volcano), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Volcano adds gang scheduling, queues with fair-share and preemption, and GPU-aware placement, so a distributed training job either gets all the accelerators it asked for or waits rather than deadlocking on a partial allocation.

chunks.title: Vosk
chunks.text: Vosk (by Alpha Cephei), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Alpha Cephei's offline speech recognition toolkit built on Kaldi: a streaming recognizer for 20+ languages with small models for phones and Raspberry Pi boards and large ones for servers, speaker identification, and bindings for Python, Java, Node.js, C#, Go, Rust and more.

chunks.title: VoxCPM
chunks.text: VoxCPM (by OpenBMB), catalog entry under Speech & audio: OpenBMB's tokenizer-free diffusion-autoregressive text-to-speech line. VoxCPM2 has 2 billion parameters, covers 30 languages at 48 kHz, and adds voice design and controllable voice cloning; full and LoRA fine-tuning are supported.

chunks.title: Voxtral
chunks.text: Voxtral (by Mistral AI), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Mistral AI's speech models: Voxtral Mini 4B Realtime is a natively streaming recognizer for 13 languages with a configurable transcription delay of up to 2.4 s, Voxtral Mini 3B transcribes and answers questions about audio, and Voxtral TTS speaks nine languages with voice adaptation for voice agents.

chunks.title: Voyage Embeddings
chunks.text: Voyage Embeddings (by Voyage AI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Voyage AI’s text embedding line, currently the Voyage 4 series: voyage-4-large, voyage-4, voyage-4-lite and voyage-4-nano. All four share one embedding space, so a corpus embedded with the flagship can be queried with a cheaper sibling. voyage-4-large is the first production embedding model built on a mixture-of-experts architecture.

chunks.title: Voyage Embeddings
chunks.text: Voyage Embeddings (by Voyage AI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Sold through Voyage’s own API and natively through the MongoDB Atlas Embedding and Reranking API.

chunks.title: Voyage Rerank
chunks.text: Voyage Rerank (by Voyage AI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Voyage AI’s cross-encoder reranking line, currently rerank-2.5 and rerank-2.5-lite: given a query and up to 1,000 candidate documents from a first-stage retriever, they return relevance scores that reorder the shortlist.

chunks.title: Voyage Rerank
chunks.text: Voyage Rerank (by Voyage AI), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: Both carry a 32,000-token limit on query plus any single document, are multilingual, and accept a natural-language instruction appended to the query to steer relevance.

chunks.title: Vuk'uzenzele corpus
chunks.text: Vuk'uzenzele corpus (by Data Science for Social Impact, University of Pretoria), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: The Vuk'uzenzele corpus is text from South Africa's government magazine Vuk'uzenzele, extracted from its PDF editions in all 11 official languages.

chunks.title: Vuk'uzenzele corpus
chunks.text: Vuk'uzenzele corpus (by Data Science for Social Impact, University of Pretoria), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: It ships as a monolingual set with train, test and eval splits and as a sentence-aligned parallel set of more than 60,000 pairs across 55 language combinations, aligned with LASER embeddings. The Data Science for Social Impact group (DSFSI) prepared it.

chunks.title: Wan
chunks.text: Wan (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Wan is Alibaba's family of video generation models. Its current release, Wan 3.0, generates clips of up to 30 seconds with sound from text and up to 20 reference assets and supports instruction-based editing, and is served only through Alibaba Cloud Model Studio.

chunks.title: Wan
chunks.text: Wan (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: The earlier Wan 2.1 and 2.2 releases, from a 1.3B model to a 27B mixture-of-experts at up to 720p, remain downloadable.

chunks.title: WangchanThaiInstruct
chunks.text: WangchanThaiInstruct (by VISTEC), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: WangchanThaiInstruct is a human-authored Thai instruction dataset for both instruction tuning and evaluation, covering four professional domains (medical, finance, retail and legal) and seven task types from summarization to multiple-choice QA.

chunks.title: WangchanThaiInstruct
chunks.text: WangchanThaiInstruct (by VISTEC), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Annotators, domain experts and researchers wrote and checked it through a multi-stage quality-control process, and it has about 40,000 rows split into train and test sets. It is published by the VISTEC-depa AI Research Institute of Thailand.

chunks.title: WangchanX-FLAN
chunks.text: WangchanX-FLAN (by VISTEC), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: WangchanX-FLAN is a FLAN-style instruction-tuning mixture centered on Thai, combining about 3.6 million examples converted from more than two dozen existing datasets for summarization, translation, question answering, classification and text generation.

chunks.title: WangchanX-FLAN
chunks.text: WangchanX-FLAN (by VISTEC), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Sources range from ThaiSum, the scb-mt-en-th-2020 parallel corpus and Wisesight sentiment to English sets such as UltraChat, FLAN v2 and xP3x. VISTEC-depa AI Research Institute of Thailand assembled it, and the build script is public.

chunks.title: wav2vec 2.0 / HuBERT
chunks.text: wav2vec 2.0 / HuBERT (by Meta), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Meta's self-supervised speech encoders: wav2vec 2.0 and HuBERT learn speech representations from unlabeled audio and are fine-tuned into English recognizers with a CTC head. They remain a common starting point for speech fine-tuning and forced alignment.

chunks.title: WAXAL
chunks.text: WAXAL (by Google), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: WAXAL is a speech corpus for Sub-Saharan African languages in two parts: about 1,250 hours of transcribed natural speech for speech recognition in 19 languages, and single-speaker recordings of phonetically balanced scripts for text-to-speech in 17 languages.

chunks.title: WAXAL
chunks.text: WAXAL (by Google), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Partners including Makerere University, the University of Ghana and Digital Umuganda collected the audio. Google Research publishes it.

chunks.title: WeatherNext
chunks.text: WeatherNext (by Google), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: WeatherNext is Google DeepMind's global medium-range weather and tropical-cyclone forecasting line.

chunks.title: WeatherNext
chunks.text: WeatherNext (by Google), catalog entry under Scientific AI models: One repository now hosts WeatherNext 2, the WeatherNext Cyclones checkpoints and their lightweight Mini variants, together with the earlier GraphCast and GenCast models republished as WeatherNext Graph and WeatherNext Gen, plus a demo notebook that runs forecasts, tracks cyclones, and takes a training step.

chunks.title: Weave
chunks.text: Weave (by Weights & Biases), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: Toolkit for developing and monitoring AI applications from Weights & Biases, providing tracing, evaluation and dataset management for LLM applications. Functions are traced with a decorator, and it builds on the same platform as W&B's experiment tracking. The published package requires a Weights & Biases account to send traces to.

chunks.title: Weaviate
chunks.text: Weaviate (by Weaviate), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: Weaviate is an open-source vector database that stores objects and vectors together, combining vector search with structured filtering, keyword and hybrid search behind a GraphQL and REST API.

chunks.title: Weaviate
chunks.text: Weaviate (by Weaviate), catalog entry under Storage & Retrieval: It runs embedded for development, self-hosted as a Docker or Kubernetes cluster, or on the vendor's hosted service, with optional modules that call out to embedding and reranking models.

chunks.title: WebContainers
chunks.text: WebContainers (by StackBlitz), catalog entry under Deployment: Boots a full Node.js dev environment inside the browser tab as WebAssembly, running native npm, pnpm and yarn with a filesystem, terminal and dev server and no remote VM. StackBlitz builds and hosts it, and distributes the client as the `@webcontainer/api` npm package.

chunks.title: WebContainers
chunks.text: WebContainers (by StackBlitz), catalog entry under Deployment: SvelteKit, Astro, Scrimba, egghead.io and Xata embed it for in-browser coding experiences.

chunks.title: Whisper
chunks.text: Whisper (by OpenAI), catalog entry under Speech & audio: OpenAI's open-weight speech recognition and translation model family, from tiny to large-v3 and the faster large-v3-turbo. It transcribes about 99 languages and translates speech into English.

chunks.title: whisper.cpp
chunks.text: whisper.cpp (by ggml-org (Georgi Gerganov)), catalog entry under Speech & audio: A dependency-free C/C++ port of Whisper on the ggml tensor library, with integer quantization and GPU backends including Metal, CUDA and Vulkan. It runs on desktops, servers, iOS, Android, WebAssembly and the Raspberry Pi.

chunks.title: WhisperX
chunks.text: WhisperX (by m-bain), catalog entry under Speech & audio: A transcription pipeline around Whisper that adds accurate word-level timestamps through wav2vec 2.0 forced alignment, speaker labels through pyannote.audio diarization, and voice-activity-based batching on the faster-whisper backend, for up to 70 times real-time transcription.

chunks.title: WhyLabs
chunks.text: WhyLabs (by WhyLabs), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: AI observability platform for monitoring machine-learning models and LLM applications in production, covering data drift detection, performance monitoring and LLM security guardrails.

chunks.title: WhyLabs
chunks.text: WhyLabs (by WhyLabs), catalog entry under Telemetry & observability: It is built on the whylogs profiling library and the LangKit monitoring toolkit, and takes a statistical profiling approach that monitors distributions rather than individual requests.

chunks.title: Wikipedia
chunks.text: Wikipedia (by Wikimedia Foundation), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: Cleaned article text from the Wikipedia dumps in more than 300 languages, one subset per language, published as Parquet in the wikimedia namespace on Hugging Face. The current release is a single dump from November 2023. Wikipedia text is a small but widely reused component of pretraining mixtures.

chunks.title: WildChat-1M
chunks.text: WildChat-1M (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: WildChat-1M is a corpus of real user conversations with ChatGPT, drawn from about one million conversations gathered by offering online users free access to GPT-3.5 and GPT-4. It covers 68 detected languages and records timestamps, hashed IP addresses, country and state, the OpenAI model used, and moderation scores.

chunks.title: WildChat-1M
chunks.text: WildChat-1M (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Training & synthetic datasets: The public release omits conversations flagged as toxic or as containing sensitive information, and is published by the Allen Institute for AI on Hugging Face.

chunks.title: WildGuard
chunks.text: WildGuard (by Allen Institute for AI), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Ai2's safety moderation model at 7B, fine-tuned from Mistral 7B, that jointly detects harmful prompts, harmful responses and model refusals across thirteen risk subcategories. It was trained on the WildGuardMix corpus, which is published on the Hub alongside it.

chunks.title: Windsurf
chunks.text: Windsurf (by Codeium), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: AI-native IDE, forked from VS Code, built around an agentic flow engine that keeps context across multi-step coding tasks and suggests and executes terminal commands, file edits and debugging steps. It runs multi-model and multi-agent over the Agent Client Protocol, blending inline suggestions with autonomous agent actions.

chunks.title: WURA
chunks.text: WURA (by Castorini), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: WURA is a pretraining corpus of whole web and news documents in 16 African languages plus Arabic, English, French and Portuguese. Its builders audited mC4 for thirteen African languages to strip low-quality text and crawled additional verified news sources, keeping headlines and source URLs with each document.

chunks.title: WURA
chunks.text: WURA (by Castorini), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Castorini released it alongside the AfriTeVa V2 models it was built to train.

chunks.title: XGBoost
chunks.text: XGBoost (by DMLC), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: Optimized gradient-boosted decision tree library for classification, regression, ranking and survival analysis, running on a single machine, on GPUs, and distributed across Kubernetes, Spark, Dask and Ray. Bindings cover Python, R, the JVM and several other languages.

chunks.title: XGBoost
chunks.text: XGBoost (by DMLC), catalog entry under Classic ML & computer vision: It began as a University of Washington research project and is governed by a project management committee.

chunks.title: XLA
chunks.text: XLA (by OpenXLA project), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: XLA (Accelerated Linear Algebra) is a machine learning compiler that takes models from PyTorch, TensorFlow and JAX and optimizes them for execution on CPUs, GPUs and ML accelerators.

chunks.title: XLA
chunks.text: XLA (by OpenXLA project), catalog entry under Compilers & Model Optimization: It sits inside those frameworks rather than being invoked directly, so the repository is aimed at compiler contributors and at integrators adding front ends or hardware backends.

chunks.title: xLLM
chunks.text: xLLM (by xLLM-AI), catalog entry under Inference code: xLLM is an efficient LLM inference framework specifically optimized for Chinese AI accelerators. It separates a service layer that handles scheduling and availability from an engine layer that handles computation, and is deployed at scale across JD.com's core retail business.

chunks.title: XTTS
chunks.text: XTTS (by Coqui), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Coqui's voice-cloning text-to-speech model: XTTS-v2 clones a voice from a six-second sample and speaks it in 17 languages, including across languages, with streaming output. It runs on the Coqui TTS engine, now maintained by Idiap as the coqui-tts package.

chunks.title: XTuner
chunks.text: XTuner (by Shanghai AI Laboratory), catalog entry under Fine-tuning code: XTuner is a training engine for large mixture-of-experts models. Version 1 targets dropless MoE training at up to 1T parameters, long-sequence training through memory optimization rather than sequence parallelism, and FSDP-based throughput for MoE models above the 200B scale. It is maintained by Shanghai AI Laboratory.

chunks.title: Yi-1.5
chunks.text: Yi-1.5 (by 01.AI), catalog entry under Base / pretrained models: 01.AI's foundation model family at 6B, 9B and 34B with 32K-context variants, open sourced in May 2024. It continues pretraining from the original Yi release with a further 500 billion tokens, for 3.6 trillion in total.

chunks.title: YoMo
chunks.text: YoMo (by Vivgrid), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: LLM function-calling framework for building serverless AI agents on geo-distributed edge infrastructure. Developers write strongly-typed tools in TypeScript or Go, which YoMo deploys and runs across edge nodes behind an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API.

chunks.title: YoMo
chunks.text: YoMo (by Vivgrid), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: It has a Rust core with QUIC transport and TLS 1.3, and integrates MCP and A2A for agent tooling.

chunks.title: You.com Web Search API
chunks.text: You.com Web Search API (by You.com), catalog entry under Search & retrieval: Web search API returning structured results for AI applications. Results carry keyword snippets by default, and an extraction mode on the same endpoint returns the whole page as markdown or the passages that address the query. One of six separately metered APIs You.com sells.

chunks.title: YYLO
chunks.text: YYLO (by JUNO AI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Command-line orchestrator for coding agents that runs each task in a dedicated branch and worktree, with typed task, validation, merge, and release-readiness boundaries and receipt-backed repository changes.

chunks.title: YYLO
chunks.text: YYLO (by JUNO AI), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: It delegates model work to the coding agent the user installs and configures, ships repeatable command workflows, and distributes as the @yylo/cli npm package.

chunks.title: YYLO Benchmark
chunks.text: YYLO Benchmark (by JUNO AI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Benchmark harness for coding agents that runs every candidate attempt in a dedicated fresh repository with private home, temp, cache, and config roots behind a selective filesystem sandbox, and retains one hash-verified evidence chain linking the plan, attempt, workspace receipt, post-execution repository manifest, terminal, and evaluation IDs.

chunks.title: YYLO Benchmark
chunks.text: YYLO Benchmark (by JUNO AI), catalog entry under Evaluation code: Recovery, doctor, and report fail closed unless the complete chain verifies. It offers isolated v2 attempts plus an explicitly authorized governed-workflow lane, and distributes as the @yylo/benchmark npm package.

chunks.title: Z-Image
chunks.text: Z-Image (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Z-Image is a 6B-parameter single-stream diffusion transformer for text-to-image generation from Alibaba's Tongyi-MAI lab.

chunks.title: Z-Image
chunks.text: Z-Image (by Alibaba Cloud), catalog entry under Image, video, 3D & music generation: Z-Image-Turbo is a distilled version that generates in eight steps and fits in 16 GB of GPU memory, with photorealistic output and bilingual English and Chinese text rendering; the undistilled Z-Image base model supports full classifier-free guidance for fine-tuning.

chunks.title: ZA African Next Voices
chunks.text: ZA African Next Voices (by Data Science for Social Impact, University of Pretoria), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: ZA African Next Voices, also called Swivuriso, is a speech recognition dataset of about 3,000 hours of scripted and unscripted speech in seven South African languages: isiZulu, isiXhosa, Sesotho, Setswana, Xitsonga, isiNdebele and Tshivenda.

chunks.title: ZA African Next Voices
chunks.text: ZA African Next Voices (by Data Science for Social Impact, University of Pretoria), catalog entry under Language-specific datasets: Topics span agriculture, health, finance and general subjects, with speaker-disjoint splits. The South Africa Next Voices team publishes it under the dsfsi-anv Hugging Face organization, alongside a compressed copy.

chunks.title: Zapier MCP
chunks.text: Zapier MCP (by Zapier), catalog entry under Agent tools & connectors: Hosted MCP endpoint that puts Zapier's 9,000-app integration estate behind one connection: the client signs in through Zapier, Zapier holds the app credentials, and tool calls run as Zapier tasks.

chunks.title: Zed
chunks.text: Zed (by Zed Industries), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: High-performance multiplayer code editor written in Rust by the creators of Atom and Tree-sitter, built for human-AI collaboration. It offers agentic editing, parallel agents across projects, an inline assistant and its own open-weight edit-prediction model, and plugs in external agents over the Agent Client Protocol alongside MCP servers.

chunks.title: Zed
chunks.text: Zed (by Zed Industries), catalog entry under Orchestration & agents: Models run on the user's own key or on Zed's hosting.

chunks.title: ZenML
chunks.text: ZenML (by ZenML), catalog entry under ML orchestration: Framework for writing machine-learning and agent pipelines once and running them on whichever infrastructure stack is configured underneath.

chunks.title: ZenML
chunks.text: ZenML (by ZenML), catalog entry under ML orchestration: A stack names an orchestrator, an artifact store and the rest of the components; ZenML containerizes the pipeline code and hands execution to that orchestrator, which may be Airflow, Kubeflow, SageMaker, Vertex, AzureML, Databricks, Tekton, Kubernetes or a SkyPilot VM.

chunks.title: Zenodo
chunks.text: Zenodo (by CERN), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: Zenodo is a general-purpose research repository run by CERN, where anyone can deposit datasets alongside papers, software and other research outputs. Each record gets a DOI, files can be versioned under it, and a REST API handles deposit and retrieval.

chunks.title: Zenodo
chunks.text: Zenodo (by CERN), catalog entry under Data hubs & catalogs: It was launched with OpenAIRE as a catch-all repository for EU-funded research and runs on the open-source InvenioRDM platform in CERN's data centre.

chunks.title: Zentropi CoPE
chunks.text: Zentropi CoPE (by Zentropi), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Zentropi's Content Policy Evaluator (CoPE-A, 9B, built on Gemma-2-9B with LoRA) is a steerable, policy-conditioned content-labeling model.

chunks.title: Zentropi CoPE
chunks.text: Zentropi CoPE (by Zentropi), catalog entry under Safety & Guardrails: Rather than a fixed taxonomy, it evaluates content against a supplied natural-language policy and returns a binary label, with training coverage across harm areas such as hate speech, sexual content, self-harm, harassment and toxicity.

chunks.title: Zephyr
chunks.text: Zephyr (by Hugging Face), catalog entry under Fine-tuned / chat models: Hugging Face H4's open chat model line. The flagship zephyr-7b-beta is a DPO fine-tune of Mistral 7B trained with the open alignment-handbook recipe on the public UltraChat and UltraFeedback datasets, making the whole run reproducible. The line also includes a 141B mixture-of-experts ORPO variant.

chunks.title: zerank
chunks.text: zerank (by ZeroEntropy), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: ZeroEntropy's reranker line. zerank-2 is a 4B Qwen3-derived cross-encoder with a 32K context, trained through a multi-stage pipeline that models query-document relevance as adjusted Elo ratings; its card reports an average 0.6714 NDCG@10 across seven domains against 0.5847 for Cohere rerank-3.5.

chunks.title: zerank
chunks.text: zerank (by ZeroEntropy), catalog entry under Embeddings & retrieval models: The earlier zerank-1 and zerank-1-small ship alongside it. Notion acquired ZeroEntropy in July 2026 and the weights were released under Apache 2.0.

chunks.title: ZKML (ddkang)
chunks.text: ZKML (ddkang) (by Daniel Kang), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: ZKML (ddkang) compiles a TensorFlow Lite model into a Halo2 zero-knowledge circuit and proves that an inference ran on that model, so a verifier can check the output without re-running the model or trusting whoever ran it.

chunks.title: ZKML (ddkang)
chunks.text: ZKML (ddkang) (by Daniel Kang), catalog entry under Assurance & compliance evidence: It is a Rust library with Python converters for models and inputs, and proves with either KZG or IPA commitments. Daniel Kang publishes it from a personal GitHub account, with the paper that describes the method.

chunks.title: ZML
chunks.text: ZML (by ZML), catalog entry under Inference code: ZML is a production inference stack built in Zig on MLIR and Bazel, compiling models directly for NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, TPU and Trainium so that a workload is not tied to one vendor's accelerator.

chunks.title: Zonos
chunks.text: Zonos (by Zyphra), catalog entry under Speech & audio: Zyphra's expressive text-to-speech models with voice cloning and emotion control: ZONOS2, an 8B mixture-of-experts model trained on more than six million hours of speech, streams in three tiers of languages, and the earlier Zonos v0.1 outputs 44 kHz speech.

chunks.title: Zvec
